# Experiments

What has been tried, so it isn't repeated: lessons, and the ideas that lost, were level and dropped, or are held.
Kept changes are in [hyperion/CHANGES.md](hyperion/CHANGES.md), not here. The untrimmed file (every measurement and
the per-round fuel details) is `git show 1d5ddf0:research/EXPERIMENTS.md`.

Win rates are against the bot's previous version, all maps from both sides at the real fuel budget, unless noted.
`tools/ab.py` runs 1094 games: ladder (70) + `maps/gen` (512) + fresh `maps/gen-s1` (512); results before 2026-10-21
used 390-582 games. Noise is about ±2.1 points on 582 games; "level" means within noise. Don't retry a lost or level
idea as is: it needs a new mechanism or ladder evidence. Results on older bots are hints, not rules.

## Lessons

- The emblem lab's per-decision randomisation misreads policy-level effects (round 4, 2026-11-10): 1.28M games
  scored ocean without its learned table as level where an A/B reads 47.0%, and its best selection (+0.15 ± 0.05
  cross-fitted, all folds positive) lost 2 points. Calibrate a lab on an effect an A/B already knows, replicate on
  later games, and A/B a mid-run candidate before the final fit.
- A joint SPSA over a large set of level changes and their constants finds nothing (soup tune, 2026-11-07: 92 params,
  6.5M games, every checkpoint within noise of the base). Level members stay level when fitted together, and
  members that read ~50 alone can sum to -4 to -16 points through fuel and interactions: bisect a pooled start at
  the real budget before tuning it.
- Gains on the committed suites shrink on fresh seeds (crews +22/320 -> +8/320; a 54.6% hecate bundle was 47.8% on a
  fresh suite): confirm on a fresh seed.
- Self-play hides ladder behaviour. Our bots start a recall at every turn end and cancel it the next turn, so locally
  enemies look like they are recalling in ~90% of rounds (5-8% on the ladder): any value for cancelling an enemy
  recall is inflated locally, and an ally's `channel == recall` does not mean it is going home. Changes level or
  better locally have lost on the ladder (the big-bag escort, the stunned-turn skip, the shared-gem caster draft).
- Bug fixes, drafts and map-type strategies have paid off. Retuning tactics or pricing against our own bots rarely
  has; whole-model ports (morgana's farm pricing into nemesis 43.0%, a pack zone decided by the fight sim 46.9%,
  farming stage 2 45.1%) lost.
- Who wins: in the mirror the side that dies first loses 70%, and +1 net kill at round 300 takes the win rate from 56%
  to 85%. A fight's swing is predicted by HP fraction, lifetime gold and the initiative; head count adds nothing once
  those are in. contest is the only ladder map that reaches round 2000: 31% of its games tie on gems, then gold
  decides.
- Loss analysis (mirror, 390 games): winners die 2.0 times a game against 4.1. 86% of deaths carry no gems; 79% are on
  our own ground, but the risk per champion-round is 3.4/1000 on enemy ground vs 0.7 on ours; 88% follow a retreat
  within 4 turns. Weak families against other bots: huge, large-open, islands, Monolith-only, maze, rows.
- Single-map flips between versions follow fuel trajectories, not regressions; two games a map is noise.
  `results.json` match `winner` is the 0-based bot index; reading 1 as bot 1 inverts every per-map table.
- Predicting the fight better is not winning it (combat lab, 2026-11-08): a learned enemy-reply danger with a third
  less log-loss than the flat term (0.42 vs 0.64) was level in games, and even computed and discarded it lost a point. A cost that grows with
  the number of danger queries lands in the heaviest turns, and ocean's fuel gates absorb a flat cost of the same mean
  but not that. Judge a new per-query term's fuel against a burn arm of equal cost.
- ocean's fight model is calibrated where it decides (2026-11-09, [combat-lab/cal-notes.md](combat-lab/cal-notes.md)): on
  1,966 debug mirror games, stand and chase verdicts logged with a margin (log2 of our health that flips them) and joined
  with outcomes. For stands P(our side dies first | a death) crosses 50% at margin 0, and a regression discontinuity at
  the boundary is flat for both stands and chases (bodies and games won within ±0.01-0.02). Its parts are biased: members
  hit 20-50% as often as the sim assumes, unseen enemies 19%. But the biases cancel. Healthy (90%+) champions that
  leave a narrowly lost stand are right to. Recalibrating the model has nothing to correct; the level combat and team
  arms opened opportunities at this boundary, where fighting and declining are worth the same.
- A per-champion rate gap to Fish is not a lever by itself (spell, 2026-11-08): making Cassi cast her exclusive spell
  like Fish (31% -> 53% at 2-4 tiles) added +0.02 kills a game, and weighting more capture gold to Marcella (+85 at
  r400) cost her teammates 230. Check kills and team totals before building an arm from a rate.
- A risk change can win the mirror and nothing else (nuke guard, 2026-11-08): +0.22 held out over 149k, panel -0.02.
  The v84 pattern again: a risk or greed change needs its panel H1 before it ships.

## Fuel after 496 (ocean, 2026-11-10; CHANGES 497)

[Campaign, manifests, oracles and rejected experiments](fuel-2026-11-10-third/README.md). Worked alone.
Fresh 4,096-game bench: **OOF 40,183 → 34,789 (-13.42%, 95% -16.43 to -10.07)**; shortcuts
**1,419,556 → 1,327,255 (-6.50%)**. Per-turn reductions are 12.96% and 6.00%; mean fuel falls 0.89%.
Fresh release A/B: **51.0% (49.4–52.5)**, OOF 37,031 → 32,964 (**-10.98%**). Standard release: 47.8%
(45.1–50.6), OOF -8.14%. No failed games or broken/capped drafts. Frozen as `variants/oc-fuel-497`.

Kept: compile-time strike coefficients (SIMD evaluation), derived champion metadata, SIMD team ranks,
compile-time Reach geometry/merges, ward window masks, and an exact early exit once Reach's damage/basic
follow-up/stun result is settled. No budgets, thresholds or draft changes. Matching ≥100k turns save
1,645 fuel on average. 100M: 93/96 own-draft replays directly identical; the three differing maps become
6/6 identical without either bot's next-turn walk preparation (the existing cache-readiness coupling).
Forced compositions covering all 13 bodies and large camp groups: **108/108 identical**. Actual-source
checks cover 2.08M strikes in scalar and SIMD, 3.38M ordered Reach recipes, 1.7M rankings, all derived
metadata, and over 325k same-state engine Reach queries.

The first five changes screened at -14.4% OOF but confirmed at only -9.3% debug/-9.7% release. The early
exit was added; the final independent suite is ladder-v2 seeds 1461410–1461417. Do not count the first
suite's development reruns as fresh evidence. The exact final source totals -11.43% OOF over both 4,096-game
debug suites. The final suite also reduces farm cuts from 586,607 to 556,458 and prey cuts from 174,045 to 156,239.

Dropped after measurement: compact Fighter fields, quiet-damage batching, extra strike/camp/HealGate
caches, relative-order caching, dominated-way pruning, redundant-bound caching, shared stun/shield reads,
camp-stun guards, a strike-tile heap, and scalar pairwise ranking. Most add bookkeeping to already cheap
paths. Reusing attack-range boxes costs 74 fuel per heavy turn; a stored maximum reach saves mean fuel
but costs heavy turns. The paused fuel-prover handoff was reviewed: more farm-loop slack increased OOF
without a clear win-rate gain; those reserve reductions are not included. Its queue guard, ported onto
this bundle and screened on 1,024 games, gives OOF 8,671 → 8,772 (+1.16%, within noise), shortcuts +0.84%
and mean fuel +0.28%; dropped. Details and the preserved handoff are in this campaign's notes.

## Emblem lab round 4 on ocean (2026-11-10, tools/emblab; nothing shipped): 1.84M games, no table beats ocean's, and the dense per-decision design cannot see what the A/Bs see

Run by [RUNBOOK.md](../tools/emblab/RUNBOOK.md) (written from this run) on ocean b0eeff17e (= CHANGES 496).
Tools and tables: `tools/emblab/` (README "Round 4"), `research/ideas-2026-11-10/emblab4/`; data in
`replays/emblab/{r4,r4b,r4c,r4d}`.

**The lab.**
- **Games:** 1,840,000, every batch 0 errors and 0 draft mismatches (about 20 games a batch end by round 5: a
  body's unfinished draft). 80k-game batches at slot weight 35, ~6.5 minutes each (~195 games/s) beside other jobs.
- **Maps:** the 128 ladder maps and fresh-3100000..3100399 (`--mix ladder-v2`; 100,481 maps of published size),
  the non-ladder ones walked in a fixed shuffle. Held out: fresh-3110000..3110119 (`merged/emb4-h1`, `-h2`, `-h3`).
- **Drafts** of the lab side: 40% random (half holding Cassi & Issac, none Stellar), 30% the top 10 other teams'
  ladder compositions since 2026-11-06 (4,219 ranked groups; 4,965 / 6,340 / 19,461 team-games at 3 / 4 / 5 picks),
  30% the shipped draft model's team on the map.
- **Opponents (new):** 40% a second lab team, 30% the Fish body, 30% the Mite body (`spar-dvn952/953-Flp4`, `-Mt3q`),
  which draft and shop for themselves. The lab side won 58.6% / 51.0% against the Fish / Mite body under dense
  forcing and 62.1% / 54.6% under sparse: dense forcing alone costs a team about 3.5 points.
- **Dense phases** (1,280,000 games; 35% / 50% of every new-emblem decision below k12 drawn, as rounds 2-3): `r4`
  480k with the proposal steered by round 3's static gains, `r4b` 400k steered by this round's own 240k-game fit,
  `r4c` 400k by its 720k-game fit (every row logs its own probabilities, so the steer may change).
- **Sparse phase** (`r4d`, 560,000 games): only the first three emblems, each drawn 10% of the time.
- **Checks:** over rows with k < 12, the mean of 1 / P(base) where the base was taken is 1.0004 and the summed
  1 / P(chosen) elsewhere 28.400 a row against 28.406 other drawable arms.

**What the dense lab reads** (`dfit.mjs --variant static`, round 3's penalties; `select.py`; win points a decision,
cross-fitted over maps; a team makes ~28 decisions below k12):

| rule | 720k games (mid-run) | the next 240k (`--on`) | all 1.28M |
|---|---|---|---|
| per cell (pick count, type, ordinal), z 2 | -0.03 ± 0.05 | +0.01 ± 0.09 | +0.03 ± 0.04 |
| per (type, ordinal bucket), z 2 (`tb-z2`) | **+0.149 ± 0.050** | -0.02 ± 0.09 | +0.07 ± 0.04 |
| per (type, ordinal), z 2 | +0.135 ± 0.049 | -0.06 ± 0.08 | +0.09 ± 0.04 |
| the fit's own best arm (any lead) | -0.27 ± 0.07 | | -0.16 ± 0.05 |

- **Map-keyed** (9 features named before the run: gold_side, contested_share, spawn_dist, area, gems_side,
  big_share, cluster_share, altar_centre, altars; cuts at bins 2, 4, 6 of 8; 312 configs), nested: static configs
  +0.05 ± 0.04, map-keyed configs -0.01 ± 0.05. The best single config (per type, gold_side split, z 1) reads
  +0.20 ± 0.06 and is the best of 312. As in round 3, no map split survives nesting.
- **Per opponent kind and per draft source** (`--kinds src`) the readings agree within their errors: `tb-z2`
  +0.05 / +0.05 / +0.14 against self / Fish / Mite, +0.08 / +0.07 / +0.06 on random / ladder / model teams.

**What the A/Bs read.** Every row: 20,480 games on a held-out merged suite, own drafts, release builds, fast
runner, against `variants/ocean-b0eeff1`; ± is the 95% interval.

| candidate | the lab's estimate | A/B |
|---|---|---|
| mid-run `tb-z2`, arms written into `learned_arm` (207 cells) | +0.149 a decision | 47.9% (47.2-48.6) h1; fresh gate -2.9 ± 1.7 after 8 blocks, ladder -1.1 |
| the same at the purchase only (`candidate.py --buy`) | | 48.1% (47.5-48.8) h1; fresh gate -2.0 ± 1.3 after 10 blocks, ladder -0.2 |
| its first-emblem cells only / second only / k >= 3 only | k0 +0.50 ± 0.17 a k0 decision | 49.7% / 49.8% / 48.6% h1 |
| Prism's first emblem Jungle-Focus alone | +3.2 a decision (in sample) | 49.8% h1 |
| all 1.28M games' `tb-z2` (225 cells), purchase only | +0.07 a decision | 48.4% (47.8-49.1) h2 |
| all 1.28M games' per (type, ordinal) z 2, k < 3 only (69 cells) | +0.065 a decision | 50.0% (49.3-50.7) h2 |

**Calibration: what ocean's existing table (CHANGES 233, round 2) is worth, which the lab should also see.**

| change to ocean | A/B (h1 unless noted) | the dense lab |
|---|---|---|
| no table (every cell the current logic) | **47.0%** (46.3-47.7) | +0.010 ± 0.030 a decision: level |
| no table at the purchase only (forecasts keep it) | 47.4% | |
| the same on ladder test drafts (both bots `test_draft`) | 45.6% (44.9-46.3) | model teams -0.01 ± 0.05, ladder +0.04 ± 0.05, random 0.00 ± 0.05 |
| no table from k3 on | 48.1%; purchase only 48.3% | -0.003 ± 0.022 |
| no table at k0-2 | 50.5%, 50.4% (h2), 49.9% (h3): 50.3% of 61,440 | +0.012 ± 0.020 |
| k >= 3 without its Collectors cells (39) | **48.3%** (47.6-49.0) | |
| k >= 3 without its Home (40) / Tribute (21) / Monster (36) / Durability (27) cells | 49.8% / 50.0% / 49.7% / 49.9% | |
| Collectors as everyone's k-th emblem where the table has none by then: k 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 6 / 8 | 48.7% / 49.4% / 49.8% / 50.2% / 49.9% / 50.4% | |
| family F as everyone's 5th emblem (k 4) where the table has none by then: Skirmish / Durability / Monster / Prospector / Jungle / Capture / Treasure / Hunter / Home / Tribute | 50.7% (50.0-51.3) / 50.1% / 50.1% / 50.1% / 50.0% / 49.8% / 49.7% / 49.7% / 49.7% / 49.1% | |
| Skirmish as everyone's k-th emblem: k 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 | 50.1% / 50.7% / 50.3% / 50.5% | |
| Skirmish at k 4 on the other holdouts | 50.5% (h2), 50.5% (h3): **50.55% of 61,440** (z 2.7) | |
| Skirmish at k 4 and no table at k0-2 | 50.4%, 50.8% (h2), 50.2% (h3): 50.46% of 61,440 | |
| Skirmish at k 4, fresh gate (Flp4 / Mt3qro) | 32 blocks, 4,096 fresh units: fresh **+0.59 ± 0.61**, ladder +0.43 ± 0.59, pooled +0.51 ± 0.42; Fish +0.54, Mite +0.65; SPRT undecided (LLR -0.09 at 50.5 / 50.75) | |

**Findings.**
- **Nothing to ship.** No selection from 1.28M dense games beats ocean: the mid-run and final candidates lose 1.6
  to 2.1 points, their early-ordinal parts are level.
- **The existing table is worth about 3 points to ocean, nearly all of it late Collectors** (+1% damage per family
  owned; `current_emblem` credits it for camp damage only). Its k0-2 cells are worth nothing (50.3% of 61,440 without them);
  its Home, Tribute, Monster and Durability cells are each level. Collectors is already placed about right:
  earlier costs, later or wider is level.
- **Why the lab misread tables** (checked afterwards on its own data: `selfheal.py`, `pooled_edits.py`). It
  measures one cell changed with every other cell of the build as the base has it; a table changes many cells of
  one champion at once.
  - **The base heals a single deviation.** A champion drawn away from a passive the base wanted owns it anyway
    within three more emblems 60% of the time (Prospector 77%, Capture 75%, Collectors 49%): a later table cell, the
    current logic or a later draw buys it. So the lab scores dropping the late Collectors cells at -0.49 ± 0.24
    points a team where dropping all 39 plays -1.7, every late cell at -0.06 ± 0.56 against -1.9, and the whole
    table at +0.25 ± 0.77 against -3.0. A selection's cells are each scored with the purchases they jointly delete
    still in place: the final selection overwrote 165 of the table's 328 cells, and one arm written into a bucket's
    consecutive cells falls back to the current logic after its first purchase, which drops the table's arms there.
  - **Noise, and a noise pick is not neutral.** A fixed policy is resolved to ±0.5-0.8 points by 1.28M games; a
    selection is the best of 43 candidates in each of 468 cells. A proposal-drawn arm costs about 0.25 points
    against the base (dense forcing costs a team 3.5 points over ~14 draws), so a selection that is mostly noise
    and moves 45% of decisions loses points rather than reading level.
  - **The data is sound for what it measures.** For edits that change one cell a champion, pooled over types and
    stated beforehand (family F as everyone's k-th emblem), the same sums agree with the A/Bs: over the 19 such
    edits A/B'd above, correlation +0.42, rms gap 0.51 points (the size of the errors), mean +0.09 against -0.10;
    Collectors at k8 reads +0.34 ± 0.11 (A/B +0.4), Tribute at k4 -0.46 ± 0.41 (-0.9).
  - Not a fitting bug (a model-free Hajek check agrees with the fit; the candidates buy what their tables say:
    `emblem_orders.mjs`), not the forecasts (purchase-only builds read the same), not the draft mix or the opponents
    (per source and per kind the readings agree).
- **A cross-fitted +0.15 ± 0.05 with all five folds positive did not replicate** on the next games (-0.02 ± 0.09).
  Require the replication (`select.py --on`) and an A/B of a mid-run candidate before trusting a fit.
- **The sparse design is honest but far too thin at this size:** three batches gave 200-350 draws an arm at a main
  champion's first emblem (±3 points). It needs 10M+ games, or draws limited to a handful of arms.
- **One lead: Skirmish as every champion's fifth emblem** (`tables/emblem_table-skirmish4.h`: Skirmish in the type's
  usual stat at ordinal 4 of the 37 rows with none by then; `collectors.py --family skirmish --at 4`): 50.55% of
  61,440 over three held-out suites (50.7 / 50.5 / 50.5), ordinals 3, 5 and 6 at 50.1-50.5%. Skirmish went to x1.10
  in patch 4.0.0, after the table was learned (9 of its cells hold it); it was the only one of ten passive families to read
  above level in this slot (ten looks: the first reading alone was a 1-in-4 chance, the two repeats and the gate
  are the evidence). The fresh gate reads the same against the bodies, +0.51 ± 0.42 pooled over 32 blocks, and its
  SPRT stays undecided: about half a point, at the 50.5 bar rather than over it. Not merged.
- **What measured correctly tonight was the clean A/B of a policy-level change** (20,480 games, ±0.7, ~10 minutes
  beside other jobs). The next emblem work should randomise whole tables or build orders per team-game, not
  single decisions inside a shared build.
- **Tooling:** the CPU-slot pool's member-file race lost the lab's weight for a batch (19 of 86 slots, 25 minutes
  instead of 6.5; `tools/emblab/slot_keeper.py`, RUNBOOK section 9). Not fixed in `cpu_slots.py` / fastrunner.

## Fuel after 495 (ocean, 2026-11-10; CHANGES 496)

[Full campaign](fuel-2026-11-10-next/README.md), with manifests, compact results, arithmetic/support oracles
and the rejected variants. Fresh 4,096-game bench: **OOF -19.3%, shortcuts -4.9%, mean fuel -0.54%**.
Fresh release A/B: 50.8% (49.2–52.3), OOF -16.3%. The requested further 10% OOF reduction is met.

The largest gain came from following support's callers: they need a threat boolean or `safe()`, while the
nine-tile station builder calculated full damage and stun bounds. Only the independent heal step needs those
bounds. Precomputed champion output coefficients and explicit-mask strike caching add smaller exact savings.

Dropped: two-spell closed forms (dearer than strike caching), extra wake-cache buckets (+1 mean fuel),
gold/cooldown/item caches (+55 mean/+74 heavy), earlier stale checks (no real-budget OOF gain), lazy station
entries (small gain, more cache complexity), ground-centre special cases and retreat/reach loop changes
(only 1–4 mean fuel). Don't repeat them unchanged. High-budget differences in the kept bundle all disappear
when both sides omit next-turn walk preparation: the existing cache-readiness coupling, not different risk
answers. Forced Stellar/Willow teams and 352-member camp groups cover cases absent from the normal suite.

Measurement lesson: bench.py's `out_of_fuel` field and stdout recovery lines undercount actual engine OOF.
The campaign comparison tool uses runner totals and excludes OOF from shortcut counts. On fresh games the
improvement remains -19.1% OOF and -4.6% shortcuts after normalising for the number of play turns.

## (ocean = d4f6e68a6, CHANGES 495, 2026-11-10) Fuel ceiling re-measured: 54.2% at 10M; cut work +2.9, out-of-fuel +1.3

The same design as "Fuel ceiling (ocean, 2026-11-08)", on current `bots/ocean`. Copies `variants/oc-ceil-ref`,
`oc-ceil-10m` (same code) and `oc-ceil-view` (`fuel()` reads the budget less one 1x budget, set per turn in main.cc:
the 11-08 fv-a patch). The extra fuel goes by name (`FASTRUNNER_BOT_FUEL=oc-ceil-10m:10000000,oc-ceil-view:200000`).
Both arms play against oc-ceil-ref at the real budget. Fast runner (cambc 5.0.1), release builds, own drafts, the
same 20,480 games each: `merged/fceil-2020` (ladder-v2, 2020000-2020039). Each run took about 7 minutes.

| arm | win % (CI) | OOF arm / ref |
|---|---|---|
| 10M a turn | **54.2 (53.5-54.9)** | 0 / 198,439 |
| 2x quantum, gates read the 1x budget (view) | 51.3 (50.6-52.0) | 237 / 208,439 |
| 10M against view, paired by map | **+2.86 ±0.89** | |

- **The ceiling has not fallen since 11-08.** It was 53.4-53.5 on oc-base25 (cambc 5.0.0 semantics) and 56.3 on
  astraeus 5b66bde.
- **The cut work is worth the same as before:** +2.9 against 11-08's +2.8 (53.5 - 50.7).
- **Never running out is worth +1.3, up from +0.7,** although CHANGES 495 cut OOF turns by 13%. One untested reading:
  under 5.0.1 a turn that runs out stops right after the host call that spent the fuel, which changes ~7% of
  outcomes.
- Results, 95% CI and OOF counts: `replays/ab/fceil-{10m,view}/summary.md`.

**Which subsystem's fuel pays** (same games). `variants/oc-fz2-*` = oc-ceil-ref + the 11-08 refund (`fz_scope`: fuel
spent inside one subsystem is refunded to every later `fuel()` read), on a 10M quantum with every gate reading the
1x budget. Paired by map against the arm that refunds nothing (`oc-fz2-view`, 51.6%):

| freed | win % | paired diff (95%) | results changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| everything (10M arm above) | 54.2 | +2.55 ±0.89 | 46% |
| world update | 52.8 | **+1.14 ±0.89** | 45% |
| farm (`farm`, `farm_reprice`) | 52.7 | **+1.11 ±0.89** | 45% |
| prey | 52.1 | +0.43 ±0.83 | 39% |
| strike search | 51.8 | +0.20 ±0.79 | 33% |
| fight trade | 51.6 | -0.03 ±0.81 | 36% |
| turn-end queue (new) | 51.5 | -0.15 ±0.72 | 29% |
| step guard | 51.4 | -0.23 ±0.76 | 32% |
| turn order (new) | 51.4 | -0.27 ±0.60 | 19% |
| the first turn's gates at 50x (`oc-fz2-t1`, `t1_mult` 50; no refund) | 52.0 | +0.33 ±0.67 | 25% |

- **The prize is the world update and the farm.** Each is worth about +1.1, together most of the +2.55.
- **The step guard and turn order no longer pay.** On v87 raw fuel in each was worth +1.0 / +1.1; here about 0.
- **A free queue is worth nothing,** although it then fills its whole list: what it warms now is not what cut turns
  lack.
- `replays/ab/fz2-*/summary.md`; the 2x view arm (51.3) reads -0.30 ±0.61 against the 10M one.
- **The world update's +1.14 is not reachable by reordering** (lane A, research/fuelgap-2026-11-10/laneA.md):
  - On farm-cut turns it costs 10.2k, but nearly all of its output is read before the turn's first action.
  - At most ~1.1k could be deferred: far tracking 0.5k, altars and scores 0.6k.
  - Skipping unchanged entities is already done wherever the engine can prove it.
  - No candidates were built.
- **Lane C (around the farm loop) is no-go on all three directions** (research/fuelgap-2026-11-10/laneC.md):
  - Fuel at farm entry is 57k on cut turns against 83k on uncut ones. The biggest pre-farm parts on cut turns:
    `chase_with_guard` declining to chase (14.2k) and the feint recall's want_home (9.1k).
  - Refunding everything spent before the farm (`fgc-fzpre`, the most any reordering could buy) cuts 77% of cut
    loops, yet reads +0.31 (-0.55 to +1.20).
  - The whole farm free only after a turn with 30k+ spare (`fgc-fzspare`, the most any prefetch could buy):
    +0.43 (-0.45 to +1.27).
  - Post-loop shortcuts fire on ~2% of cut turns.
  - fzpre against fz2-farm reads -0.81 (-1.71 to +0.04). So the farm's +1.11 may come less from finishing its loop
    than from what that scope also refunds: `farm_reprice` in continue_recall, and the step guard and route searches
    the farm calls.
- **Lane B (inside the farm loop) is no-go** (research/fuelgap-2026-11-10/laneB.md):
  - Refunding the loop alone (`fgb-fzloop`) reads +0.65 ±0.88. Finishing every cut loop at the cut's own fuel
    (`fgb-flcut`) reads +0.52 ±0.87. The farm's other ~+0.5 lies outside the loop.
  - At 10M, 82% of loops that would be cut keep the same pick. The other 18% (~22 a game a team) pick a median 0.63
    of the full pick's value; the full pick is 1-4 groups past the cut, ~775 fuel a group.
  - Measured and dropped: fallbacks for a cut with no pick (the full loop has none in 54%; the rest is spread over
    k..k+9); last turn's values as extra candidates (right 1.3k times, wrong 24.9k); exact crew memos (keys match in 4%
    of calls).
  - Candidate `fgb-plan`: reuse a one-round-old crew plan when output, claimers in sight and expect are unchanged.
    100M identical 96/96, fires 64 times a game, but cut loops are unchanged (144.5 against 144.8 a game): the reusable
    fuel is in only 16% of cut loops. Not gated.
- **The farm's +1.11, split** (refund arms, same games, paired against `oc-fz2-view`):
  - The group loop alone (`fgb-fzloop`): +0.65 ±0.88.
  - Everything the farm spends outside its loop (`oc-fz2-fout`): +0.77 ±0.89. That is the work before and after the
    loop and the step guard and route searches it calls; a `PauseScope` stops the refund inside the loop.
  - `farm_reprice` alone (`oc-fz2-rep`, the repricing bank.cc calls in recalls): -0.16 ±0.57. It is not the missing
    half.
  - The whole farm against fout: +0.35 ±0.84.
  - The parts sum past the whole (1.42 against 1.11) and neither is significant alone. The farm's prize is split
    about evenly between its loop and its route and field work, with no single piece.
- **Programme verdict: no lane found a reachable lever.** The +2.55 of cut work is spread out:
  - the world update needs its output before acting;
  - reordering and prefetch around the farm are worth at most ~+0.3 to +0.4;
  - the farm loop is worth ~+0.5, and its misses are near-misses;
  - the first turn is worth +0.33.
- **The first turn is small** (+0.33). It spends 146k of its 200k before acting (world build 63k), and its farm is cut
  almost every game, but freeing its gates buys little. No lane opened.

## (ocean = oc-wdash-494, 2026-11-10) Ward spread: a bush preference per champion, ward announces in priority, ward sightings shared; all level

The user's idea: give each champion preferred bushes to ward and announce wards, so the team's wards spread and, through
shared enemy sightings, see more enemies in aggregate. Arms `variants/wp-*` (dev copy `wp-dev`, knobs
`params::wardpref`, all off: bench wide 52/52 identical at 100M). Script and wp-dev's diff: `research/wardpref-2026-11-10/`.

- **The premise is wrong:** ocean posts no enemy sightings in either channel. The shared bytes carry claims, bag, camp
  respawns and, while a healer lives, ally positions (CHANGES 465). `World::note_sighting` has no caller. Vision is
  personal, so without sharing a spread ward changes only its owner's own vision. Sharing sightings had already lost
  three times (CHANGES 236, macro-4/river, cm-sight1-3 in "Position comms").
- **Measured** (512 games of oc-wdash-494 against Flp4/Mt3q on fresh f0, replay vision, rough line of sight):
  - the team sees 31% of enemy-rounds, 2.0 of ours per seen enemy, and 28.5% of what it sees only through wards;
  - 15.9% of pairs of our wards share a bush cluster;
  - an enemy unseen in a bush within 8 of one of ours is ~1.1% of enemy-rounds, 88% of those in clusters we have not
    warded;
  - a ward sighting that an ally within 8 lacks: ~154 enemy-rounds a game.
- **Arms:**
  - `wp-pref1`: bush tiles of our colour on a 3x3-block lattice, (bx + 2 by) mod bodies, count double in
    `ward_bushes`. It needs no table: no DraftPlan bits.
  - `wp-pw9`: priority payload bits 14-15, the only free ones, announce "my ward is in a bush within 3 of me"; a new
    cluster near a visible announcing ally scores x0.1.
  - `wp-sh`: the visible enemy we see only through our ward, nearest a teammate within 12, goes in a new shared record
    (the ally record's bits when no healer is drafted) and fixes readers' beliefs. It fits in 49% of games.
  - `wp-pref05` and `wp-pw5` were stopped after the trace: the stronger settings already moved nothing.
- **Trace** (256 debug games each): the dedup discount fired ~58 times a game. Pairs sharing a cluster stayed 15.9-16.0%
  for every arm, and pairs within 3 stayed 15.2-15.5%. The ward choice is mostly forced: few clusters lie within
  placement range, and planned wards come first.

Results against oc-wdash-494 (fgate, Flp4/Mt3q, 16 blocks, 16,384 games each, 8,192 of them fresh; win %):

| arm | fresh | pooled | ladder | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wp-pref1 | 50.0 (49.2-50.8) | 49.7 (49.1-50.4) | 49.5 | undecided (LLR high -0.84, low +0.19) |
| wp-pw9 | 49.9 (49.2-50.7) | 49.9 (49.4-50.5) | 50.0 | undecided (LLR high -1.18, low +0.07) |
| wp-sh | 49.5 (48.7-50.3) | 49.7 (49.1-50.3) | 49.9 | undecided (LLR high -1.54, low -0.51) |

Dropped. Preference and dedup don't change where wards go. Shared ward sightings are the only arm with aggregate vision,
and they read -0.5, as sharing sightings has before. Open: priority bits 14-15 are also the round tag of the
`prio_stream` mask (not live), so a later ward or comms arm in them would conflict with it.

## (fishx = ocean-16d6f78 + classifier, 2026-11-10) Cohesion exploiter: packing near allies moves cohesion a little and wins nothing

Idea (fish-re, [oppmodel/fish.md](ideas-2026-11-09/oppmodel/fish.md) "Deaths"): Fish is no better at equal numbers but
packs (1.54 mates within 5 vs our 1.14), so we meet it outnumbered. Notes and data:
[oppmodel/cohesion.md](ideas-2026-11-09/oppmodel/cohesion.md); tools ~/tmp-offload/fishcoh/tools.

- **Live (544 latest-Fish games, r20-400).** Nearest teammate within 2: Fish 52%, us 39%. Early deaths level (1,530 vs
  1,579), nearest ally at death about as near; foes - mates >= 2 at 38% of our deaths vs 27% of Fish's. Our contact
  samples at Fish's foes-mates mix and our hazard: about 13% fewer deaths in contact, the ceiling of this lever.
- **Arm.** farm.cc: a group's value x 1 within 6 of the nearest live ally's anchor (its claimed group's centre, else its
  seen or told tile), falling linearly to 0.75 at 14 and beyond (a discount, so the prune bounds hold).
  fc1-coh75 = while fishx::on (classifier Fish >= 0.8), fc2-coh75 = always. bots/fishx: params::coh_mode, and
  params::fishx_deny = false turns the parked deny arms off.
- **Mechanism.** Ours within 5: 1.17-1.20 -> 1.27-1.31 (Fish 1.54). Against Flp4 (packs like live Fish), fresh
  slice f0: our deaths 5.4 -> 5.1 a game, the body's 10.1 -> 9.4, gold level. Against Flp3 (spreads), ladder: our
  deaths 5.8 -> 6.7, gold -5% at r400, the extra deaths healthy ones in fights where we have the numbers. Floor 0.5
  read no better on 256-game smokes (Flp4 79.3% vs 80.9%, Mt3q 69.9% vs 73.8%). Head to head against the base
  (ladder, 256): fc1 53.1%, fc2 48.8%.

Results against ocean-16d6f78 (fgate, bodies Flp4/Mt3q, fresh ladder-v2 maps decide; points of win rate, 95% CI):

| arm | fresh | ladder | Fish / Mite (fresh) | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fc1-coh75 (Fish only) | -0.22 ±0.70 of 4,352 units | +0.56 | +0.03 / -0.48 | high LLR -1.68 at block 34; stopped |
| fc2-coh75 (always) | -0.76 ±0.82 of 4,352 units | +0.38 | -0.69 / -0.84 | high LLR -2.00, low -0.92 at block 34; stopped |

Level for Fish, below zero unconditioned. The two 256-game Flp4 smokes (+5 and +2.7 points) were lucky draws. The
farm discount moves only a third of the cohesion gap, and the deaths it saves against a packing team (~0.3 a game)
are paid back in farm or in fights taken with the numbers. Being outnumbered at contact is not the general weakness
it looked like: a stronger form would need a different mechanism than farm's pick (travel together, or decline
contact against a seen pack), not a heavier discount.

## (ocean = ocean-16d6f78, 2026-11-09) Camp health weight: farm already prices live health; abandonments come from other branches

Idea (user): weigh a camp's live health, preferring to finish low-health camps. Tools and patches:
[ideas-2026-11-09/camphp-tools/](ideas-2026-11-09/camphp-tools/).

- **Today's bot.** Camps never regenerate. Farm's rate already uses each member's last-seen health (`clear_health`,
  `fastest_clear`, `min_camp_damage`), so a part-cleared group is priced by the clear it has left; there is no
  separate health weight. Camp health is personal (vision is per champion, comms carries no camp health).
- **Ladder (11-08 on, 4,299 extracted games; abandonment = a gap of >= 10 rounds in a group's damage while members
  live).** All three teams leave 7-11% of the groups they damage; afterwards the same team resumes ~80% (median
  22-27 rounds), the enemy captures ~11%. The enemy captures 18-26% of groups left under half health, 4-5% of
  groups left above 3/4. Against each other, Fish/Mite steal ~1.0-1.1 groups a game from us (~28-33 gems) and we
  steal 1.0-1.3 from them: no deficit. The difference: we leave groups we could finish in < 3 rounds of our
  recent damage 1.04 times a game, Fish 0.45 and Mite 0.55.
- **Why (local debug traces, base vs spar-dvn1-Flp, 128 ladder maps both sides).** The same 1.0/game locally. Of
  near-finished abandonments: retreat while still targeting the group 0.25/game (31% then stolen), incidental hits
  (never our target) 0.19, a farm switch 0.15-0.19, chase 0.13, still targeted but unhit 0.11. The farm switches are
  mostly the claimed path's `health_left <= 0`: an ally claiming the group is expected (Chebyshev arrival, optimistic)
  to finish the last few hundred health before we arrive, so we leave; the claimer is usually farming it from far
  off (20 of 40) or in Willow support, banking, chasing or recalling, and the group waits 10-40 rounds. Over all
  damage levels, 29 gems a game of ours are stolen locally; retreats with an enemy within 6 tiles are 8.3 of them,
  the claimed deferral 0.8, value-based farm switches 2.5.
- **Arms** (farm weight on live groups seen part-cleared: 1 at 90% health left, rising linearly to 1 + c at 50%
  and below; boosted groups are never pruned): c = 0.15 (the ladder's steal-probability gap, the denial value) and
  c = 0.5. Smoke, 256 games each against spar-dvn1-Flp: near-finished abandonments 1.00 base, 0.90 (c 0.15), 1.09
  (c 0.5); stolen and stealing unchanged; ~25% of winners flip, as a reroll does.

Results against ocean-16d6f78 (fgate, fresh ladder-v2 maps decide; bodies Flp2/Mt3p, the defaults when started; units
are maps, points of win rate, 95% CI):

| arm | fresh | ladder | Fish / Mite (fresh) | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| camphp-w15 (c 0.15) | -0.27 ±0.54 of 8,960 | +0.36 | -0.39 / -0.15 | high SPRT H0 (LLR -2.98) at block 70; stopped |
| camphp-w50 (c 0.5) | -0.11 ±0.50 of 11,648 | +0.22 | -0.37 / +0.15 | high LLR -2.88 at block 91; stopped |

Level: no meaningful change. The weight moves no behaviour it aims at, because farm already prices the clear left and
the groups we leave are left by retreat, chase and the claimed deferral, not by farm's pick. What the data points
at instead: (1) the claimed path's `health_left <= 0` (crew_work's Chebyshev, optimistic claimer arrival) on groups
we could finish in a hit or two; small (~0.2 abandonments, ~1 gem a game). (2) Retreats with an enemy near leave
part-cleared groups that the enemy takes (8 of 29 stolen gems a game): a fight decision, not a farm weight; finishing
first mostly hands the enemy a cleared group to hold.

## (ocean, 2026-11-10) Prism's bag: a recall line and health buying as functions of its gems; both level or lost

The user's idea: Prism's recall health threshold, and its health items, as functions of the gems it carries (and of
game state and map features). Arms on `variants/ocean-16d6f78`. Tools and the a2/bt patches are in [ideas-2026-11-10/prismhp-tools](ideas-2026-11-10/prismhp-tools/); data in `~/tmp-offload/prismhp/`
(`tools/pdeaths.py`, `traj.py`, `hazard.py`, `fit.py`, `pair.py`).

**Data**
- Live, our Prism against Fish since 11-08 (411 games, fish-re's decoded captures):
  - It dies before r600 in 41% of games. We win 80% when it survives and 34% when it dies; 24% when it dies with 200+
    gems.
  - On the new base locally (824 Prism games against the dvn1 Fish/Mite bodies, fresh slices f0/f1): 26%, with a win
    of 83% against 53%. The stake holds, and it is larger live.
- How it dies:
  - Rarely a one-shot. With 50+ gems, 7-8% die from >=80% HP in the last round, and 75% spend 2+ turns below 45% HP
    before dying.
  - Its death episodes start from >=80% HP 56-66% of the time and last a median 4 rounds.
  - Typical traces show a 100-300-gem Prism at ~50% HP that keeps casting at enemies 4-5 tiles away, then dies to an
    885-1540 burst.
- Hazard fit: P(killed within 6 rounds | an enemy within 6), 64k live rounds, logistic:
  `logit p = -0.418 - 3.70 h + 0.039 ln(1+g) - 0.298 h ln(1+g) + 0.776 n_e - 0.368 n_a`.
  - h is the health share, g the gems carried, n_e and n_a the enemies and allies within 5.
  - Holding the share and the round fixed, max health is worth logit -0.66 per 1000 HP.
- Shop:
  - Our Prism already puts ~2/3 of its shard stats into Health (13.7 Health, 6.4 Focus, 2.1 Strength shards'
    worth at r600).
  - With 200+ gems it holds a median 100 gold, and 150+ 35% of the time.
  - Its kill death rate falls with the bag: 0.0021 a round at 1-29 gems, 0.00059 at 200+.

**Arm A: the recall line as a function of the bag** (`combat/fight.cc` `bag_line`, Prism only, threatened line only)
- Retreat when p x stake exceeds the heal trip.
- The line is anchored to the tuned (map-conditioned) line for an empty bag, which prices the trip.
- A bag scales the stake from a death's respawn and walk out by `gem_stake` rounds a gem.
- The line solves the fit at that price, clamped to [tuned line, 0.8].
- It is a function of gems, health share, enemies and allies near, spawn distance and the map's tuned line.
- At a tuned line of 0.315 with one enemy near: 0.42 at 20 gems, 0.51 at 50, 0.60 at 100 and 0.69 at 200
  (`gem_stake` 2.3, `prismhp-a`); 4.6 (`prismhp-a2`, the swing of a kill's gems) reaches 0.8 at 200.

**Arm B: health as a function of the bag** (`economy/shop.cc`)
- `upkeep_cost` adds the bag at risk: death rate(g) x (respawn + walk out + 2.3 g) x exp(-0.00066 x max health
  added). The same price drives the stat choice and the trip home.
- `prismhp-b` also lets a learned arm's stat move to Health. `prismhp-bq` refits the odds to b's observed effect
  (0.000135). `prismhp-bt` has no stat switch.

**Smokes** (1024 games, vs dvn1-Flp/-Mt3p on fresh f0/f1, paired on the same games; base 72.75%)
- a 71.6, a2 72.5, b 70.9, bq 72.5, bt 73.0.
- Mechanism in Prism games, against the base:
  - a2: Prism deaths -18%, gems lost -25%, tributed -0.8.
  - b: max health +40%, deaths -11%, tributed -22: it overbuys Health.
  - bt: max health +29%, deaths -11%, tributed -21. bq's max health still rose by 534.

**Results against ocean-16d6f78** (fgate; fresh read in points, 95% CI; stopped by the coordinator)

| gate | fresh | units | ladder | Fish / Mite (fresh) | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prismhp-a2 (Flp2 Fish body) | -0.40 ±0.33 | 11,648 | -0.38 | +0.00 / -0.81 | high H0 (LLR -9.05), low -2.44: reject |
| prismhp-bt (Flp3 Fish body) | -0.09 ±0.77 | 3,584 | -0.34 | +0.17 / -0.35 | high LLR -1.14: stopped, level at best |

- Fewer Prism deaths and gems lost don't turn into wins. Retreating earlier with a big bag takes the strongest caster
  out of the fights it would have won (Mite -0.81). More Health costs the Focus that farms; the base's mix of ~2/3
  Health is already about right.
- The fit's hazard is what the base's own play produces. Lowering it by retreating costs more than the deaths it
  avoids, so a fitted stake does not give a better line.
- Not tried: the same line for all carriers; a burst-aware stand (Marcella's ready 2x-Focus spell in reach), which
  fish-re's lane (Fish threat reads) covers.

## (ocean, 2026-11-10) Farm economy against live Fish and Mite: no gold left in aggregate; the backyard discount is denial

Question: does ocean's camp choice leave gold on the table, given that real Fish and Mite earn more gold a capture
than our bodies? Data: decoded live games from 11-08 on (544 Fish vs us, 2,409 Mite vs us), local ocean against the
bodies, and fgate. Scripts are in `~/tmp-offload/farmecon/`: caprows, agg, decomp, idle, idle2, pergroup, elk,
perchamp, both, vesp, budget and mech.py.

**Live, our capture economy matches theirs.** Capture gold a game, us against them:

| | r100 | r200 | r400 | r600 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| vs Fish | 370 / 379 | 831 / 835 | 1931 / 1806 | 3090 / 2788 |
| vs Mite | 379 / 409 | 857 / 898 | 1920 / 1912 | 3147 / 3077 |

- We capture more gems: 79 against 69 by r100 and 177 against 153 by r200 against Fish; +13 against Mite by r200.
- Fish's earned-gold lead (+50 at r100, +73 at r200) is kill gold (+21/+26) and Marcella's tribute gold (+20/+43).
  Captures add only +9/+4.
- Our lower gold a capture is composition: 33% of our captures are gem clusters, against Fish's 19%.
- Local ocean earns as live ocean does (375 capture gold by r100). The bodies are the ones short: our code with Fish's and
  Mite's drafts, 350 / 410 / 442 a 100-round bucket against real Fish's 379 / 456 / 478. The bodies' economic gap is
  theirs, not ocean's.

**Where the allocation differs** (same champion type on both sides of a game, by r300):
- Their Vesper Vale takes more shares: Fish's 7.3 against our 6.8 (1007 gold against 875); Mite's 8.0 against 6.5
  (981 against 846, 100 gems against 74).
  - Vesper's share of the team's base gold is 0.41 for us, against 0.53 for Fish and 0.49 for Mite.
  - Our Vesper hits camps as many rounds as theirs (86-87 against 83-88). It joins fewer crew clears; when it hits a
    group, it holds it 87% of the time.
  - Our Cassi and Issac take the extra shares (Cassi 60% gem clusters).
- Own-half Elk is cleared later and by smaller crews:
  - first clear at a median r64 against Fish's r48 (r52 against Mite's r45);
  - second at r184 against r154;
  - 3.45 hitters against 4.7, and 22% solo against 3%.
  - Own Golem first clears: r242 against r150.
- The deep backyard (our walk share < 0.3) is under-farmed, live and local alike:
  - own Elk 12-20 walks away is never captured by r300 in 28% of our games, against 10-11% for Fish and Mite;
  - at walk 30+, 63% against 12% for Mite;
  - against Mite it holds for every group type.
  - We take more of the middle instead. Farm's middle band (`mid_exposure` 1.36 for `home_side` 0.254-0.683) prices the
    backyard 26% below the front yard.

**`variants/fe-yard` (`own_ground_share` 1.1: no own-side cap on the band, so the backyard is priced like the front
yard) is REJECTED.** fgate (Flp4/Mt3q, 30 blocks, 3,840 fresh units):
- fresh **-2.58 ±0.89** (Fish -2.21, Mite -2.94);
- ladder -2.38;
- one-site -1.97, multi-site -2.78.

Mechanism, paired on 1,024 fresh games (f0 and f1, both bodies; fe-yard minus base, the range over the four runs):

| | r200 | r400 | r600 |
|---|---|---|---|
| backyard captures | +1.0 | +2.0 | +3.0 |
| middle captures | -0.5 | -1.0 | -2.0 |
| our capture gold | +10 to +31 | +33 to +45 | -65 to +32 |
| body's capture gold | +4 to +49 | +47 to +136 | +100 to +150 |
| body's tributed gems | +4 to +8 | +10 to +25 | +17 to +36 |
| our kills | -0.25 to +0.07 | -0.35 to 0 | -1.1 to 0 |

The backyard's gold is real, but smaller than the middle's denial. Every middle group we leave feeds the enemy, and we
meet them less, so we kill less. The middle premium prices that denial; SPSA found its height for this reason.

The same reading explains live: Fish and Mite farm their backyards and lose the middle to us.

No narrower arm: the cost is leaving the middle, not anything in the backyard. Early-only is the one form left, and
there both effects are small (+10 capture gold by r100, middle -0.1).

Leads for others, not tested:
- Vesper's share of crew clears (crews and packing, not farm pricing);
- own-half Elk crews.
Earlier packing arms (pair-pack, pos-crew, open-pack) moved Elk/Golem gold but not wins.

**Body arms after Flp2** (ocean-16d6f78 against each, 256 ladder games; ±5 points at this size):

| Body | ocean win % | What it changes | Fidelity read |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flp2h | 73.8 | Flp2, prey chases any visible enemy (patch_hunt.py) | not kept: the body gets no stronger |
| Flp2np | 71.9 | Flp2 without ocean's priority payload | payload costs nothing |
| Flp3x | 79.7 | Flp2, Fish's exact encoding (idle = health band) | the body loses ~8 points: idle order matters |
| **Flp3** | 74.2 | Flp2, Fish's encoding keeping the body's idle order | classifier: Fish 0.97 at r100 (Flp2: 0.20, "other") |
| Mt3p2fight | 73.8 | Mt3p, a bag never brakes | mite-re: deaths gap unmoved (ours 6.0 vs real 10.4 one-site) |
| Mt3p2bank | 73.0 | Mt3p, Fish's 8 × (walk − 2) floor | mite-re: real Mite banks smaller bags, so the wrong way |
| Mt3p2 | 69.1 | both of the above | |
| Mt3p3 | 73.8 | fight + no banking trips on one-altar maps | mite-re: overshoots (altar time 1% vs real 4%, bags 3x) |
| Mt3pqo | 73.8 | Mt3p, Mite's values spread over 1000..1049 | classifier: Mite 0.68 at r100 |
| **Mt3q** | 73.4 | Mt3p, Mite's encoding (alert 0, quiet ±2 by idle order) | classifier: Mite 0.98 at r100 |

Flp3 and Mt3q are fgate's defaults. What still separates the bodies from live, from fish-re and mite-re:
- Kill pressure. Real Fish kills our bodies 9.6 times a game against the body's 6.5, and real Mite 10.4 against 6.0
  on one-site maps. fish-re traces it to cohesion: real Fish has 1.54 teammates within 5 against the body's 1.20,
  so we are outnumbered at contact. The death hazard at equal numbers is the same, so it is numbers, not fighting
  skill.
- Mite's softer banking trips, and its mid-altar locks from about r400.

**Cohesion (Flp4 = Flp3 + `patch_coh.py 0.5`, fgate's Fish default).** In farm choice, a group that no visible
off-spawn ally is nearer to is worth `lone` times its value, per Fish's ally_closer (joins, never partitions).
Sweep, 256 ladder games each:

| Body | Mates within 5 (live 1.54) | Nearest ally ≤ 2 (live 52%) | Our deaths a game (live 9.6) | ocean win % |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Flp3 | 1.20 | 42% | 5.8 | 74.2 |
| lone 0.8 | 1.29 | 44% | 5.6 | 77.0 |
| lone 0.6 | 1.42 | 49% | 5.8 | 75.0 |
| **lone 0.5 (Flp4)** | 1.50 | 52% | 6.6 (bursts +33%) | 75.8 |
| lone 0.4 | 1.62 | 56% | 6.0 | 79.7 |
| Flp4 + hunt | | | | 81.6 |

Cohesion now matches live, but the win rate does not move, so packing is not the main gap.

The early economy is (fish-re's econ.py; `fishfid` econ2.py and capby.py). Gold earned minus ours:

| | r100 | r200 | r600 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Real Fish | +50 | +73 | −91 |
| Body | −50 | −106 | −745 |

By r200 the body takes as many captures and gems as real Fish (11.1, 154 gems), but less gold a share: Marcella 53
against 76, Vendetta 66 against 76, Vesper 115 against 133. Gold-weight arms (`patch_gold.py`) follow.

**Mite arms on Mt3q** (256 ladder games; Mt3q 73.4%):

| Arm | Adds | ocean win % |
|---|---|---|
| Mt3qe | real Mite's emblem orders (`patch_mite_emb.py`, from `possq_mite.py`) | 77.3 |
| Mt3qc | cohesion 0.5 | 81.2 |
| Mt3r | both | 80.1 |

Each makes the body weaker, not closer to live. mite-re's fidelity set on 400 multi-site fresh games found:
- Our deaths stay put: 3.1-3.3 against 7.9 real.
- Mt3qe's stats trade one for another: Vesper Strength 246 → 278 but max hp 2672 → 1771. Real Mite has both, from
  more gold.
- On map-matched ladder games, real Mite takes 22% more capture gold, 15% more gold per capture before r300, and
  ~5 more late camps a game.

**Gold-weight arms on Flp4** (`patch_gold.py X`: farm's per_gold × X; 256 ladder games):

| Body | Earned r100 (real 452) | Earned r200 (real 1001) | Marcella gold/share (76) | ocean win % |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Flp4 | 348 | 792 | 53 | 75.8 |
| ×1.5 | 370 | 824 | 56 | 77.0 |
| ×2 | 373 | 838 | 54 | 80.9 |
| ×3 | 392 | 883 | 57 | 78.1 |

Pricing gold higher closes about half the r100 gap, but the body gets weaker. Every lever tried so far (banking,
emblems, cohesion, hunt, gold price) moves its own statistic toward live without moving the win rate toward ~64%.
The bodies' strength gap is not one missing rule; Flp2's banking rule is the only change that moved it (80.5 → 71).

## (ocean, 2026-11-09) Draft first-turn fuel 2 (CHANGES 493): dash-travel flood kept, ward-cast cache dropped

Two leads that 491 left. All headroom figures are from `firstturn.py --need`; identity was checked with dumps of the
features, team and plans against `variants/ocean-16d6f78`.

**Profile** (PROF prints, the 50 heaviest held-out ocft-1950 drafts)
- `travel<1>`:
  - setup 0.15-0.56M (~40 a tile);
  - Dial loop 0.02-1.64M (~220 a popped tile; about 1 walk push and 1 dash end tried a pop);
  - output ~0.1M.
- Wards 0.4-2.1M. A ward cast is ~490 fuel on a 100x100 map, about half of best_ward's ~980 a candidate.

**Kept: SIMD neighbour relaxation and a cheaper `dash_short` index (CHANGES 493)**
- The loop was 961k -> 756k on gen-huge-195000912002.
- ocft-1950: max 9.88M -> 9.67M, 25 -> 14 team-drafts over 9M.

**Didn't pay**
- **Counting `dash_short` after the flood**, as 491 suggested: a vector pass over d and the base, fused with the output
  loop. It cost +52k on every draft, because wasm counts every local.get and constant, so the 4-lane loop is ~11
  fuel a tile. It saves only ~25 a pop, so 70% of drafts got dearer by up to 57k; the 768 set's max rose
  8.83M -> 8.88M.
- **A padded copy of the base distances** for a division-free index: the fill cost +16-67k (most on maps with many
  mixed 16-tile blocks), and it saved ~6 a pop more than the division formula.
- **Ward-cast cache** (lead 2): 9.1% of r6 casts repeat (10,248 of 112,936 on the 50 heaviest drafts; 2-27% a draft).
  - The bound is the repeats times the cast cost: 50k mean and 191k max a draft, at most ~0.8% of the heaviest
    turns.
  - The cache, with casts written straight into raw slots and a per-tile slot table, cost a median +57k a draft (to
    a max of +208k): +30k for the table's memset on the first site, and +3-4k a site (~90 a candidate) of bookkeeping.
  - Even an uncached raw cast through the helper cost +25 a candidate.
  - Dropped.

**Left for later** (not tried): `travel<1>`'s setup (~40 a tile), the rest of its per-pop cost (`leap`, buckets: ~170 a
pop), best_ward's non-cast half (~490 a candidate), and the open-plan search, attack tiles, candidate floods and
sight gap as 491 listed.

Asked (user): "test feint tributes locally in our bot to see if it works, can use multiple variants". Tools
`research/ideas-2026-11-09/feint-tools/` (`build.sh` rebuilds the variants), data `~/tmp-offload/feint/`.
- **Why it can pay.** A tribute started at the turn end costs no action: the turn has acted, and next turn
  `continue_tribute` keeps it or cancels it to act (damage doesn't interrupt it; stun or lock cancel it with the gems kept).
  A bag of ≤10 completes at our next turn start. It replaces the recall feint, which the base almost never keeps there:
  of its recall starts at an altar with gems (one-site, r<600) 22 a game are cancelled the next turn and 0.05 run to
  the end (`feintkept2.py`). Our champions end 33-43 rounds a one-site game at an altar with gems and no tribute.
- **Variants** (oc-base25 + `patch_mite.py --v3`, then cut down; all yield to a `want_home` recall):
  - `v87-ft-m3`: Mite's habit, including its first-turn cancel in contact when our tribute check fails;
  - `v87-ft-k`: without the contact cancel; `v87-ft-1`: k, one-turn channels only;
  - `v87-ft-w`: k's longer channels only where the turn wanted to bank (`memory.banking` or `wait_altar`);
    `v87-ft-b`: w plus one-turn channels anywhere.

  lost one-site gems (−20 at 600 against Fl); the full gate did not bear that out.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## (ocean, 2026-11-09) Priority stream mask: the payload coded per round, the rank by a keyed per-game gap table

- **Why:** the user found the per-game mask (below) too easy to reverse-engineer: equal values show as equal numbers
  all game, and the payload's xor keeps every bit flip visible.
- **What:** `prio_stream.h` and `stream_patch.py`, beside `prio_mask.h` in `~/tmp-offload/handoff/sched/prio_mask/`
  (not switched in; the key stays in `~/.config/cambc-secret/`).
  - Payload: its low 14 bits are xored with a mask drawn per round and champion. Bits 14-15 carry the round mod 4,
    so `payload_of` undoes the right round's mask for a value up to 3 rounds old. With the mask changing, every turn
    publishes.
  - Rank: a strictly increasing map drawn per game. Each idle or negative rank code (99.7% of values in force) starts
    a random gap above the last: k to ~400-500 coded units, against a plain step of 8. The protect and kill bands keep
    plain steps. Ranks written in any rounds still compare as the plain ones, so there is no turn-start rewrite and
    nothing to decode in World.
- **Checks** (ocean f6623073f, bench `--set wide` against a copy of hyperion blind to our priorities):
  - A host test covers every rank, index and age 0-3: the round trip, order and sign within a round, order across
    rounds, and our unpublished rank against an ally's published one. 5.5e8 checks, 0 failures.
  - With a zero key, the patched bot is byte-identical (52/52, the same fuel).

  | | current mask | stream mask | per-round rank (rev A) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | fuel per turn at 100M: mean, p50, p99 | +30, +28, +80 | +209, +203, +1461 | +1214, +1143, +4107 |
  | fuel per turn at the real budget: mean, p50, p99 | +30, +28, +74 | +197, +190, +1271 | |
  | same play at 100M | 51/52 | 51/52 | 50/52 |
  | same play at the real budget | 44/52 | 18/52 | |
  | team order against the plain game, rounds of same-play games | 35894/35894 | 35894/35894 | |
  | payload bit against plain bit, per game, mean \|r\| | 0.999 | 0.015 | |
  | payload repeats when the plain one repeats | 100% | 0.04% | |
  | rank repeats when the plain one repeats | 99.9% | 99.9% | |
  | gaps between allies' ranks against plain gaps, per game, r | 0.993 | 0.72 | |

  - The p99 is mostly the bot moving work between turns: the 100M tails are symmetric (p1 −1138; turns over +1000
    net +7 a turn against the negative ones). The steady part, by instrumenting one game: publishing 44, a
    `set_priority` every turn 23, and 40 for each `payload_of` (1-3 a turn).
  - The 1/52 game that differs at 100M differs at the same step for the current mask (gen-chambers b, round 702,
    our move). Likely a fuel-budgeted subsystem reacting to the extra fuel. ocean 6f9f7246b (CHANGES 478) patches
    cleanly and reads the same: +209 mean, 51/52.
- **What did not work:** a rank code that changes every round costs ~5x the stream mask.
  - Allies' ranks then change every round, so World re-ranks the team every turn (`rank_turns`, +640). Keyed jitter
    per round cost +867.
  - Decoding allies as read and rewriting last turn's value at turn start (to keep the engine's order with
    different rounds' codes in force) cost +1214. That revision also diverged at our own move once (00corners a,
    r629), not chased.
- **What an observer of our replays can still read:**
  - our champions' order each round, and each rank's sign;
  - when a champion's rank changes, and which rank values recur within a game;
  - rank gaps only blurred (r 0.72);
  - nothing of the payload (claims, support intents, chase);
  - a round a champion didn't publish (ran out of fuel), and a round-mod-4 counter in bits 14-15.
- **Wins (dgate, stream against the current mask, both on oc-base25 with one throwaway key):** ZONE at 23,936 units
  (96k games a bot): +0.32 ±0.31 pts, low SPRT H1 at 9,216 units, high H0 (Fish +0.37, Mite +0.28). The opponents
  don't read our priorities, so this measures the fuel alone: no loss. On oc-base25, +201 a turn at 100M (52/52 same
  play) and +193 / +190 / +1051 at the real budget. The real-budget p99 tail is not in fights: turns with an enemy
  within 5 tiles are 7% of turns but 3.3% of those over p99, and their own p99 is +305 (quiet turns +1277).
  `stream_patch.py` also patches bots from before the chase bit (oc-base25: payload bits 0-10).
- **Verdict:** ready for the live scheduler at about +200 fuel a turn. Unlike the current mask's +30, it changes
  real-budget play in most games, as any +200 does.

[retreat-2026-11-09/chase-verdict.md](retreat-2026-11-09/chase-verdict.md).

## (ocean = oc-esc-478, 2026-11-09) Escape planner after 478: an exact fuel pass merged (CHANGES 480); model fixes and smarter gates level

Three lines of work from 478, run in parallel. Only the fuel pass changes the bot. All A/Bs are release builds,
`--no-test-draft` and normal fuel.

**Fuel pass, exact (fo-lean, merged as CHANGES 480).** [retreat-2026-11-09/fuel-opt.md](retreat-2026-11-09/fuel-opt.md).
- The build falls from 10,193 to 9,622 mean (-5.6%; p90 14,032 → 13,521; slack pass 1,110 → 1,040). This is bench
  `--set wide --test-draft` at 100M against oc-cl2-seat5m: 52 games, 13,705 builds.
- **Where the saving comes from:**
  - grows reused across a pursuer's strike, walk and dash landings, with `moved` = walked | dashed;
  - `grow_by` split into `widen`, which carries on from a set already within 1;
  - one grow of a union in the backward pass;
  - four static boards in one row loop (`Span`), where 478 read seven with a `RowAt` table a row; the spawns are
    read only on rows their box meets;
  - one plan read in `escape_landings` when the slack goal is off.
- **The profile:** the grows are not the cost. A pursuer class costs ~2.1-2.4k of loop, spill and lambda overhead,
  however few grows it does, and ~20% of escape.cc's fuel has no source line.
- **Identity:** the plan-hash dumps (every hit layer, the window, the goals and both passes) of 478 and fo-lean match
  over 13,705 builds and 7,080 slack passes, and the bench replays are 52/52 identical. The merge's own check is
  oc-esc-merge against oc-esc-478, wide set, `--test-draft`, 100M: identical replays 52/52 (total fuel 13,337.7M → 13,329.3M; 13,120 turns cheaper, 1,587 dearer).
- **Rejected:** merged strikes for classes that share a reach (~3% of the planner), a per-tile flag grid (~100k+ to
  build once), a byte-aligned board stride (~15k repack), camps folded into the static boards (~1.5k a flip), a lazy
  slack goal (~60 a build net), and reusing the build after a dash (not exact: the window moves and `see_again`
  changes the beliefs).
- **On `merged/esc2-dev`** (40,960 games against oc-cl2-seat5m): fo-lean 51.3% (50.8-51.8), and oc-esc-478 51.4%
  (50.9-51.8, OOF 461,924 against 432,918).
  - fo-lean's run printed no OOF counts because it played on stock cambc: its launcher's env line read
    `CAMBC_SLOT_WEIGHT=12CAMBC_BIN=...`, a missing space, so `CAMBC_BIN` was never set. Its win rate stands, since
    stock and the fast runner play the same games.
  - Its replay proxy (fuel entries of exactly 100k, the 988 games both batches saved) reads CAND OOF -4.1%.
- **Held out** (`merged/esc2-held`, 61,440 games against oc-cl2-seat5m, fast runner): oc-esc-merge **51.3%
  (50.9-51.7)**, OOF 679,972 against 637,483 (11.07 a game, 6.7% over the reference, as 478's on esc2-dev). Level
  with 478, as an exact change should be: the planner's gain holds on unseen maps.

**Logic audit (la-*, nothing merged).** [retreat-2026-11-09/logic-audit.md](retreat-2026-11-09/logic-audit.md);
tools `esc_diag_trace.patch`, `esc_diag.py` and `chase.py`.
- **The trace:** a traced 256-game batch replayed each plan's hit layers against the damage taken after it.
  - The layers are a sound superset: 1.7% of predicted-clear turn-2 intervals were hit, mostly by camps.
  - But only 9.5% of predicted hits land, because 62-72% of the counted pursuers do not follow.
  - 37% of plan-ranked walks had every option at "many", and those turns took 1.06M of the 1.5M hp that followed
    plan-ranked walks.
  - The step taken when the homeward step is clear of every reach (path B, no plan) was damaged within 3 turns in
    only 3%.
- **The rules audit:** turn order, dash paths, the ranged walk and bush sight are right. The mismatches: stunned
  pursuers act; awake camps are only terrain; Vesper-style walk, reset, attack is missing; hits saturate at 2.
- **Arms** against `variants/oc-esc-478` on `maps/suites/merged/retreat-911000b` (10,240 games):
  - `la-cnt` (hits counted exactly to horizon - 1; build 9.8k → ~11.2k): 49.6% (48.6-50.5).
  - `la-cf` (la-cnt + stunned pursuers lose a turn + awake camps strike every turn): 49.9% (48.9-50.9).
  - `la-fid` (stunned pursuers + awake camps + ranged attack-reset bursts, no exact counts): 49.0% (48.0-50.0).
  - Deaths a game rose slightly (la-cf 6.04 against 5.85 in its first 1,000 games) and gems fell ~25.
- **The reading:** adding sound hits to an already pessimistic model saturates more options. The evidence points to
  less pessimism, but nothing cheap separates chasers from the rest. Nothing merged; no final.

**Fuel gate (fg-*, nothing merged).** [retreat-2026-11-09/fuel-gate.md](retreat-2026-11-09/fuel-gate.md); tools
`fg_instrument*.py`, `fg_parse.py`, `fg_summary.py`, `fg_hazard.py` and `fg-site.patch`. Debug checkpoints over 1,600
games, at the 20k and 50k gates.
- **Why lower gates lost.** A planned turn runs out according to X, the fuel left after the build, exactly as an
  unplanned turn does with the same fuel. The plan adds no work after it, so a lower gate leaves too little for the
  same retreat_step pricing. At 20k/12k, OOF turns in retreat rose from 1,304 to 6,213, and 4,580 of them lost the
  move (2,931 in retreat_step's pricing).
- **The hazard differs by caller.** The walk's ask (retreat_step) reaches 1% at X ≈ 35k; the dash's ask
  (escape_landings, before the dash and all of retreat_step) at X ≈ 53k. The flat 50k leaves X ≈ 40k at a 10k
  build: 0.3% for the walk, ~3% for the dash.
- **Gate tested:** the fuel left must pay for the caller's reserve plus a running mean of the measured build cost,
  and a gated plan is retried by the next ask. Screens against oc-esc-478 on merged/retreat-911000b (10,240 games
  each):

| Variant | dash / walk / slack reserve | win % (95% CI) | OOF CAND / REF |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| fg-site | 53k / 35k / 16k | 49.8 (48.8-50.7) | 112,025 / 114,561 |

## (ocean, 2026-11-09) Escape planner fuel: the same plans at a quarter of the fuel; 33.9% -> ~51.6% at normal fuel

The retreat planner (`model/escape.cc`, research/retreat-2026-11-09) read 53.1% against `oc-cl2-seat5m` with unlimited
fuel but 33.9% at normal fuel (`oc-escape-v1`, release, 600,725 OOF turns against 90,034). All A/Bs here: CAND vs
`variants/oc-cl2-seat5m`, `--no-test-draft`, release, fast runner, `maps/suites/merged/retreat-911000b` (10,240 games).

**Where a retreat turn's fuel went** (debug, 128 ladder games vs astraeus, checkpoints in debug blocks): on turns with a
plan, world/pre-decide 8.9k, decide up to `retreat()` 18.8k, `retreat()` 46.8k (the plan 26.5k of it), after 9.6k:
84k of 100k on the turns that finished. The pre-change bot's retreat turns were 59.6k (its `retreat()` 16.3k). The
planner's own build was p50 ~41k a build at 100M fuel (bench, `--set wide`, 7,964 builds).

**Exact rewrite** (same plans: every plan's rows dumped and compared with oc-escape-v1's over 8,895 builds of 52 bench
games, no mismatch; bench replays 51/52 identical, the other diverging through the turn-end queue, which fills by fuel spent):
- Rows as two u16x8 vectors (8 rows a vector) instead of four u32x4, ops written on values (always_inline) so they
  stay in wasm locals; one mask at the end of a dilation instead of one per step.
- Static boards combined once a game (open-to-walk, open-to-dash for both teams); a window row's position worked out
  once per row for all boards; rows gathered into a u16 array and loaded as vectors (no per-lane inserts).
- `grow_by` by doubling (1, 2, then the rest); the backward pass as a template on the dash, no arrays.
- Build cost 42.9k -> 10.4k mean (p90 62.0k -> 14.4k, max 108k -> 23k) at 100M. Phases after it: hit layers 5.0k
  (~2.2k a pursuer class: ~40 wasm ops a dilation, so near the floor for this model), backward pass 1.3k, pursuers 1.3k,
  goals 1.2k, terrain 1.0k.
- **A/B `oc-esc-f1`: 51.9% (51.0-52.9), OOF 113,797 against 104,150.** From 33.9%; the unlimited ceiling is 53.1.
- Reusing the previous turn's dash landings and starting a pursuer's turns at its arrival: 10.4k -> 10.0k (exact).
- **Gates** (`params::escape`: the build needs `min_fuel` left, the slack pass `slack_fuel`). In a debug batch of f1
  (128 ladder games vs oc-cl2-seat5m) 16% of builds were skipped by the 50k gate (at p50 42.6k left) and 38% of slack
  passes by the 40k one; OOF turns were level with the reference (1,683 against 1,666). Lowering the build gate loses:
  30k/20k (`oc-esc-f2`) 50.5% (49.5-51.5), OOF 161k; 20k/12k (`oc-esc-f3`) 50.0% (49.0-51.0), OOF 178k. The turns
  the gate skips are ones whose retreat code after the plan (Safety pricing, HomeWalk; `retreat_step` p90 ~50k) would
  run out. Keeping 50k and lowering only the slack gate to 15k (`oc-esc-f4`, with the 10.0k build): 51.6% (50.6-52.5),
  level with f1. 40k/15k (`oc-esc-f5`): 50.6% (49.6-51.6).
- **Headroom** (diagnostic, `oc-esc-fva`/`fvb`: f1 on a 100x quantum, `FASTRUNNER_BOT_FUEL`, every gate reading the 1x
  budget, as the fuel-ceiling arms; the reference at normal fuel): no OOF, plan paid 53.1% (52.1-54.0); no OOF and the
  plan's fuel refunded to every later read 54.0% (53.0-55.0). Making the plan cost nothing is worth at most ~+0.9
  (within the noise of a difference of two runs); the rest of f1's gap to its no-OOF arm is ocean's general OOF cost,
  which the reference pays too. So the remaining ~10k a build has little left to win.
- **Cheaper model**: horizon 4 instead of 5 (`oc-esc-f6`, slack gate 15k): 8.6k a build (-14%), 51.8% (50.8-52.8),
  level with f1. Not taken: the same win rate with less look-ahead.
- `oc-esc-f9` (= ocean now: f1 plus the 10.0k cut, same gates): 51.3% (50.3-52.3). f1, f4, f6 and f9 make the same or
  near-same choices at the 50k gate and read 51.9 / 51.6 / 51.8 / 51.3: about 51.6 pooled over 40,960 games, against
  33.9 before the rewrite and 53.1 with unlimited fuel.
- Next, if anything: the rest of a retreat turn (decide up to `retreat()` ~17k, `retreat_step`'s own ~8k) is shared with
  every turn and was mined by the fuel campaigns; a smarter build gate (fuel left against an estimate of what the
  retreat still runs after the plan) is the one lever the gate arms point at.
- **The idea itself, at unlimited fuel** (`oc-escape-v1` against `oc-cl2-seat5m`, both bots unlimited,
  `FASTRUNNER_UNLIMITED_BOTS`): ab.py 53.1% (52.1-54.1) of 10,240 (`replays/ab/retreat-unl-911000b`). dgate on renamed
  copies (`oc-escv1-unl` against `oc-pre5m-unl`, so no unlimited run enters the shared reference cache; the panel bodies
  at normal fuel): **ACCEPT** (screen H1) at block 43, +2.18 ±0.70 pts over 5,632 units (23,040 CAND games); Fish picks
  +3.14, Mite picks +1.22, one-site +2.09, multi-site +2.23. Deaths barely move (first 1,000 A/B games,
  `tools/replay/fight_metrics.py`: 6.01 against 6.08 a game, to champions 5.74 against 5.84, kills 5.84 against 5.74);
  gems +4% (795 against 764). The gain is keeping champions in play and earning, not a clear cut in deaths.
- **Shipped as CHANGES 478** (bots/ocean = f9's plans) by the user's call, without a final normal-fuel dgate; further
  fuel work is left to a follow-up.

## (ocean = oc-base25, 2026-11-09) Opponent tribute fidelity: Mite's tribute habit and both teams' lock policies in the spar bodies

Asked: make the local opponents reproduce the Fish/Mite tribute behaviour local gates miss (section "Why v90-v93 lose
live"), and check fidelity on 470. Tools `research/ideas-2026-11-09/oppfidelity-tools/`, data `~/tmp-offload/oppfidelity/`.
- **Only Mite feints; Fish doesn't.** Live r2, one-site maps, rounds ≤ 600 (v86/87/89/95; `episodes.py`, `chanturns.py`):
  - Mite: 11.1 tribute starts a game, 1.71 manual cancels (3.21 against v91/v93); 90% are cancelled on the channel's
    first turn and 64% restart within 3 rounds. On a channel's first turn with one of ours seen within 5 it cancels
    59% (65-80% at 1-4 tiles, ~45% at 5, ~10% at 6); later turns 4-6%.

## (ocean = oc-base25, 2026-11-09) Generalised nuke guard (nukeguard2): four forms, all H0 on dgate; lethal steps are trapped retreats

The user asked how the nuke guard works (`v87-rv-ngd`: one seen enemy's ready abilities alone, a hard ban, from outside every
zone) and to test a general form: a price instead of a ban, enemies counted together, and a check on whether we kill first.
Data first, then four arms. Tools, arm patches and the probe patch: `research/ideas-2026-11-09/nukeguard2-tools/`.
- **Live data** (4,631 v83-v95 scrims against Fish and Mite; `steps.py`). A step is lethal when the enemies the mover saw,
  by a wall-free compute_strike bound with cooldowns, add up to its health before its next turn.
  - Our steps from a safe tile into a lethal one: 0.70 a game against Fish, 0.50 against Mite. Of these, 26-34% die before
    their next turn in single-nuke zones and 35-43% in combined ones. Their steps into ours: Fish 0.87 a game, Mite 1.67.
    Of those, 17-22% die in single-nuke zones and 28-43% in combined ones.
  - Most of our deaths come later, on moves already inside lethal zones: about 4 a game, of which 54-75% die.
  - A step into a lethal zone almost never kills (0-2% of them). The kill-first check has nothing to act on.
- **Local trace** (debug probe, v87 against spar-o25-F/M, 512 games; the probe printed which sub-step moved and Safety::lethal before and after).
  - Most lethal moves are retreat steps (`retreat_step`): 3.4 a game inside lethal zones, of which 63-68% die. Of the
    retreat turns judged lethal by the bot's own model, 4.9 a game had every step and staying lethal (trapped).
    Only 0.5 a game had a non-lethal alternative that the damage-bound ranking passed over.
  - ngd guarded none of this. Retreats and game-ender stops never read its zone. It reached only plan ends and goal walks
    (farm, chase, bank, altar guard) into single-nuke tiles, about 0.2 a game.
  - Lethal plan-search ends are rare: under 15 in 512 games.
- **Arms** (oc-base25 + one diff each, `bots/variants/v87-ng2-*`):
  - `rs`: retreat_step tries the ranked steps that Safety::lethal (every credible threat and camp together) clears before the lethal ones.
  - `rs2`: rs plus, when every ranked step is lethal, an unranked non-lethal step (sideways or away), or staying if here is not lethal.
  - `wg`: ngd generalised. The step and work guards ban every Safety::lethal tile, from a tile that is not lethal.
  - `pr`: the price form. On a plan-search end where the camps and the hits no leaf removes (by a kill or a stun) add up to our
    health, 0.4 x kill_distance(our health, max, bag) is charged. The 0.4 is the local death rate after such steps.
- **Mechanism** (1,024 games each against spar-o25-F/M): our deaths a game were base 7.01, rs 7.11, rs2 7.13, wg 7.26, pr 7.11.
  Death rates inside the zones did not move: a retreat that steps to a non-lethal tile is still caught a turn later.
- **Fuel:** in the 256-game smoke, the arms had 3,606-3,678 OOF turns against 3,652 for the base.
- **2x fuel**, on dgate's block-0 opponents (1,024 paired games each), every arm read level:
  - rs 49.90 (49.11-50.69), rs2 49.90 (48.41-51.40), wg 50.10 (48.58-51.62), pr 50.10 (49.91-50.29).
  - At 2x only 0.1% of pr's games and 6% of wg's change result. At the real budget, wg changed 78% of games and pr 39%.
    Most of their real-budget differences come from fuel, not from the rule.

Results against oc-base25 (v87), dgate 0.505/0.5075:

| arm | dgate |
|---|---|
| v87-ng2-rs | 49.89% (49.43-50.35) of 4,096: H0 |
| v87-ng2-rs2 | 50.05% (49.64-50.46) of 14,336: H0 |
| v87-ng2-wg | 50.01% (49.56-50.46) of 40,960: H0 |
| v87-ng2-pr | 49.53% (48.95-50.11) of 9,728: H0 |

- No form of the guard is a meaningful change. Lethal steps are almost all retreats that are already caught; choosing the
  step differently, banning entry, or pricing death in the plan does not change who dies.
- Leads, not built:
  - Upstream: not getting caught. Want_home's timing and engagement choice decide the 4.9 trapped turns a game.
  - Punishment: Fish's entries into our zones die 17-28%, ours into theirs about 35%. Unused exclusive spells are the
    known part (fight-execution.md).

## (ocean = oc-base25, 2026-11-09) Draft-solved opening farm plan (draftfarm): following it loses; as a bias it is +0.6 on dgate, under the bar

[draftfarm-2026-11-08/README.md](draftfarm-2026-11-08/README.md) has the design, the forensics and the tools. The
draft's first turn solves a team route plan over our half (event sim plus anytime local search, horizons 60/100/150);
farm biases toward the planned group (x1.5).
- **Screens (old bar 0.50,0.5025), all H0.** Real budget: h60 48.66% of 19,858; h100 48.31% of 16,163; h150 46.85%
  of 9,201. 2x fuel: 48.92 / 48.94 / 46.82. Spar h100 -3.19 ±3.66. The longer the horizon, the worse.
- **Forensics.** Debug pairs against the base mirror on 1,000 maps. The plan moves the first walk in nearly every game.
  At r100 our gold is +5 ±3 and gems +0.3; the enemy's gold is +15 ±3 and gems +3.5 ±0.7. Their middle captures by
  r150 rise +0.20 a game and ours fall -0.11.
- **Two causes.** (1) Writing the plan into `memory.farm_group` stole farm's stickiness, so it thrashed: A-B-A target
  flips 5.6 a game against 1.3. (2) Candidates on our half only, since the sim has no enemy, cede the contested middle.
- **Fixed arm v87-dfp-pure.** The weight is applied on its own and `farm_group` is untouched. Thrash is gone and the
  middle concession is smaller. The plan's own value is nil: gold +3.8 ±4.2 and gems +0.1 at r100. Debug smoke 49.7%
  of 2,000. Against live-pick opponents (2,048 pairs) our gold is +8 at r100 and +16 at r200, and their gems +2.5
  (the middle is still ceded). dgate (0.505/0.5075): 50.63% (50.26-51.00) over 23,296 units, LLR +0.07. It sits at
  the bar's midpoint, so I stopped it undecided. Runs are reused: rerunning `dgate.py variants/v87-dfp-pure
  variants/oc-base25` resumes it.
- **Carry routing, v87-dfp-carry.** The plan's gold is weighted by relative_efficiency at base stats. Gold by r400
  in the mirror: Vesper +35, HoR +11. dgate 50.51% (50.03-50.99) over 14,336 units, no better than pure; stopped.
- **Enemy model on pure (v87-dfp-race, 2026-11-09).** The middle is a symmetric race in live data (first middle
  captures r50/72/104 both sides). So the plan adds middle candidates, an enemy timeline taken from the mirror of our
  own greedy opening, and raced and contested values. Two forms: deny 1 and deny 0. In the mirror the middle
  concession is gone, but so is the own-half gain. dgate against pure: H0 for both (-0.25 ±0.53, -0.16 ±0.50). Against
  oc-base25 at stop: 50.16 and 50.26. Pure stays the form.
- **Verdict.** Forcing or following an enemy-free plan cedes the middle. As a bias it is a real, small gain
  against non-mirror drafts, in rule 0's 50-50.5 zone. Merge read: weak no (~330 lines of draft code; it cedes the
  middle, which live Fish and Mite contest harder). At most it merits a live pair against v87. The sim's +14-18% at
  H100-150 was a model artefact (fidelity r ~0.3). The HoR gold gap is not closed by own-half routing.

## (ocean, 2026-11-07) Rejection audit

Every rejected, level or null verdict was reclassified by power: (a) decided, (b) underpowered, (c) flawed. The table is in [rejection-audit.md](ideas-2026-11-07/rejection-audit.md). Most "level" calls were 1-20k games with upper bounds of +0.5 to +1.3; 36 frozen pairs that still exist and differ only by the idea were rerun to a decision. Every pair ran on both sides' own drafts (all `test_draft` off) under fastrunner.

**Method.**
- **Common gates:** ab.py `--sprt 0.50,0.5025` (H1 +0.25), each run with its own seed. The screen was at 2x fuel (200k) on unused `audit-p1` (791001-791600, 153,600 maps); its minimum was 200 games for the first five runs and 20,000 after.
- **Held out:** each H1 went to 40,960 real-budget games on `audit-p2a` (792001-792080). Every held-out run whose CI still held 0 was rerun as a real-budget SPRT, minimum 40,960 games, on a second unused pool, `audit-p3` (793001-793600).
- **Rare gates:** paired per map and side against a base-vs-base mirror on the same maps (deterministic, so games the change never touches score 0), in 12,800-game chunks until the paired CI decided. Scripts, queues and logs: [audit-tools/](ideas-2026-11-07/audit-tools/) (`paired.py`, `driver2.sh`, `driver3.sh`).
- **Caution:** an SPRT can stop after a few thousand games when nearly every map pair splits 1-1, where its normal approximation is poor (sge's first H0 at 2,747 games). That is why the later runs use a 20,000-game minimum.

**Winners at the real budget** (2x SPRT H1, then a real-budget confirmation on unused maps):

| idea | pair | 2x SPRT | held out, real (p2a) | real SPRT (p3) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Opening gate + re-pick (EXPERIMENTS "Chases and leaves") | astraeus-gatefix-9465660 vs astraeus-5713135 | H1, 50.74 of 32,644 | 50.72 (50.24-51.20) | H1, 50.42 (50.05-50.78) of 72,343 |
| Opening gate alone | astraeus-gate-ca78811 vs astraeus-5713135 | H1, 50.39 of 75,410 | 50.30 (49.81-50.78) | H1, 50.56 (50.11-51.00) of 48,413 |
| Kill-now value on kills only | ast-kill1b vs astraeus-294 | H1, 50.74 of 20,061 | 50.52 (50.04-51.01) | H1, 50.78 (50.30-51.27) of 40,987 |
| Area control a3 (a guard joins a held cleared group an enemy closes on) | oc-ac-a3 vs oc-combo2 | H1, 50.52 of 22,547 | 50.19 (49.70-50.67) | H1, 50.29 (50.00-50.58) of 112,340 |
| value3 SPSA type weights | oc-v3-tuned vs oc-base3 | H1, 50.33 of 130,044 | 49.94 (49.46-50.43) | H1, 50.28 (50.05-50.52) of 174,811 |
