## (ocean = oc-base25, 2026-11-09) Camp aggro: waking a Monolith onto a nearer enemy is an even exchange; stopped

Write-up [campaggro-2026-11-08/NOTES.md](campaggro-2026-11-08/NOTES.md), arm patch `ca-flee.patch`, scripts alongside.
Live: in 15% of 2,555 Fish/Mite games, an enemy sits strictly nearer a sleeping Monolith than any of us while one of ours
can wake it. We are nearly always inside its range then (3-4 tiles to their 2-3). Fish and Mite never do it on purpose
(~7 incidental HoR landings). The conservative arm (Monolith only, worst-case moves, blow gate) fired ~2.8 times per 100
games. Its woken camps dealt 77k to the enemy and 81k to us: we stay near it for our own farming, chases and retreats.
Triggered games paired against a base mirror read 42% vs 50% (64 games). A Safety fix (an enemy yet to act shields a
Monolith tile only after its flee) changed neither. Screens on ca-scr (ladder-v2 1330000-079, seeds 1335001-006):
ca-k1 50.0% of 40,960 undecided, H0 at 2x; ca-flee 50.0% of 40,960 undecided, H0 at 2x; flee alone H0 at both. Spar
+0.24 / -0.44 / +0.69 (±2.4-2.9). Not leaned into: ties, golems and elk repeat the same even exchange more often.
The one-sided cases (a victim pinned by a tribute, us out of range) are ~1% of fires.
Lean-in (user: act last next round so ties and walk-outs go our way): the waker at the lowest priority, tie wakes
against a settled enemy acting first next round, a step clear of the woken group (`ca-last`), or every body clear of
any awake unclaimed Monolith (`ca-last-all`). The trade per fire improves to 1.2:1 and 1.84:1 (210k vs 115k, enemy deaths
95 to our 50). dgate H0 on both: -0.49 ±0.60 (21.5k games), -0.53 ±0.61 (22.0k games). Stopped: ~5 fires per 100 games
of a few hundred hp don't move games, and the steps cost tempo and +4% out-of-fuel turns.
Strict gate (user: wake only when the waker can't attack or cast at an enemy champion this turn; `ca-strict` on
ca-last): 4.5 fires per 100 games, 1.24:1, the victim dies in 15% of fires (28% with our own follow-up hits); dgate H0,
-0.52 ±0.60 (21.5k games).

Yield generalisations on dgate (pts vs oc-base25 ± 95%, cand games; all H0): y2t (y2 + receivers told) -0.94 ±0.71 of
26,112; yh (value yield, only to receivers already coming this way) -1.19 ±0.76 of 24,576; yv (value yield, anyone)
-1.43 ±0.81 of 20,992; yc (anyone to the carry) -1.67 ±0.83 of 19,968; ycw (yc + Willow follows the carry) -1.53 ±0.83
of 19,968. Old screens agree (y2t 49.0, yh 48.5, yv 47.5, yc 47.2, ycw 48.2; all H0 at 0.505).
- Reweighting the split in any direction is H0 or level: the current `relative_efficiency` (stat-growth^1.47) is at a
  local optimum.
- A yield's worth (bin/yieldvalue.py, base side, 512 games, r<=400): 12.2 single-holder gold captures a game have a
  more efficient ally alive; 3.8 a game had one no farther away at the clear (worth ~210 gold x efficiency gap a game),
  0.5 a game each at +1, +2, +3 steps, 5.6 beyond +6. The receiver was heading there (distance down 2+ in 3 rounds) in
  only ~19% of them, and passed within 1 of the tile in the next 10 rounds in 23% (+0) falling to 4% (+7). The free
  cases are mostly both bodies 4+ away, the receiver bound elsewhere. Pulling a receiver off its plan costs more than
  the efficiency gap gains: telling receivers (y2t) turns y2's +1.0 into -0.9, and each wider yield loses more.
- **Reopened (user: "there's no less or equidistant gate?", "it worked with c&i so surely the model should learn
  that"):** y2's distance gate kept, no telling, only who yields to whom generalised by `holder_value` (mode 1, step
  price 0). Sanity first: at base stats a 2x value gap picks y2's yields (Cassi to all 10 non-shy types, Issac to 8),
  plus Prism/HoR/Stellar to Ryth/Vesper/Vendetta and Willow to all. In games (vg2, 512): Cassi 92 -> 77, Issac 208 ->
  180 (y2: 91 -> 82, 199 -> 187), Vesper +70, Ryth +67, team -0.8%. dgate, all H0: vg2 (ratio 2, +2 steps) -1.56
  ±0.83; vg0 (ratio 2, no farther) -0.95 ±0.70; vg2w (ratio 1.5, +2) -1.39 ±0.80. Controls: y0 +0.19 ±0.37 of 13,952
  units (H0); y2 on the new bodies (dgate2) ZONE, +0.18 ±0.25 over 36,608 units (146,944 games). Only the shy holders' yields pay;
  each yield the efficiency model adds for a non-shy holder costs. So C&I's gain is the pair's death risk (both bodies
  and bags), not stat efficiency, and a value model that sends gold to the carry by efficiency rates that gold too high.

- Carry (carryhold.py): Vesper holds 45% of captures paying >= 80; for the rest it was within 2 steps in 2.6%.
  Holder-side funnels can't feed it. What's left is farm choice (the draftfarm line).

How far each local test reads above live, for the merge chain v86 → v87 → v89 → v91. Bots: v86 `oc-base23`, v87
`oc-base25`, v89 `oc-base27`, v91 `oc-base29`. Mirror runs are own drafts, release builds, fast runner, on the fresh
`ch-held` suite (maps/SUITES.md "Chain ends against v86"), with SPRT 0.50/0.5025 from 40,960 games. Panel is
astraeus-td, proteus-td and the test-draft mirror on `ch-pan`, pooled by `panel_sprt.py`. Spar is `spar_ab.py` with
release copies (`variants/chain-b*`), 6,656 paired games. Live is r2, paired against v86 on the same 512 games
(`ladder-scrims-2026-11-06/data/cells-r2.tsv`). Logs: `~/tmp-offload/chain/logs`.

Results against oc-base23 (v86), in points (cand − v86):

| step | mirror (held out) | panel | spar | dgate | live (paired, n 512) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v87 oc-base25 | +0.27 of 167,789, H1 (LLR 2.96) | +0.46, H1 (dir +0.62, ast +0.09, pro +0.68) | +0.78 ±2.9 | (its REF) | **−1.8 ±4.7** (−9, z −0.74) |
| v89 oc-base27 | — | — | +0.63 ±3.5 | — | **−2.3 ±4.9** (−12, z −0.94) |
| v91 oc-base29 | **+1.95** of 40,962, H1 (LLR 8.1) | **+2.12**, H1 (LLR 22; dir +2.43, ast +1.96, pro +1.97) | **+4.07 ±3.4** | **+1.81 ±1.03** of 3,200 units (blocks 0-24), LLR +1.06, stopped undecided | **−4.3 ±5.0** (−22, z −1.69) |
| v93 oc-nosoup (v91 − soup-k + mask) | — | — | — | — | −5.3 (−27, z −2.04) |

- **Local is consistent with itself.** The steps' own mirror gains (CHANGES 465-471, ~+0.2-0.5 each) add to ~+2.1;
  the end-to-end mirror reads +1.95 and the panel +2.12. Nothing is lost in composition.
- **Live is consistent with itself too, in the other direction.** Every live step is ≤ 0 (v87 −9, v88 −2, v89 −1,
  v90 −12 on 200, v91 −3 on 200), none significant; the end of the chain is at z −1.7 (v91) and z −2.0 (v93).
- **The gap.** v91: mirror +1.95 against live −4.3 is a 6.3-point gap at z ≈ 2.5 (live's SE 2.5 dominates); spar's
  +4.1 is 8.4 points above live (z ≈ 2.7). For v87 the gap is 2.0 points (z ≈ 0.8). So the overfit grows with the
  chain: most of it sits in v87 → v91's +1.7 local points (Heart of Ruin 467/468, the altar-deny lock and soup-k's
  emblems and casts, 470/471), which live reads at about −2.5. The live-like designs (spar, dgate) read the same sign
  as the mirror: they raise per-map r, not the chain's sign.
- **dgate calibration.** `dgate.py variants/oc-base29 variants/oc-base23 --stage screen` reads v91 at +1.81
  ±1.03 after 25 blocks (z ≈ 3.4), where live reads −4.3: **dgate fails its key calibration** and reads the chain
  like the mirror. Block 0 (v87 and v91 as opponents) read +0.68; the running mean rose to +1.8 as noise seeds were added. It was
  stopped at LLR +1.06 because the screen needed about 45 more fresh blocks (~4 h) and the sign was already settled;
  the runs are cached (`spar-cbase29-dvn*`, `spar-cbase23-dvn*`) if anyone resumes it. A dgate H1 doesn't predict a
  live gain on this chain.
- **What it means for gates.** A local +2 on this chain is worth ≤ 0 live. Until a local test reads v86 → v91 at
  ≤ 0, local H1s are a filter, not evidence of a live gain; only live paired results decide merges (TEST-STANDARD
  rule 7).

## (ocean, 2026-11-09) Why v90-v93 lose live: v86's lucky draw, then a real ~5-point gap on altar/lock play

Tools `research/ideas-2026-11-09/liveforensic-tools/`, data `~/tmp-offload/liveforensic/`. Inputs: the r2 replays of
v86-v95 (512 paired cells each), decoded per game, and new local runs of oc-base27 and oc-base28 (= 27 + 470) against
spar-oc29-F/M (live picks, 512 games each, `lf-c2[78]-o29[FM]`).
- **Part of the chain's slide is v86's own draw.** Any build change rerolls most games: two unrelated builds flip
  ~165 of 512 cells (32%), so each version's live score carries ±1.8 points of reroll noise. v86 is the best of the 7
  rerolls (65.8%). Every chain step is read against that one draw, so their negative signs aren't independent evidence.
  Across versions the spread of scores matches reroll noise (χ² p ≈ 0.25). The ordering doesn't: the last ones are lowest (p ≈ 0.03-0.07).
- **Pooled over independent rerolls the drop is real.** v86/v87/v89/v95 (no soup-k, no 470) 63.5-65.8%, mean 64.6;
  v91/v93 61.5 / 60.5; v90 58.5 on its 200 cells (A there 64.1). B (v91, v93) − A = **−3.6 ±1.6 points** live,
  where the local tests read v89 → v91 at +1.2 to +1.7: a **~5-point gap, z ≈ 3**. 465-468 (v87-v89, v95) are level
  live. The loss arrives with soup-k (v90) and/or 470 (v91, v93). An additive fit gives 470 −2.7 ±2 and soup-k −1.7
  ±2; they can't be separated (v93 reverts soup-k and doesn't recover).
- **Where.** By B − A: 600-1200-round games carry it all (−19 net games of −18), with one-site maps −6.6 pts (−12.5
  games) and non-Willow −5.7. **One-site games past round 1200 are not it** (33 cells, A 33% / B 27%, −2 games). Every
  version loses ~70% of those, so they're a shared weakness, not the regression. All of v90, v91 and v93 lose most
  on one-site maps (−8.6, −4.3, −9.0).
- **470's mechanism, live and local alike.** Without deny locks before round 600, our early locks fall 3.1 → 0.5 a
  game and the opponents' lock attacks fall by ~7 (live −7.3, local −6.0), and their gold at 600 rises (+74 / +62).
  **The response differs on one-site maps.** Live, Fish/Mite tribute **+28 ±23** more gems by round 600 and earn +138
  gold; local spar bodies tribute −7 ±24 and earn +29. The win effect differs too: live −6.6 pts, local −0.5 (local
  470's +2.9 is all on multi-site maps, +4.9). Per map, local 470 effect against live B − A: r = −0.16.
- **The behaviour our bodies lack: threat-reactive tribute feints.** On one-site maps Fish/Mite cancel their own
  tribute 1.9 times a game against v89 and 2.6 against v91 (no early locks). Ocean bodies cancel 0.55 times. 87-92% of
  Fish/Mite cancels come with one of ours within 5 tiles, 70-81% within a round of starting (ocean bodies: 55-72%,
  41-51%). They start, cancel when we come, and restart: an unlocked lone altar pays them, while a lock costs them ~4
  attacks. Against ocean bodies, which neither feint nor retry, a deny lock is mostly wasted gold, so 470 reads as a gain.
- **What a local test needs.** (1) Read live as reroll-pooled levels (several builds a line), not one pair against a
  pinned base. (2) An opponent with Fish/Mite's tribute policy on contested altars (start/cancel/retry within 5
  tiles of us, ~2 cancels per one-site game). Calibrate it on the c27/c28 pair: the gate should read 470 ≤ 0 on one-site
  maps and op600 +25 before it's trusted on altar/lock changes. (3) Cheap live candidate: restore deny locks before
  600 on one-site maps only. Local sees 470's gain only on multi-site maps, so it costs nothing there.

lk-600 read +2.15 ±3.05 on block 0 (v87/v91) and +0.62 ±0.76 at 31 blocks, then fell to +0.05. **Closed, and the
dgate reading isn't trusted either way:** the live forensics (section "Why v90-v93 lose live") put 470's rule at about
-2.7 ±2 live, on one-site maps. Without early locks, Fish and Mite tribute ~28 more gems by round 600. Our local
opponents rarely cancel and restart tributes, so no local gate sees that cost. Don't retry an early-lock cut without
an opponent that feints tributes.

**Badmaps closed.** Fix A (camp-bound enemies neither pull a pursuit nor raise the recall line) was built from a few
bad maps (00fragment's centre clear) but changes ~22% of spar games, so it is a broad fight-policy change, not a
targeted one: what it gains where tanks stood on a mirrored clear it gives back where a camp-bound enemy is about to
be free and does fight. Every subform is H0 or level on the mirror at both fuels; only pursuit-only (bm-ap) is not
negative, and nothing nears 50.5%. Fix B (bank_floor) touches ~5% of maps (gem-scarce); a tiny real effect (+0.19 on
the panel) cannot clear the all-maps bar, and it is H0 at 2x.

**wx closed.** Exact ward sight only sharpens which tiles a ward reveals; decisions rarely change (mirror 50.0% of
163,840) and where they do it is slightly worse at 2x (H0) and on the spar (-1.5): the old approximation was not a
source of losses. Rejected: none of these is queued for live.

## (ocean, 2026-11-08) Diverse panel: noise-seeded live-draft opponents; per-map r 0.10 → 0.37, chain still reads above live

[research/ideas-2026-11-08/diverse-panel.md](ideas-2026-11-08/diverse-panel.md), tools in `diverse-tools/`. This
answers the user's overfit question (opponents built from other tunings, randomness and ladder drafts).
- **Setup.** Each design was calibrated on the 128 ladder maps with oc-base23/25/26/27/29 and oc-s2-soupk27
  (v86-v91) as cands, 256 games per run, ~50k games in all.
- **Bodies** are oc-base25 (oc-tune3) with one of:
  - oc6's SPSA iterate, its reverse, or an aggressive, passive or greedy style;
  - noise: the 26 tuned knobs redrawn every 100 rounds as × exp(0.2 N), seeded per game (seeds 1310001-1310008).
- **Drafts:** Fish's and Mite's live picks (spar tables) or ladder compositions (test_draft).

| design | per-map r with live | v86→91 (live -4.3 ±5.0) | chain signs right (of 6) | games per A/B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| current panel (astraeus-td, proteus-td) | +0.10 | +6.6 ±5.1 | 1 | 1,024 |
| spar (oc-base29 + 12 jitters, live picks) | +0.38 | +3.3 ±3.5 | 0 | 13,312 |
| 5 tunings/styles, live picks | +0.35 | +2.6 ±2.4 | 2 | 5,120 |
| 5 tunings/styles, ladder comps | +0.37 | +2.9 ±3.0 | 1 | 2,560 |
| **8 noise seeds, live picks** | **+0.37** | +1.4 ±1.9 | 0 | 8,192 |
| all of the above with live picks | +0.40 | +2.6 ±2.2 | 1 | 22,528 |

- **Draft and strength decide the per-map r; body variety doesn't.** Every ocean-strength body on live or ladder
  picks reads 0.35-0.40.
- **Noise games are independent.** The cell-clustered CI equals the per-game CI (spar's is 2.4x), so precision
  grows with seeds instead of stopping at the 512-cell floor.
- **Not reproduced: live's chain.** No design reproduces the negative live chain (live ±4.6 a step: every design
  passes χ² against it). The first 4 noise seeds' +0.2 for v86→91 did not replicate (seeds 5-8: +2.6).
- **Gate:** `diverse-tools/dpanel_ab.py CAND REF` runs per-map units pooled over noise seeds 1-32 with ab.py's SPRT.
  Use it as a live-likeness gate next to the held-out suite: non-negative required. It replaces the
  astraeus-td/proteus-td panel, not the held-out SPRT.
- **Gold/gem cheats** (user idea) were not built. Strength isn't what limits r, a round-1 gold lump distorts the
  openings where live flips diverge, and noise already gives the diversity. A per-team income multiplier is the form
  to try if the carry gap is chased.

## (ocean, 2026-11-08) Priority mask: our live priorities coded per game, from v93

- **Why:** replays record every champion's priority, though not the shared or draft bytes. Ocean packs a rank and a
  payload (claim + 1, support intents) into its priorities, which anyone can read, as we read Mite's.
- **What:** live builds only. The live scheduler patches `prio_mask.h` into its build copy
  (`~/tmp-offload/handoff/sched/prio_mask/`; the key is in `~/.config/cambc-secret/`, outside git). The code is set up
  once at World's init, seeded from the key, the map, our side and our picks.
  - `packed_priority` shifts the rank by a secret amount on each side of 0, which keeps the order and the sign, so the
    engine's turn order and every comparison of ranks are unchanged.
  - The payload is xored with a mask fixed per game, and `payload_of` undoes it. Nothing else changes.
- **Checks** (oc-base29, bench `--set wide` against the uncoded bot):

  | | own drafts | test drafts |
  |---|---|---|
  | same play at 100M (`same_play.mjs`) | 52/52 | 52/52 |
  | same play at the real budget | 48/52 | 47/52 |
  | fuel per turn at 100M: mean, p50, p99 | +30, +28, +76 | +29, +28, +72 |

  - The ±3k (p99.9) and ±25k per-turn extremes come from the bot's fuel-budgeted searches, which react to any extra
    fuel. A flat +70 shows the same swings.
  - With a zero key, the patched bot is byte-identical (52/52, the same fuel).
  - In every coded replay, the coded rank is a strictly increasing function of the plain one, and the payload map is a
    bijection. Read the public way, the values give no ranks and no claim bytes. A host test checked the round trip and
    the order over 3.9e9 values.
- **Earlier revisions** (fuel per turn at 100M, own drafts): decoding every ally's priority on each read cost +244
  (mean). A keyed 16-bit multiply-xor payload with decode on change cost +74 mean and +255 at p99; v93 went up with a
  version of it at about +80. The cost was in re-encoding the payload, which changes nearly every turn.

## (ocean, 2026-11-08) Carry: Fish and Mite out-earn the same picks by +14-18% at r200; neither copied habit ships

Write-up `research/ideas-2026-11-08/carry.md`, tools and patches `carry-tools/`. Data: 500 v89 live games against
Fish and r2 Mite, paired with the same (map, side, drafts) game against spar-oc29.
- **Spar's fidelity table was partly wrong.** Local replays were keyed by file name, which the F and M runs share, so
  232 of 500 Fish rows read a Mite-drafted game. `fidelity.py` and `early_types.py` are fixed. Corrected r200: team
  +14% / +18%; Vesper +38 / +37%; Marcella +46 / +71%; HoR −3 / +84%; Issac −45%, Tavi −62%.
- **What differs.** Same camp-hit count and gold per camp damage, but +12-17% camp damage by r600 and fewer
  champion-attack turns (77 vs 98).
  - Joint clears: 53% of captures have ≥ 2 dealers, against 42%, and the carry holds (Vesper does 0.43 of the damage
    on its holds, against 0.62).
  - Cohesion: the nearest ally is ≤ 2 tiles 61% of the time, against 45%.
  - After a capture with a bag under 40 they ride home 22-33% of the time, against 51-53%. The ocean body has 14
    healthy gem-carrying recalls a game, against 7.5-9.
  - 41-51% of their tributes are under 25 gems, against 5%.
  - Carry gold share predicts nothing with team gold held fixed.
- **Arms on oc-base29** (panel on `cr-panel-122` pooled through `panel_sprt.py`, varied on `cr-varied-122`; seeds
  1220000-1220139):

  | arm | panel (0.4975/0.50) | varied | spar_ab (6,656) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | nosmallride: no capture ride for a bag unbankable after payout (rides 16.3 → 6.1 a game) | −1.55, H0 | 49.7% | −1.9 ±3.1 |
  | join15: a group claimed by an ally that out-holds us rates ×1.5 | −0.26, undecided | 50.5% | −0.9 ±3.4 |
  | join20: the same, ×2.0 | −0.79, H0 | 50.3% | −1.9 ±3.6 |

  - join moves cohesion from 45% to 47-49% (live: 61%).
  - Earnings stay flat, apart from +5-15% for the Mite-draft carries.
- **Verdict:** ocean's rides home pay for themselves through the shop. A claim-join multiplier doesn't reproduce
  Fish's joining. join15 is level and is queued live at priority 30, for the coordinator to keep or drop.

## (ocean, 2026-11-08) Spar: live drafts make a local opponent see the ladder maps (r 0.06 → 0.34); not yet a gate

Tool, no ocean change; full note: [spar.md](ideas-2026-11-08/spar.md) (tools in `spar-tools/`).
- **Setup:** an ocean-family opponent that plays Fish's or Mite's exact live picks per ladder (map, side). The table
  is keyed by `map_hash`, and the bodies are `bots/variants/spar-*`, rebuilt by `build_panel.sh`.
  - Cand = the live versions (oc-base23/25/26/27), so every local game pairs with a live cell.
  - Both teams' local picks equal the live ones in 512 of 512 games.
- **Per-map r with live** (v86-89, Fish + r2 Mite, 128 maps):

  | setup | r |
  |---|---|
  | old opponents | -0.10..+0.20 (pooled 0.15) |
  | oc-base29 on its own draft | 0.06 |
  | spar-oc29 | **0.33** (0.16..0.48) |
  | spar-o29gs | 0.36 |
  | jitter panel (52 games a map) | 0.34 |
  | weaker bodies on live drafts (astraeus, proteus, bots/fish...) | ≤ 0.22 |
  | live Fish against live Mite | 0.38; a second top bot would read ~0.46 |

  - Ocean wins 66-69% against the spar (live 64%).
  - The maps lost ≥ 75% live are won 49-56%, against 81% against the old opponents.
- **What is left is behaviour.**
  - In the same map, side and draft, the live opponent earns +14% gold by r200. The extra goes to its carries
    (Vesper +32-42%, HoR +20-84%, Marcella +24-89%).
  - It does 14% less champion damage and 10% more camp damage.
  - Seven knob bodies (brave, cautious, camp-bold, gold price) span r 0.20-0.36, all within noise of each other.
- **Deltas (6,656 paired games a bot against Fish and Mite live, CI by cell):**

  | change | spar | live |
  |---|---|---|
  | v86→v89 | +0.9 ±3.4 | -2.3 ±4.9 |
  | soup-k (v89→v90) | +1.4 ±2.8 | -6.0 ±6.9 |

  - Opposite signs, neither significant.
  - Per-cell delta correlation 0.01.
  - Precision is capped by the 512 deterministic cells for both. 3% jitter re-draws only 18% of games.
- **Verdict:** use it for per-map diagnosis and big changes on the live pool, not for merge gates. Next: a
  carry-first gold body, judged by `fidelity.py` before r.

## (ocean, 2026-11-08) Big levers: loss modes against Fish and Mite; local tests are blind to the losing maps

Analysis only; full note: [big-levers.md](ideas-2026-11-08/big-levers.md) (tools in `big-levers-tools/`).
- **Data:** 2,555 v86-89 scrims against Fish and Mite (1,762 distinct), decoded.
- **The losses are a symmetric snowball.**
  - End owned-gem gap -594 (captures -346, kill transfers -264).
  - Gaps are small early (-34 at r200); the first kill swings 77% against 53%.
  - Death contexts, opening steals, fight-free farming and clear speed are even or in our favour.
- **The losses are concentrated by map:** 8 maps are ≤ 30% against both opponents, and 12% of (map, side, opponent)
  cells are lost in every version.
- **Per-map win% locally against live** (oc-base27 against 11 local opponents on the 128 ladder maps):
  - r = 0.07 for the panel-td pair, and 0.04-0.22 for every other bot;
  - local half against local half is 0.26, but live Fish against live Mite is 0.55;
  - the 9 maps lost ≥ 75% live are won 81% locally.
- **Paired live v86 to v89:** -2.9 points (CI -7.6..+1.8) across four locally-H1 merges.
- **Closed** (with numbers in the note): draft like the top teams (Prism is +0.93 logit against Fish/Mite in the
  archive), endgame close-out (we blow 7% of crossings, they 16%), big-bag channels, Mite intent reading.
- **Proposed:** a live-correlated sparring partner (gate: per-map r ≥ 0.4), and live-judged map-class fixes on the
  robust-loss maps.

## (ocean, 2026-11-08/09) v87 Heart of Ruin: contested camp landings H0; 468's hurt landing floor and enemy fight_scale level on dgate; closed

Against oc-base25 (v87), own drafts, real budget, release, fast runner; write-up research/ideas-2026-11-08/hor-camp-dash.md,
arms `variants/v87-*`, data `~/tmp-offload/v87hor/`. Screen suite v87hor-scr-1241 (ladder-v2), SPRT 0.50/0.5025.

- **Contested camp landings (the user's camp-dash idea) rejected, all three H0.** Live, with an enemy 5-6 tiles away
  Mite's HoR lands on camps 44% of ready-dash rounds and ours 11-16%, because `camp_cast` stands down while
  `engagement_near` holds. The arms let the landing through when no visible enemy is within `near` of the HoR or the
  landing tile: `v87-cd-k4` (near 4) 49.9% of 21,100, `v87-cd-k3` (near 3) 49.8% of 16,952, `v87-cd-k3h6` (near 3,
  health at least 0.6) 50.0% of 25,634. The mechanism works (k3: 5-6 band 13% -> 19% camp landings, 7-8 band
  40% -> 49%), but it doesn't win. Decisive map pairs (both sides won by the same bot) are 7-8% for every cd arm, split
  evenly (k3: +323 -349; k4 +378 -395; k3h6 +431 -439), on ladder-shaped and other maps alike. Spar with live drafts
  on the ladder maps reads the same: k3 -0.12 (±0.97), flips +116 -124. Mite's contested-landing rate is a rate gap,
  not a lever: closing part of it moves no results.
- **468's hurt landing floor (`landing_floor`: below `hor_hurt_fraction` of max health, a landing on enemies needs
  `hor_hurt_landing` x 250)**, by threshold: `v87-nh-6-3` (0.6, x3) H1 50.7% of 13,052; `v87-nh-6-2` (= 468) H1
  50.5% of 18,543; `v87-nh-5-2` H1 50.3% of 33,744. Decisive pairs: +431 -344 (11.9% of pairs), +518 -434 (10.3%)
  and +795 -700 (8.9%). The gain is weakest on ladder-shaped maps (net +0.36, +0.59 and +0.59 pair points, against
  +1.1 to +2.5 on the other generators). Spar is negative for both arms it has read: nh-6-3 -0.53 (±1.06), nh-6-2
  -0.92 (±1.20). nh-5-2 is the weakest sibling of one mechanism and gets no gates of its own; nh-6-3 leads and
  nh-6-2 is its comparison.
- **nh-6-3 meets the 99% live bar and is queued** (2026-11-09; "base oc-base25, pair vs v87"): held out
  (v87hor-held-1242, alpha/beta 0.01) H1 50.30% of 62,879, LLR 4.62; 2x fuel H1 50.23% of 65,018; old panel pooled
  +0.93 pts of 61,440 units, H1 (direct 51.15% of 40,960); varied 50.05% of 20,480, LLR +1.35, undecided, not H0.
  The screen's ladder-map caveat doesn't replicate on the held out (ladder-shaped pairs +0.71 pair points, others

budget. Screens: ab.py `--sprt 0.50,0.5025`, `--sprt-min-games 20000`, own `--sprt-seed` each (11-15), on unused
`merged/port-scr-630` (630000-630467, 119,808 maps). Plan after an H1: 40,960 held out on `port-held-631` (and
`port-held-632` while its CI held 50), varied `port-varied-633`, panel `port-panel-634` paired per map against
oc-base23 (members gp-panel-astraeus-td, gp-panel-proteus-td, oc-base23-td). Scripts: `/home/ubuntu/tmp-offload/port/`.

What each port is (the idea's own diff, read against its frozen base):
- **kill1b**: `converts()` and the search's `banked` term only (a kill now credits the damage already on a foe
  by 1 - its conversion rate). ast-kill1b's audit pair against astraeus-294 also carried ast-follow v2 (the kept kill
  bid, no bid while channelling), which shipped in CHANGES 295 and is in ocean; the idea's own diff is
  ast-follow-v2 -> ast-kill1b. In astraeus follow v2 alone read 50.3 / 50.2, so most of the audit's +0.78 may be it.
- **gate** (gatefix 9465660): the strike search drops a plan whose hit on a champion (none reaching our start tile,
  killing none) ends on a tile where want_home's stand (`stand_lost_at`) would send us home, re-picks up to 3 times,
  and the goal's steps keep off the vetoed tiles (work guard). It gates opening a fight, not the draft or the game's
  opening. **gate1**: the same veto with no re-pick (ca78811, the turn's strikes dropped).
- **ac3**: `guard_hold` (a free ally within 10 steps joins an ally's held cleared gem group while a seen enemy is
  within 4 of its centre), as a contest branch after `contest_capture`.
- **v3tw**: value3's SPSA type weights as farm's per_gold factor (ours over the living team's mean) in place of
  420's `relative_efficiency`, holders (419) unchanged. value3-tuned was mode 3 (type weights instead of an
  efficiency) on the wealth funnel; ocean's 420 is e1 (fight-power gain x gold rate) in that same slot, so the
  faithful port is the substitution. Multiplying both would count the gold rate twice with weights never fitted so.

## Combat lab experiments 1-2 (ocean v83, 2026-11-07; lab only, nothing shipped)

The combat lab (`research/combat-lab/PLAN.md`, `fastrunner scenario`): lab copies of v83 (`variants/lab-v83`) and
astraeus (`variants/lab-astraeus-8c0343f`) replay bank2 fight frames for 30 rounds. Reward from the deciding
team's side: hp/max hp of each live fighter, -1 a death, +0.01 a gem, ours minus theirs. Each experiment ran
ocean vs ocean, ocean vs astraeus and astraeus vs ocean on the same 20k frames; frames are split by hashed id, and a
model fitted on half of the ocean-vs-ocean frames is judged on the other half of every run, so the astraeus runs
are an opponent it never saw. Lab copies' hooks cost ~217 fuel a turn: never ship one.

- **Exp 1, the strike search's next-best candidates** (`--alt 8`, 20k frames, ~150k alternatives a run). With
  hindsight the best of 9 beats ocean's choice by +0.84 a decision, and an alternative's gain replicates on the
  same frame against the other opponent (corr 0.33-0.35, shuffled 0.00). It does not carry to other frames: no
  single reweighting of the score's parts (raw, danger, progress, camp, shield, each x0-3) moves held-out gain
  beyond +-0.005, a least-squares refit is worse than ocean (-0.007 to -0.034), and a boosted model of state and
  both candidates' parts predicts held-out gains at corr 0.03-0.06 and loses at every threshold. Ocean's tile
  choice is as good as these features allow; the gains are one fight's geometry.
- **Exp 2, flipped fight-or-leave verdicts** (`--flip 1,5,30`: each fighter's first want_home and first chase
  verdict forced the other way for 1, 5 or 30 rounds; 20k frames held out from exp 1; ~410k applied flips a run;
  a chase forced on with no target does not apply). Mean gain of a 30-round flip, ocean vs ocean:
  - Retreat overridden to stay: -0.93 (31% better, 61% worse).
  - Stay overridden to retreat: -0.19.
  - Chase stopped: -0.39.
  - Chase started where ocean declined: +0.04 (+0.05 / +0.03 by side).

  Same-frame replication across opponents: corr 0.10-0.47. Learnable from state, on held-out frames: only stay ->
  retreat, +0.048 / +0.043 / +0.037 a stay decision (oo / oa / ao), flipping 25-47% of them (+0.08 to +0.17 a flip).
  Chase -> start gains +0.02 / +0.02 / +0.00, and the other two lose. Top features: allies' hp and fighter count,
  ocean's branch, our gems, foes' hp. **Open:** whether a learned retreat rule survives full games, since the
  reward counts no farming time lost to a retreat. It needs a distilled rule in ocean and an ab.py test.

## Backlog (ocean, 2026-11-06)

A serial queue of low-priority items, each a variant of `variants/oc-base10` with `params::bl::` knobs. The design
and status of every item are in research/ideas-2026-11-06/BACKLOG.md.
- With the knobs off, each variant replays oc-base10 identically at 100M (bench.py, default 16 and wide 52).
- Screens: 2x fuel, SPRT 0.50/0.51, own drafts, one `--sprt-seed` per arm (660001+), on `maps/suites/merged/bl-dev`
  (s660000-s660039, 20,480 games).

**1. Tiebreak awareness (`oc-bl-tbg`, `oc-bl-tbd`, `oc-bl-tb1`): level, too small to measure.**
- Reach of the round-2000 rules, in 20,480 oc-base10-like games (p2-1-held):
  - 2.4% of games reach round 2000;
  - 44 of those (0.2% of all games) are tied on tributed gems, 36 of them at 0-0, decided on gold;
  - in 63, the loser's carried bag exceeded the gap. Nearly all of those are bags of hundreds to thousands of gems
    that no channel could land in time; the bank already takes any risk on a last-chance tribute (bank.cc
    `any_risk`).
- The knobs:
  - `tb_gold`: from round 1200, with tributed gems tied, farm prices gold at a floor of 0.1 gems a gold;
  - `tb_deny`: in the last 150 rounds, a visible enemy channel that lands by round 2000 and draws them level or
    ahead is denied whatever its size.
- Subset (the 341 maps of those round-2000 games, 682 games), paired against a knobs-off copy on the same maps.
  Real-budget flips are mostly fuel divergence, so the clean read is at 2x:

  | Arm | 2x, paired | Real budget, paired |
  |---|---|---|
  | `tb_gold` | +5 net (7 / 2 flips) | |
  | `tb_deny` | 0 (1 / 1) | |
  | both | +5 (8 / 3) | -10 (9 / 19) |

- Held-out subset (275 round-2000 maps of three other batches, 550 games, 2x): `tb_gold` +2 net (5 / 3).
- Full screen (`oc-bl-tbg`, seed 660001): 50.4% of 651 games, H0. The SPRT stops this early because nearly every
  map pair is the same game.
- Forensics: the flips are 0-0 and tied games (homonoliths, shared-gems, one-gem mutations) that the gold
  tiebreak decides, so the decision has the right sign. Pooled, it is +7 of 1,232 games where it can fire, about
  +0.02 points overall.
- Not a merge candidate. Knobs for the soup: `bl::tb_gold` 0.1 and `bl::tb_round` 1200 (a binary gate, of no use to
  SPSA).

**2. Grouping, round 1 (`oc-bl-grp*`, farm-choice leans): no pack formed, so grouping is not yet tested. The
early and big-map gates lose; the cooked gate is level.**
- Mechanism. The anchor is the lowest-index living ally. Every other body either adds `grp_w` x max(0, distance to
  the anchor - `grp_r`) to each group's walk, or values the anchor's claimed group at `grp_join` x itself.
- Gates: (a) before round 200, or on maps of 4,900 tiles or more; (b) cooked, comeback's cbdp gate (enemy 400+
  and 150+ ahead); (c) either.

  | Arm | Gate | Setting | Win % | Games | SPRT | Nearest ally, early / cooked (cand vs ref) | Comeback cand / ref |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | grp1 | a | w 0.5, r 5 | **46.1** | 1,764 | H0 | 5.20 / 6.24 vs 5.45 / 6.28 | |
  | grp2 | b | w 0.5, r 5 | 50.1 | 4,495 | H0 | 5.44 / 6.05 vs 5.44 / 6.13 | 16.2 / 16.5 |
  | grp3 | a or b | w 0.5, r 5 | **46.4** | 1,742 | H0 | | |
  | grpj1 | a | join 2 | 48.7 | 4,473 | H0 | 5.19 / 6.02 vs 5.37 / 5.89 | 16.0 / 18.3 |
  | grpj2 | b | join 2 | 50.1 | 3,491 | H0 | 5.40 / 6.06 vs 5.40 / 6.14 | 17.3 / 17.3 |
  | grpj2x | b | join 10 | 49.4 | 1,212 | H0 | 5.36 / 5.92 vs 5.35 / 5.96 | 17.2 / 17.6 |

  Screens ran at 2x, seeds 660002-660006 and 660010. Spacing is the mean Chebyshev distance to the nearest living
  ally, from snapshots every 20 rounds; "early" is rounds up to 200.
- Forensics.
  - A trace copy (20 maps) shows the gate firing on 98% of follower farm turns with a known anchor claim.
  - Spacing still moves by at most 0.25 tiles early, and by 0.1 while cooked. Followers keep their own groups (claims,
    crews and holds outweigh the lean); what changes is which camps they farm, and the farm loses for it.
  - With cbdp's pull on, the cooked pack is no tighter, and its comeback rate does not move.
- The earlier cohesion leans (EXPERIMENTS "Cohesion, four parallel attempts") lost the same way. A real pack would
  have to move bodies together, not reprice camps.
- Not a merge candidate. Knobs: `bl::grp_gate`, `grp_w`, `grp_r`, `grp_join`, `grp_early`, `grp_area`.
- A real-pack arm (movement coupling, cooked only) follows; its behaviour is verified before its A/B.

**4. Capture-reset loop fix (`oc-bl-crh`, `crb`, `crhb`, `crz`): level; the loop is rare locally.**
- Reach, in 512 oc-base10-like games (`hold_metrics`): 2,216 walked capture resets. 48 of 1,024 team-games have 10
  or more, 2 have 30 or more, none has 100 (the worst is 55). 03colosseum-a's 1,328 is a ladder outlier, and
  `fixm::finish_wait` already ends it. Seven games hold tight F/R loops; the other resets are real fights.
- One inconsistency was found and fixed in `cr_hold`. capture.cc's `holding_capture_now` keeps a hold by
  `winning_bag` (the full horizon, counting a long ally channel), while farm uses `gems_short(tribute_window)`.
- The arms:
  - `cr_hold`: the hold uses farm's test;
  - `cr_ban` 10: no re-claim of a group retreated from for 10 rounds;
  - `crhb`: both;
  - `cr_zone`: farm zoning always on.
- Results at 2x: crh 49.9% of 387, crb 50.3% of 3,095, crhb 49.7% of 600, crz 49.8% of 8,770, all H0 (seeds
  660007-660009, 660011). crz has +64% out-of-fuel turns (1,176 against 718).
- The ban leaves F/R alternation at about 1.3 a game. Those are retreats from a real threat and returns once it has
  gone, which is the right decision.
- Not a merge candidate. Knobs: `bl::cr_hold` (a consistency fix, harmless) and `bl::cr_ban`. Drop `cr_zone`.

**Method from here.** Rare gates make SPRT accept H0 early whatever the effect, so it is no evidence. Each arm
instead plays all 20,480 bl-dev games at 2x and is paired game by game against a mirror on the same maps; the effect

## Terrain windows (ocean, 2026-11-09; `bots/variants/oc-terrain`, not A/B'd; merged as CHANGES 474)

Exact savings in `model/safety.cc`, for any map (nothing precomputed per map):
- **`sight()`'s plain test:** "no bush or wall within win_r" is one bit lookup. The first turn after the draft dilates
  bushes and walls by win_r with host shifts (`make_near`). Doing it eagerly in round 1 added fuel to round 1.
- **`attack_viewers`' bush window** is kept per tile for the game. A tile next to a kept one in y shifts that window by
  a row and reads one new row.
- **`static_window`:** the same vertical slide (one row read in place of nine).

**Bench at 100M** (`--set wide`, opp oc-base29, against ocean):
- 52/52 byte-identical.
- Mean -4.3% (50,926 -> 48,728); p50 -3.6%, p90 -1.3%, p99 -0.1%.
- Round 1 is unchanged.
- Most of the saving is in cheap turns, so the heavy turns where budgets bite gain ~1k.

Tried and reverted: reading `Terrain::test` from an exported linear board in place of `sdk_Bitboard_Test`. It was +2.1%:
the raw host test (~16) costs less than our own bounds-checked bit read (~20 ops).

**Profile after** (fuelprof, 48 games):
- Flat: no line above 2.5%. Operators are 89% of the fuel, host calls 11%.
- Allocation is <0.1%, field reads 0.8% and `static_window` 1.2%.
- Our own record reads are 1.1% over 174 sites (campaign 16's cache of them was level).

At ~+0.17 points per 1k a turn (fuel ceiling, below), the expected gain is ~+0.4: under 20k games' noise.

**Follow-up tables on 474** (`variants/oc-tables2`, not merged; 52/52 identical in every arm):
- **Horizontal slide** (`variants/oc-tables-h`): each terrain board's 8x8 chunks are transposed once after the first
  turn (~15k ops), so a window column is two word reads. A 512-entry table spreads it into the window. -0.14%.
- **Near sight by table:** the 3x3 bush pattern indexes 512 compiled-in masks. Alone, with a bush test first, it adds
  only -0.05%. Without that test it costs +1.0%: most tiles are not bushes, and the old path returned after one bit
  read.
- Together -0.19% (~90 fuel a turn, ~+0.02 points). Compiled-in tables work, but nothing hot is left for them.

## Fuel ceiling (ocean, 2026-11-08; measurement, nothing merged)

Against oc-base25, own drafts, fast runner. Ceiling (mirror, ~20k games a stratum, weighted): 10M ~53.5%, 2x ~53.3%.
2x carries the whole ceiling (~+3.4). Panel 10M-1x pooled +1.67 ±0.78.

**Decomposition** on `maps/suites/merged/fuelceil-decomp` (5,120 ladder-v2 maps, 10,240 games each), paired by map
against fv-a. fv-a is ocean at a 100x quantum with every gate reading the 1x budget: no OOF, the same cuts, 50.70%.
"X free" refunds X's spending to every later `fuel()` read (`bots/variants/oc-fz-dev`: `fz_scope`, `fz_when`, `t1_mult`).

| Arm | Win % | Paired diff vs fv-a (95%) |
|---|---|---|
| 2x gates | 52.69 | +1.98 ±1.25 |
| world update free | 52.31 | +1.61 ±1.25 |
| world free, all turns but the first | 52.02 | +1.32 ±1.23 |
| world free, first turn only | 51.06 | +0.36 ±1.08 |
| farm free | 52.12 | +1.42 ±1.24 |
| farm free, all turns but the first | 51.85 | +1.14 ±1.24 |
| farm free, first turn only | 51.29 | +0.59 ±1.08 |
| prey / strike search / trade / step guard free | 51.70 / 51.65 / 51.46 / 51.41 | +1.00 / +0.95 / +0.75 / +0.70 (±1.1) |
| first turn's gates at 400k | 51.11 | +0.41 ±1.01 |

- No OOF, by construction: real-budget OOF is worth ~+0.7 on top (fv-a against real ocean).
- **The gain is general budget pressure in steady-state turns, not one subsystem and not the first turn.** The six
  subsystem gains overlap: they sum far past 2x's total.
- A free world update gives ~7.4k a turn (census p50 6.8k, p90 11.7k), before anything else runs, so every gate sees it.
  It is worth ~+1.3, about +0.17 a point per 1k a turn. The curve is concave: 2x (+100k) gives only +2.0.
- Earlier reserve rebalances (calm reserve hz40 / gf / cr60) stopped at <= level (LLR -2.00 / -1.15 / -0.16).

**Where the fuel goes** (new per-site profiler, `tools/fuel/fuelprof/`): 128 games of a `-g` copy of oc-base26
(code bytes identical but for 5 functions), exact wasmtime fuel per charge site, symbolised by line.
- The profile is flat. By file: safety.cc 22%, world.cc 17%, farm.cc 12%, util.h 11%, pathing.cc 10%.
- No world.cc line is above ~1%. Host reads of our own record, gems and the round come to ~2% together.
- The steady world update is ~7.4k a turn: champions 3.2k, camps 2.0k, update 0.7k, ranks 0.3k, tracking 0.3k.
- Caching our own record, gems and gold until an action (`oc-fx26`, which repeats campaign 16's `oc16-sc1`) gives
  -0.7% mean at 100M: 342 fuel a turn, against the ~2k the profile lines suggest.
  - A checking copy that compares every cached read with a fresh one found 0 mismatches over the 52 wide games.
  - 51/52 replays are byte-identical. The other differs because oc-base26's own choices read measured costs (e.g.
    `step_guard_costliest()` picking the route search): the checking copy, which returns fresh values, differs in 5/52.
    A uniform +1.8k a turn at the turn's start stays 2/2 identical.
  - Campaign 16's A/B of the same change was level (50.0% of 40,960). Not re-screened.

Verdict: the ceiling is real (+2 for gates, +0.7 for OOF), but it is spread thin across steady-state turns. Exact
speed-ups now come at ~0.3-0.7% a change. Matching a free world update would take ~20x that, so a fuel programme on
ocean has little left at 1x. Approximations or rebalances would have to take ~5k+ a turn from somewhere without
changing play, and the calm-reserve screens suggest no cheap one exists.

## Obese bags at a negative value, round 2 (ocean, 2026-11-06; level)

The user's refinement: a bag provably untributable by round 2000 is worth m x its gems with m < 0 (a burden to
inherit), not 0. Plus an optional penalty for the disabled body. Design, tables and replays: section 8 of
research/ladder-scrims-2026-11-06/fix-kill.md; scripts in `obese2-tools/`.
- Dev copy `bots/variants/oc-obese-dev` (oc-base10 + `params::obese::`, V0's port; a tribute already under way that
  ends in time now keeps a bag live). Knobs off: bench identical at 100M, 16/16 and 52/52.
- **Fires in 0.7% of ladder-like games** (144 of 20,480 at 2x on fresh 600100-600139). All of them are in the last
  rounds: first obese round median 1999, median largest bag 36.
- **SPRT can't screen it.** The arms play as the base until a bag goes obese, so maps score 0.5, the variance hits
  ab.py's floor and H0 "passes" at 200 games. They were run in full on the 300 late maps and paired with a base mirror.
- **m 0 / -0.1 / -0.25 / -0.5 give the same result game for game.** 50.5% of 600 late games at 2x; fired games
  50.7% against the mirror's 50.0%. At the real budget m0 and m -0.5 both read 48.5%, and that -1.5 is fuel noise
  from the debug census (73 of 97 flips are in unfired games). The m arms differ from m0 in 15 games and in no winner.
- m -0.25 + 50-gem penalty: 50.7%, 1 flip in its fired games.
- **Why:** each changed game was decided on tributed gems by 45+. A dead bag can't move that total, and the kill
  gold and kill counts it does move are tiebreaks after a tied score. A negative m only gives those away.
- Not run: held-out, `--mix varied`, panel, the race-tiered gate (no winner).
- Don't retry obese valuation at any m.

## Algorithm polyfills (ocean, 2026-11-06)

The user's idea: fushia's `algo/topk.h` (SIMD top-k and sort on packed integer keys) as a model for cheaper
algorithms and data structures in ocean. Profile, candidates and tables: research/ideas-2026-11-06/algo-polyfill.md;
files in `/home/ubuntu/tmp-offload/algo/`.
- **Nothing to replace.** On the decision path (turn-end queue off, 38.8k a turn), sorts are ~5 fuel a turn, malloc
  and free 74, bulk memset/memcpy ~0, memcmp and `vector::assign` ~60; there are no heaps or maps outside the draft.
  powf is the largest library item, 422 a turn (1.1%). The rest is flat bespoke code, already in host calls, SIMD
  and memos (the farm loop's branch and bound is the biggest block, 19%).

  it on hides a saving (a cheaper warmed item warms more tiles). Copies of both bots with the queue off
  (`mknoq.sh`) give the decision path's fuel.

  fuel -0.27 to -0.40%. **oc-algo-2** adds memos of `attack_viewers` per (tile, range) and of bush tiles' near sight:
  identical 246/246, ~0 more saved (the warm-up already caches viewer rows) and a dearer warm-up; dropped.

## Turn-end feint fixes, feintfix (astraeus, 2026-11-06)

`variants/astraeus-feintfix` against `variants/astraeus-9e1fad3` (astraeus at 9e1fad36), both on their own drafts.
**Level: 49.5% of 20480 games (95% CI 48.9-50.2) on `merged/ff-745`. OOF turns CAND 94661 in 12428 games, REF 94870
in 12464. Not shipped yet.** Self-play over-weights fixes 2-3: only our own bots feint, so they mostly change how we
read our own copy (Lessons); on the ladder fix 3 is held back by the feint detector below.

*The changes* (each a skew from the feint CHANGES 439 made universal):
- Basic attacks counted (`count_use`, bot.cc): `could_attack` was read at act()'s start, while the feint's channel
  cleared the bit, and the count ran after `start_recall`, which clears it again (a phantom attack). Now
  `turn_acts.could_attack` is read in decide() once the tribute/recall branches settle, and the count runs before
  the feint. `use.attacks` (main_stat, emblem/shard choice) is now several times larger than before.
- Camp wakers (`find_wakers`, plan.cc): an enemy counted as held in place if it had acted or showed any channel, so
  an unacted enemy's feint, or a recall/teleport completing at its turn start this round, priced woken hits on us at
  0. New `held_this_round` (world.h): acted, stun pending, or a tribute/teleport/kept recall ending after this round.
- Unseen-enemy heal (world.cc): any last-seen recall healed the enemy and reset its scale at `channel_end_round`.
  `recall_kept` is now computed for enemies too, and the heal needs it once `enemy_feints_` is set (an enemy seen
  after its turn restarting a recall in two consecutive rounds, unhurt); the spawn union stays unconditional.
- The lost round (`recall_to_bank`, bank.cc): it needed last turn's `memory.banking`, so a bag new this turn cancelled
  the feint and restarted the recall a round later. It also takes a new bag that carry_bag is sure to bank
  (`banks_bag && (closing || !may_chain)`). The farm half (`recall_farm`, set by the farm loop) is left: repricing
  every gemless feint runs the farm loop (~9% of fuel) twice a turn. Home, shop and siege keeps already read this turn.

*Audit* (one read-only reviewer): no correctness bugs. Taken: the ladder regression of a gated heal (a non-feinting
enemy's real recall seen only at its start no longer healed), fixed by the per-team `enemy_feints_` detector;
`stun_pending` added to `held_this_round`; a stale comment in capture.cc. Left, pre-existing: our own hits do not
clear an enemy's recall in the belief (only stuns do); an unacted enemy on a kept recall or tribute may still cancel;
the new-bag keep has no `recall_outruns` check when not wanting home, as the old banking path had none.

*Fixes 2-4 alone* (`bots/variants/astraeus-ff24` = feintfix with bot.cc and util.h of the base, so no attack
count change) on `merged/ff24-746` (fresh-746001..746040, unused): 49.9% of 20,480 (49.2-50.5), out-of-fuel turns
96,517 against 94,402. Level; with fix 1 49.5% on other maps, within noise of it. Fixes 2-4 shipped (CHANGES 440);
fix 1 held with the camp models for a retune.

## Area hits and stuns in the camp-clear estimate, areaclear (astraeus, 2026-11-06)

`variants/astraeus-areaclear` against `variants/astraeus-0305953` (today's astraeus), both on their own drafts.
**Lost: 48.3% of 20480 games (95% CI 47.6-48.9) on `merged/ac-743`. Not shipped.**

*The error, re-measured.* A trace copy printed predicted and actual rounds and damage for solo clears of fresh groups
(maps/gen, 512 games, own drafts). Actual over predicted:
- Prism: rounds 0.75, damage 0.69. Single-member groups are 0.81 rounds, because spells are front-loaded.
- Varg on multi-member groups: rounds 0.67.
- Heart of Ruin: rounds 0.94, shielded damage 0.78.
- Stunners on single-member groups (Marcella, Ryth, Ren, Tavi): damage 0.74-0.82.
- Non-stunners (Vesper, Vendetta): about 0.96-1.0.

So the estimate overcounts area clearers' and stunners' clear time and damage.

*The change*, derived from cambc-rules.yaml with no tuned constants:
- `camp_kit` records per champion:
  - the round rate of each area footprint: ground casts, Heart of Ruin's landing, Varg's splash;
  - its stuns by kind: unit, bare (Cassi, only at Strength >= cast_cost as `camp_cast` casts it), ground, landing. Marcella's reset-stun isn't counted, because it re-attacks the weakest member.
- `warm_covers` measures each group's best cover per footprint in the turn-end queue. Until every group is measured, the estimate is unchanged.
- `group_output` adds each footprint's rate times the mean extra live members it hits.
- `min_camp_damage`:
  - kills each target at the single-target part, while the area part wears down the members still waiting;
  - takes off what the kit's stuns skip: one stun per kind per cooldown of fire rounds, at most each cast round's fire.
- Call sites, all on this one model:
  - `min_camp_damage` and its overloads, `finishing_camp`, `warm_clears`;
  - `plan_crew` and the joint and partner pricing;
  - farm's `affordable`, `struggling`, `fastest` and the prune bounds (scalar and SIMD lanes, per group);
  - `siege_ready`, through `stunned_fire`;
  - `kite_plan`;
  - home trips and spare-health checks;
  - `recovered_for_work` (Willow and heal planning).
- Left on raw output on purpose: shop's emblem pricing, capture's shard choice, draft valuations.

*Audit* (one read-only reviewer). Fixed before the A/B:
- the area was counted as single-target speed, which made damage optimistic (front-loading);
- stale farm `FarmClearing` and `kite_plan` caches when covers become ready;
- stuns credited past one round's fire (stuns don't stack);
- Marcella's credit;
- siege's striker count against `siege_load`'s, and `top` above `fire - tanked`;
- per-member stun skips recomputed on every uncached call (now precomputed with the sort).

Left as is:
- covers are a static best case, ignoring `camp_cast`'s stand and landing constraints;
- every stun slot is taken as ready when the clear starts;
- Varg's targeting doesn't seek its cover on 0-Strength clusters;
- the reflect path's stun rounds;
- looser-than-needed prune bounds.

*Fuel*: out-of-fuel turns rose to 115341 in 13491 games for the candidate, against 93255 in 12498 for the reference (+24%). Most came in decide (86.5k vs 70.1k), led by `mut-the-pack` maps. This is mostly behavioural: the candidate now farms the big pack (on 02the-pack, 234 out-of-fuel turns against 40). The estimate's own cost is small.

*Result by family:* the loss is broad, not one map type. Candidate win rates are 48.0% on gen-ladder (8960 games) and
48.8% on gen-classic (2400).

*Read:* a more accurate estimate makes the farm take clears, such as packs, that the old pessimism kept it out of.
Fixing the estimate alone doesn't pay. A follow-up would have to change what the estimate is used for; making it
more accurate isn't enough.

## SPSA retune round oc5, and the map-conditioned constants diagnostic (ocean, 2026-11-06)

`replays/tune/oc5` on `bots/ocean_tune5`, the tunified `variants/oc-iw8-clean` (CHANGES 429). **Level: not kept.**

*The set*, 26 constants (18 floats, 8 ints):
- oc4's 23 less 414's `funnel_wealth` and `funnel_power`, which CHANGES 420 removed;
- 421's `reveal_mass` and `reveal_prior`;
- three new knobs, at values that change nothing:
  - `lock_stage_steps` 8: the timed lock's nearest waiting distance (fight.cc `lock_plan_wait`);
  - `deny_gems` 100: `channel_to_deny`'s least bag;
  - `efficiency_power` 1: `relative_efficiency` raised to it, for both 419's holders and 420's funnel, the analogue
    of oc4's `funnel_power`.
- Ranges run from half to double the current values, with `efficiency_power` [0, 2.5] and `lock_stage_steps` [3, 14].
- At its current values the copy replays identically to oc-iw8-clean at 100M: 16/16 default, 52/52 wide with test
  drafts, and 80/80 on 40 ladder maps plus 03homonoliths-a, 00quarry and 04plaza. Fuel is +0.06-0.09%.

*The run* used oc4's settings:
- opponents oc-iw8-clean twice, `variants/astraeus-now-1106` and panel-proteus;
- pool: the ladder at weight 8, plus fresh-546000..546019;
- 64 maps and 4 sign pairs an iteration;
- weights win 0.75 and gems 0.25; a 0.25, A 100, c 0.12; real fuel;
- per-game `games.jsonl` logging on.

It ran 11:45-16:45 UTC: 939 iterations, 1.92M games. The mean candidate win rate rose from 53.8% (iterations 1-100) to
54.7% (501-600), then stayed flat at 54.3-54.4% to the end. Moves (current value -> final):
- `efficiency_power` 1 -> 1.465
- `hurt_retreat_ratio` 3.96 -> 3.34
- `reveal_prior` 2 -> 1.65
- `pair_hold_share` .494 -> .550
- `fight_weight` .611 -> .688
- `shop_gain_scale` .822 -> .751
- `home_retreat_ratio` 2.36 -> 2.17
- `deny_gems` 100 -> 112
- `heal_trip_fraction` .495 -> .536
- `chip_value` .223 -> .247
- `pick_up_radius` 6 -> 7, `threat_radius` 7 -> 8, `tribute_window` 10 -> 11
- the rest within 6%: `lock_stage_steps`, `chain_bag_limit`, `brake_bag` and `track_horizon` are unchanged.

*Port* (`research/ideas-2026-11-05/oc5-tools/port.py`):
- Every value is an exact float32 `constexpr`, and safety.h's static_assert is restored.
- The diff to oc-iw8-clean (params.h, fight.cc, capture.cc) was applied to `variants/oc-base9` as
  `bots/variants/oc-tuned5` (the version that would ship) and to `variants/oc-base8` as `bots/variants/oc-tuned5-b8`.
- On oc-iw8-clean the port replays identically to `tune.py apply`'s bot (2/2 on 00gemfight, where oc-tuned5-b8 does
  not).
- oc-tuned5-b8 replays identically to the applied bot on 147 of 148 bench games at 100M. The exception is 00gemfight
  side b, where the two diverge at round 430: champion 8 walks in one and dashes in the other.
  - With these constants patched in, `oc-fuel8` and `oc-base7` (fuel9) replay identically, but `oc-base8` does not.
  - So CHANGES 436 (fuel round 10, astraeus 435's safety.cc savings) is not exact in a state these constants
    reach. It was exact on the default-constant benches.
  - No bisection over subsets of the constants reproduces it: it needs the full set.
  - Cause, found by bisecting the code between oc-base7 and oc-base8 with these constants:
    - The safety.cc hunks other than simulate()/decided() are clean. The simulate() rework is clean in each of its
      three pieces alone, but not all together.
    - Turning off main.cc's tile-warming pass, or `Pathing::route`'s `cheap_guard` switch (`step_guard_costliest()
      >= 15000`), makes the pair identical.
    - So the rework is semantically exact, but it shifts fuel. The warming pass spends the leftover as if the budget
      were real even at 100M, so the shift changes how far the caches are warmed. That changes the step guard's
      measured cost, which flips the switch. This is the same mechanism as 435's td game.
    - No exact fix in 436 exists: a deterministic stand-in for the measured cost would be a behaviour change. Notes
      added under CHANGES 435 and 436.

*Held-out A/Bs*, own drafts, fast runner, real fuel:

| A/B | games | win % (95% CI) | OOF cand / ref |
|---|---|---|---|
| oc-tuned5 vs oc-base9, `oc5-confirm` (546100-546139) | 20,480 | **50.3 (49.6-51.0)** | 124.2k / 119.1k (+4.3%) |

Panel (panel-check-514510; oc-base9's rates measured alongside; logs in `replays/ab/oc5-pchk-*`, `oc5-p2-*`):

| Member | oc-tuned5 | oc-base9 | Diff |
|---|---|---|---|
| astraeus-now-1106 | 58.8 | 57.0 | +1.8 |
| panel-proteus | 67.9 | 66.1 | +1.8 |
| panel-demeter | 69.8 | 68.9 | +0.9 |
| panel-ocean-td | 83.8 | 83.7 | +0.1 |
| baselines/v67 | 80.0 | 80.1 | -0.1 |
| astraeus-now-1106, `oc5-panel2` (546300-546309) | 58.4 | 57.2 | +1.2 |
| panel-proteus, `oc5-panel2` | 66.1 | 68.3 | -2.2 |

- The panel mean is +0.9, with no member down on panel-check.
- Pooled over 10,240 games, astraeus is +1.5 and proteus -0.2.
- Head to head the retune is level on both bases (50.25% of 40,960 pooled), and out-of-fuel turns rise 4-6%: it
  fails the keep bar. After oc4 the constants sit at a plateau: the tune's own gain (+0.6 over its four slots) does
  not survive head to head. It may be the draft6 draft (oc-base9) or no real gain at all; the oc-base8 copy, under the
  draft the tune ran on, is level as well. The panel's +0.9 alone does not justify a ship.

**Map-conditioned diagnostic** (mapcond.md Stage 1, run on oc5's games.jsonl; `oc5-tools/feats.py`, `het.py`,
`ab_het.py`).
- *Model.* Per constant i, each pair's per-game difference d times the pair's sign Δ_i is regressed on 2 c_i [4 epoch
  dummies, z]. z holds 12 standardised draft-time features: log area, picks, rotational and vertical symmetry, spawn
  distance, camp density, log gems and log gold a side, big_share, contested share, altars and bushes.
- *Errors.* SEs are clustered by map (5,247 maps, 961,536 paired games), and the null permutes z across maps 1,000
  times.
- *Power.* SE(W) is about 0.010-0.017 per SD, as mapcond.md predicted: 10 times tighter than the iteration-level fits.

| Stage 1 test | result | bar | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| omnibus Σt² over 312 pairs | 396 (null mean 320, 95% 376, 99% 402; perm p 0.014) | beyond the 99th | fails, narrowly |
| pairs beyond Bonferroni (\|t\| > 3.77) | none; largest `gold_price_scale` x altars t -3.7 (halves -2.4 / -3.6), then `recall_health_fraction` x spawn_dist -2.9, `brake_bag` x spawn_dist +3.0 | 1+, same sign in both halves | fails, narrowly |
| debiased prize W'ΣW · 0.6/(2h), h 0.19 | +3.0 ± 1.0 points (permutation null mean +0.07, 99% +1.26; p < 0.001) | ≥ 1 point | passes on the model |

- *Where the prize lies.* Two constants carry almost all of it, each with a per-constant Wald permutation p < 0.001
  over 12 features, which survives a Bonferroni correction over 26 constants:
  - `recall_health_fraction` (+1.9 ± 0.5): the gradient falls with spawn distance, log gems and log area, so the
    recall threshold should be lower on big, long and rich maps;
  - `gold_price_scale` (+0.8 ± 0.45): lower on maps with many altars, higher on big_share and vertical maps.
  - `chain_bag_limit` (p 0.01) and `brake_bag` (p 0.02) are weaker. The other constants show nothing.
- *The prize is an upper bound.* It takes oc2's isotropic curvature (h 0.19 per scaled unit²). At that h the optimal
  shift of `recall_health_fraction` is about 0.23 a feature SD, against a current value of 0.315. That is outside
  any local quadratic, so the true curvature is surely higher and the gain smaller. A realistic estimate is ≤1-2
  points for the two constants together, unproven.
- *No held-out confirmation.* The held-out A/Bs' per-map outcomes are uncorrelated with the SPSA fit's predicted
  map-dependent gain for the move actually shipped (slope -0.24 ± 0.27 on b8, -0.09 ± 0.27 on b9, against about
  +0.6 if right). That test has little power, since the tuned move barely shifted the two constants.
  - The per-map Wald tests read p 0.05 (b8; `bushes` +1.1 points a SD, t 3.1), 0.29 (b9) and 0.32 (varied): no
    stable profile.
- *Verdict.* A real but small gradient heterogeneity, limited to two constants. A full contextual SPSA is not
  warranted. The one test worth running is a narrow Stage 2: condition only `recall_health_fraction` (on spawn
  distance, log area and log gems) and `gold_price_scale` (on altars and big_share), as θ0 + B z with B trained by
  SPSA from B = 0 and a ridge, then a 40,960-game held-out A/B. Expect at most 1-2 points.

*The narrow test (`bots/variants/oc-mapcond2`, 2026-11-06): lost nothing, gained nothing.*
- *Change:* oc-base9 with `recall_health_fraction` and `gold_price_scale` made per-map variables. Each is the fitted
  linear function of its three most significant features (recall: spawn_dist, log gems, log area; gold price: altars,
  big_share, vertical symmetry), z-scored with the fit's means and SDs. The shift is W·z / 0.19 in the tune's [0, 1]
  scale, shrunk by `params::mapcond_shrink` and clamped to oc5's ranges.
  - Arms: half shrink (`oc-mapcond2`) and a quarter (`oc-mapcond2-q`). At half, recall spreads 0.15-0.50 (SD 0.11,
    12% clamped) on the ladder; gold price spreads 0.73-2.13 (SD 0.39).
- *Where it is measured:* on each champion's first play turn, from the StaticMap. Each champion is its own instance,
  so values set by the draft never reach play: a first build did that and played the base values.
  - spawn_dist comes from one distance field with the camps blocked, else one without them; gems and big_share come
    from every camp halved, by the symmetry. It costs 8k fuel at the median and 44k at most.
  - It matched features.json (mapgen metrics) exactly on 192 of 200 maps: the 128 ladder maps and 72 from 546100,
    546200 and 546300. The other 8 are maps joined only by dash or crystal (archipelago, atoll, topo-split, all
    from the varied mix), which keep the base values.
- *Screen at 2x fuel* (`--fuel 200000`), `merged/mc2-screen` (546400-546439, fresh, ladder mix), own drafts,
  fast runner, no SPRT:

| A/B | games | win % (95% CI) | OOF cand / ref |
|---|---|---|---|
| oc-mapcond2 (half) vs oc-base9 | 20,480 | 50.0 (49.3-50.7) | 1,052 / 898 |
| oc-mapcond2-q (quarter) vs oc-base9 | 20,480 | 50.3 (49.6-51.0) | 1,022 / 979 |

- *Against the fit's prediction:* the fit's quadratic (h 0.19) predicts +1.7 points (half) and +1.1 (quarter) on
  these maps. The A/Bs observed -0.0 ± 0.34 and +0.3 ± 0.34, which excludes the half arm's prediction.
  - Per map, the observed result tracks a quarter of the prediction: the slope is 0.26 ± 0.23 (half) and
    0.26 ± 0.28 (quarter).
  - On the top decile of predicted gain (+5.2 / +3.9 points predicted), they observed +1.1 ± 1.1 and +0.8 ± 1.1.
  - So the SPSA interaction slopes overstate the gain about fourfold. This is consistent with a higher curvature
    than h 0.19 (as suspected above) plus selection of the largest slopes.
- *Not shipped.* Neither arm won at 2x, so the real-budget held-out, varied and panel runs were not played. The
  map-conditioned constants line is closed for these two constants; the rest showed less.

## Camp damage by the nearest-champion rule, retried (astraeus, 2026-11-06)

Base astraeus 0305953 (frozen `variants/astraeus-0305953`); candidate `variants/astraeus-campdmg2`, a re-implementation of
the held `merge/funnel` 6b0fe83 idea (TODO "Held branches") with one model everywhere: `model/camp_target.h`.

- **The model** (rules camps.attack, rounds.sequence): per monster, the nearest champion of either team in its reach
  takes the hit in phase R = round + 1. Next phase (`camp_pick_reach`): a rival shields the asked champion only if
  present then (`camp_present`: no recall/teleport completing at its turn start this round) and, for an enemy, held
  (`camp_held`: acted this round, pending stun, respawn turn, teleport; a recall or tribute can be cancelled), for an
  ally held or claiming the group. Ties go to a rival only if it surely acts first: an enemy at the latest slot its
  team could give it (`camp_slot`; settled = acted and read this round), allies by `World::slot`. Past the next phase
  (`CampSide::allies`): only claimers not leaving. A crew clear (`share_damage`): each member stands at its attack range
  (`camp_stand`); the nearest stand water-fills the hits down to the tank line, the rest levels over the whole crew
  (replaces the x1.5 melee weight). Solo, every member reaching our stand hits us (unchanged).
- **Call sites moved onto it:** `Safety::find_members` (so `camp_damage`, `tie_hit`, home boards, turn order; others
  stand only if rival-counting, ties by `camp_slot`) and a cached `Safety::camp_rivals()`; `threats_near`,
  `ally_camp_fire`, the shield trigger in `dash_to_attack` (now `camp_damage > 0`); `find_wakers`/`wake`; `camp_cast`'s
  stun value; `siege_ready` (no enemy tank), siege cover and `tanked`, `kite_productive_action` covers; home
  `sleeping_fire`; `mono_trapped`; `share_damage`, `crew_tank`, new `crew_part`; farm's passing `affordable` with an
  ally engaged (our `crew_part` beside committed claimers, was free), kited joins (`plan_crew`, was output share) and
  the kited unclaimed partner (`crew_part`). Left as solo worst-case readings: breach, finishing_camp, bank tribute
  fire and ring fire, Willow's exposure_at, landing threats, `struggling`, `recovered_for_work`.
- **Audit** (read-only, one round), fixed: multi-phase readings counted an ally that had merely acted (now claimers
  only); `engaged_part` counted recalling/tributing allies; `find_wakers` lost the ally-harm bans for uncommitted
  allies (kept as a second nearest); the stun value counted uncommitted allies as exposed; `Safety::camp_rivals()`'s
  self entry went stale after a step; the shield trigger ignored the model; zero-fills in `share_damage`. Kept:
  kited crews priced at attack-range stands (kiters cast from stations); `struggling`/`recovered_for_work` solo.
- **Result** on `merged/cd2-742` (fresh-742001..742040, unused), both on own drafts, fast runner: 50.4% of 20,480
  (49.7-51.1), out-of-fuel turns 100,043 (12,727 games) against REF's 93,730 (12,475), +6.7%. Level; not shipped.
- **Confirm** on `merged/cd2-744` (fresh-744001..744160, unused; 40,960 maps): 50.0% of 81,920 (49.7-50.4),
  out-of-fuel turns 395,076 (50,856 games) against 373,463 (49,915), +5.8%. Level: no measurable effect on win rate.

## The goal field off spawn, retried (astraeus, 2026-11-06)

A retry of "The goal after the strike search" part (1) on today's astraeus (`bots/variants/astraeus-gf2` against
`variants/astraeus-0305953` = 0305953, own drafts). The bug was still live. The strike search reads the walk to the
farm group (`goal_field`) only when ready. `walk_target` counted start_recall's turn-end recall as a channel, so off
spawn neither act()'s turn-start `approach` nor `prepare_next_turn`'s ran. On the ladder (256 games, a `GFPROBE`
debug line in goal_field), 3322 of 9264 reads (35.9%) found no field, all of them off spawn.
- **Changed:**
  - **The feint.** `recall_feint` is set when start_recall's recall starts and cleared when continue_recall keeps it.
    `channel_held()` (bank.cc) is `channelling()` but for the feint. `walk_target` (now farm.cc, by group) and the
    self branch of capture's `held_back` read it, the latter as its comment already said.
  - **Engine guards unchanged.** Wards, locks, start_recall and `strike_after` keep `channelling()`: a channel refuses
    those actions, feint included.
  - **Turn-start approach.** act()'s still skips every channel. On a feint turn, `goal_field` searches when it reads
    the field (`prepare_approach`, floor `act_reserve + 30000`).
  - **Turn end.** `prepare_next_turn` searches on feint turns too, but not when farm means to keep the recall
    (`recall_farm`).
  - **Goal gain.** It is `max(0, steps here - steps there)`, the past audit's fix. `same_labels` was already in.
- **Auditor** (read-only): no real bugs. Fixed: `held_back`; the turn end's search while a farm recall is planned;
  walk_target tests the group before the host call. Left:
  - siege turns' turn-end search, often unread;
  - the turn-end search now running ahead of the warm-ups;
  - act()'s two state reads;
  - a flag left `true` after an out-of-fuel resumption that never reaches continue_recall (fuel only).
- **Firing counts** (ladder, 256 games, before the auditor's fixes): reads without a field went 35.9% -> 6.7%
  (616 of 9165). 753 searches ran in goal_field; the turn end made the rest ready.

| | CAND win % | Games | 95% CI | OOF CAND | OOF REF |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `merged/gf2-741` (fresh 741001-741040) | 50.1 | 20480 | 49.5-50.8 | 90295 | 92095 |

Level, with out-of-fuel turns 2% fewer (`replays/ab/gf2/`). The fix costs no out-of-fuel turns this time, unlike
the 2026-10-28 attempt (47.3-47.6%), but the field in nearly every search gains nothing measurable, as it did at
100M then. Shipped as the rules' reading of our own recall (CHANGES 439).

every knob off).

  back to the real budget): oc-tuned4 at 10M 53.6%; the gate view (gates cut as at the real budget, no out-of-fuel)
  51.6%, so OOF turns are worth ~1.6 and gate cuts ~2.0. **25% more budget for the gates recovers all of the cut
  prize** (b125 53.6, b150 53.7). By family freed: the farm group loop +1.4 (non-banking +1.2), prey +0.8, step
  guard +0.7; the strike search, turn order, the stand and the queue ~0.
- **Re-allocating the same budget is level.** No rebalance, reserve or amortisation won: prey's reserve and check
  order (50.1, 50.1), the step guard's entry reserve 12k / 30k (49.9, 48.8), an anytime strike search floor (50.1,
  OOF -8%; with a grow floor 41.3), the farm loop's walk reserve 80% / 130% (49.9, 49.2), farm_turn's struck branch
  below 20k / 30k (49.7, 49.7), the turn-end queue continuing a cut loop (49.0: 9% of its runs find a better group),
  a stale-value prune of groups recently far below the best (49.0-49.9), a light loop that keeps a steady choice
  (48.3, 49.3), and combinations (c1 49.3, c2 50.0, 20,480 each).
- **The banking loop's walk reserve at 60% (r1) is the only positive, and it is level:** 50.3 (dev, 20,480), 50.4
  (confirm 533100-533139, 20,480), 49.9 on `--mix varied` (533200-533209, 5,120); panel against oc-retest-clean's own
  rates: astraeus-now-1106 52.6 (53.1), proteus 64.0 (63.3), demeter 66.7 (66.0), ocean-td 81.9 (82.1), v67 77.9
  (77.2), mean +0.3. 40% lost (48.3), 60% with the non-banking loop at 90% 50.3.
- **A low-fuel watchdog loses.** Throwing out of the decision below 8k / 12k left (strike search, farm loop, fight
  sims, route searches) and playing a cheap fallback (hit in range, else step toward last turn's farm group) cut OOF
  turns 23% and read 49.3 / 48.5: a turn that runs out keeps its plan's first actions, which beat a generic fallback.
- So the cut prize is in cheaper work, not in moving fuel between subsystems: making the cut-prone work (the farm
  loop, prey, the step guard) ~20% cheaper is worth up to ~2 points.

## Pre-loop scopes on the final candidate: altar access without floods, a box round each unseen enemy (2026-11-05, astraeus 28cc1105)

Branch `worktree-agent-acc27a63a46e6663a`, from 28cc1105. Three exact, fuel-only commits: 311d1ec7, c74930d8 and
b0e437ab. The final candidate is frozen there as `bots/variants/astraeus-b0e437a`; the reference is
`variants/astraeus-final` (28cc1105).

**Method.** The cut-turn anatomy's trace was re-applied to 28cc1105 by line content. It gives exclusive fuel per
scope, sub-scopes for World::track, the altar-access rebuild, Safety's foe/strike and the unseen queries, and
any_within calls and fuel by calling scope. The A and K lines give each rebuild's path and fuel, and each track
growth's shape and fuel. Self-play on fresh-192561 and fresh-192581 (1,024 games). Statistics are over farm loops
that are not banking and not in the opening.

**Breakdown before (28cc1105) and after (b0e437ab).** Mean fuel per cut and uncut farm turn. The two runs are
different self-play games: the cut turns that remain are the dearer ones.

| scope | cut before | cut after | uncut before | uncut after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pre-loop spend | 43.9k | 42.9k | 22.4k | 22.0k |
| chase (16k when an enemy is seen; 11.7k on <12-group maps) | 5.5k | 5.9k | 0.54k | 0.54k |
| x_track (World::track's growth) | 3.2k | 3.2k | 0.68k | 0.72k |
| x_rebuild (altar access) | 2.8k | 1.8k | 0.79k | 0.36k |
| w_camps | 2.6k | 2.6k | 1.8k | 1.9k |
| x_within (any_within itself) | 2.0k | 0.69k | 0.33k | 0.17k |
| any_within calls | 6.8 | 2.7 | 1.5 | 0.8 |
| x_strike (threat_strike) | 1.6k | 1.5k | 0.34k | 0.34k |

65% of cut turns see no enemy. On those turns the excess over uncut turns was x_track +3.2k, x_within +2.1k,
x_rebuild +1.7k and x_strike +1.3k.

**1. Altar access rebuilds without a flood from spawn (311d1ec7, c74930d8).**
- Before, every change to `live_flips` ran either an incremental update (~3.5k) or a flood from spawn. The flood
  costs one whole-board step per BFS layer: 17.9k on 100x100, 8.5k on 80x80.
- Deaths only grow the walk. When no tribute tile flipped (`plain`), the open tiles stand, so the walk is caught up
  only when read (`behind`, `catch_up_walk`). That path costs ~830 on cut turns.
- Returns are dropped from the walk when the walkable tiles round them are connected among themselves
  (`round_returns`), with or without deaths, at ~3.0k.
- Rebuild paths on cut turns after c74930d8 (fresh-192561):

  | path | rebuilds | fuel each | share of rebuild fuel |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | returns whose ring is disconnected even on our walk: flood | 1,864 | 25.2k | 38% |
  | returns with deaths, ring disconnected: flood | 1,772 | 12.6k | 18% |
  | quick returns | 4,450 | 3.1k | 11% |
  | quick deaths | 14,204 | 0.8k | 10% |

**Tried on the remaining floods, no cheaper (not committed).**
- Deaths first, then the ring test on our walk. Exact, but -0.60% against c74930d8's -0.62%: catching up deferred
  deaths costs 4.1k a time.
- A reach capped at the ring's size + 12 over our walk less the returns. It decides 99.2% of these cases, and its
  go-around is 17 layers at the median, 60+ at the tail. It costs 1.8k, the catch-up before it 4.1k and the ring
  test 1.4k, so the path still costs 15-17k against the flood's 25k. Total fuel -0.01%.
- `distance_field::compute_to` stops only once every destination is reached (a one-off probe: two destinations
  searched the whole walk, the near one alone 36 tiles). A field flood costs more than `reachable_tiles_into`'s:
  20.1k against 17.9k on 100x100.

**2. A box round each unseen enemy (b0e437ab).**
- `ChampionBelief::possible_box` holds every tile of `possible`. World's writers widen it: walks by `turns`, a dash
  by `dash_range` more (`undashed` lies within `possible`), spawns and teleports are added, fixes reset it, and
  lineage copies copy it. Pruning by vision leaves it.
- `possible_within` and `possible_count_within` answer any_within and count_within on `possible` with no board
  calls when the tile is beyond the box plus r. Unseen enemies are tracked at most 9 rounds, so the box stays
  within ±27 of the fix.
- Box pre-checks before the combat listings (`area_targets`, `add_unseen`, the unseen-Ren skips) and the
  approach-field reads gave +0.00% (more turns dearer than cheaper) and were dropped.

**Exactness and fuel at 100M** (bench.py against `variants/astraeus-final`: default 16, wide 52, fresh-192300 every
4th map 128 games):

| commit | identical replays | total fuel default / wide / fresh | p99 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 311d1ec7 | all | -0.42 / -0.41 / -0.47% | |
| c74930d8 | all | -0.62 / -0.58 / -0.68% | |
| b0e437ab | all | -1.04 / -1.00 / -1.18% | -2.1 / -1.3 / -2.2% |

**A/B, real budget, own drafts.** 40 suites, 20,480 games a row, fast runner.

| candidate | ref | suites (fresh-) | win % (CI) | OOF cand / ref | farm-partial-evaluation cand / ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c74930d8 | final | 192561..600 | 51.0 (50.3-51.7) | 190,277 / 195,545 | 2.747M / 2.935M |
| b0e437ab | final | 192561..600 | 50.0 (49.3-50.7) | 172,540 / 195,880 | 2.662M / 2.936M |

- Paired on the same games against final, c74930d8 and b0e437ab differ in 69% of them. Of the 6,275 games whose
  result flips, 3,240 go to c74930d8 and 3,035 to b0e437ab.

  divergence noise between two exact bots.

**Left as is.**
- World::track's dash growth, 60% of its fuel. It is a distance field of 3 steps over walls, ~3.2k on 100x100,
  most of that the field's fixed cost. Shift dilations cost more (~1.6k a step), and a reach per tile pays only up
  to 6 tiles.
- threat_strike is memoized per champion and round; it costs more on cut turns only because more enemies are asked
  about.
- chase's fuel is prey() and pathing's step_towards.
- update_camps already settles groups without reading their members.

the ref. Shown: replays identical to the ref's, and total play fuel from round 2 against the ref's. The real budget
gives farm-partial-evaluation cuts (fpe) on `wide` and fresh, one side; at 52-104 games these are noisy. Steps are
cumulative, and s3 and s5 are each measured on top of s4.
