## The farm walk's route search and travel plan, per call; the dash class's reserve refit (2026-11-05, astraeus 28cc1105)

Branch `worktree-agent-ab4ebc4c0ecb8a725`, on the final candidate 28cc1105. Tools are in `research/walkfuel-2026-11-05/`
(written to run from `wfscratch/`):
- `winst.py` patches a copy with `WLK` lines: scopes, searches, kept-route tests and finer marks;
- `wan.py`, `wtail.py`, `wpart.py` and `wpair.py` read them;
- `exact.sh` and `cmp.sh` are the 100M benches;
- `paired.sh` and `rsvmeas.sh` run the instrumented copies;
- `xcls.py` and `refit.py` do the reserve refit;
- `metrics.sh` and `table.py` do the A/B tables.

**Profile** (instrumented, 64 fresh-192300 maps × 2 sides, 360k walks). At the real budget the cut non-banking walk is
8.8k mean, 31k p99. Its shares:
- the host search 28.5%;
- `step_guard` 12.5%;
- the travel plan 12%;
- `pull` 9.7%;
- the route's first-step scan 6%;
- descend and closer 8%;
- `ahead` 4.5%;
- `kept_steps` 2.8%.

The pieces that cannot be cut, or are not worth cutting:
- **Host search.** Its cost is chunks × (16 + layers) + 30, to within 1.00-1.04 (p10-p90), so only fewer searches
  cut it.
- **Kept-route misses.** Different goals miss with a median of 23 tiles apart, and a multi-slot cache would hit
  1-2.6% of those. Misses on more than 4 wall changes would pass an all-tile test 16-24% of the time: ~100 a walk.
- **Failed searches** are 2% of walk fuel.
- **Field reads.** `steps_at` costs the same as a direct buffer read (~32-46).

**Per call at 100M, paired walks** (`wpair.py`, base and candidate games identical):

| part | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| walk, mean / p90 / p99 | 6.50k / 12.67k / 23.11k | 6.36k / 12.04k / 21.53k |
| per turn, p99 | 25.70k | 24.34k |
| travel (0.36 a walk) | 3,510 | 3,127 |
| plan | 1,816 | 1,427 |
| plan's boards (shut, no-pass, vetoed) | 2,859 | 1,769 |
| plan's ends loop | 4,491 | 3,382 |
| plan's dash_from | 903 | 692 |
| route, search, kept_steps, pull, ahead | unchanged | unchanged |

**What changed (2107c44d, exact, fuel only).**
- The plan's 7×7 windows are a byte a row:
  - a window is extracted from one gather of its 2×2 chunks, with no per-tile loop;
  - shut, no-pass and vetoed take one gather and cut each, instead of a `bits` call per board;
  - `grow` and `inside` have no loops;
  - set bits still run in row-major order, so the ties are unchanged.
- The ends loop skips the ends off the search's reached tiles, since a field reads unreachable off them. This was
  checked on 128 games at 100M with 0 violations.
- `route_around`'s crossing test is hoisted out of the neighbour scan.

**Dropped.** A table of `pull`'s term by squared distance was exact, but dearer than the float work it replaced:
total -0.17% against -0.22% without it, and 26k turns dearer against 1.6k.

**Exactness** (`bench.py`, 100M, against 28cc1105): default 16/16, wide 52/52 and fresh-192300 104/104 identical.
Total fuel -0.22%, p99 -0.3%. On wide, 141k turns are cheaper and 4k dearer.

**The reserve refit (a650e7e1, changes play at the real budget).** The RSV instrumentation (`rsvmeas.sh`: 768 games
on maps/gen and the ladder against `variants/astraeus-5b66bde`, real budget) ran on the final and on the candidate.
X (loop exit to the turn order) on cut loops, p50 / p95 / p99 in k, final then candidate:

| class | final | candidate |
|---|---|---|
| not banking, no dash | 13.1 / 24.8 / 33.2 | 13.1 / 24.7 / 33.1 |
| not banking, dash | 16.5 / 33.2 / 40.7 | 15.9 / 31.8 / 39.3 |
| banking, no dash | 12.9 / 21.3 / 26.7 | 12.8 / 21.3 / 26.8 |
| banking, dash | 19.5 / 30.0 / 35.4 | 17.9 / 28.1 / 34.1 |

Only the dash classes moved, since the plan runs only with the dash ready. Each class's flat term was refit at the
quantile today's term sits at on the final's run (`refit.py`), with b and d kept.
- **Not banking, dash:** 23.0k sits at q96.3, and the candidate's q96.3 is 21.4k. That is the change.
  - Simulated on the candidate's cut turns: post-loop OOF ~445 against the final's 427, and turn-order shortfalls
    ~1,480 against 1,491.
  - It frees +1.5k a turn on 29% of non-banking cut turns, about +0.45k a non-banking cut turn.

## Farm memo keys: what moves them, and the cold clears instead (2026-11-05, merged stack 53add725)

Goal: stop the farm loop re-paying for group facts whose inputs did not really change, by finer exact keys. Branch
`worktree-agent-ae2d1e3a633687fcc`; scripts in `research/memokeys-2026-11-05/` (`mkprof.py` adds an `MK` line per
farm loop: which keys moved and by which input, each fact block's recomputes, their fuel and whether they gave the
same values, StandReach builds and clear_fire inside min_camp_damage; `mkan.py` reads them; `mklite.py`/`mlan.py`
give loop fuel by class, paired per loop when the games are identical). Measured on the merged stack, real budget,
128 games on 64 fresh-192300 maps against `variants/astraeus-5b66bde`: 302k farm loops, 7.4% cut.

**The keys rarely move, and the facts are a small part of the loop.** Moves against the champion's previous farm call:

| loops | context (bag / short_by / banking / emblems) | gold (per_gold / tribute_gold) | clearing (strength / basic) |
|---|---|---|---|
| all | 5% (2 / 5 / 2 / 0) | 26% (26 / 4) | 3% (3 / 2) |
| cut, not banking | 13% (7 / 11 / 4 / 1) | 28% | 6% |
| cut, banking | 18% (14 / 18 / 11 / 2) | 42% | 8% |

Spells, reflect and range almost never move alone: strength, spells and basic share camp_scale (a health-dependent
passive or a purchase moves them together; strength's median move is 4%).

Fuel per loop of each fact block, and the recomputes that gave the very values they replaced (the most any exact
finer key could save):

| loops (mean loop fuel) | context | gold | fastest | pre-facts kf | clearing (of it: StandReach builds, clear_fire) | facts' share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all (15.8k) | 118: 0.69 recomputes, 0.26 same | 87: 1.84, 0.33 same | 130: 0.70, 0.12 same | 13 | 408: 0.35, 0.10 same damage (107, 136) | 4.8% |
| uncut nb (12.8k) | 69 | 50 | 104 | 16 | 244 (54, 112) | 3.7% |
| uncut bank (19.0k) | 106 | 137 | 128 | 0 | 347 (26, 65) | 3.8% |
| cut nb (23.0k) | 467: 2.34, 0.68 same | 137 | 293 | 64 | 1,923 (826, 736) | 12.5% |
| cut bank (29.3k) | 531: 2.60, 0.83 same | 240 | 404 | 0 | 1,498 (467, 410) | 9.1% |

- Context: when only short_by moved (any team's score), the facts came out the same 0.22 of 0.23 times; it and
  bag+short_by are the only reasons with same values. The other recomputes are genuine (sticky choice, banking).
- Gold: per_gold moves with gold-dependent prices; 82% of recomputes change the value, and one costs ~48 fuel.
- Clearing: the dear recomputes are the group's first (cold) and belief-version moves, both genuine. When only the
  farm's counter moved, min_camp_damage and spell_clear_rounds already hit their own value-keyed caches (~160).
  min_camp_damage also reads `home_survivable` (our health) where the group has spawn stands, which is not in the
  farm key: the kept damage is stale until the key moves, so a key by value would not be exact against the base.
- On cut loops, most of the clearing block is static or once-a-group work: StandReach builds (~2.2k a group) and
  the first clear_fire (~1.2k a call). 57% of StandReach build fuel lands on cut loops; 54% after round 30.

**Tried: the context facts kept by value (a1813d9a, reverted in 9db2e96d).** A per-group key (bag, short_by,
banking as last read; the facts kept when the win, min(gems, short_by), the chained tribute, banking, emblems and
the sticky choice all hold). Exact (196/196 replays at 100M), but loop fuel +0.04% (342,744 paired loops at 100M)
and total +0.01%: ~40 fuel a loop saved is less than the check and the larger GroupFacts cost. Not done: a split
clearing key (the callees' caches already answer it) and rescaled gold (no cheaper than the recompute).

**Shipped instead: the turn-end queue builds each group's clear stands, then its clear order, once** (13d308f8,
d66506cc: `warm_clears` in camps.cc, called after the map-wide warm-up in main.cc's TurnEndQueue). Stands are
static; the clear order (min_camp_damage's sorted members and fire, for our output now) is updated in place by
later beliefs while the order holds (`order_holds`), so what the loop reads is unchanged. The queue's floor keeps
it to the real budget's spare fuel at any budget.
- Exact: 196/196 identical replays at 100M (16 default, 52 wide, 128 fresh) against 53add725.
- Fuel at 100M: total +0.04% (the queue spends spare fuel), p99 -0.8/-0.8/-0.5%, wide max -7.9%; loop fuel
  -0.47% over 342,744 paired loops (stands alone -0.29%).
- Real budget, the same 128 games (different trajectories): farm-partial-evaluation 25,436 -> 23,684 (-6.9%; stands
  alone 24,553); loop fuel mean cut nb 21.8k -> 21.3k, cut bank 28.8k -> 28.1k, uncut nb 12.58k -> 12.56k, uncut
  bank 18.57k -> 18.49k; OOF turns 1,721 -> 1,717.

A/Bs of d66506cc (`variants/astraeus-warm2`) against `variants/astraeus-5b66bde`, own drafts, real budget, fast
runner, 10,240 games each. Buckets from `bymap.py` (camp groups per map):

| suites | win % (CI) | OOF cand / ref (oof_bot) | round-1 OOF cand / ref | farm-partial-evaluation cand / ref | by groups <12 / 12-23 / 24-47 / 48+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fresh-192501..520 (varied) | 50.6 (49.7-51.6) | 94.7k / 110.0k (-14.0%) | 7.3k / 6.0k | 1.910M / 2.682M (-28.8%) | 50.7 / 49.6 / 50.7 / 56.6 (752 games) |
| fresh-192541..560 (ladder mix) | 50.4 (49.4-51.3) | 115.2k / 130.2k (-11.5%) | 8.3k / 5.9k | 2.006M / 2.996M (-33.0%) | 51.2 / 49.9 / 50.5 / 50.7 (134 games) |

Pooled: 50.5 over 20,480 games. These measure the whole stack against astraeus 5b66bde, not the increment: the
merged stack alone read 51.4 on other varied suites, and its farm-partial-evaluation was -28%, so the warm's own
effect (-7% cut loops in the 128-game bench, -0.5% loop fuel) is too small for an A/B to see. Other cuts against
the ref: turn-order -24/-25%, farm-no-route -38/-35%, static-descend -30/-29%, step-guard-entry -4/-5%. The round-1
OOF rise is the stack's spawn field on the first turn.

Conclusions:
- Finer exact memo keys are not a lever: their invalidations are rare and mostly genuine, and all the facts together
  are ~5% of loop fuel (9-13% on cut loops, where the dear part is cold groups' first clears, not key moves).
- The cold first reads are. The warm takes the stands and clear orders off them; it ships as exact and fuel only.
- Next: start the warm before the map-wide warm-up finishes (p50 round 15, p90 32; 46% of StandReach build fuel
  falls before round 30); warm other once-a-group first reads (home_ground's flood, centre_to_altar, the steps the
  loop takes from the centre fields); the remaining ~90% of loop fuel is steps, live_steps, prunes and crew pricing.

exact checks), `variants/astraeus-ml-*` (loop-fuel copies, `mklite.py`).

## The farm loop's reserve sized by what the rest of the turn runs (2026-11-05, astraeus 5b66bde0 + the two stacks)

Base: astraeus with both audited branches merged (`worktree-agent-a8566433ce7bbd6ac` 93b08b2b, then
`worktree-agent-a120b00b8f933c88a` 5e755b4a), frozen as `variants/astraeus-mstack` (53add725). Branch
`worktree-agent-a7617aa5334d83490`. Tools in `research/rsvfuel-2026-11-05/` (paths inside assume `rsvscratch/`): `instrument.py` patches a copy with `RSV` lines, `rsv_an.py`
parses them, `tab*.py`, `sim*.py` and `cmp.py` tabulate and simulate.

**Measurement.** An instrumented copy of the merged stack (debug build) played `variants/astraeus-5b66bde` at the real
budget on maps/gen and the 128 ladder maps (768 games, 1.9M farm-loop turns, 144k of them cut). On each loop it logs
the state at the loop's exit, the fuel at marks to the turn's end, each post-loop part's cost and the gates that fired
after the loop. X is the spend from the loop's exit to `set_turn_order`. The turn order itself keeps `end_reserve`.

| part (cut loops) | p50 | p99 | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| X, all cut loops | 14.2k | 37.9k | uncut loops: 10.3k / 26.9k |
| the pick (loop exit to the walk) | 0.9k | 4.7k | |
| the walk (`step_route`: route search + travel plan) | mean 8.4k | 27.5k | 82% of cut turns. The route is 6.0k mean, 1 search a turn, at 0.7x `search_cost_estimate` p50 and 1.7x p99. |
| the travel plan, dash ready | 6.5k | 19.6k | the flat term is 12k |
| the approach search (`prepare_approach`) | | 5.8k | runs on 10% of cut turns. The reserve kept `approach_cost` (8-12k) on the 90% where it was not ready. |
| banking, the bag taken to an altar (carry_bag after farm) | 13.5k | 29.9k | 40% of banking cut turns |
| pack zone | 0.7k | 3.8k | |
| the act tail (ward, lock, recall, shield) | 1.4k | 7.0k | |
| turn order | 0.9k | 4.7k | p99.9 7.9k, against its 10k check |
| turn end and comms send | 1.8k | 4.3k | |

Everything else after the loop is many calls of 0.1-0.6k each. There is no single big exact saving there.

X by class on cut loops, p50 / p99, with the old reserve's p50 in brackets:

| chunks | not banking, no dash | not banking, dash | banking, no dash | banking, dash |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| up to 25 | 10.3 / 20.2 [22.0] | 10.7 / 27.2 [33.7] | 11.5 / 23.0 [25.6] | 15.4 / 28.2 [37.6] |
| 26-64 | 11.8 / 22.2 [27.1] | 14.3 / 32.1 [38.6] | 11.6 / 21.9 [30.3] | 18.2 / 32.0 [42.2] |
| 65-100 | 14.2 / 29.1 [33.3] | 20.9 / 39.5 [44.1] | 13.2 / 24.6 [35.5] | 20.0 / 35.0 [47.5] |
| 101+ | 17.0 / 41.0 [41.1] | 24.0 / 50.0 [50.7] | 14.5 / 32.6 [45.2] | 21.9 / 43.2 [54.1] |

- The old reserve was 15k (18.5k zoned) + `approach_cost` + `search_cost_estimate(steps + 16)` + 12k with the dash
  ready. Banking loops were over-reserved by 10-17k against X's p99. Non-banking loops were reserved at about X's p99
  with nothing over for the turn order's 10k, so 5% of cut turns reached the turn order short.
- The rest of the risk is the last group's overshoot: fuel at the exit less the reserve is p50 -1.3k, p10 -6.7k and
  p1 -24k. On today's cut turns, 1.6% ran out after the loop and 7% reached the turn order below 10k.
- The approach state (ready, centre field made), foes within 6 or 10 and the steps add little within a class. Joint
  fits with foes classes freed 4.30k against 4.28k without them.

**The new reserve, after the first turn** (the first turn keeps the old terms):

    end_reserve + a + b * chunks + d * chunks * (steps + 16)

The constants are fitted per class (banking × dash ready) as quantiles of X:

| class | a | b | d |
|---|---|---|---|
| banking, dash | 24.7k | 40 | 0.5 |
| banking, no dash | 20.4k | 0 | 0.75 |
| not banking, dash | 23.0k | 30 | 1.5 |
| not banking, no dash | 18.7k (c1) / 16.4k (c2) | 30 | 0.75 |

`ample` is the same reserve at width + height + 16 layers. The inner breaks use it in place of `loop_floor + loop_reserve()`.

The quantiles were chosen by replaying the cut turns with the new reserve: L' = L - R + R', T' = L' - X. The
constraint was that post-loop OOF and turn-order shortfalls, in total, stay at or below today's.
- c1 (96-98th percentile) simulated OOF -7%, shortfalls -12% and +4.3k loop fuel a cut turn. The gain was +7.4k on
  banking and +0.8k on non-banking, and 0.5% of uncut loops would now be cut.
- c2 moves the non-banking, no-dash class to its 95th percentile: +2.3k on non-banking, simulated post-loop OOF +10%.

Instrumented c1 against the instrumented base (same 768 games):
- Banking loops were cut on 9.2% of turns, against 14.3%; the share weighed at the cut rose from 0.54 to 0.58.
- Non-banking loops: 5.09% against 5.15%.
- Post-loop OOF 2,333 against 2,944. Turn order reached short 9.6k against 14.4k times. Walk gates after the loop
  4.5k against 7.9k.

A/Bs: own drafts, real budget, against `variants/astraeus-5b66bde`, 10,240 games each. FPE is farm-partial-evaluation.

| bot, suites | win % (CI) | OOF cand / ref | runs of 50+ | FPE cand / ref | turn-order | farm-no-route | by groups <12 / 12-23 / 24-47 / 48+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| merged stack (mstack), V1 fresh-192481..500 | 51.4 (50.5-52.4) | 90.3k / 102.8k | 2,822 / 3,452 | 1.914M / 2.647M | 185k | 58.8k | 49.3 / 50.5 / 52.7 / 58.9 |
| c1 9dba3ed8, V1 | 50.4 (49.5-51.4) | 86.1k / 102.3k | 2,165 / 3,417 | 1.599M / 2.642M | 154k | 29.3k | 49.6 / 49.0 / 51.1 / 59.2 |
| c2 1310d649, V1 | 51.1 (50.1-52.0) | 87.9k / 102.8k | 2,335 / 4,226 | 1.513M / 2.642M | 162k | 38.2k | 50.0 / 50.1 / 50.9 / 60.7 |
| c2, L1 fresh-192521..540 (ladder mix) | 51.3 (50.4-52.3) | 112.0k / 132.4k | 2,294 / 3,344 | 1.510M / 3.015M | 211k / 321k | 47.3k / 107k | 51.2 / 51.6 / 50.9 / 53.0 |

On the same maps against the merged stack:
- c1 has 16% fewer farm-partial-evaluation cuts, 5% fewer OOF turns, 17% fewer turn-order cuts and half the
  farm-no-route cuts.
- c2 has 21% fewer farm-partial-evaluation cuts and 3% fewer OOF turns.
- Static-descend and crow-flies-farm are level.

c1 reads 1.0 points below the merged stack and c2 0.3 below, within the noise of paired 10k A/Bs (about ±1). L1
has no merged-stack run, so c2's 51.3 there is against the ref only.

The reserve does what it was sized to do: fewer loop cuts at fewer OOF turns. Most of the freed fuel goes to banking
loops, though, and the earlier banking study found their chain-or-bank outcome rarely changes. Within the state known
at the loop, non-banking X cannot be told apart any further, so a fuller non-banking loop costs post-loop OOF in step
with it.

Inconclusive in wins. c2 is the candidate to keep: its fuel numbers are better than the stack's at no measurable
cost. Next:
- Make the walk's route search cheaper. It is ~40% of post-loop spend, and its tail sets the non-banking reserve.
- Bound the overshoot of the last group weighed, whose p1 is -24k.
- Rerun c2 against the merged stack on suites neither has used, to settle the ±1.

## Pre-loop cuts and tighter pre-facts bounds stacked; the spawn field on the first turn (2026-11-05, astraeus 5b66bde0)

The two sections below, merged with their audits' fixes, plus one logic fix. Branch `worktree-agent-a8566433ce7bbd6ac`.

**Fixes to the merged branches (fuel only).**
- Pack zone. It is now drawn after the farm loop, and the loop's floor did not cover it. With a bag at stake the
  floor now holds `pack_zone_cost_bound` = 3.5k. Measured cost (wa50, real budget): p50 0.7k, p99 3.3k, max 9.8k.
- The struck path draws the zone only after its `banks_bag` and stale returns.
- The two branches' per-group version hooks are now one helper, `World::camp_moved`. It bumps `camps_version`, marks
  `camps_dirty` and resums `clear_health`.
- Lazy pre-facts pass. The PreUpper bounds are computed per block of 4 groups, at the loop's first test of a group
  in the block, instead of for every group up front. The constants live in farm_turn's locals.
  - It is exact against the eager pass at 100M: 16/16, 52/52, 99/100. The one game that differs is
    gen-wild-15044906207's path dependence, below.
  - It is **not** cheaper. Mean fuel at 100M is +0.5-0.6%. The loop reaches nearly every block: 5.0 of 5.5 a farm
    turn, 7.0 of 10.2 on cut turns, 15.6 of 24.3 on cut turns of maps with 80 or more groups. Each block, with its
    done-bit test a group, costs more than a step of the eager loop.
  - The eager pass itself costs (real budget, a farm turn with the pass): mean 1.3k, cut 2.7k, 80+ groups 5.1k
    (6.5k cut). `variants/astraeus-m12eager` is the merge with the eager pass.
  - An inline pass with a cached worth column was no cheaper (+0.5%). A noinline block was +1.0%.

**Logic fix: the spawn field on the first turn.** Until `from_ally_spawn` is made, `home_gap` (farm's heal-trip
`gap`) returns the distance to our spawn's box as the crow flies. Other readers (`fight.cc`, `pathing.cc`) also
branch on whether it is ready.
- At the real budget (wa50, 504 champion instances) the field was made in round 1 by 174 instances, in rounds 2-4
  by ~200, and as late as round 21. Most were made by the turn-end queue, whose room follows each turn's fuel.
- Farm read the bound in 91 of 100 games. The field costs 1.5k-21k by map.
- main.cc now makes the field right after the first `World::update`.
- This removes branch 2's path dependence. With the fix in both bots, the stack without d737bcf6 (the prices
  tolerance, logic) against astraeus 5b66bde0 is byte-identical at 100M: 16/16, 52/52, 100/100 (wa50).
  Fuel: mean -3.7/-4.5/-4.6%, p50 -4.7/-6.2/-6.1%, p99 -5.4/-5.1/-8.5% (default, wide, wa50).
- Without the fix in both, the same comparison differs on gen-wild-15044906207 (both sides).
- The fix alone against the base changes 3 of 168 games at 100M.
- The full candidate against the base: mean -5.3/-5.1/-4.3%, p50 52.5k/54.2k/49.3k -> 49.1k/50.5k/46.1k, p99
  109.3k/115.3k/114.2k -> 101.9k/107.9k/104.4k.

Ref is the frozen `variants/astraeus-5b66bde`, byte-identical to astraeus 5b66bde0. Own drafts, real budget, fast
runner, 10,240 games a row:

## Fuel before the farm loop on cut turns, banking or not (2026-11-05, astraeus a67cb2ca)

The study used fuel marks in `debug_block`s at decide's branches, World::update's parts and farm_turn's preamble,
printed on every farm-partial-evaluation turn.

**Base code.** On `maps/wa-30k`, 400 games, 57% of the cut turns were banking:

| Turn | Before the loop, p50 / mean | Loop | Evaluated share at the cut, p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Banking, cut | 33k / 35.5k | ~31k | 0.53 |
| Not banking, cut | 38k / 40.8k | ~26k | 0.41 |
| Banking, uncut | 25k | | |
| Not banking, uncut | 21k | | |

Where the mean went on banking cut turns:
- World::update ~8.3k. Of that, update_camps is 2.6k and the champions 2.7k.
- decide's first banks_bag 3.2k: altar_access and the live_camps scan.
- continue_recall ~4k: want_home 1.6k, and recall_to_bank's home_trip.
- carry_bag before the farm ~3.5k.
- farm_turn's preamble ~12k: home_trip 3.6k, setup prices 2.3k, pre_prune_upper 2k and pack_zone 1k.

Repeated calls on a banking turn:
- gems_short 16.6x;
- race_left and bag_rounds_left 7.5x each;
- gems_share 2.7x at ~1k each;
- prices 2.4x.

best_emblem (6.5k) ran again on 47% of banking cut turns, because prices keyed it on gems_share, which moves most rounds.

On non-banking cut turns the costs are siege() 4.6k (altars_sealed rebuilding altar_access), chase 4.1k (p90 19k), and want_home 3.6k.

**Banking turns are farm turns with a bag.** A pass over 80 games found 50.8k banking loop turns, 19% of them cut.
- 70.7% chained (farmed on with the bag).
- The chain-or-bank outcome changed between a champion's consecutive banking turns only 3.9% of the time, and runs were mostly 10 or more turns.
- The best value over from_altar_value had p50 1.38.

The lever is therefore their pre-loop overhead, not a different decision.

**Changes.** Three exact changes, fuel only. bench.py at 100M gave byte-identical replays, 16/16 and 52/52:
- gems_short, race_left and gems_share are kept per (round, World::observations, our gems).
- Pathing::live_camps rescans only the groups whose camp version moved (World::camps_dirty).
- farm_turn draws the pack zone after the loop. Nothing in the loop reads it.

Fuel against base, default set: p50 52.5k→50.9k, p99 109.3k→106.5k. Wide set: p50 54.2k→52.4k, p99 115.3k→112.4k (-2.5% mean).

With the first two changes, 200 wa-30k games at the real budget (different games, not a matched pair):
- Banking cut turns spent 33.8k→29.2k before the loop (mean).
- Non-banking cut turns: 39.7k→38.3k.
- farm-partial-evaluation fell 44.3k→38.4k.

One logic change: prices keeps best_emblem's choice until the gem share moves by a tenth; gain and per_gold still follow the share. affordable_prefix already kept its choice whatever the share. Fuel: def p50 -1.9%, p99 -1.7%.
It also leaves best_emblem's other inputs stale between purchases: the income and upkeep stats, the bag_rounds_left
horizon inside passive_saved, and economy_three. The choice is refreshed only on a tenth move of the share or a change
of the key's stats. Purchases themselves call best_emblem directly.

Ref is astraeus a67cb2ca. Own drafts, real budget, fast runner:

| A/B | Suites | Win % (CI) | Games | OOF cand / ref | farm-partial-evaluation cand / ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| exact (682d6dc8) | fresh-192101..120 | 50.7 (49.7-51.6) | 10,240 | 99.2k / 105.1k | 2.18M / 2.69M |
| exact + prices (d737bcf6) | fresh-192121..140 | 50.9 (49.9-51.9) | 10,240 | 91.8k / 100.6k | 2.14M / 2.73M |
| exact + prices (d737bcf6) | fresh-192101..120 | 51.1 (50.1-52.1) | 10,240 | 96.0k / 105.4k | 2.11M / 2.68M |

Results:
- The exact changes alone are level and ship on that.
- With prices, pooled over 20,480 games: 51.0 (50.3-51.7).
- farm-partial-evaluation fell 19-22% and OOF 6-9%.
- The other cuts fell 2-12%: step-guard-entry, turn-order, prey-cut-short, static-descend.
- What prices adds on top of the exact changes is within noise: 50.7 vs 51.1 on the same maps.

Tried and dropped:
- A begun_emblem memo on the owned items cost 2.4% more fuel: affordable_prefix's hypothetical item sets miss it and pay a copy and compare.
- Raw item reads in has_family were level.

## Cheaper farm-loop facts: tighter pre-facts bounds (2026-11-05, astraeus 5b66bde0)

Goal: the farm loop weighing every group within budget, by making its per-group work cheaper. A profile of cut turns
(wa maps, real budget, `debug_block` fuel marks) put the loop at ~30k ordinary and ~34k banking (60% of cuts are
banking turns), weighing 40-50% of the groups. Per cut ordinary turn: the pre-facts `rated_below` bound ~5.5k (424 a
group, 13 groups), our crew plans 4.1k (`plan_crew` ~3.5k a call: its free-ally expansion ~2.3k, `share_damage`
~0.9k), ally-claimed share pricing 3.5k (~2.4k a group), steps and `live_steps` ~300 each a group. Banking: nearly
every group pays ~1k (steps, `live_steps`, facts) before half fall to the plain-ratio prune. Cold clear facts
(`min_camp_damage`) were only ~10% of it.

Two commits, both bounds before the facts (no new fuel gate; a group is skipped only when its value provably
cannot change the pick):
- 501e32e0: `pre_prune_upper`'s bound adds the fastest clear (health left / our output; per group, kept by camp
  version), the home weight read so far (`home_weights`), a floor on banking's walk home; banking gets the
  plain-ratio prune's two ratios as vector tests too.
- 2a2ee15f: the crew's clear bounded as `crew_rate` does (the clamped best crew size k in [1, team / ours], not the
  whole team's output on the clear alone: up to k times tighter on strong groups); ally-claimed groups get their
  share bound before facts (`claim_most`); World keeps each group's clear health as its version moves.

Checks at 100M (`bench.py`: default, `--set wide`, 50 wa maps; 168 games): identical replays 16/16, 52/52, 99/100.
The one that differs (gen-wild-15044906207) is not a wrong prune: a no-skip build that reports any skipped group
that would have become best, shared, risky or raised the cycle from the altar found none in 400 games (2.6M skips).
Farm's `gap` reads home_gap's crow-flies bound (7 there) until the spawn field is built and the walk (57) after, and
which turn builds the field depends on which groups the loop read: heal trips price differently (14 vs 62 rounds)
for a while. Any change to what the loop reads moves it. Fuel at 100M on those games: total -1.9/-2.5/-2.3%, p50
-2.6/-3.6/-3.0%, p99 -3.0/-3.5/-6.3%. Profile (wa50, real budget): farm-partial-evaluation 27,271 -> 21,947; the
pre-facts bound's per-turn fuel on cut ordinary turns 5.5k -> 3.1k; full loops 16.1k -> 13.3k ordinary, 24.8k ->
20.6k banking. The pass itself costs ~60 fuel a group (80 banking), 2.6k -> 3.7-4.1k a cut turn.

| A/B (own drafts, real budget, vs astraeus 5b66bde0) | Win % (CI) | Games | OOF cand / ref | farm-partial-evaluation cand / ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 501e32e0, fresh-192021..192040 | 49.3 (48.3-50.3) | 10,240 | 115.3k / 111.4k | 2.53M / 2.74M |
| 2a2ee15f, fresh-192041..192060 | 49.7 (48.7-50.7) | 10,238 | 108.4k / 106.0k | 2.25M / 2.68M |
| 2a2ee15f, fresh-192021..192040 | 50.5 (49.5-51.5) | 10,240 | 113.1k / 109.5k | 2.30M / 2.74M |
| 2a2ee15f pooled | 50.1 (49.4-50.8) | 20,478 | 221.5k / 215.4k (+2.8%) | -16.1% |

Level: 16% fewer cut loops buy no measurable win, and out-of-fuel turns rise 2-3% in all three A/Bs. The extra OOF
turns are mostly in decide before its `D` line and in OOF-heavy games (`batch_oof.py` on the second row: games with 50+ hold 42.4k vs 39.4k);
one guess is that a loop now gets further down its order and reads cold groups (a first StandReach or sort costs
several times the estimate) close to its reserve. Next: build the spawn field at a fixed time (a logic change: the
bound underprices heal trips early); a static walk bound tighter than Chebyshev for banking (each group pruned at the
plain ratio has already paid ~800 for steps and `live_steps`); `plan_crew`'s expansion and `crew_work`.


## Cheaper crew pricing, same answers (2026-11-05, astraeus 5b66bde0; exact, level)

Goal: make the farm loop's crew pricing (`plan_crew`, `crew_work` and the `may_beat` bound) cheaper without changing
what it returns. Two commits on branch `worktree-agent-a120b00b8f933c88a`: bd30ed16 (c2), then 5ffd89be (c5). Both
leave the 196 `bench.py` replays at 100M identical: 16 default, 52 `wide`, and 128 on 64 fresh-192300 maps against
`variants/astraeus-5b66bde`. The profiler is `research/crewfuel-2026-11-05/` (`mkcprof.py` for the base,
`mkcprof2.py` for the rewrite, `cprof.py` to read them). It adds `CREWPROF` lines with fuel by part per farm loop.
The numbers below come from 64 games at the real budget on fresh-192300.

**Where it went, per call (base).** Most of the cost was small passes over every ally, repeated for each group and
each pricing, not one big simulation:
- `plan_crew`: 3.3k for an ally's claimed group, 4.2k for our own crew plan.
  - Claimers and survivable: 0.4k.
  - First `min_camp_damage`: 0.5k. A cache hit costs 160 and a miss 830-890; 58% hit.
  - First `share_damage`: 1.0k. Rebuilding its pool cost 0.8k, ~170 a `crew_arrival`. The sort and level cost 0.25k.
  - Free-ally list: 0.7-0.8k (`crew_available` is ~70 a call, ~9 calls a loop).
  - Each expansion step: 1.4-1.8k. Of that, `share_damage` is 1.1k again and `min_camp_damage` 0.36k.
- `crew_work`: 1.4-1.6k. `work_arrival` is 750 a claimer; its spawn-distance loop runs on half the calls.
- The `may_beat` block: 0.75-0.95k a call. The crew table build: 0.6k a farm call.

Per cut loop, crew pricing came to 6.3k non-banking and 8.8k banking; per finished loop, 3.0k and 4.2k.

**What changed (c5):**
- **Per-call tables.** `CrewAllies` gained the claiming allies in ally order, a joinable list, and availability bits
  for the last group asked. `plan_crew`, `may_beat` and the claimed branch's bound loop now walk these lists, not every
  ally.
- **The share pool is built once.** `share_damage` takes it in ally order. Expected allies merge in by slot, so
  `std::sort` sees the same input order and ties fall as before. Float sums keep their order throughout.
- **Arrivals.** The pool's arrival test is settled by bounds where it can: the walk to the members' box and to the
  centre, less the range. `crew_arrival` runs only when the bounds overlap.
- **`work_arrival` is kept per group and ally** while its inputs hold: belief version, position, visible, the dash
  and recall offsets from the anchor round, and `acted`. It is skipped when we would work 0 rounds.
- **A tighter bound before the claimed `plan_crew`.** It is the existing pre-`crew_work` bound with `health_left` in
  place of `health`. It prunes ~20% of those calls.
- **`crew_work` reads the crew table only for an operation**, or once the table has been read. For a harmless claimed
  group it makes one pass over the allies.

**What failed or cost fuel:**
- A team-output pre-bound ahead of `may_beat`'s reads cost more than it saved (0.95k -> 1.2k a call). Dropped.
- c2's `KeptArrival` table held a `vec2`. A struct with members left uninitialised beside a constexpr-default member
  cannot be constant-initialised, so the 2048-entry static got a run-time initialiser. That added ~4k on first use:
  round 1 was +2.0% at 100M, and A/B 1's OOF rose in rounds 1-10. c5 uses plain ints, and round 1 is -0.9%.
- The `work_arrival` memo hits little on cut turns (750 -> 700 a call), which come after things change. On finished
  turns it saves more (670 -> 500).

| measure (real budget, 64 games, per loop) | base | c5 |
|---|---|---|
| crew pricing, cut non-banking loop | 6,345 | 5,178 (-18%) |
| crew pricing, cut banking loop | 8,759 | 7,144 (-18%) |
| crew pricing, finished non-banking / banking | 3,018 / 4,221 | 2,618 / 3,607 |
| `plan_crew` a call, claimed / crewable (cut nb) | 3,234 / 4,192 | 2,909 / 3,102 |
| `plan_crew` claimed calls per cut nb loop | 0.42 | 0.32 |
| `crew_work` a call (cut nb) | 1,563 | 1,306 |

At 100M, c5 changes total fuel by -0.56%, p50 by -0.9%, p99 by -1.0% and round 1 by -0.9% (fresh set; wide and
default are the same within 0.1).

A/Bs: own drafts, real budget, against `variants/astraeus-5b66bde`, 10,240 games each. Buckets come from
`bymap.py` (camp groups per map); the 48+ bucket has 136-156 games.

| candidate, suites | win % (CI) | OOF cand / ref | farm-partial-evaluation cand / ref | by groups <12 / 12-23 / 24-47 / 48+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c2 bd30ed16, fresh-192301..192320 | 50.1 (49.2-51.1) | 127.1k / 121.6k (+4.6%; rounds 1-10 +5.4k) | 2.862M / 2.970M (-3.6%) | 51.8 / 49.5 / 49.9 / 55.8 |
| c5 5ffd89be, fresh-192321..192340 | **50.5 (49.5-51.4)** | 126.2k / 128.2k (-1.6%) | 2.875M / 3.052M (-5.8%) | 51.3 / 49.6 / 51.1 / 55.1 |

In c5's A/B the other gates also cut less: turn-order 303k / 313k, farm-no-route 100k / 111k, static-descend 41.1k /
42.2k. Runs of 50+ OOF turns fell to 2,651 / 3,397.

Level, as an exact fuel-only change should be, so c5 can ship. These suites are the new ladder mix (1.4% of maps
have 48+ groups), so a fuel gain shows less here than on the older suites. Next:
- `may_beat` is still ~1k a call, most of it the first read of every ally's availability and output.
- `work_arrival` is still 700 a claimer on cut turns.
- In expansion steps, `min_camp_damage` misses cost ~830; a cheaper way to reprice with only the strength changed
  would help.
- The crew table build is 0.7k a farm call.
- Nothing in these passes is a single big cost. Each pass over the allies runs ~70-170 fuel, so further gains mean
  computing less, not computing it faster.


## proteus turn windows on ocean (ocean, 2026-11-06)

proteus's combat coordination ported onto `variants/oc-retest-clean` (= `bots/ocean`) as `params::ptw::` knobs in
`variants/oc-proteus-dev`: enemy turn windows (`model/turn_window.{h,cc}`), the team seat ledger in comms, seats
assigned by the chance each need is met over the feasible enemy orders (turn_order.cc), with the revised fixes (dead
enemies' slots unknown, the escape blow split over two turns, ledger and order model built lazily). Added:
`after_nearest` (this round's enemy turns after ours go to the unseen enemies nearest our turn start, not to every
unseen one), an unseen enemy's moved strike when the window lets it act after us, and drop-one ablation knobs
(`w_next`, `w_tbo`, `w_tbo_now`, `w_tbo_next`, `w_repeats`, `w_reach`, `w_slots`, `w_moved`, `cheap_after_heavy`).
With every knob off, bench replays are byte-identical to oc-retest-clean at 100M (16/16 default, 52/52 wide with test
drafts; +5 fuel a turn). Fast runner, own drafts, `--no-test-draft`; suites `maps/suites/merged/ptw-a` (fresh
543000-543039) and `ptw-b` (543040-543079), 20,480 games each. **Dropped: no variant is significant locally, so none
went to the live gate.** Variants `bots/variants/oc-ptwd-*` (deleted); `variants/oc-proteus-dev` is kept as the
knob copy.

- **Windows win a little at 2x fuel, not on the held-out suite, and are level at the real budget.**

  | Variant | Fuel | ptw-a | ptw-b | Both (40,960) | OOF cand / ref |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | windows + after_nearest (wn) | 2x | 51.2 (50.5-51.9) | 50.2 (49.5-50.9) | 50.7 | 2,773 / 2,411 |
  | windows (w) | 2x | 50.8 (50.2-51.5) | | | 1,375 / 1,198 |
  | windows + seats + ledger (wsln) | 2x | 50.7 (50.0-51.4) | | | 1,665 / 1,245 |
  | seats + ledger (sl) | 2x | 49.5 (48.8-50.2) | | | 1,476 / 1,160 |
  | wn | real | 50.4 (49.7-51.1) | 50.2 (49.5-50.8) | 50.3 | 439k / 318k (+38%) |
  | w | real | 50.1 (49.4-50.8) | | | 214k / 160k |
  | wsln | real | 50.1 (49.4-50.7) | | | 229k / 160k |

  Ladder maps at 2x against astraeus-now-1106 (256 games each): wn 54.7, w 52.7, oc-retest-clean 50.0. At 10M (runs
  stopped at ~15k games): w 50.2, ws 50.4, wsl 50.3, sl 49.6. Seats and the ledger add nothing and cost fuel.
- **The gain and the fuel are both in one piece: next round's turn before ours** (`turns_before_ours` with
  `enemy_turn_before_ours_next`: the `room` enemy slots before ours go to the nearest unsettled enemies, so a near
  enemy gets two turns and `threat_strike` widens). Drop-one ablations of wn at 2x, both suites (40,960 each): without
  it (`w_tbo_next` off) 50.0, without all of `turns_before_ours` 49.8; without `next_turn_round` 50.5, without
  `repeats` 50.7 (=wn); without Reach's latest slot 50.4. Out-of-fuel turns on the real-budget bench (poolR +
  heavyR + bigR, 128 + 50 + 32 games against oc-retest-clean): base 1,921, wn 2,646, without `w_tbo_next` 2,083, without `turns_before_ours` 2,069,
  every other drop 2,481-2,916. Mean fuel a turn (poolR) 52.8k, wn 54.4k (+3.0%), without `w_tbo_next` 53.6k.
- **The cost is behaviour, not the window code.** The windows' own code costs ~630 fuel a turn (builds ~0.7k at 0.33 a
  turn, picks ~0.7k); calling it with the answers discarded costs +1.3% and an optimised build saved 0.12%. Traced
  census (146 games, wn against base, real budget): OOF-first turns 1,332 → 1,768, the mean per OOF-first turn up in
  channels (continue_recall → want_home every recall turn) 14.5k → 17.3k, retreat 4.6k → 6.7k, camp_trapped 1.4k →
  1.7k, route 3.2k → 4.2k. The widened threats send more turns down the dear branches.
- **A heavy-turn fallback trades the gain away with the fuel.** `cheap_after_heavy`: after a turn that ran out or used
  more than `heavy_used`, the next reads next round's order as the base does. heavy_used 70k: OOF 2,257 on the bench,
  +19% in the A/B (376k / 317k), **49.7 (49.2-50.2) of 40,960** at the real budget (ptw-a 50.0, ptw-b 49.4);
  heavy_used 50k: OOF 2,177 on the bench, +15% in the A/B (362k / 315k), **49.8 (49.3-50.3)**. Both read below wn
  at the real budget (50.3).
- **Back-to-back kills** (an enemy hitting twice across a round boundary before the victim acts), from extracted
  replays (turn order from `prio[r-1]`):
  - Local, 2x: wn's games (ptw-a, 2,000): its deaths 11,328, 2,004 b2b (17.7%); base's deaths 12,166, 2,031 b2b.
    sl's games (no windows, same maps): its deaths 12,136, 1,989 b2b; base's 12,221, 1,985 b2b. ptw-b (4,000, wn):
    22,854 deaths, 4,099 b2b, against 24,609, 4,187. So windows cut deaths ~7% but not the b2b ones.
  - The windows predict the second turn in 90% of our b2b deaths (the base order model 60%): ~70% of them come to a
    champion already retreating (54% after 6+ retreat turns, begun at ~70% health) and 17% while stopping a game
    ender. They are chases lost, not surprises: knowing the order does not save them.
  - Live losses (`replays/ladder-scrims-2026-11-06/`): against Fish, 73 of our 492 deaths were b2b (14.8%); the base
    model predicted 8, windows 64 (56 that the base missed); against Mite, 85 of 384 (22.1%), base 37, windows 72 (35
    missed by the base). In wins: Fish 36 of 175 (windows 31, base 8), Mite 26 of 155 (21, 17).
- **Why the edge does not convert.** In wn's ptw-b games (4,000, 49.7%): deaths to champions 7.43 a game against
  8.07, kills +0.5, but gems lost at death 153 against 155, gems collected +0.4%, gold +1.1%. The deaths saved carry
  no bags.
- Scripts: `research/ideas-2026-11-05/ptw-tools/` (variant builder, benches, A/B queue, `b2b.py` back-to-back
  deaths and the two order models, `b2b3.py` the victim's branch, `sides.py` and `deaths.py` per-side totals);
  summaries in `replays/ab/ptw-*`, benches in `replays/fuel/ptw/`. No SPRT was used: every A/B above is a full
  fixed-size run. A fresh suite made for a confirm, `maps/suites/merged/ptw-c` (543080-543119, `--mix ladder`), is
  unused.

## Endgame race model, informational (ocean, 2026-11-06)

The user's idea: a projected win round for each team (tributed gems, carried bags with their walk, channel and
cancellation risk, and the recent tribute rate), shared by the endgame rules other agents are building.
- `bots/variants/oc-race` (READY; dev copy `oc-race-dev`) is `variants/oc-retest-clean` plus `model/race.{h,cc}`.
  No decision reads it.
- With it, bench replays are byte-identical at 100M (16/16).
  - The per-turn update costs +311 fuel a turn.
  - The race is computed lazily, ~3.5k on a turn's first `current()`.
  - A first, eager build cost ~10k a turn and tripled out-of-fuel turns in the debug A/B.
- Validated on 768 traced local games against astraeus-now-1106 (tuned on half the maps) and on 560 live v78 scrims
  (a fog replica that agrees with the bot's own trace on 99.3% of rounds).
- **Predicted-winner accuracy** with a side at 500 or more tributed:
  - local test: tributed-only 0.859-0.860, model 0.887;
  - live: tributed-only 0.793-0.794, model 0.852.
- **Endgame flips of the projected winner** precede a loss 58-64% of the time, against a base of 43-45%, and catch a
  third of the losses about 70 rounds out.
- **What carries the gain:** the bags and a long (600-round) rate window. The walk, channel, risk and lock terms add
  ≤0.3 points to the sign; they matter for timing, and the projection runs late (+53 to +76 rounds bias 0-50 rounds
  from the end).
- Design, API and tables: research/ladder-scrims-2026-11-06/race.md.

## Kill assignment and reactive Tribute emblem (ocean, 2026-11-06)

The user's ideas on who takes a killing blow: a big-bag carrier refusing the kill when an ally could take it, a
kill-gold funnel, routing the victim's gems to a small-bag ally, a Tribute emblem priced from the bag, and later
"obese" bags. Design, counts and tables: research/ladder-scrims-2026-11-06/fix-kill.md; scripts in `kill-tools/`.
- Dev copy `bots/variants/oc-kill-dev`: `variants/oc-retest-clean` with `params::kill::` knobs, all off. With them
  off, bench replays are identical at 100M (16/16, 52/52).
- Suites: kill-dev (542000-542039, 20,480 games) and kill-confirm (542100-542139). Late-round subsets: kill-late (662
  maps) and kill-latec (503).
- **Nothing is significant, so no finalist and nothing for the live gate.**
- **Refusal at 2x fuel.**
  - The race-model arm (kr0h) passed SPRT at 400 games, then read 50.0% of 20,480 on both kill-dev and
    kill-confirm, with 39-54% more out-of-fuel turns.
  - The fixed (300/600/1000, own or own+bag), dynamic (local win-round projection, Y 0/5), routing and funnel arms all
    stopped on H0 at 48.9-50.2%.
  - At the real budget, kf600s, kd0s and kfp600s read 49.7-49.8% of 20,480 each.
- **Why the refusal is level.**
  - It fires in 3.5-16% of games, nearly all of which we already win (78% for base on the same games).
  - Paired with base-vs-base at 2x, kr0h's fired games read +1.0 points (55 games turned to wins, 45 to losses) and
    the rest -0.08.
  - With an ally required, the able ally is seldom there: a big-bag carrier that kills is usually alone or first,
    since the kill bid seats it first.
- **Race model's sign:** `if_kill`'s delta has the expected sign. A kill makes our win sooner with a small bag and
  later from about 600 gems.
- **Reactive Tribute:**
  - Priced from the current bag (T1b, from 100 gems) it is level: 50.3% of 14,422 at the real budget, 50.1% of
    8,569 at 2x.
  - Prism does buy it before big channels: 400 bought in 800 games against 39, and half as many channels of 61+
    turns. But a long channel still completes about 9% of the time.
  - Without the 100-gem floor it lost (47.8-48.4%). Forward pricing for Prism lost 42-45%.
- **Obese bags:**
  - A bag that no channel can score by round 2000 (whole-bag tributes, best emblem, walk 0) exists in about 1.4% of
    self-play games, nearly all in the last 20 rounds.
  - The bot already refuses such a channel (`tribute_ok`), but walks the bag to an altar.
  - V0 (kill values, `obese_bank`, both) reads 49.6-50.2% on the late suites, and it changed one game's winner of
    the fired ones.
  - V1 (discount when `if_kill` keeps the projected winner, m 50-300, x0 or x0.5) stopped on H0 at 49.1-49.9%. It
    fires in ~93% of games.
- **Long channel forensics** (fix-kill.md section 6; no A/B):
  - Our 60+ turn channels complete 8% of the time in the mirror and 16% live. We cancel 41-65% of them ourselves
    (`tribute_safe`), and about two thirds of those start again within 3 rounds.
  - Being seen at the start halves completion.
  - Winning bags complete 14-15% of the time, carrying a median 169-380 gems over the need. They lost 3.6% of mirror
    games and 11 live scrims.
  - Levers: stop a winning bag growing, start long channels unseen, and no cancel-restart cycling. Escorts and
    perma-locks are not levers (our lock is up 88-93% of the time already).
- **Long channel fixes C1-C4** (fix-kill.md section 7; 2x fuel, kill-dev, full 20,480-game runs). None wins.
  - C1, cancelling only for a kill within 1 turn: **48.8%**. It cuts self-cancels from 38% to 9%, but stuns and
    locks take their place, and bags later lost at a death rise 65%.
  - C1 with a restart cost: 49.9%.
  - C2, a winning bag refusing gem kills: **49.1%** for all carriers, **49.2%** for Prism only.
  - C3, an unseen start for 20+ turn channels: 49.9% with or without the altar switch.
  - C4, a winning bag taken at any risk to 30 turns: 49.3%. A Prism cap of 300 from round 1200: 49.9%.
  - The rest (C1 slack, C2 slack 100, C3 T 30, C4 to 45 turns, cap 450) stopped on H0, also with fresh
    `--sprt-seed`s.
  - The self-cancel is the bot escaping a stun-and-kill that is coming: a watched long channel fails anyway.
- The seed-0 SPRT stops above shared their first games. kr0h's H1 was held out (50.0% on two full suites); the
  arms that only had H0 stops each had a sibling run in full.

**Self-play forensics:**

- Prism loses 154 gems a game in bags, with no narrow size cut.
- In 86 games lost to an unguarded long channel, interrupt wins 23, against 1 for the base. The pattern is that each
  lock cancels the channel, then the carrier dies, the lock breaks and the channel restarts.

  divergence in about as many won pairs as lost ones.

**Round 2: a timed lock wins.**

`variants/oc-fixm-iw8` (READY) is interrupt plus `lock_wait` 1 and `lock_stage` 8. A carrier holding a lock for a
winning or denied channel waits 8-11 steps from the lock tiles, out of the guards' reach, and keeps the plan while
the channel is out of sight. It locks on our last turn before the channel lands, so the enemy loses the whole
channel.

Opponent census:

So the unguarded big channel is rare locally, even against Fish-like bots.

## Perma-lock when ahead (ocean, 2026-11-06)

The user's idea: on one-altar maps, while we lead in tributed gems, keep our lock on the altar, and re-lock
whenever the enemy breaks it, ideally just before their channel lands. Altar tiles within 3 are merged into one
site of at most 2 tiles.
- Dev copy `bots/variants/oc-lock-dev` (`params::plock`, economy/perma_lock.cc), from `variants/oc-retest-clean`.
- With the knobs off, bench replays are byte-identical at 100M (16/16, 52/52).
- Design, knobs, gate firing tables and every variant: research/ladder-scrims-2026-11-06/fix-lock.md.
- All runs are against oc-retest-clean, own drafts, fast runner.

Dev: `lock-one-dev`, the 1,602 one-site maps of fresh 541100-541119 (3,204 games), with SPRT stopping losers.
- The user's gate (lead ≥ 1) fires in 92% of one-site games, from a median round of 92, for ~450 rounds.
- Keep only (l0) reads 51.3. Ocean already locks an on-side altar in passing, so on one-tile maps this is a no-op.
- Seek 12: 48.6. One holder: 44.3 immediate, 44.3 timed. Two holders, or a holder tethered to nearby enemy
  carriers: 47.4-49.6.
- Narrower hold gates are level:

  | Hold gate | Win % |
  |---|---|
  | G2 bag ≥ 500 | 51.1 |
  | sum ≥ 500 | 50.9 |
  | winbank (their tributed + bags ≥ 1000) | 51.2 |
  | lead ∧ bag ≥ 200 | 50.5 |
  | lead ∧ bag ≥ 100 | 48.9 |
  | lead ∧ flip (G3) | 48.7 |

- Timing margin 0/1/3 or immediate, Willow beside the holder, Tavi selling, and stun walks change 6-78 winners
  of 3,204.
- The ~51 readings are fuel noise shared by every oc-lock build. At 10M fuel the finalists read gwin 50.2,
  g2b500 49.9, n8l50 48.2. At 2x (200k a turn) they read 50.0, 49.8, 48.8.
- Why it does not pay: while we lead, the enemy lands 11.3 tributes a game on the site (8.8 of them with no lock
  of ours believed). A lock costs them 5 attacks, but each re-lock costs us a spawn trip (carry 1), and a holder
  costs a farmer. The big-bag gates fire in games we mostly lose anyway (we win 14-24% of those).

Confirm on fresh 541000-541039 (20,480 games, real budget):

| Finalist | All | one-tile | 2-tile site | multi |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gwin | 49.9 (49.2-50.6) | 49.6 | 49.2 | 50.1 |
| g2b500 | 49.9 (49.2-50.5) | 49.7 | 48.9 | 50.1 |
| n8l50 | 49.7 (49.0-50.4) | 48.7 | 48.0 | 50.2 |

- 128 ladder maps against astraeus-now-1106: base 56.2, g2b500 55.9, gwin 53.5, n8l50 52.7 (±6).
- L4 (every altar kept, multi-site maps): 49.8 of 2,022, H0.
- No local gain.

  Mite lock and tribute unlike our mirror).

  v79, and its tasks were dropped. v78 was re-pinned, so the team is in pinned mode. The one group labelled v79
  was played by v78 (byte-identical replays). See fix-lock.md "Live gate".

Round 2 (the user: the gate was too weak, not the idea). Forensics, a guaranteed-hold gate, all-hands defence,
the race model, a learned EV gate, burst and fight vetoes, and a cooked mirror. Every screen ran at 2x fuel on
lock-one-dev, 3,204 games each.
- **Forensics.** Most enemy landings while we led came after our lock was broken with no carrier close enough to
  re-lock, or by the spawn trip; 80% came from carried bags already above our lead. Leads in lost games are lost
  by round ~480, to the enemy reaching 1000, not at round 2000.
- **Paired reading** (`lock-tools/paired.py`). A gate changes nothing before it first fires, so each game pairs
  with normal play (oc-lock-obs2, 50.1%) on the same map and side. Where the gate never fired, 98.6-99.5% of
  outcomes agree.
- **Ahead holds.**
  - All hands from the first lead: 17-25%.
  - All hands while an enemy is near: 36.8%.
  - All hands from round 1000: 48.2% (net −47 of 716 fired games); with the fight veto 48.3 (−44), with the
    burst veto 47.8 (−60).
  - From 1500, 1700 or 1850: 49.8-50.0 (−7 to +1, in 3-6% of games that normal play wins 85-92% of).
  - Convex lead-over-bags gates: 47.6-49.3 (−13 to −66).
  - Race-gated: 20.4% and 48.0%.
  - Learned EV gate: 49.5% (−18) and 47.1%.
  - No cell of round × lead × bags gains. The holders die at the site: 42% of our body-turns in the 10 rounds
    before a landing were dead or idle.
- **Against bots/fish** (normal 82.7%): every hold is level or worse (gwin −12, ah1t −41, h1t −151 net).
- **Cooked mirror** (all hands at the site while 200+ behind with 600+ tributed; bait-and-snipe without a
  standing lock): 48.7-50.0%; comebacks fall (126 to 106, 133 to 113-119).
- **Grid exhausted; no winner.** Nothing reached SPRT significance, so there was no real-budget or held-out
  confirm. Details: fix-lock.md "Round 2".

## Farm turn fuel (ocean, 2026-11-05)

Track Z: exact fuel savings in the farm turn, so that at the real budget the loop cuts less often or later. Every
decision at unlimited fuel is unchanged. Design and evidence: research/ideas-2026-11-05/fuel.md. Dev copy
`bots/variants/oc-fuel-dev`, knobs `params::fuel::`. With all knobs off its bench.py replays at 100M are identical to
oc-base1's (and +0.3% fuel). Every step's replays at 100M are byte-identical to oc-base1's: 16/16 default and 52/52
wide. Everything is against `variants/oc-base1`, own drafts, real fuel, fast runner.

**Diagnostics: what the loop is worth** (fresh-513001..513010, 5,120 games each). Rows 1-4 are astraeus 5b66bde with
`fuel()` reading the real-budget view under `--fuel 10000000`, against the real-budget cap.

| Copy | Win % | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|
| gate view, unchanged | 51.2 | 49.8-52.5 |
| loop 25% cheaper (`DiscountFuel` refunds a quarter of its spend) | 52.1 | 50.8-53.5 |
| loop 50% cheaper | 53.3 | 51.9-54.6 |
| loop free (`FreeFuel`) | 54.4 | 53.0-55.8 |
| ocean never cutting the loop, real budget (`oc-fuel-nocut`) | 50.1 | 48.7-51.5 |

- The loop holds ~3 points: about +1 per 25% of it saved.
- Never cutting it is level: OOF turns go from 52.6k to 340.9k.

**Where cut turns' fuel goes.** A private fastrunner patch counts exact block fuel and block executions per turn,
filed by turn: a turn that cut the loop, and the part of it before the loop starts (an `@L@` marker). Bots built
`-g` and symbolised. 24 games on fresh-513000.

- A cut turn uses ~71k block fuel (host fees not included), ~31k of it before the loop.
- Before the loop, fuel goes to the loop one for one: `room()` cuts at a fixed reserve. Cut loops end with a median
  31-35k left, the walk's reserve.
- Biggest single item: the race chain, `race_left` (~6 calls, ~520 each per cut turn) and `gems_share`, through
  `prices`, `home_trip`, `farm_recall` and `closing`. It is 14% of pre-loop fuel.
- Stage probes in the loop (57.6k cut loops). A cut loop spends 21.7k and weighs k≈9 of n≈25 groups. 54% of cut
  loops carry a bag (24.5k each, against 18.3k).
  - Each group costs ~1.5-1.7k before clearing.
  - Crew work is ~27% of the loop: `crew_work` ~1.5k a call, `plan_crew` 0.7-2.5k, the crewable bound ~1k.
  - `live_steps` is ~210 a call, 7 calls a cut loop. 65% of calls find no slot; the slot checks cost ~385 each and
    79% of them fail.
- Ordering by the pre-facts bound would not help (an `@B` trace at 100M, 64 games). Among loops costing over 20k, the
  final best is found after 20k in 11% (no bag) and 16.5% (banking). Those bests mostly rank 5th-10th or lower by
  `pre_prune_upper`, so the bound does not predict them. Not pursued.

**Steps** (cumulative, each its own knob or step). Fuel is bench.py's wide set (52 games). The 100M mean is per turn
from round 2. The farm-partial count is over the 52 real-budget games, one side (base: 16,259, OOF 803, mean 54,550,
p99 95,967).

| Step | What | 100M mean (p99) | farm-partial, real |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | oc-base1 | 55,771 (119,182) | 16,259 |
| s1 `race_memo` | the allies' sums in `gems_short` (by horizon), `race_left` (posted bags) and `gems_share` (allies alive), and `World::ally_rate`, kept by `(world.observations, round)`; our bag still read each call (a kill mid-turn changes it) | 54,821 (-950; p99 116,977) | 13,878 (-15%) |
| s2 `loop_memo` | in the loop: `strong`/`kited` read once for the loop's group, `exposure` kept per group (`home_side` is static), the walk range from the belief, `too_late`'s tribute from the facts, the travel dash read once | 54,458 (-363) | 13,508 |
| s3 `race_results`, `expect_memo`, `early_prune` | race_left and gems_share kept by observation and bag; `may_expect`'s enemies in sight read once a loop; the last prune before clearing tried first at the static walk (a lower bound on the trip: the walk round live camps is never shorter, and by way of spawn takes the recall's trip), skipping `live_steps`, the respawn wait, via and healed for groups it rules out; not for a group that may become the help call | 54,397 (-61) | 12,839 |
| s4 | `held` tests the claim before `strong` (the skip loop past `stop`) | 54,373 (-24) | 12,787 |
| s5 | a turn handed to `farm_banking` delegates before reading our own facts (recall line, output, health), which the banking call reads again | 54,344 (-29); p99 114,978 (-3.5%) | 12,370 (-24%) |

At 100M no loop cuts and every group is weighed, so the 100M mean understates what s3-s5 save on cut loops. The
farm-partial count is the better measure.

| A/B (vs oc-base1) | Suites | Games | Win % | 95% CI | OOF cand / ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| s1 | fresh-513011..513050 | 20,480 | 50.6 | 49.9-51.3 | 211.0k / 226.5k |
| s3 | fresh-513011..513050 | 20,480 | 50.7 | 50.0-51.4 | 210.9k / 228.1k |
| s5 (SPRT 0.50/0.51: H1 at 7,874 games; early stop flatters it) | fresh-513011..513050 | 7,874 | 51.4 | 50.3-52.5 | 77.8k / 84.0k |
| **s5 confirm** (unused seeds) | fresh-513051..513090 | 20,480 | **50.5** | 49.8-51.2 | 213.5k / 228.3k |
| s5, `--mix varied` | fresh-513091..513100 | 5,120 | 51.9 | 50.5-53.3 | 59.7k / 63.5k |
| s5 vs panel-astraeus | fresh-513101..513120 | 10,240 | 55.2 | 54.3-56.2 | 103.1k / 113.2k |
| oc-base1 vs panel-astraeus (same suites) | fresh-513101..513120 | 10,240 | 54.5 | 53.6-55.5 | 111.2k / 112.2k |
| s5 vs panel-proteus | fresh-513101..513120 | 10,240 | 53.9 | 52.9-54.9 | 100.5k / 109.9k |
| oc-base1 vs panel-proteus (same suites) | fresh-513101..513120 | 10,240 | 52.0 | 51.0-52.9 | 109.0k / 109.7k |

Verdict: kept (s5, all knobs on). The gain is small and the same everywhere: +0.5 to +0.7 against oc-base1 (s1, s3, and
s5 on the confirm seeds, 20k games each), +1.9 on varied maps, and +0.7 and +1.9 more than oc-base1 against astraeus and proteus.
OOF turns are 6-9% fewer. Every replay at 100M is identical to oc-base1's. The size is what the diagnostics
predict: the steps save ~10-15% of a cut loop's equivalent fuel, worth about half a point.

What lost or was dropped, and why:
- **Never cutting the loop** is level. The extra OOF turns cancel the gain, so fuel has to be saved, not spent.
- **Ordering groups by the pre-facts bound** was dropped before coding: the bound ranks missed bests low (above).
  The loop's tie-breaks also favour whichever group is weighed first, so a new order is not exact at 100M.
- **Cheaper `live_steps` slot checks** were not built. A log of flipped camp tiles could shortcut the failing
  `same_labels` checks, but the probe puts the whole `live_steps` cost at ~1.4k a cut loop. That is ~0.15 points
  at best.
- **`crew_work` and `plan_crew` memos** were not built. Each runs once per group per loop with inputs that change
  every turn, so there is nothing to keep.
- The rest of the pre-loop cost is diffuse: `update_champion` ~2k a cut turn, `pre_prune_upper` 1.3k (already
  SIMD), World update ~5.8k in all. Each item is 1-2% and not worth the risk.
- The early prune also skips `live_steps`' label snapshot updates for the groups it prunes. In principle that history
  could change a later label check. Every bench replay at 100M stayed identical.

Tools (private): the patched runner is in the session scratchpad (`FASTRUNNER_PROF_BLOCKS`, `_COUNT`, `_CUT`, `@L@`).
Scripts are in `replays/fuel/ocfuel/` (`bench.sh`, `ab.sh`, `prof/mkprof.sh`, `prof/run{b,c,d,f}.sh`).

## SPSA retune (ocean, 2026-11-05)

`tools/tune/tune.py` run `replays/tune/oc2` on `bots/ocean_tune`: ocean's draft5 bot before R1+F1 (CHANGES 402, no
resign check), tunified with 61 constants, one more than d1's 51 (`crew_tank_line` and `max_exposure` tuned apart
from `recall_health_fraction` and `mid_exposure`; `life_value`, `gem_value`, `tribute_value` and `recall_value`
tuned, with turn_order.cc reading fixed `turn_*` copies because its rank codes need them modulo 15). Panel: astraeus,
proteus and `variants/ocean-pretune` (ocean before the tune), own drafts, ladder maps only (`pool: maps`), 64 maps and
4 sign pairs an iteration, weights win 0.7 / gems 0.2 / gold 0.1, a 0.3, c 0.12. 06:40-12:10 UTC, 1,288 iterations,
1.98M games. The candidates' mean panel win rate by iteration: 49.5% (1-100), 50.8% (101-300), 51.9% (301-600),
52.8% (601-900), 53.0% (901-1288).

Biggest moves (default -> it 1288): `draft_recall_health_fraction` .329 -> .227, `safe_recall_health_fraction` .144
-> .109, `chip_value` .334 -> .217, `track_horizon` 9 -> 4, `chain_bag_limit` 45 -> 34, `big_gems` 55 -> 70,
`tribute_value` 100 -> 83.2, `life_value` 300 -> 273, `siege_hit_share` .781 -> .893, `siege_rounds` 64 -> 76,
`gold_price_scale` 1.41 -> 1.64, `crew_ban_rounds` 33 -> 26, `tribute_window` 8 -> 10.

**Port.** `tune.py apply` (`bots/variants/ocean_tune-oc2`), then each `diana_tune` reference in ocean_tune's params.h
becomes an `inline constexpr` holding the float32 the tuner patched (`struct.pack('<f')`; a literal already in
params.h is kept when it is the same float32), and turn_order.cc takes ocean_tune's `turn_*` reads. A check parses
every literal back: all 33 floats and 28 ints are byte-exact; tune.h's double literals compile to the same float32s
(no double-rounding case). R1+F1 rule out replay identity with the tuned run's bot, so the same params.h went onto
ocean as it was before R1+F1 (`bots/variants/oc2-final-port`): at 100M it replays identically to the applied bot
(16/16 default set, 52/52 wide with test drafts), with 0.26-0.31% less fuel (constexpr instead of the patched block).
`bots/variants/oc-tuned` is oc-base1 with that params.h and turn_order.cc.

**Held-out A/Bs.** Own drafts, fast runner, real fuel, ladder-mix suites from seeds 509100-509199 (never in the
tuning pool), 20,480 games each.

## Map-conditioned constants: diagnostic (ocean, 2026-11-05)

Could constants pay as functions of draft-time map features, θ(map) = θ0 + W·z? Existing data only, no games.
Details, the logging patch and a contextual-SPSA design are in `research/ideas-2026-11-05/mapcond.md`; scripts are in
`mapcond-tools/`.

- **Data.** tune.py keeps no per-game scores (`work/` is deleted, despite the docstring's "games/"). Its seeded
  `plan()` rebuilds every iteration's Δ, c_k, maps and sides exactly: the recomputed x updates match `history.jsonl`
  to 1e-16 on all 78,507 (oc2) and 92,460 (oc3) coordinates.
- **SPSA logs, iteration level: no signal, and no power.** The fit is the paired differences on Δ ⊗ [epoch, mean z],
  over 9 features (log area, picks, rotational symmetry, spawn distance, camp density, log gems, Monolith and Golem
  gem share, contested share, altars), against 500 permutations. Interactions with |t| > 2: 26 against a null of 25.4
  (oc2) and 32 against 27.9 (oc3); omnibus p 0.31 and 0.19. An iteration's 64 maps vary its mean features by only
  0.09-0.12 SD, so SE(W) is 0.14 / 0.07, ten times the main gradients themselves. The prize bound is vacuous.
- **Held-out A/Bs, per map.**
  - oc2's gain (oct-a, 20,480 games) depends on the map: p 0.002, replicated on oct-b paired against astraeus and
    proteus at p 0.018 (slope correlation +0.89). It never changes sign: +1.5 to +4.7 in every bucket, smallest on
    rotational and many-altar maps.
  - The profile is mostly generic: divided by mean effect, it correlates +0.89 / +0.75 with the pooled profile of 8
    unrelated 20k-game A/Bs. Every edge shows less on high-gem, long-spawn and many-altar maps.
  - oc3's direction: no dependence (p 0.12, 0.88 and 0.43 on confirm, confirm2 and the panel).
- **Prize.**
  - Choosing the tuned or untuned vector per map, cross-validated between independent A/Bs: +0.05 ± 0.05 (oc2) and
    -0.10 to +0.10 (oc3).
  - A per-map step length along oc2's direction, on a quadratic model: ≤ 0.26 points, mostly generic, so it can't
    be harvested.
  - Directions the global tune never moved (gradients flipping sign between kinds of map) are unmeasurable with this
    data.
- **Decision: not run.** Next step: the 10-line per-game logging patch to tune.py (applied 2026-11-06: `games.jsonl`).
  Per-game z brings SE(W) to about 0.010 / 0.0075 in one oc-sized run, enough to detect any interaction worth about
  0.25 points and to pin the total prize to about ±0.5 points. Run the contextual SPSA (no extra games per iteration,
  since ∂f/∂B_ij = z_j ∂f/∂θ_i) only if that run passes the decision rule in mapcond.md.

**SPSA retune round oc4** (`replays/tune/oc4`, 2026-11-05/06, ocean). Retunes for CHANGES 413-414 (the emblem fight
value and the gold funnel), which moved the farm/fight balance oc2's constants were tuned on.

*Why oc3 was level, and what oc4 changed.* The per-parameter gradients of oc2 and oc3, rebuilt from history.jsonl
(the sign vectors replay from the seed; scratchpad `oc4/gradsig.py`), show three things:
- Most of oc3's 67 constants carried no signal. 55 had |t| < 2, and several of its "biggest moves" flipped sign
  between oc2 and oc3 (`big_gems`, `siege_rounds`, `safe_recall`, `camp_risk`): that is drift around an optimum.
- The largest t were the ints whose range spans only ±1 at 2: `pursuit_steps` (t -10 in oc2, +11 in oc3),
  `ostrich_rounds` and `max_wait`. Their ±1 probe measures curvature, not slope, and they never moved off 2.
- Real, same-sign signal in both runs was confined to a few: `track_horizon`, `pick_up_radius`, `chip_value`,
  `threat_radius`, `pair_hold_share`, `tribute_window`, `chain_bag_limit` and `brake_bag`.
Each candidate's score is about 0.07 noise over its games, and that noise is game noise, so dropping constants does
not cut it. What a smaller set saves is the random walk of flat constants. oc3's other problem was the objective:
only 1 opponent in 5 was its own base, and older bots made up the rest. It gained +0.9 there but nothing head-to-head.

*The set*, 23 constants (17 floats, 6 ints):
- 413/414's `fight_weight`, `fight_camp_prior` and `funnel_wealth`, and a new `funnel_power` (the -1 exponent).
- Shop timing: a new `shop_gain_scale` (wants_shop's purchase saving against the trip; 1 = off), and `heal_trip_fraction`.
- Farm: `gold_price_scale`, `pick_up_radius`, `chain_bag_limit`, `pair_hold_share`.
- Combat values: `life_value`, `gem_value`, `chip_value`.
- Retreat/engage: `recall_health_fraction`, `hurt_health_fraction`, `hurt_retreat_ratio`, `home_retreat_ratio`,
  `brake_bag`, `threat_radius`, `track_horizon`, `tribute_window`, and the never-tuned `safety_params`
  `hit_given_reach` and `recall_risk` (now params.h constants that safety.h reads).
- Dropped: the ±1 ints, the constants that were flat or flipped sign in both runs (crew radii, mono, mid-band,
  siege and altar constants, `home_power`, `camp_risk`, `safe_recall`, `big_gems`), Tavi's `gold_farmer_weight`
  and the draft's `draft_recall_health_fraction`.

*The run.* The tunified copy is `bots/ocean_tune3`: oc-base3 plus the four knobs, at their defaults. At 100M it
replays identically to oc-base3 (52/52 wide with test drafts, 92/92 one-altar and df-mono), with +0.06% fuel. The
opponents were oc-base3 twice (half the games head-to-head), `variants/astraeus-now-1105` and panel-proteus. The pool
was the ladder maps (weight 8) and fresh-526000..526019. Each iteration drew 64 maps with 4 sign pairs, 2,048 games.
Weights were win 0.75, gems 0.25 and gold 0 (gold-pricing constants were in the set), with a 0.25, A 100 and c 0.12.
It ran 23:13-02:54 UTC, 750 iterations and 1.54M games, and was stopped by STOP on a plateau. The mean candidate win
rate over the four slots by iteration: 53.15% (1-200), 53.51% (201-300), 54.31% (301-400), 54.30% (401-500),
54.15% (501-600), 54.29% (601-700), 54.22% (701-750). That is +1.1, flat from iteration 300.

Moves (default -> it 750, t over the run):

| constant | value | t |
|---|---|---|
| `fight_weight` | 0.5 -> 0.611 | +2.0 (+3.4 at it 300) |
| `chain_bag_limit` | 34 -> 26 | -2.9 |
| `track_horizon` | 4 -> 3 | -2.9 |
| `shop_gain_scale` | 1 -> 0.822 | -1.9 |
| `funnel_power` | -1 -> -1.161 | -1.5 |

| `gold_price_scale` | 1.641 -> 1.365 | -1.4 |

| `hurt_health_fraction` | .441 -> .488 | +1.2 |
| others | within 6% (`hit_given_reach` .25 -> .236, `recall_risk` .2 -> .194, `funnel_wealth` 300 -> 292, `fight_camp_prior` 500 -> 518) | \|t\| < 1 |

The gold moves agree with each other: with the funnel pricing gold higher on the rich body, the uniform scale falls
and the funnel steepens. `track_horizon` 3 and a lower `chain_bag_limit` continue oc2/oc3's direction.

*Port* (scratchpad `oc4/port4.sh`). `tune.py apply` gives `bots/variants/ocean_tune3-oc4`. Its diff is ported onto
a copy of oc-base3: every constant becomes an exact float32 `constexpr` (all 17 floats and 6 ints parse back
byte-exact), safety.h's two become `constexpr` again from params.h, and the static_assert is restored, since
.236 >= .194 still holds. That copy replays identically to the applied bot at 100M (52/52 wide, 92/92 one-altar and
df-mono), with -0.06% fuel. The same diff was patched onto `bots/variants/oc-base4` (the base by then:
oc-fuel4 + CHANGES 416 and 422): `bots/variants/oc-tuned4`, frozen (READY). Its diff to oc-base4 touches params.h (16
values, 4 new constants), farm.cc (the funnel's power), shop.cc (`shop_gain_scale` in both wants_shop tests) and
safety.h.

## Farm routes via spawn (2026-11-05, ocean)

Farm's pricing of a recall to spawn and on to a group (FarmRecall), and of a walk home: three accounting bugs and six
ideas, each one a compile-time knob in `params::route` of one dev copy (`bots/variants/oc-dev`: `bots/ocean` as copied
at 04:26 that day, before its later draft.h and world.cc edits, plus the knobs). Each variant is that copy with its
knobs set. All rows are against `variants/oc-r0` (a plain copy of ocean), both bots on their own drafts, under the fast
runner. The suites are ladder-mix fresh ones at 2,560 maps a chunk, which is 5,120 games:
- stage 1: `ocr-c0..c5`, seeds 506000-059;
- combinations: `ocr-c20..c39`, seeds 506200-399;
- per-idea confirmation: `ocr-c40..c47`, seeds 506400-479;
- final: `ocr-v0..v3`, seeds 506900-939;
- `--mix varied` check: `suites/merged/ocr-varied0..3`, seeds 506600-639.

Stopping: a run stopped once at least 2 chunks were in and the 95% CI excluded 50%, or after 6 chunks (4 for a
confirmation). The control, oc-dev with every knob off, plays byte-identical replays at 100M fuel; at the real budget
it read 50.43% (5,120 games, OOF +1.9%), so the build alone moves fuel-gated turns.

**Bugs.**
- **B1 (real, its fix lost).** FarmRecall charged a heal turn and measured the walk from spawn's centre. mend_step,
  though, takes the heal turn on the landing tile and moves only to strictly closer spawn tiles. So the first step out
  costs nothing when it stays on spawn, and the walk starts at the landing tile, one tile off the centre.
  - The fix: a per-landing-tile walk (`recall_walk`, shop.cc) and a per-group landing table for the bound
    (`landing_near`).
  - It loses: cheaper via-spawn routes are taken more and are worse. The fix's own fuel was cut from +12% to +1.5%
    farm partial evaluations.
- **B2 (real, rare, level).** recall_to_farm's keep test walked the static distance without the loop's live-camp
  detour (`live_steps`). In the bench, only 41 of 82 drops were walk drops, and those mostly came from
  respawn ≥ walk.
- **B3 (real double count, its fix level).** By way of spawn, the loop credits the stop's heal value and also budgets
  the trips against usable_health (the full-health budget) instead of trip_spare. Worked example: M=1000, H=500,
  line 0.144, crew_trip_risk 0.769 give usable_health 1113 and trip_spare 463. With damage 600:
  - the walk route takes 1 extra trip home and the via route 0;
  - the heal credit is ~11.1 rounds and a trip ~17, so via gets ~28 rounds for one heal, against ~11-15 if consistent.
  - Fix: `overlap` = min(credit, the trips' rounds saved), counted once (farm.cc).
- Turns against rounds: a channel is 5 turn ends, and FarmRecall, HomeTrip and the loop price them alike. No other
  mismatch was found.

**Ideas.**
- R1: a recall out while carrying, where the bag banks after the group (farm.cc recall_out, the per-group via; bank.cc
  recall_to_farm's healed-trip test).
- R2: a kited group's spare health by way of spawn is the full-health spare, at weight r2. It barely applies: kited
  groups occur only on shared-gem maps with big groups.
- R3: the stop's heal weight (`r3_heal`), and its shop value as everything our gold buys (`r3_shop`).
- R4: the recall out of an altar, priced as FarmRecall with its stop's value at weight r4 (the altar_recall and pre_alt
  bounds).
- W1: an empty-handed walk to spawn for the turn-end heal, when it beats the other routes by ≥ w1 rounds.
- F1: during our recall's channel, the farm pick is re-weighed each turn (`farm_turn<..., repricing>`) instead of
  freezing the group chosen at the start. It keeps going while some group still goes by way of spawn and may switch
  groups.
  - In the bench: 98 switched keeps and 197 drops.

**Result.**
- Kept: R1 and F1. Of the single ideas only R1 passed its confirmation clearly. F1 confirmed above 50 but not
  significantly, and its stage-1 read came from an early stop.
- R1+F1 beats R1 alone (51.33, 10,240 games) and reads 51.37 on the fresh final seeds. Neither R4 nor W1 adds anything
  on top (49.41 and 50.26).
- Lost or level: B1-B3 (the fixes are right as accounting but don't win), R2 (a near no-op), every R3 weight with and
  without shop value (heal 1 is best: the stop is priced about right), R4 and W1 (level, and W1 costs +2-3% OOF).
- R3 and B1 say the same thing: making the via-spawn stop look cheaper or more valuable loses. R1 and F1 win by using
  the recall in more situations, and re-deciding during the channel, not by pricing it higher.
- `bots/variants/oc-best` is oc-dev with `r1` and `f1` on, the other knobs off and their code left in under the knobs.
- Merged into `bots/ocean` as plain code (CHANGES 404, frozen as `bots/variants/oc-base1`): bench.py at 100M replays identically to oc-best
  (16/16 default, 52/52 wide with test drafts). Real budget, wide with test drafts: mean 54,375, p99 95,580, 831 OOF
  (oc-best 54,683 / 95,645 / 840; oc-r0 53,705 / 95,419 / 813).

## Fresh suites recalibrated to the ladder (2026-11-05, tools/mapgen calibration 2)

`mapgen suite --out DIR` now makes `--mix ladder` suites: ladder-like presets and mutations under calibration 2,
fitted to the 128 ladder maps, no stress families. **Fresh suites made from here on are not comparable with earlier
ones**: the `maps/fresh-*` used by every result above are `varied` suites of calibration 1 (three quarters stress
maps, 29% with 6+ altars, half the guarded camp groups the ladder has). `--mix varied-v1` remakes those maps byte for
byte (index.json records `mix: varied-v1`); a rebuild of `maps/gen` or `maps/gen-s1` (no `--out`) still defaults to
it. On 20 held-out suites the ladder mix's mean KS against the ladder is 0.067 (calibration 1's suites 0.209) and 8% of
its maps are beyond the ladder's p90 nearest-neighbour distance (35%): [mapgen-vs-ladder-2026-11-05.md](mapgen-vs-ladder-2026-11-05.md#after-calibration-2).
astraeus mirror games: 256/256 complete on a ladder suite (sides 28-29 included). No bot has been A/B'd on the new
suites yet, so how much a win rate moves between the two kinds is unknown. The first, ocean's draft (below), moved
not at all: 53.0% on both kinds.

## Idea C: object permanence and bush play (ocean, 2026-11-05)

Design, evidence and knobs: [ideas-2026-11-05/bush.md](ideas-2026-11-05/bush.md). Dev copy `variants/oc-bush-dev`,
knobs `params::bush::`, all off = oc-base1 byte-identical (bench 16/16). Against oc-base1, own drafts, fast runner,
real fuel; `bush-s1` = fresh-512000..512019, `bush-s2` = fresh-512020..512039 (ladder mix, 5,120 maps each).

Ladder evidence (1025 post-patch ranked games from big-arm): hiding in a bush halves a hurt retreater's death rate
(13% vs 28% under 25% health), but pursuers walk the same way whether they see it or not. A ranged shooter hidden in
a bush takes 24 damage back over 2 rounds against 85 from the open (self-play: 41 vs 64). 62% of bushes near
enemies hold an enemy ward. Our bots place ~105 wards per team per game, 74 of them bush wards.

bl0 on the panel (panel-check-514510, 5,120 games each; the base's rate in brackets): astraeus 55.3 (55.6),
proteus 54.0 (53.7), demeter 57.4 (56.3), ocean-td 73.5 (74.4), v67 70.4 (69.9). The mean difference is +0.1, with no
member below its fail line. Assuming enemies don't follow into bushes they can't see costs nothing against these
five, and gains nothing either.

A trace of rw2 (16 bench games) shows where its fuel goes. It placed 35 wards, each followed by a ~2k Safety rebuild,
but the scan ran on 23% of turns at ~580 fuel (up to 7k), nearly all of it in the per-enemy reach bound
(`attack_reach_in_turn`) before any cheap test. Reordering the tests, skipping the scan within ward cooldown of our
last ward and replacing the reach call by a static bound (rw2e) still cost +0.25% fuel over identical bench games, on
41k of 42k turns: the per-enemy loop itself, ~140 fuel a turn. Out-of-fuel turns on fuel-saturated maps are that
sensitive: +0.25% of fuel gave +5-6% of them, and it ate the 10M ceiling's +1.1 points. rw3 runs the loop only after
a fight or a health loss (+0.09% fuel, +1.6-2.0% OOF) and is still level, so the reveal ward wins too rarely to show.

No knob of idea C is kept: every one is level against oc-base1 after its sweep.


reveal_ward fires rarely: in 400 rw2 games the ward-placer hits an enemy later in the same turn 0.43 times a game
(REF 0.06). Its ward is usually spent on the turn-end bush ward.
