## Turn order and ally coordination (2026-11-02, astraeus e9c37971)

Against frozen `variants/astraeus-e9c3797`, own drafts, fastrunner, 10,240 games a row (20 fresh suites of 512) unless
noted. Notes, traces and scripts: [turn-order-2026-11-02/](turn-order-2026-11-02/README.md).

| Change | Win % | 95% CI | OOF cand / ref | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Idle allies nearer an enemy act later (`ast-idle-nearlate`, `plain_priority` only) | 51.5 / 52.3 (6,828, unused) / 52.3 | ~52.0 of 27,308 | level | **kept: CHANGES 293** |
| Idle allies nearer an enemy act earlier (`ast-idle-nearearly`) | 44.4 | 43.4-45.4 | 72,968 / 74,109 | lost |
| Dead allies ranked below idle ones (`ast-deadlast`) | 48.2 | 47.2-49.2 | 73,678 / 73,653 | lost |
| Ally seat commitment v1 (top-seat planning + soft holds) | 46.6 | 45.6-47.6 | 81,883 / 77,739 | lost |
| Ally seat commitment v2 (no soft holds, move priced at the release seat) | 49.45 of 20,480 | ~48.8-50.1 | +2.6-6% | level, held as a base |
| Worst-case enemy order (`ast-wc`: no persistence fallback, permutation bound, Safety) | 49.6 | 48.7-50.6 | +14% | level, held |

- **Act late when nothing needs you early.** An idle champion near an enemy that acts earlier only hands the enemy the
  reply: in rounds with a dead ally, deadlast's idle-near allies acted 1.4 enemy turns sooner, took 38% more damage and
  died 35% more, dealing no more. Ordering idle allies by nearness swings 7 points. The baseline's dead-above-idle rank
  gets part of this. Seat v1 lost the same way: each of its two parts moved low-need allies earlier, ~2 points each.
- **Ally commitment is real but rare.** 3.0% of bids assuming acting first acted after their enemy (0.28 a game), 89%
  pushed down by a later teammate's kill bid; outcomes were no worse. v2 cut hard breaks from 1.9% to 0.25%.
- **Safety's next-round count is wrong in 32.6% of reads within 4**: 49% of its underestimates from our own slot
  moving after the move, 31% from an unsettled enemy moving up.
- **Round-boundary doubles** in contact land kills at 2.9% against 1.3% for a single turn, but only 14.5% go to one
  champion (no ladder team over 13%). Unbuilt.
- **Small:** forks 0.25 a game; an ally holding our only hitting tile 0.8% of strike turns.
- **Kill conversion is not order:** astraeus kills 30% of enemies under 25% health in reach, Fish and PBG 45%; enemy
  acting first is no more common in escapes than kills.
- Worst case costs fuel mostly through `double_unacted` doubling a blow already widened to two turns (more often now).
  The adversarial sparring bot (`ast-adv`, static between bids) is as strong as astraeus but punishes neither.

Follow-up on astraeus 294 (against `variants/astraeus-294`, 10,240 games a row unless noted):

| Change | Win % | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Worst case ported, `double_unacted` fixed (`ast-pwc`) | 50.5 / 49.8; 50.4 / 51.2 | level, +21% out-of-fuel turns; held |
| Predicted enemy order for kill bids and `drop_stun` (`ast-pred`) | 50.3 / 49.7 | level, +37% out-of-fuel; dropped |
| Learning a static opponent online (`ast-pred-learn`, against the user's rule) | 49.8 / 49.3 | dropped |
| Joint worst case per tile (`ast-safety`: base blows + the m largest second turns) | 46.6 / 46.9 | level at 100M fuel, 2.1x out-of-fuel turns; held for a cheaper form |
| Strike pledges in the payload (`ast-comms` v1) | 50.8 / 50.8 | the gain is keeping our own bid; readers +0.00 |
| Keep our own kill bid, no message (`ast-follow` v1, + no bid while channelling v2) | 50.3 / 50.2 | level; base of CHANGES 295 |
| Kill-now value on all partial damage (`ast-kill1`) | 49.7 (-0.92 paired) | lost: fewer engagements; don't retry |
| Kill-now value on kills only (`ast-kill1b`) | 50.5 / 50.3 | level |
| Bids at the real distance (`ast-kill2`, = v2 + reach) | 50.5 / 50.5; 50.4 of 40,448 | **kept: CHANGES 295** |

- Enemy order: a predictor beats both fixed rules on calibration (ladder Brier 0.086 against last-read 0.101 and
  worst case 0.476) but makes the same calls at 0.5. The worst-case kill bids were already in force against astraeus
  opponents (the fallback is off in 99.8% of turns); worst case in Safety halves undercounts and adds as many
  overcounts. Old damage sums gave every unacted enemy a second turn: more than the order allows in 45% of reads with
  2+ enemies (`safety-fuel.md`).
- Kill conversion is not a choice problem: kills on offer are taken 97.4% of the time. Near an enemy under 25%,
  33% of our champion-turns can't reach it and 20% retreat on Safety's call; ~2% would kill with another choice.

## Camp aggro: waking camps onto enemies (2026-11-02/03, astraeus 294 variants)

Camps attack at the next round's start, before any champion moves, hitting the nearest champion in reach (ties to the
earlier seat). An enemy that has already acted, or is channelling, is held in place for that first hit: damaging or
stunning any member of a sleeping group whose strikers reach it, from outside their reach, puts the camp on it.
Variants and diffs: [aggro-2026-11-03/](aggro-2026-11-03/README.md). All against `variants/astraeus-38aa25c` (CHANGES
294), both bots on their own drafts (`--no-test-draft`), fastrunner native, on alext (whose `maps/gen` differs from
the local, recovered one).

- `aggro-s`/`s6`: at the turn's end (bot.cc `aggro_camp`), an unused basic attack or a damage/stun cast when every
  woken striker's nearest champion is a held enemy, never us or an ally (seen, or seen within 5 rounds near).
- `aggro-x2`..`x8`: the strike search credits a woken hit on a held enemy with `hit_worth` (combat/plan.cc `wake`) and
  may basic-attack or ground-cast such groups; x3-x8 make the same decisions as x3 at falling cost.

Fixed samples, 52,394 games each (ladder, `maps/gen`, `maps/gen-s1`, `maps/fresh-92001`..`92100`):

| Variant | Win % | 95% CI | Out-of-fuel turns vs REF |
|---|---|---|---|
| aggro-s (turn end) | 50.05 | 49.6-50.5 | +20.3% |
| aggro-s6 (s, cheaper) | 50.05 | 49.6-50.5 | +10.3% |
| aggro-x8 (search credit) | 49.68 | 49.3-50.1 | +9.1% |
| aggro-x8-nomono (sleeping Monoliths stay banned) | 49.77 | 49.3-50.2 | +9.6% |
| aggro-x2-safe-nomono (no credited wake with an unseen ally maybe near) | 49.56 | 49.1-50.0 | +10.9% |
| aggro-x6-null (the search code, weight 0: the base's decisions) | 49.77 | 49.3-50.2 | +8.6% |
| aggro-x8s6 (x8 + s6's turn-end hook) | 49.95 | 49.5-50.4 | +18.7% |
| aggro-x8-w05 / -w3 (aggro_weight 0.5 / 3) | 49.73 / 49.67 | 49.3-50.2 / 49.2-50.1 | +9.9% / +8.1% |
| aggro-s6-min10 (= s6 game for game: no striker is under 20) | 50.05 | 49.6-50.5 | +10.3% |
| aggro-s6-min40 (no lone-Wolf wakes; 272 games differ from s6) | 50.04 | 49.6-50.5 | +10.0% |
| aggro-s6-selfin (may stand in a woken reach) | 50.07 | 49.6-50.5 | +10.6% |
| aggro-s6-mem0 / -mem12 (ally memory 0 / 12 rounds) | 50.04 / 49.97 | 49.6-50.5 / 49.5-50.4 | +10.3% / +10.2% |
| aggro-s6-nospell / -spell30 (basic attacks only / casts worth 30) | 49.94 / 50.09 | 49.5-50.4 / 49.7-50.5 | +9.5% / +10.4% |
| aggro-s6-nomono | 50.07 | 49.6-50.5 | +10.2% |
| aggro-s6-unheld (wakes onto enemies yet to act too; 4054 games differ, 1332 winners flip, 666 each way) | 50.05 | 49.6-50.5 | +10.3% |

Screens before (SPRT 0.50 vs 0.52 stopping low on ladder, gen, gen-s1, fresh-9100..9115; then 0.50 vs 0.51 on
gen..fresh-92040): x2-nomono 50.2 of 2731, s 48.9 of 1193, x2-safe 49.8 of 2592, x2-safe-nomono 50.0 of 2002, x3
50.1 of 2018, s6 50.4 of 4143; x6 49.3 of 3378, s6 49.9 of 8143, x6-nomono 49.6 of 3158, x6-w2 49.4 of 3919, all H0.
The local 1196-game reads (x2-nomono 52.3, s 52.1) were noise.

- **Nothing reaches significance; the wake is real but small.** In x8's games (1196, ladder/gen/gen-s1, `ab_farm.py`)
  REF dies to camps 1.2 times a game against CAND's 1.1 (-0.1, CI [-0.2, +0.0]); gold, captures and camp damage are
  level. A held enemy is in a sleeping striker's reach in ~21% of the strike searches that read camps.
- **The out-of-fuel increase is the code's cost, not different games.** x6-null plays the base's decisions (bench:
  52/52 replays identical at 100M fuel) yet has +8.6% out-of-fuel turns. Paired on identical bench searches it costs
  +1528 fuel a search, all in `read` (`srch_pair.py`); searches run ~1 turn in 12, so +0.2% of all fuel. The excess is
  broad (CAND more on 6959 maps, fewer on 3938; the top 200 maps hold half; `oof_maps.py`), mostly `decide`: turns
  near the cap anywhere tip over. Its price in games is at most a few tenths (x6-null 49.77, CI 49.3-50.2).
- **Where the fuel went** (x7/x8 meters, `aggro-x8-meter-on-x8.diff`, `agm.py`): with no held enemy in reach,
  `aggro_possible` still costs a median ~0.9k, a groups_near query at our tile the base never makes for a plain
  attacker; with one (21%), read_members +2.1k (touches flips on), the group checks and find_wakers ~3.7k (x7: 5.4k),
  read_camps' member loop ~2k. Cheaper forms: x7 (cached group verdicts) +27 a search; x8 (static per-group reach boxes,
  held enemies and find_wakers' champion list once a search) -49 a search; x9 (boxes instead of groups_near) +454,
  since groups_near's per-tile cache persists across turns and x8's query was warming later reads; x10 (a static
  dilated camp board before groups_near) +38. All exact (bench replays identical).
- The turn-end hook (aggro-s) cost fuel the same way: s6's cheaper hook halved its out-of-fuel increase (+20% to
  +10%) with identical replays, and neither moved the win rate.

Held: nothing kept. If revisited, luring awake camps (an awake monster stays awake while any champion is in its range,
and hits the nearest) is a different mechanism from waking sleeping ones.

Fuel alone reshuffles games: aggro-s and s6 decide identically at unlimited fuel, yet 26k of their 52k games differ in
length under the real budget. A change touching a few percent of games reads as noise beside that.

## Fuel campaign 6 summary (2026-11-04, astraeus d6e74b6f -> fc6-m6)

Goal: undo the out-of-fuel cost of CHANGES 337 (d6e74b6f, the oscillation fixes; 458,674 / 111,324 OOF turns against
its parent in 20k games) without changing its play; target OOF -50% against d6e74b6f at scale. Six rounds, 14 workers
(hyperion/fuel-campaign-6/BRIEF.md, NOTES.md). **Result: OOF -34.6% at 20k, win rate level (50.1%), and at 100M fuel
every bench replay (322 on nine sets plus the 16-game default bench) is still byte-identical to d6e74b6f's**: the
campaign's play changes act only when fuel is short. The -50% target was not reached.

**Shipped, by round** (effects as measured in each round; the 20k rows are against d6e74b6f on suites unused before):

  +1.4% at the real budget; its census saving did not show at scale.

  (+0.03% to +1.55% total on fight / osc): a check costs 225-1.2k and fires too rarely against the 1.3-3k sim it ends.
- **Reserves that lost** (round 3, tail): farm's loop keeping a cold-pass reserve (48.7%, 48.3%, 49.8% with OOF only
  -0.7%), and the walk sites keeping back the veto's whole turn (49.6%, OOF -1.9%).
- Smaller: cross-turn Reach and distance memos (share; ~250-460 a heavy turn at most), a cross-turn fight-sim memo
  (sides; a content key costs ~400-500 a sim against ~300-700 saved), an exact walk_allies_in table (+0.03 to +0.24%),
  lazy altar steps (init; fs total +0.046%), per-turn veto-count caps (bind on 0.8-2.6% of turns).

**Open leads** (from NOTES):
- The no-check fight work is most of what is left: 84% of first-in-streak OOF turns end before the branch line, in
  want_home's stand, the strike search and the post-strike veto. On OOF turns a `new_fight` is mostly its sim (8.5k);
  only a cheaper sim or fewer stands reaching one (0.91 an OOF turn, a decision-level change) moves it.
- Runaways (games with 50+ OOF still hold 44%): standoffs repeating the same failed searches (make_way/step_field) or
  fight_of each turn; a per-turn failure memo keyed on goals/walls/me would be exact. gen-leaky-diagonals-6811007814's
  overrun in step-guard / static-descend is one such state, reachable from m5b's code.
- Round 1 is now 5% of OOF, all farm: a fs body still needs ~201k for world init (static_camps ~105 a member,
  init_beliefs ~93 a group), so only an indexed plan at 200+ groups or fewer instructions a member lets it act.
- 342's measured loop reserve: dropping it reads -0.7% wasted turns (CI crosses 0) for +5.8% OOF; a tighter reserve
  (skip landings already in the veto's boards) is the lead. Static StandReach tables built mid-game could move into
  the turn-end queue (3% of OOF turns hold one, ~10-13k); the walk_on veto after a strike (~13k a tile).

## Teleport crystal shortcuts (2026-11-03, astraeus 296 variants)

A crystal (10 gold, carry 1, bought on spawn or dead) hops to a free tile within Chebyshev 3 after a 3-turn channel,
walls ignored. astraeus buys one only for pockets no walk reaches (StaticMap::hops). Variants against
`variants/astraeus-10b2313` (CHANGES 296), own drafts, fastrunner native on alext, 52,394 games each (ladder, gen,
gen-s1, fresh-92001..92100); diffs in [crystal-2026-11-03/](crystal-2026-11-03/).

| Variant | Win % | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|
| v1: hop on any walk when it beats walking by 4 turns (lookahead 3, safe start); buy first on spawn | 46.84 | 46.4-47.3 |
| buyonly (v1's buying, no hops) | 47.03 | 46.6-47.5 |
| nobuy (v1's hops with crystals bought only as before) | 49.99 | 49.6-50.4 |
| v2: buy last (after shards) | 48.67 | 48.2-49.1 |
| v2-buyonly | 48.55 | 48.1-49.0 |
| v3: v2, buying only when a static plan (BFS from spawn, then landings by channel time, steps of 3) saves 8 steps to the farm choice | 49.81 | 49.4-50.2 |
| v3-b4 (saves 4) | 49.64 | 49.2-50.1 |
| v5: v3 plus routing: with a crystal, walk to the plan's best hop source for the farm choice or any altar, and hop | 49.69 | 49.3-50.1 |
| v4: v3's plan, buying when the rounds saved times the farm value a round beat 1.5x the gold's price (and 4 steps) | 49.71 | 49.3-50.2 |

- **The buying is the cost.** v1's hops added nothing over its buying (v2 48.67 vs v2-buyonly 48.55); bought first,
  the 10 gold held back emblems (-3.2). Gated by a plan of the real saving (v3) it is level, not a gain.
- **v3 across a panel** (gauntlet.py, 11,436 games an opponent, paired by map and side): vs v67 -0.7 [-1.4, +0.0],
  v66 +0.5, v65 -0.2, demeter +0.6; mean +0.08 points.
- **Univardisty of Shingtonwash** (fetch_replays, 98 games): ~4 hops a game, all on wall maps, from the same few sources
  next to their spawn. In their 01concentrated_wealth game (`cambc matches download ce8e0389...`) they bought 42
  crystals in 1192 rounds and hopped 42 times over the NW wall at (13,22) to (17,25), the way out of their spawn to
  the altar (23,24) and the centre group. Our walk there through the NE gap is ~26-32 steps against a hop's ~24:
  ~8-10 steps a trip, which they buy every trip (their gold allows it; ours is short: most of v5's buy attempts on
  that map failed for gold). team_crystals.py's static BFS overstated that walk (87).
- v5's routing works (traced on 01concentrated_wealth: routes built for every group whose hop saves 8, carriers walk
  to the sources) but rarely has a crystal to use. The first v5 build never built its routes (warm_crystal_plan
  returned before the routing step once the levels were done); fixed before its A/B.
- v4's value test (`saved * memory.farm_rate >= 1.5 * prices().per_gold * 10`): the trace put that ratio between 0.5
  and 37 (median ~2.6) over buy checks; level with v3 (49.71). v4 ran with the fresh suites merged
  (`maps/fresh-92all`), the same maps.

Held: nothing kept. Crystals pay for UW, whose economy has gold to spare; ours spends it on emblems first.

## The ostrich and SPSA-tuned constants (2026-11-03, astraeus 6265c2cb; CHANGES 321)

Shipped: diana's ostrich (turn order: an enemy in reach moves us to the danger band's early seats only once we or an
enemy near us lost health within `ostrich_rounds`) and the 51 constants of diana's SPSA run `replays/tune/d1` at its
final iteration (1312), ported to astraeus as `constexpr` values (exact float32s). The port is exact: on fc99b84 it
replays identically to `bots/variants/diana-d1-final` at 100M (24/24 games), with 0.4% less fuel (constexpr instead of
the tuner's patchable block).

05:57-14:51 UTC) against a fixed panel: astraeus fc99b84, demeter, hyperion, v66, v67, crystal-v3, own drafts, on
`maps`, `maps/gen`, `maps/gen-s1` and `maps/fresh-92001..92100`. Mean candidate win rate against the panel by
iteration: 63.3% (1-100), 64.3% (100-300), 65.1% (300-600), 65.7% (600-900), 65.7% (900-1312). The biggest moves:

.6 -> .484, `burst_rounds` 20 -> 15, `help_radius` 8 -> 6, `tribute_window` 6 -> 8, `max_wait` 3 -> 2.

## Exploiter search against the tuned constants; main against v66 and v67 (2026-11-03, astraeus 8a2e8afb)

**Exploiter search** (`tools/tune/league.py`, run `replays/tune/x1`, from d1): the tuned constants (d1's iteration
1312, = CHANGES 321) held fixed (`a` 0, no main games); optuna TPE exploiters over the same 51 constants and ranges
(about 0.5x to 2x each default), 32 trials a round, each on 24 maps from both sides (48 games) against the tuned bot,
d1's map pool, own drafts (Cassi & Issac mirror), diana's base (fc99b84 + the ostrich). The first round was seeded
with the default constants and d1's iterations 100, 300, 454 (d1a), 700 and 1000. A round's best trial with 56%+ was
replayed on 500 more maps (1,000 games) and would have joined the league at 54%+.
- 26 rounds, 832 trials, 15 minutes. Round bests on their 48 games: 54-67% (the best of 32 noisy trials). All 25
  confirmations failed: 42.4-50.7% of 1,000, mean ~46%. None of the seeds came close either.
- A weak adversary (TPE on 51 dimensions with 48-game trials) that probes only the Cassi & Issac mirror, so this rules
  out broad weaknesses of the tuned constants, not narrow ones.
- Tooling: after a fast-runner rebuild changes native cache keys, a tune or league run started before its base bot has
  played once under the new runner patches only the old key's library and compiles every candidate (~15 s each; a
  round took 3 min instead of ~35 s). Restarting the run after the base has played fixes it.

**Main against v66 and v67.** Main at 8a2e8afb (fuel campaign 5, the ostrich and the tuned constants; frozen as
`bots/variants/astraeus-8a2e8afb`) against `bots/baselines/v66` and `v67`, own drafts, real budget, fast runner, on
40 new suites `maps/fresh-97001..97040` (10,240 maps, both sides: 20,480 games each). Logs in
`replays/ab-main-8a2e8afb-vs-v66.log` / `-v67.log`.

| **A1 + A2 + C (kept)** | **50.0** | 49.3-50.7 | 109,707 / 109,265 | 4,710 (3,438) | 904 / 900 |

## v69 against v68: farming and pathing (2026-11-03, astraeus 0c332d65; CHANGES 335-336)

Why v69 did slightly worse than v68 on the ladder: the farming, banking and pathing side. All runs use the fast runner,
own drafts on both sides, and `--no-test-draft`.
- **Ladder.** Corrected extracts of 258 ranked games (sides fixed, extractor 42d84240): v68 59% of 69, v69 63% of 189,
  against different mixes of opponents. v69 captured more (63.5 groups a game against 53.6) and earned more (3,862
  gems by round 600 against 2,884). It took more camp damage (23.3k against 17.2k; 366 a capture against 321) and
  recalled more (51 against 42). Opponents changed between the sets: in several same-map pairs the enemy diverges
  first (rounds 3-4). Where we diverge first (lost_world, the_pond, 01broken_curve, 02fields), v69's opening economy
  was equal or better, and the games were lost in later fights. boss_battle losses are Monolith sieges against
  Vesper (siege area).
- **Local, v69 against v68 head to head** (ladder + fresh-43001..43004, 2,220 games): 52.0% (49.9-54.1); ladder
  49.4% of 172. `ab_farm` farming was equal or slightly better for v69. Camp damage was 23.0k against 22.5k a game,
  recalls 57.6 against 60.7. Flips per 1k alive rounds were 28.1 against 28.3. Oscillation episodes (3+ quiet flips)
  were 2,159 against 2,172.
- **Against ladder compositions** (`variants/v68-td`, test drafts; 5,292 games each): v69 65.6% (64.4-66.9), v68
  65.2% (63.9-66.5); ladder 65.1% against 62.8% of 172. No local sign of a farming or pathing regression in v69.
- **Found and fixed** (in v68 too): the static-descent and wide-route two-turn cycle (CHANGES 335), and a walk
  standing on a respawning group's tile (336), each level on 20,652 games. Together (55805d38) against `bots/baselines/v69`
  (fresh-43021..43040 + ladder, 10,412 games): 49.5% (48.5-50.5); ladder 52.3% of 172; out-of-fuel turns 63,155
  against 64,723.
- **Open, not fixed:**
  - **Ward bumps.** `ward_bushes` (bot.cc) retries the same first 3 tiles of a bush cluster every turn. An ally's
    unseen ward is a hidden blocker, so every try fails. That is ~49 blocked placements a game a side; 42% repeat
    a tile within 2 rounds. It costs fuel and leaves the ward unplaced. Allied ward tiles are not remembered across
    turns.
  - **gen-topo-gatehouse (a 1x10 corridor spawn).** The team jams in single file; v68 jams too. 1,188 quiet spawn
    flips in one game.
  - **An ally holding the only tribute tile.** A banker routed to it waits, and the static descent can walk it back
    (02guardians, mut-fan). `make_way` yields only between two movers.
  - **Ladder 63fd3ae8 game 1** (00rushbait_v2): Issac (480/900) dashed across a hole line to hit an Elk alone at
    round 256. He left at round 259 with 360 hp, walked 5 tiles still in the Elk's reach, and died at round 264
    (Cassi with him). With the walk out priced (`camp_trapped`), round 258 sat on the one-hit margin. Farm's trip
    budget (`trip_spare`, health above the recall line) does not include the walk out of a pocket under fire. Not
    reproduced locally.

## Siege and risk review of v68 against v69 on the ladder; the camp exit's shelter (2026-11-03, astraeus 0c332d65)

**Ladder.** 195 games (v68: 49, v69: 146, many of v69's scrims), re-extracted after a fix to `tools/replay/extract.mjs`.
It read the teams from the group's sides, so in a scrim group whose sides were chosen (`tools/scrim_ladder.py --sides`)
a match on the other sides credited our play to the opponent. Ranked groups were not affected: none of the 54,725
ranked matches on disk has its sides swapped. Now it reads each match's own sides (`EXTRACTOR_VERSION` 2).

On the three opponents both versions met (NEETCoders, Trzy Kwaterki, subscribe to caterpillow), v68 won 63.3% of 30 and
v69 69.0% of 29. Per game:

| | v68 | v69 |
|---|---|---|
| Our deaths | 6.07 | 6.83 |
| Deaths to camps | 0.10 | 0.55 |
| Deaths at an altar | 0.10 | 1.10 |
| Camp damage taken | 15.5k | 22.3k |

All are small samples. 22 of the 32 altar deaths come from one game (047ecefb-4, 03showdown): there Marcella killed
NEETCoders' Prism and took its 1061 gems (r570). She held them for 340 rounds, starting a 107-turn tribute 14 times.
Each start was cancelled under fire, the longest after 64 turns, and she died with the bag at r908, which lost the game
at 874 to 1023. This is the designed rule: `tribute_safe` judges again each turn, over at most `tribute_window` turns.
The 00anvil deaths to the Monolith come from capturing and tributing inside its reach; v68 has them too.

**A death traced exactly.** The harness puppet (`decode_all.mjs`, `gen_puppet.mjs` for the opponent's team) replays
63fd3ae8-1 (00rushbait_v2, v69 against Trzy Kwaterki) exactly in a release build: 1038 to 247, and the same positions.
A debug build matched as far as r260.

1. At r256 Issac (480 hp) dashed across the x=14 hole line and attacked Elk 16 at (16,14) alone (branch `B`, farm group 16).
2. At r258, with 360 hp, `camp_trapped` read a walk out of 4 steps. The Elk's reach had been cut to 2 because Vendetta,
   at (13,11), was 3 from it and acts first (`find_members`): Vendetta "sheltered" every tile 3 or more from the Elk.
3. Vendetta left at r259. The walk out was 6 steps, all in reach, and Issac died at r264 at (20,16).

So the shelter is right for the next camp phase only. The exit walk (`camp_exit_field`, `exit_hits`) priced it for the
whole walk.

**The fix lost.** Each member's own range was carried in `CampHit::range`, with `Safety::camp_range_area()` and
`camp_fire()` for the walk. A/B against astraeus 0c332d65 (frozen as `variants/astraeus-0c332d6`): own drafts, fast
runner, `maps/fresh-7101..7120` (unused before, 256 maps each) plus the 86 ladder maps. Diffs are in
`research/shelter-2026-11-03/`.

| Variant | Win rate of 10,412 | Ladder (172 games) |
|---|---|---|
| shelter1: both the trap test and `flee_camps` use the unsheltered walk | 47.0% (46.0-48.0) | 43.6% |
| shelter2: only `camp_trapped` uses it; `flee_camps` steps as before | 46.6% (45.7-47.6) | 45.9% |

Every suite was below 51%. Leaving the camps earlier costs more than these deaths, so the trap test's optimism is
load-bearing. Both variants were reverted. A fix would have to tell a shelter that stays (a tank on the group) from one
passing by, and nothing here does that cleanly.

## proteus ported into astraeus: dropped (2026-11-04, astraeus aa594c49 + bots/proteus 75d6d885)

Proteus is astraeus d04b171e with enemy turn windows (`turn_window.cc`), a seat ledger in the shared bytes, and seats
assigned by the chance each need is met over the feasible enemy orders (`turn_order.cc`). Every run: own drafts,
fast runner, 40,448 games on maps no A/B had used.
- **proteus against astraeus aa594c49** (fresh-61001..61079): 50.0% (49.5-50.5); out-of-fuel turns 374k against 232k.
- **Ported onto aa594c49** (fresh-62001..62079): 50.3% (49.8-50.8); out-of-fuel turns 361k against 224k.
- **With fixes** (fresh-63001..63079): 49.7% (49.2-50.2); 332k against 227k. The fixes: a 1 KB subset table filled and
  copied for every candidate need, replaced by a direct sum; an escape blow over two turns counted in both the
  unavoidable part and the seat-dependent part; a dead enemy's turn after ours counted as an unseen one's.
- **Revised** (fresh-64001..64079): 50.2% (49.7-50.6); 330k against 229k. Dead enemies' slots are unknown again
  (they set priorities: `probe-dead-priority`), an escape blow over two turns splits into its one-turn strike now and
  the rest, and the ledger and order model are made only when a need is priced (fuel only: 52/52 replays identical,
  -0.9% fuel).
- **Where the fuel goes** (census, 100 games at the real budget): the ledger and model ~0.8k a turn before the lazy
  change; the rest, ~1.2k a turn in `channels`, `s.lethal` and `want_home`, is the windows' premise itself: an unseen
  enemy may act after us while any enemy turn after ours is unaccounted for, which widens the threats.

Level in every run with about 45% more out-of-fuel turns, so the port was dropped.

hold start. The one asymmetry is in value, not in clearer: gold-only groups are never contested (capture.cc:636 and
contesting, capture.cc:524). `oc-inv2-cg` contests them too: 50.1% (49.5-50.8) on inv2-e, 20,480 games. Level.


## Area control around held camps (ocean, 2026-11-05)

The user: "area control around waiting for capture camps if opponents are nearby". **What oc-combo2 does now:** a
holder stays on its tile (holding_capture, capture.cc:307 / holding_capture_now :278; bot.cc:339-349) and, while
holding, the strike search runs with `holding` set and hold_capture (capture.cc:653) hits other camps in reach; it
leaves only through want_home (combat/fight.cc:437: drawn home, camp-trapped, or stand_lost_at weighing the fight
there) or the hold's own pay-timing checks (fight.cc ~265-275, hold_rounds / paying_soon). Allies do nothing for a
hold of ours: contest_capture (capture.cc:629) is for enemy holds, and guard_turn (economy/altar_guard.cc:101) guards
altars only.

**How often it matters** (`area.py`, every hold; "near" = an enemy champion within Chebyshev R of a group tile during
the hold):

| Games | holds / game | broken / game | holds with an enemy within 4 | of those: paid / contested / emptied |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ladder, 965 top-team games (`replays/invade-ladder`) | 118.4 | 10.8 | 14.3 / game | 66.6 / 9.8 / 23.6% |
| ours, 960 base sunfam games (both teams) | 73.9 | 1.9 | 5.4 / game | 77.1 / 4.2 / 18.7% |

Without an enemy within 6 holds pay 95% (ladder) and 99.5% (ours). Broken holds near enemies are mostly emptied,
and the holder walks off alive (ours 0.96 a game against 0.06 deaths on the tiles; ladder 3.15 against 0.23).

**Variant** (`bots/variants/oc-ac-dev`, knobs in `params::area`, all off replay 52/52 byte-identical to oc-combo2 at
100M): guard_hold (capture.cc, run after chase and contest_capture in bot.cc): while an ally holds a cleared gem
group, the hold has not paid and we see an enemy within `guard_radius` of its centre, a free ally within
`guard_reach` steps walks to it and stays within one tile of its tiles; the strike search fights as usual. Fresh
ladder-mix `ac-e` (517210-517249), 20,480 games each against oc-combo2:

| Variant | radius | reach | gold groups | Win % | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a1 | 4 | 6 | no | 49.96 | 49.27-50.64 |
| a2 | 6 | 6 | no | 49.54 | 48.85-50.22 |
| a3 | 4 | 10 | no | 49.93 | 49.25-50.62 |
| a4 | 6 | 10 | yes | 49.57 | 48.88-50.25 |

a1 changes 30.6% of maps (not 1-1), so it acts often. In a 1,000-game sample of a1's games, a1 breaks 2.59 holds a
game against oc-combo2's 3.14, but it starts fewer (58.6 against 59.7) and pays fewer (56.0 against 56.5): the
guards' rounds come out of farming. With an enemy within 4 its holds pay 67.4% against 69.1%. Level everywhere; not
run on the confirm suite `ac-c` (517310-517349), `ac-v` or the panel, as nothing gained. Not shipped.

## Mirror pull: invades later in the game (ocean, 2026-11-05)

The user's idea: "on sunburst perhaps test scoring invades properly later on in the game ... perhaps a dumb thing like
min(dist from our pos, dis from symmetric of our pos) when considering dist scoring", then "(2) could just be generally
good ... tune conservativeness by a coefficient on symmetric pos".

**How often we are camp-bottlenecked** (`bneck.py`; every 10th round; a team is bottlenecked when, of its side's groups
worth at least the floor in gem-eq, none is alive with no body of the team within 3, or respawning and back within 10):

| Games | floor 8, none free | floor 20, none free | floor 20, at most 1 free |
|---|---|---|---|
| ladder (965 top-team games), r0-100 / 100-300 / 300-600 / 600+ | 4.6 / 4.4 / 4.4 / 4.3% | 11.2 / 10.6 / 10.6 / 16.6% | 23.1 / 22.2 / 22.6 / 33.5% |
| oc-combo2 on fresh ladder-mix (1,000 games of ac-e) | 2.4 / 1.4 / 1.4 / 1.8% | 7.4 / 5.7 / 6.1 / 12.1% | 20.4 / 18.2 / 18.2 / 30.9% |
| oc-combo2 on sunfam (960 games) | 36.0 / 8.5 / 2.9 / 2.5% | 36.0 / 8.5 / 2.9 / 2.5% | 47.9 / 52.6 / 48.1 / 40.1% |

We are bottlenecked less often than ladder teams. Sunburst is bottlenecked in the opening, while every elk is cleared
or respawning, and about half of the time later on with at most one group free.

**Variant** (`bots/variants/oc-late-dev`, knobs in `params::late`; all off replays 52/52 byte-identical to oc-combo2 at
100M, fuel +0.03%). In farm_turn a group's walk counts as `steps - lam * max(0, steps - c * mirror_steps)`. Here
`mirror_steps` is the group's centre field read at the mirror of our tile, falling back to the crow's distance. Each
prune's lower bound gets the same discount from the mirror's Chebyshev distance: the SIMD pre-prune, rated_below,
beaten_near and the steps prune. The ordered stop is off while the pull is on.

The gated track (`gated`, `enemy_only`) pulls only enemy-side groups, from `min_round`. It needs at most `bottleneck`
of our side's groups worth `worth_floor` to be up and unclaimed, and fewer than `cap_k` allies on enemy-side claims.
`deny` weighs pulled groups by 1 + d. The unconditional c = 1.5 is +2.0% mean fuel and +3.8% at p99 on the bench.

**Results.** Fresh ladder-mix suites against oc-combo2 are 20,480 games each. Sunburst families are paired with
oc-combo2 on the same map, side and opponent over 6 opponents: `sunfam2` (320 maps, 640 games a cell) and the unused
`sunfam3` (319 maps). `realfam` is 19 ladder maps x 16.

| Variant | late-e (521000-039) | late-c (521100-139) | sunfam2 paired | sunfam3 paired | realfam paired |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| u3: c = 3 | 49.10 (48.42-49.79) | 49.19 (48.51-49.88) | +1.2 | | -0.6 |
| u2: c = 2 | 49.05 (48.36-49.73) | | -3.5 | | |
| u15: c = 1.5 | 48.59 (47.90-49.27) | | -5.8 | | |
| u125: c = 1.25 | 48.66 (47.97-49.34) | | -1.8 | | |
| u1: c = 1 | 48.49 (47.81-49.18) | | **+9.8** | **+9.2** | -0.8 |
| g1: gated, c 1, enemy side, r >= 100, floor 20, none free, cap 1 | 49.49 (48.81-50.18) | | +0.7 | | |
| g2: g1 + deny 0.3 | 49.62 (48.93-50.30) | | -0.4 | | |
| g3: at most 1 free, cap 2 | 48.16 (47.48-48.85) | | +2.2 | | |
| g4: g3 + lam 0.5, deny 0.3 | 49.38 (48.70-50.07) | | -6.7 | | |
| nulls on sunfam2: probe / L0s / ac-a1 / ac-a3 / cg | | | +5.0 / +3.6 / -2.0 / -2.0 / -2.0 | probe +5.5 | |

The mutation families move as a block: the probe null reads +5.0 and +5.5 on the two families, with the same cells
(-40 against proteus, +23 against the crew). So the null band is about -2 to +5.5, not a sampling error.

u1 is above every null on both families. Its gain is against the crew (+34.5 / +34.6, nulls at most +23.8) and against
astraeus (+19 / +17). Against the crew in the late game it captures 103 gold a game on their side in
rounds 300-600 (base 34) and 418 in rounds 600-1000 (base 114). The crew's captures on our side fall from 418 to 129 in
rounds 600-1000, and on its own side from 1,630 to 1,152. So on sunburst the trick does what the user said: late invades
that also deny.

**It does not generalise.** Every c loses on fresh ladder-mix suites (-0.9 to -1.5), and so does every gated variant
(-0.4 to -1.8). The per-map split of u1's paired difference on late-e (`featsplit.py`, quartiles) has no positive bin.
Features: area, high-value groups, the gap between the two sides' home groups, its ratio to the spawn gap, home group
distance, enemy-half and middle worth shares, contested share, chokes, picks. u1 loses most on big maps (-3.2), large
home gaps (-3.4) and enemy shares of 0.4 or more (-2.5). On the 154 fresh maps whose nearest ladder map is 04sunburst it
reads -5.5 ± 2.9.

u3 had pockets on late-e: home gap / spawn gap <= 0.5 and area >= 4000 read +4.5 ± 1.8 over 378 maps, and adding <= 6
high-value groups read +7.5 ± 2.4 over 206. On late-c they read -0.3 ± 1.9 and -3.0 ± 2.6: fitted noise. No feature
gate survives. Not shipped. Gating u1 on the 04sunburst map itself would be worth about +9.5 / 128, or +0.07 points on
the current ladder pool, and is the user's call.

### Mirror pull, second pass: scale, mechanism and statistical gates (ocean, 2026-11-05 night)

The user: "isn't this a map analysis skill issue then?", "if you test like 10k that you fresh gen surely it does
something?", "maybe you make a statistical model as a gate". c = 1 is `oc-late-u1`. Labels are per-map paired
differences against oc-combo2: base self-play counts 0.5 a game. Each label covers oc-combo2, `oc-inv2-crew`,
panel-astraeus and panel-proteus, both sides, 8 games a map.

**Mutation gradient on 04sunburst** (`maps/suites/inv2/sungrad`, `mkgrad.py`, mutation seeds 522200000+):

| Arm | Maps | Mutation | c = 1 minus base | combo2 / crew / astraeus / proteus |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | 800 | 1-2 of walls/bushes/holes +-1-2 (sunfam's) | **+15.2** ± 0.7 | +3.8 / +42.6 / +21.4 / -7.0 |
| L2 | 800 | 3 such, walls x0.8-1.25 | +4.6 ± 0.7 | +2.0 / +12.4 / +4.5 / -0.4 |
| L3 | 800 | L2, camps x0.85-1.15 (distance from spawn), bushes x0.6-1.6 | +0.6 ± 0.8 | |
| L4 | 800 | walls, holes, bushes, camps x0.75-1.3, camps +-1 | +1.9 ± 0.8 | |
| L5 | 800 | L4, econ retype, altars +-1, picks 3-5, camps +-2 | -0.4 ± 0.8 | |
| walls | 448 | walls and holes x0.5-2 | +3.9 ± 1.0 | |
| bushes | 500 | bushes x0.2-3 | +6.8 ± 1.0 | |
| camppos | 500 | camps x0.7-1.35 | +3.1 ± 0.9 | +13.8 / -10.9 / +9.2 / +0.1 |
| econ | 500 | rich / poor / gold / gems | +3.0 ± 1.0 | |
| campcount | 500 | camps +-1-3 | -0.6 ± 1.0 | |

The gain needs sunburst's camp economy. Over all gradient maps, those keeping sunburst's count of worthy groups read
+5.0 (5,095 maps) against 0.0 for those that changed it (1,353). Its home group worth reads +4.9 against +0.5, its
group count +5.6 against +0.4, and its share of their worth within 1.5x our home walk +4.9 against -0.2. It also
needs the paths: walls and holes changes alone halve it, and L1 to L2 drops it from +15 to +5. Bush changes matter
least.

**Why sunburst wins** (sunfam2 against the crew, base / c = 1, by round 600-1000; `unworked.py`):
- Their side is worked. On average 0.21 / 0.36 of their worthy groups are alive with no body of theirs within 3,
  and unworked spells last a median 6-7 rounds. So the gain is not from idle camps.
- We spend 10% / 19% of body-rounds on their half and do not die more there (0.71 / 1.08 deaths in the window, 1.31
  / 0.43 after).
- Our gem-eq on their side goes 41 to 150. On our own side it goes 399 to 571. Theirs on our side goes 142 to 45,
  and on their own side 554 to 394.

The win is contest and denial: the two sides' elk groups are 12 tiles apart (our home walk is 9). Bodies on their
group keep their crew home and off ours.

**10,000 fresh sunburst-like maps** (`maps/suites/inv2/sunlike`): the 10,000 of 59,904 fresh ladder-mix maps (seeds
522300-522533, generated in scratch, only the selected maps moved under maps/) nearest to 04sunburst. The distance is
scaled over worthy groups, high-value groups, home walk, enemy-home walk ratio, enemy-side worth, middle worth,
reach of their worth, bushes, walls, Monoliths, home worth, rate ratio, tortuosity, log area and spawn walk, plus
picks and symmetry. 80,000 games per bot.

| Rank by distance | c = 1 minus base |
|---|---|
| 0-100 (includes sunburst mutations from the ladder mix) | +0.1 ± 2.0 |
| 100-500 | +0.6 ± 1.1 |
| 500-1000 | -0.5 ± 1.0 |
| 1000-2500 | -2.3 ± 0.6 |
| 2500-5000 | -3.3 ± 0.5 |
| 5000-10000 | -2.3 ± 0.3 |
| all 10,000 | **-2.3 ± 0.2** (combo2 -2.7, crew -2.5, astraeus -2.9, proteus -1.2) |
| the 105 ladder-mix mutations of 04sunburst in it | -1.3 ± 2.1 |

**Map-level model (a).** Features: 40 round-1 features from `mf/mapfeat2.mjs` (walking steps by king moves from both
spawns to every group, worth by side, home and enemy-home walks, reach, rates, tortuosity, densities, Monoliths,
altars, symmetry, picks).
- Label reliability is the limit. The split-half correlation of per-map labels (combo2 + crew against astraeus +
  proteus) is 0.057 on sunlike (Spearman-Brown 0.11) and 0.017 on the gradient. A map's label at 8 games is almost
  all game chaos.
- Fit on sunlike's first seed half (5,013 maps), validated on its second half (4,987), on late-e (10,240 maps) and on
  the gradient (6,448):
  - Ridge: CV r 0.047, validation r 0.082, late-e 0.023.
  - GBM (depth 2, 150 trees): CV 0.056, validation 0.092, late-e 0.031, gradient 0.081.
- No selected subset gains on validation: the top 5 / 10 / 25 / 50% by prediction read 0.0 / -0.9 / -0.7 / -1.1
  (ridge) and -0.5 / -1.3 / -1.6 / -1.0 (GBM). The gate only learns to fire less; a gated suite is still -0.1 to
  -0.5. No map gate was built into the bot.

**In-game observation gate** (`params::late::obs`, per enemy-side group: believed alive, no damage seen for
`unworked` rounds, optionally seen alive within `fresh` rounds, no enemy seen within `danger_radius` in 10 rounds;
knobs off bench 52/52 identical). Results on late-e, 20,480 games:

| Variant | Settings | Win % (95% CI) |
|---|---|---|
| o1 | c 1, unworked 40, danger 6 | 48.28 (47.60-48.97) |
| o2 | o1, seen within 60 | 49.62 (48.93-50.30) |
| o3 | unworked 80, danger 8 | 48.25 (47.57-48.94) |
| o4 | o1, our bottleneck (floor 20, at most 1 free), cap 2, from r100 | 49.33 (48.64-50.01) |

**Situation-level model (b)** (`sit.py`, `sitfit.py`, `sitchk.py`). `oc-late-u1i` is c = 1 with a trace of every
farm pick that switches a body to an enemy-side group: walk, crow and mirror distances, the group's gems and gold,
its belief (state, rounds since seen and since damaged), enemies near, free allies, the body's bag and health, the
round and the map area. The traces cover `lab-e` and `lab-c` (1,920 maps each, copied from late-e and late-c) and
sunfam2, against the four opponents. That gives 636,133 decisions, 486,343 of them where the pull changed the pick.
The label is the body's gem-eq in the next 60 rounds minus its previous 60, with 10 off for dying. Fit on lab-e,
validated on lab-c and sunfam2.
- The average pulled pick loses: delta -9.3 on lab-c and -5.0 on sunfam2. 4% of picks pay out a capture, and 8-11%
  of the bodies die.
- Classifiers for "pays out" look strong: logistic AUC 0.79 (lab-c) and 0.70 (sunfam2), GBM 0.83 and 0.74. For
  "delta > 0" they are weak: logistic 0.57 and 0.58, GBM (40 trees) 0.60 and 0.61.
- Regressions on delta seem to find a good subset. Ridge r is 0.26 and 0.24; its pred > 0 picks are 4% and 3% of
  decisions, at +2.4 and +8.7 against -9.8 and -5.4 for the rest. GBM r is 0.32 and 0.46; its pred > 0 picks are 10%
  and 9%, at +4.0 and +8.6 against -10.7 and -6.4.
- **The subset is an artefact of the counterfactual.** In the ridge and GBM pred > 0 picks, the body's previous 60
  rounds earned 2-10 gem-eq, against 16-25 for the rest (r(pred, prv) -0.4 to -0.6). Their next 60 rounds earn the
  same or less: lab-c 12.9 / 12.2 against 14.3 / 14.6, sunfam2 12.3 / 11.8 against 11.9 / 11.9. The deaths are no
  lower, apart from GBM's 8.7% against 11.2% on sunfam2. The model has learned which bodies were idle before, not
  where an invade pays.
- No in-game state picks pulled invades that out-earn the rest, so no situation gate was built. The map gate, the
  observation gate and the situation gate all fail the same way: the pull's sunburst gain is contest and denial
  that the body's own yield does not show, and a game-level label is too noisy to fit per map.

### Mirror pull, third pass: a learned cycle-constraint gate (ocean, 2026-11-05)

The user's hypothesis: sunburst has many camps but few high-value ones (a cycle constraint), and the gate should be
learned. Plan, features and every table are in research/ideas-2026-11-05/invade-cycle.md.

**Rebase.** `variants/oc-mp-dev` is oc-base3 plus oc-late-dev's `params::late` (the patch applied cleanly). With the
knobs off, bench at 100M replays 16/16 (default) and 52/52 (wide) byte-identical, fuel +0.03% / +0.02%.
`variants/oc-mp-u1` is c = 1.

**Labels.**
- A family is a base map plus mild mutations: 1-2 of walls/bushes/holes +-1-2, picks unchanged.
- A game's label is c = 1's win minus oc-base3's on the same map, side and opponent, over oc-base3 (self-play, 0.5),
  astraeus-now-1105, panel-proteus and oc-inv2-crew.
- Split-half reliability by member (pilot, 200 families x 128 games): 0.31 / 0.49 / 0.68 / 0.80 at 16 / 32 / 64 /
  128 games. The second pass had 0.11 at 8.
- Labels were then made at 64 games for 1,136 more families (reliability 0.73): sungrad, sunfam2, sunlike, all 128
  ladder maps, fresh ladder-mix 527000-527009 and `--mix varied` 527100-527104. In all, 1,336 families and 172k
  games.
- Caveat: between opponents a family's labels correlate only 0.12, so most of the reliable spread is map x opponent.

Mean c = 1 minus off, by class:

| Class | Families | Mean |
|---|---|---|
| fresh | 670 | -2.3 |
| ladder | 126 | -1.8 |
| sun | 190 | +0.7 |
| sunlike | 120 | -1.3 |
| varied | 230 | -1.9 |

04sunburst itself reads 0.0 over 128 games against these opponents.

**Features** (map only, the bot's group data):
- the older round-1 set;
- cycle-constraint features at floors 20 and 30: high-value counts and shares, output per period, body demand,
  slack, tour against respawn, yields, distances from our high-value groups to theirs, their dependence on them;
- the enemy copy's distance from each of our groups;
- a two-team farm simulation with and without the pull.

The cycle-constraint and simulation features are all under |0.07| Spearman. The best are the cross distances
(their copy of our worthy groups near: -0.17, fresh+ladder -0.23), symmetry -0.13 and high-value yield +0.12.

**Offline models.** Grouped 5-fold CV over 980 groups (SUN one group, ladder maps with their mutations), 5 repeats.
Top-k is the mean held-out label of the top k% by prediction:

| Model | Held-out r (all / fresh) | Top 10% (fresh) | Top 20% (all / fresh) | Leave-SUN-out r |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ridge, 109 features | +0.13 / +0.15 | -2.4 | -1.3 / -1.2 | +0.05 |
| logistic on the sign | +0.17 / +0.20 | +1.9 | +1.0 / +1.0 | +0.18 |
| ridge, 6 in-fold features | +0.17 / +0.22 | +0.2 | +0.2 / +0.7 | -0.01 |
| GBM, depth 2, 150 trees | **+0.21 / +0.24** | +1.4 | **+1.2 [-0.5, 2.5] / +1.8 [-0.2, 3.5]** | +0.16 |
| GBM, 300 trees | +0.21 / +0.24 | +1.3 | +1.1 / +1.0 | +0.14 |
| GBM, 26 hand-picked | +0.19 / +0.22 | +1.7 | +0.6 / +0.6 | -0.02 |

On ladder maps every GBM top-k is negative (-1.6 to -4.8).

**Pre-registered subset on unused seeds.** The final GBM picked the top 20% of fresh 527500-527539: 2,048 maps
(`maps/suites/mp3/sel-ab`), predicted +1.78. Over 28,672 games it read **+0.75 [-0.29, +1.72]**:
- by opponent: base3 +0.4, astraeus +1.3, proteus -0.5, crew +1.8;
- no dose-response: r -0.02 within the selected maps, and the top 2% / 5% read +0.2 / -0.2.

Gated at this threshold, the bot would be about +0.15 points over off, which a 20k A/B cannot resolve.

**Verdict: no gate.** The map predicts where the pull loses (far enemy copies, rotational symmetry, big maps, many
altars), but not a subset where it wins. Nothing was built into the bot, no A/B was run, and variants/oc-mp was not
frozen. Mutation seeds 527000000+ / 527100000+; suite seeds 527000-527009, 527100-527104, 527500-527539 (partly
moved), 527600-527609 (unused).

## spawncamp (ocean, 2026-11-05)

The user's idea 7: camps hit from our spawn, where each turn end heals. Design, prevalence and replay study:
research/ideas-2026-11-05/spawncamp.md. Dev copy `bots/variants/oc-spawncamp-dev` (knobs off: bench 16/16
identical with oc-base1 at 100M). Against `bots/variants/oc-base1`, own drafts, fast runner, real fuel.
- **Prevalence:** a striker within 3 of a spawn tile on 4.7% of ladder maps and 4.6% of ladder-mix maps
  (fresh-514000..514039); the stand choice changes the fire on 0.1-0.8%; a Monolith within 3 on 03homonoliths and
  0.16% of generated maps, all of them its mutations.
- **Where the gap is:** in self-play on the 16 ladder near maps, home Golems and wolves are cleared at about the
  farm rate (plaza, quadrants, yin-yang). Of 918 uncontested home groups on df-near3 (469 maps), 157 sit idle for
  most of the game, but they are low-value singles (a lone wolf from spawn is about 0.1 gems a turn), so rate
  pricing is right. On **03homonoliths** the home Monoliths (60k health, 600 gems, fire 600) sit untouched until
  r1055: the siege waits until the team clears them within `siege_rounds` (64). First capture r1127-1212; ladder top
  teams also have median 0 tributed at r1400.
- **D1:** a Monolith group whose live strikers all fire on spawn stands the sturdiest of us outlasts
  (`home_siege`, over `home_free`) is sieged once the team clears it within `home_siege_rounds`, at its power
  scaled to the stands' share of bodies (siege.cc siege_candidate, siege_ready). A static per-group prefilter (a
  member within 3 of the spawn box) keeps StandReach builds off far Monoliths; without it out-of-fuel turns read
  +4.5% in df-c0's A/B.

| Variant | Suite | Win % | Games |
|---|---|---|---|
| L128, any | df-mono (62 home-Monolith maps: 45 mutations of 03homonoliths, 16 generated, the ladder map) | 81.5 (73.7-87.3) | 124 |
| L256, any | df-mono | 82.3 (74.6-88.0) | 124 |
| L512, any | df-mono | 84.7 (77.3-90.0): Monolith-only maps 87/90, mixed 18/34 | 124 |
| L4000, any | df-mono | 84.7, the same games as L512 | 124 |
| L512, any (no prefilter) | df-c0 (fresh-514200..514209) | 48.9 (47.6-50.3); OOF +4.5% | 5,120 |
| L512, Monolith-only maps (`home_siege_any` false) = **L512m** | df-mono | 80.6 (72.8-86.6): Monolith-only 86/90, mixed 14/34 | 124 |
| L512, any | df-monomix (60 mutations with `econ=rich/gems`) | 46.7 (38.0-55.6) | 120 |
| L512m | df-monomix | 49.2 (40.4-58.0) | 120 |

- On mixed maps (home Monolith plus other gem groups) home sieging keeps the Monolith awake while bodies walk out
  through its reach: 4.1 deaths to it a game against 0.13 on Monolith-only maps. It is level there (pooled 48% any,
  47% off), so it stays off: **kept L512m** (`home_siege_rounds` 512, `home_siege_any` false). 03homonoliths itself
  went from ~r1400 to wins in 656 and 677 rounds.
- **Confirm (L512m):** fresh-514400..514439 50.2% of 20,480 (49.5-50.9), OOF 219.9k / 220.0k; `--mix varied`
  fresh-514440..514449 50.1% of 5,118 (48.7-51.5). The change acts on 0.2-0.8% of maps, so full suites cannot
  resolve it: it is +0.27 points of the ladder (1/128 maps at ~85%). At 100M, bench `--set wide` is 52/52 identical
  to oc-base1. At the real budget, mean 54,295 to 54,315, p99 94,552 to 94,620, OOF 565 to 565.
- **Panel** (panel-514500, 2,560 games each; oc-base1's rates from PANEL.md in brackets): astraeus 54.0 (54.7),
  proteus 52.1 (51.7), demeter 55.9 (56.6), ocean-td 72.0 (71.5), v67 69.9 (69.8). No member moves significantly.
  On df-mono (124 each), L512m against oc-base1: astraeus 82.3 against 37.9, proteus 81.5 against 36.3, demeter
  86.3 against 80.6, ocean-td 86.3 against 41.9, v67 89.5 against 91.1.
- Not pursued, with reasons in the design doc: stand choice, spells from range 4, the draft's heal price, groups
  over 32 strikers (none near a spawn: at most 5).
- oc-base2 did not exist by the end, so there is no confirm on it.

## value (ocean, 2026-11-05)

The user's idea 6: a gem/gold exchange rate. Design and fits: research/ideas-2026-11-05/value.md. Against
`bots/variants/oc-base1`, own drafts, fast runner, real fuel, ladder mix (fresh-514210..514229 =
`maps/suites/merged/df-c1,df-c2`), `--sprt 0.50,0.51`.
- **Offline, 33,980 of our A/B games** (`replays/.analysis`, logistic win model with carried gems, capture gold,
  kills and deaths, 20% held out): gold improves held-out log-loss at every checkpoint. In close games, binned by
  the higher tributed score, the implied gems per gold (0.29, 0.19, 0.11, 0.063, 0.036, 0.017 from 0-100 up to
  800-1000) lies between the bot's median and mean `per_gold` (traced: oc-value-trace, 512 games). Only lopsided
  games, and the pooled fit past ~400 tributed, read higher (1.5-2.5x).
- **Ladder archive** (546k games): without carried gems the gold coefficient also carries untributed captures (0.86
  gems/gold at r100); not usable for the rate.
- A/Bs, `late_mult` M (per_gold x 1 + (M - 1) x clamp((max tributed - 250) / 250, 0, 1)) and `gold_price_scale`:

| Variant | Win % | Games | OOF CAND / REF |
|---|---|---|---|
| M 3 | 47.4 (45.2-49.6) | 2,030, SPRT H0 | 22.2k / 22.1k |
| M 2 | 48.9 (47.3-50.4) | 4,079, SPRT H0 | 42.3k / 41.9k |
| M 0.5 | 50.1 (49.1-51.0) | 10,240, undecided | 108.5k / 109.6k |
| `gold_price_scale` 2.0 | 50.0 (49.1-51.0) | 10,240, undecided | 107.1k / 106.0k |
| `gold_price_scale` 1.0 | 48.8 (47.3-50.2) | 4,601, SPRT H0 | |

- Cut. The late lean loses with a dose-response (M 3 < M 2 < M 1), halving it or doubling the scale is level, and a
  lower scale loses. `per_gold` sits on its optimum, and the data's higher late rate is the dominance confound. No
  change kept; `params::value::late_mult` stays 1 in `bots/variants/oc-value-dev`.

### Round 3: a scaling-aware funnel (ocean = oc-base3, 2026-11-05 night)

The user's follow-up: funnel harder by champion scaling (bodies that make better use of gold). Design, the offline
fits and every row: `research/ideas-2026-11-05/value.md` "Round 3". Dev copy `bots/variants/oc-value3-dev`
(`params::value3::`, off = oc-base3 at 100M: 16/16, 52/52, 128/128); against oc-base3, SPRT 0.50/0.51, own drafts,
v3-dev (fresh-523000..523039, 20,480 games at most).

- **Does ocean route by bonus or by scaling?** Both: with Vesper's +33% divided out it still captures 1.9x its side's
  mean, Prism (no bonus) 1.6x; a third of Marcella's 1.7x is tribute gold. A body's gold price is already its own
  next emblem's saving (growth, Focus multipliers, the fight value); only a comparison with its allies was missing.
- **Offline fits** (ladder 2026-11-02 top-50 games, 34,202 sides; our 4,096 games): gold or emblems on Prism,
  Marcella, Vesper and Vendetta go with wins, on Willow, Issac and Heart of Ruin against; ocean already routes that way.
- **Efficiency in play: level.** The fight power an emblem adds x gold rate, as (ours / the team's mean)^p on farm's
  per_gold: p 0.5 50.2, p 1 **50.6 (49.9-51.3)** over 20,480 (its SPRT's 51.6 at 6,767 was stop bias), p 2 49.8 (H0);
  without the wealth funnel 50.6, without the rate 50.5, with a harder wealth funnel 50.4. On the holder choice 50.0
  (H0) / 50.6. All add 10-14% out-of-fuel turns (its own read is +2.1% fuel a turn: a variant computing it at p 1e-9
  replays identically and costs that).
- **Learned type tables: level.** Ladder table at p 0.5 / 1 / 2: 50.1 / 49.6 / 50.0 (H0 each); our-games table
  50.1 (H0); their mean 49.4 (H0). SPSA on the 13 weights from the mean table (`replays/tune/v3tw`, 252 iterations, 258k games against oc-base3 and panel-astraeus, score without the gold term) moved Vesper 1.19 -> 1.33, Vendetta 1.16 -> 1.27, Prism 1.44 -> 1.20, Marcella 1.21 -> 1.05, Issac 0.80 -> 0.70; `bots/variants/oc-v3-tuned` reads 50.5 (49.8-51.2) over 20,480.
- **Harder wealth funnel: level or worse.** Power -1.5 49.6 (H0), -2 50.6, S 150 49.7 (H0).

Nothing kept: CHANGES 414's wealth funnel already captures what routing gold by scaling gains here.

  cause is the skipped `live_steps`: its `labels_hold` -> `Pathing::same_labels` copies the live camps into the
  approach slot's snapshot, so a group not read for a while builds up more than 8 changed tiles, its labels fail
  and it is searched again, and the bound `live_steps` returns differs. With the skipped call restored, both games
  are identical. The cache's answer depends on how often it is read; left as is, because s5 was confirmed as it is.

## 2026-11-05: Fish priority encoding and attack-target reconstruction

[Report, pinned corpus, predictors and counterexamples](fish-2026-11-05/README.md).
124 distinct current-engine Fish ladder games, all dated November 5; 109 training games / 22
match groups, 15 held-out games / 3 groups. Actor perspectives immediately before inputs;
no bot changes or win-rate claim. Submission versions are unavailable.

Ordinary negative priority is `-rank - (team_size+1)*floor(4*(1-h))`, with
`h=min(1,(health+shield)/max_health)`, multiplied by 0.65 when carrying any gems.
The multiplier is a compatible reconstruction, constrained approximately to (0.649350649, 0.65]
under this formula. Every alive small-negative write fits this formula or subtracts another
`5*(team_size+1)` (30,938 training, 4,624 holdout); the extra branch's condition is unresolved.
Predicting ordinary priority when no enemy is visible at turn start or before the write gives
2,902/2,919 exact held-out values (99.42%, 32.95% coverage of priority writes).
The earlier sign/combat claim is false: 894 held-out negative writes share a turn with a direct
enemy-targeted attack/cast.

At basic attacks with an enemy champion available, minimum health+shield predicts 1,637/1,650
held-out targets (99.21%), including 169/181 with multiple enemies (93.37%). Raw-health baseline
gets 168/181; the refinement is modest. A Willow healing-fraction model gets 312/348 multi-target
heals (89.66%), versus 311/348 for lowest health fraction; still exploratory. These models
predict action parameters, not whether to act. Farm destinations, retreats, altar selection,
tribute thresholds and remaining priority modes are open.

## 2026-11-05 — Fish reverse engineering continued: farm targets, stuns and holders

Continued `research/fish-2026-11-05/HANDOFF.md` across behaviors, preserving the original
priority model and results. [Report](fish-2026-11-05/CONTINUATION.md), code `tools/fish/`.
No bot source or A/B change. Original 124 games are discovery; a separate local post-patch
cohort supplies 96 distinct games, independently audited for 1,300,367 inputs / 505,474 turns.
Models were frozen before confirmation inspection, except the later holder investigation,
whose second-cohort check is explicitly exploratory replication.

- **Camp basic targets:** retain the actor's last basic-attacked group if in range; then min
  `(HP,y,x,id)`. Confirmation multiple-target exact agreement **19,440/20,646 (94.16%)**,
  against lowest HP/id **16,162/20,646 (78.28%)**. With several groups available and the previous
  group still available, retain it in **4,170/4,286 (97.29%)**. Choosing a new group is unresolved:
  fallback gets only 289/651. Conditional target models do not predict whether to attack.
- **Cassi pure stun:** exclude Marcella and positive-timer stuns, maximize Strength, lower id
  on ties. Confirmation **147/158 (93.04%)** with multiple eligible targets; 242/253 with
  multiple visible enemies before filtering. Damage-spell target models remain weaker.
- **Holder ordering:** Marcella > Vesper > Vendetta > HoR > Cassi > Issac > Willow; predict stay
  only for the highest supported type among current holders. Discovery **1,585/1,595**;
  exploratory replication **1,519/1,535 (98.96%)**, 35.16% coverage of 4,366 sampled situations.
  This does not predict the timing of lower-ranked holders' departures or incoming replacements.
- **Prism banking:** bag + score + visible allies already tributing >= 1000 fits all 33
  discovery starts, but only **21/22 confirmation** starts. Exact necessary condition refuted;
  saved exception has a gem-carrying ally recalling, not tributing. Gate alone is also not a
  full tribute trigger. Fixed gem thresholds for other types are insufficient.
- **Opening destination:** nearest static walk distance **166/453 (36.64%)**; simple
  `(gold+0.5*gems)/(1+walk+HP/100)` **224/453 (49.45%)**. Weak hypotheses, not port candidates.
- The user clarified prepared recalls: Fish starts them after productive work to save a turn
  if it continues next turn. Data agree on 504,415 sampled discovery endpoints. Even one turn
  of continuation can be waiting for a camp, so retreat needs episode/outcome labels.

All errors, cohort manifests, per-game results and model hashes are saved. Python/Node checks,
raw input accounting and supplemental altar-state checks pass. Both cohorts are now inspected;
new independent confirmation requires fresh games. Prioritize new farm destinations, holder
departure timing and retreat/action triggers over further polishing target-selection models.

## 2026-11-05 — Fish action decisions and a third independent cohort

[Report and executable formulas](fish-2026-11-05/DECISIONS.md). Continued across new
destinations, lower-holder departures, final-turn recall and action/no-action opportunities;
preserved both prior cohorts' frozen models/results. No bot changes or win-rate claim.

Downloaded 80 recent Fish games; deduplication against both inspected cohorts and known
groups leaves **43 untouched games / nine groups**, November 5 12:20–13:40 ET. Models, trees
and feature code frozen before decoding. All `v3_0_0`; submission versions unavailable.
Independent audit: **513,726 inputs / 199,550 completed turns**, exact. Both ordered drafts
match metadata in 43/43 games; every feature row's self-state matches its actor start snapshot.

- **New destination choice remains weak.** Minimize `max(walk, remembered respawn wait)`:
  post-payout **352/619 (56.87%)**, spawn return **492/1,208 (40.73%)**, versus nearest-new
  44.91% / 27.32%. Clean labels cover 1,827/3,765 non-opening episodes; other outcomes remain
  censored, not silently treated as farming trips. A 54-combination reward-rate grid gets
  only 39.08% combined, below the wait baseline's 46.20%. No recovered destination formula.
- **Lower-holder timing:** depth-three tree over self/best-holder recall timers, health and
  apparent exits **801/1,065 (75.21%)**, vs always leave 59.91%. With both holders recalling
  at timers 1–3, predict stay **143/148 (96.62%)**, 13.90% lower-holder coverage. Neither
  predicts incoming replacements; 219/264 full-tree errors are premature departures.
- **Recall completion decision:** at timer 1, keep/cancel tree **2,692/3,432 (78.44%)**, vs
  always cancel 51.84%. On an empty group above 40% HP, cancel **868/879**; off an empty group
  at <=40% HP, keep **536/570**. Approximate rules, not exact constants or retreat-start
  labels. Of 1,653 keeps, 1,640 arrive, 11 are interrupted and two censored. Model overpredicts
  keeps (684 false keeps, 56 false cancels); actual-arrival agreement is 78.10%.
- **Action taking:** with an enemy initially in melee range, attack **2,368/2,377 (99.62%)**;
  nine exceptions include teleporting instead. Ranged attack/no-attack tree **1,415/2,018
  (70.12%)**, vs always attack 58.28%. Willow any-injury heal trigger **6,020/6,422 (93.74%)**;
  tree **6,046/6,422 (94.15%)**, but injured-only accuracy is 85.39% versus always-heal
  83.99%, a modest refinement. Heals on 59/65 opportunities with at most 20 HP missing.
- **Damage-slot cast tree:** **5,877/7,630 (77.02%)**, vs never cast 62.36%; still misses
  1,389/2,872 actual casts. This is a surrogate rather than a recovered complete spell policy.

`tools/fish/decision_{data,model}.py`, `fit_decisions.py`, `evaluate_decisions.py`,

Python/Node checks and audits pass. All three cohorts are now inspected. Next work should
prioritize remembered routes/territory, incoming replacements and earlier retreat/tribute
choices, using another fresh cohort for independent confirmation.

### Fish route memory, incoming capture entry and earlier trips (2026-11-05)

Research only; **no bot changes**. [Full report](fish-2026-11-05/ROUTES.md). Fit on the
inspected 124 games, use the inspected 43 only as exploratory replication, then freeze code
and models before decoding **46 untouched games in ten groups**, November 5 15:10–16:40 ET.
Four of the planned 50 replays duplicate old bytes and are excluded. All three earlier
manifests are excluded by hashes, match ids and known groups. Raw audit: **582,762 inputs /
228,085 completed turns**, exact; all `v3_0_0`, both drafts match metadata in every game.

- Actor-local route/visit memory, public spawn territory and recent allied camp occupation
  score: **847/1,726 (49.07%)** next-camp predictions, versus travel/respawn wait **823/1,726
  (47.68%)**. The gain's paired ten-group interval is −0.82 to +3.55 points. Post-payout
  loses 370/608 to 373/608; post-spawn improves 477/1,118 to 450/1,118. Hard visited-only
  and most-frequent-transition hypotheses fail. No recovered camp score or port recommendation.
- Incoming entry to an adjacent empty group with visible incumbent: frozen holder rank
  **1,475/1,749**, shallow tree **1,476/1,749 (84.39%)**, always decline 72.27%. Two-turn
  occupation proxy **1,541/1,747 (88.21%)**, but can count transit across a large group.
  Rank is almost as accurate; the fitted late-capture/low-gold exception adds little.
- A **retrospective** endpoint audit after inspecting fresh errors follows entrants through
  observed payout: 344 paid, 135 left first, six censored. Unchanged tree **1,580/1,743
  (90.65%)**, rank 1,569/1,743. This changed endpoint is not independently confirmed and
  does not distinguish shared payouts from replacing the incumbent. Full outcomes retained.
- Earlier economic trip forecast (farm / actual home arrival / successful tribute):
  **1,951/2,727 (71.54%)**, versus always farm 63.29%; after payout only **800/1,441 (55.52%)**.
  After spawn 89.50%, versus always farm 86.94%. Gold/altar/score splits remain surrogates.
- Timer-4 same-channel arrival tree is a **failed model**: 98.76% vs negative baseline
  98.75%, detecting only **21/1,848 arrivals**. Recall preparation and brief continuation
  are not retreat labels. The high-health shopping return and interrupted low-health channel
  counterexamples are retained.

New `tools/fish/routes_*`, fitting/evaluation/pinning/audit/summary scripts and a payout
endpoint audit; all previous frozen predictors/caches/evidence preserved. Per-game counts,
192-point grid, every prediction failure and raw/provenance audits are in the report folder.
All four evaluated cohorts are now used data. Further independent tests must pin untouched
games; extra downloaded raw games were not decoded, but must be deduplicated against all
four manifests. Continue with teammate commitments/availability and genuine capture
follow-through and departure decisions, not established targeting refinements.

### Fish camp destinations as a scored choice; drafts and emblems (2026-11-05)

Research only; **no bot changes**. Reports: [CHOICE.md](fish-2026-11-05/CHOICE.md) and
[DRAFTS-EMBLEMS.md](fish-2026-11-05/DRAFTS-EMBLEMS.md). Fifth cohort: every downloaded Fish
game outside the four earlier manifests, **94 games / 20 groups** (18:50–21:10 UTC, 21 ranked,
73 unranked, all `v3_0_0`), pinned with code/model hashes before any play was decoded.

- A conditional-logit camp score (log wait, respawn wait, solo fight cost, Monolith, clusters
  only, remembered state, familiarity/route/last group, own half, recent ally sighting, a closer
  visible ally; separate payout/spawn weights) predicts the next camp in **2,351/3,819 (61.56%)**
  untouched episodes, versus travel/respawn wait 52.42% and the ROUTES fitted score 54.39%.
  After payout 69.22% vs 63.27%, after spawn 56.81% vs 45.69%; 18/20 groups; group-bootstrap
  gain +6.0 to +12.2 points. Weights are a fitted surrogate, not source constants.
- Refuted or ruled out: replays hold no shared/draft memory (the visualiser export reads zeros
  even for our comms bot); Fish never shares stdout/debug; observer-truth teammate positions add
  ≤0.4 points (no sign of hidden teammate knowledge); a closer ally *attracts* Fish (joining,
  not camp assignment); returning near the last off-spawn position picks 17% after spawn.
- Frozen ROUTES models on the fifth cohort: incoming entry through observed payout (the endpoint
  ROUTES asked to freeze) **3,256/3,628 (89.75%)**, rank 88.62%, never 79.93%; trip forecast
  70.04% vs always farm 61.02%; timer-4 recall arrival still equals always-cancel.
- Drafts (309 games of the four earlier cohorts): one pick order per map, independent of side and
  opponent. 5 picks: Marcella or Vesper, Vendetta, Heart of Ruin, Cassi & Issac, Willow (192/206);
  4: Marcella, Vendetta, HoR, C&I (53/59); 3: Vesper/Marcella-led trios with C&I. Emblem build
  orders per champion (Capture/Prospector first, then Jungle, Monster, Bruiser stacking) are in
  the report; purchases rebuilt from snapshots match engine statistics in 1,706/1,706 champion-games.

All five cohorts are now used data; confirm anything new on games after 21:10 UTC November 5.

### Fish camp choice with astraeus-style reward rate; sixth-cohort confirmation (2026-11-05)

[FARM-CHOICE.md](fish-2026-11-05/FARM-CHOICE.md). The CHOICE.md logit plus astraeus `rate()`
features (worth = 3·gems + gold over walk/respawn + kill time with nearby allies' Strength + 7
capture rounds), own-half share, stale-memory ages, crew and group size (`tools/fish/farm2_*`).
Frozen fit A (model+third+fourth) on **53 untouched games / 11 groups** (21:10–21:40 UTC):
**59.36%** vs the CHOICE logit 54.43% and wait 44.67%; payout 68.99%, spawn 54.69%; 11/11
groups, gain +2.7 to +7.8 points. Earlier held-out: fifth 65.88%, confirm 62.05%. After payout
Fish weighs worth against clear time much like astraeus; after spawn clear time barely matters.
Post-spawn misses are different choices fixed at spawn exit, not changes of mind en route.

### Fish combat rules (2026-11-05)

[COMBAT.md](fish-2026-11-05/COMBAT.md) (`tools/fish/combat_*`), fitted on model/confirm/third,
held out fourth/fifth, then checked on the never-used-for-combat sixth cohort (53 games):
- Positioning: engage iff a kill is available, or health > 0.49 and the safest engage tile's
  next-turn danger ≤ 0.28 of own health+shield: sixth 76.9% vs 60.4% majority (fourth/fifth 72-73%).
- Damage spells cast iff standing still with an enemy within 4: 97.2%. Cassi stuns unless still
  with damage ready: 93.5%. HoR shields iff a visible enemy can reach it: 92.2% (82.6% never).
  Melee attack reset after a surviving basic: 97.9%. Kill available → engage 96.9%.
- Chase when the last target is out of range: target health ≤ 0.37, or visible health ratio >
  1.24 with own gem-adjusted health > 0.44: 76.9% vs 66.2% always-chase.
Fish's 0.49 health line and 0.37 chase line sit near astraeus's `hurt_health_fraction` 0.47 and
`chase_health` 0.4; its HoR shield matches `shield_if_needed`. Single power/numbers ratios top out
at 64.5% for positioning.

### Fish shopping, altar locks, teleports, wards and openings (2026-11-05)

[MISC.md](fish-2026-11-05/MISC.md) (`tools/fish/misc_*`), descriptive over all five cohorts:
- Shopping is a reflex: at turn start, on own spawn or dead with gold ≥ 30, buy crystal (crystal
  maps), lock (lock maps, none carried, (gold − 10·crystals) mod 30 ≥ 10), then
  floor(remaining/30) shards; never saves for an emblem (10,340/10,340 shard counts; sixth cohort
  1,666/1,666 shop on spawn). An apparent off-by-one "spawn box" was a decoder misreading
  (cached `spawnA` max bounds are exclusive). The trigger for going home is not recovered.
- Altar locks are per map: bought iff the enemy's walk to the altar nearest our spawn exceeds ours
  by ≤ 4 (112/115 maps; 7/7 on fifth-only maps). Placed iff an altar within 2 has no lock of
  either team (86.99% vs 63.47% never); Fish skips altars holding an enemy lock.
- Teleport crystals: 17 maps, 881/883 hops exactly 3 tiles across walls on fixed shortcuts.
- Wards: 98.8% of failed ward inputs hit a teammate's ward; chosen tile maximises newly seen bush
  tiles 80-86% of the time; cadence/trigger not recovered.
- Openings: identical inputs for the same map, side and roster up to a median round 53; most
  divergences start at the first enemy sighting.

## Gem-aware fighting (ocean, 2026-11-05)

Make fighting use the bags: ours in the strike search's death cost and in retreat, the enemy's in engage/retreat
and recall interception. Design, evidence and code map: research/ideas-2026-11-05/gemfight.md. Dev copy
`bots/variants/oc-gemfight-dev` (oc-combo2 + `params::gemfight::` knobs; all off: bench.py default 16/16 and wide
52/52 identical to oc-combo2 at 100M), rebased as `bots/variants/oc-gemfight3-dev` on oc-base3 (identical to oc-base3,
16/16 and 52/52). Fast runner, real fuel, own drafts (`--no-test-draft`), ladder mix. Suites: dev
`maps/suites/merged/gf-dev` (fresh-520000..520039), confirm `gf-confirm` (520100..520139) and `gf-confirm2`
(520300..520339). Logs `replays/ab/gf-*`; queue and helpers in research/ideas-2026-11-05/gemfight-tools/.

**Evidence** (`gemfight-tools/gemev.py`, per game): oc-combo2 vs astraeus (1,873 games) dies to champions carrying 10+
gems 1.45 times (astraeus 2.00), losing 103 gems (12% of what it tributes). Enemy carriers with 10+ gems recall home
while we see them within 6 tiles 1.6 times a game (80 gems); we cancel a carrier's real recall by damage 0.07 times a
game. The ladder (965 games) is alike: 3.5 such escapes against 0.35 cancels. In 576 of 676 escapes within 4 tiles our
nearest champion was itself retreating (decision R): after a fight both sides go home. 69% of our deaths with 20+ gems
come within 5 rounds of a retreat decision, 26% while stopping a game-ender. Ladder recallers with an enemy in 6 cancel
to hit back within a round in ~8% of real recalls.

### Fish economy, turn order and tactics (2026-11-05, second subagent round)

Fit on model/confirm/third/fourth (309 games), held out fifth+sixth (147 games, 31 groups). No
camp-target modelling this round. Reports: [ECONOMY.md](fish-2026-11-05/ECONOMY.md),
[TEAM.md](fish-2026-11-05/TEAM.md), [TACTICS.md](fish-2026-11-05/TACTICS.md).
- **Home/recall:** every completed recall has hp ≤ 0.63·max or gold ≥ 30 at the last keep (held
  98.58%); timer-1 keep rule (empty group: hp ≤ 0.40; payout round: hp ≤ 0.63; else hp ≤ 0.63 or
  gold ≥ 30) 90.58% vs always-cancel 53.26%; walks home iff ≤ 5 steps, else recalls (96.13% vs
  85.05%). Prism tributes only if own bag + team score + every visible ally's bag ≥ 1000 (69/69
  starts). Other tributes: altar distance carries the signal; nearest-by-walk altar 95.6%.
- **Turn order, exact structure:** priority = −rank − (N+1)·L, rank by base max health; L = −1
  dead, health band quiet, band+5 "late" at contested camps, ±(99..116) contact with the sign
  positive iff Fish starts the next round (99.91%), giving the most threatened champion back-to-back
  turns. Mode selector 93.6% of enemy-visible turns vs 64.6%. Quiet order sends tied camp hits to
  the healthiest fraction (73%) and away from gem carriers (70% vs 30% id order); late mode hands
  contested-camp ties to the enemy (Fish takes 15-29% vs 43-56%).
- **Camp micro:** no stepping out of camp range (96.2% stay); Golems/Monoliths often woken alone;
  Willow stays by the ally she started nearest (83.7%).
- **Tactics:** damage spells target max (gems + 8)/(HP + shield) (91.6% vs 78.3% lowest HP), basic
  attacks ignore gems; escape dashes land on the minimum-danger tile (96.8%); HoR stun-dash lands on
  the most enemies within 1 (98.4%); stays on spawn until full health (99.7%); dash for a kill
  88.1%; holds a running capture against the retreat rule 74.6%. Refuted: prioritising enemy
  channels (recall/tribute interrupts), health/danger dash thresholds.
Where astraeus differs: shop trips (it needs ≥ 150 gold or an emblem begun), recall health (0.325
/ 0.144), Prism's bag count (only channelling allies), gems in basic-attack targeting, escape dashes
toward spawn, crews before Monoliths, Willow escort and no round-boundary priority sign.

### Fish farming, engagement, micro; forced-vs-free audit (2026-11-06, third subagent round)

Fit on the four oldest cohorts, held out fifth+sixth, then frozen and scored once on a new seventh
cohort (265 games, 56 groups, 21:40–23:40 UTC November 5). Reports: [FARM3.md](fish-2026-11-05/FARM3.md),
[ENGAGE.md](fish-2026-11-05/ENGAGE.md), [MICRO.md](fish-2026-11-05/MICRO.md); summary in the
[handoff](fish-2026-11-05/HANDOFF.md).
- **Camp choice from team-shared memory:** farm2's logit on the newest earlier-teammate sighting per
  group, seventh 63.11% vs 60.69% own memory (+2.0 to +2.9, 54/56 groups), wait 48.72%; observer
  truth adds nothing more. astraeus's `rate()` closed form 50.5% at best, per-map circuits 51.6%.
- **Engagement:** no engage mode at range 4–8 (momentum 70.8% vs 54.5%); danger-weighted route steps
  (69%, 88% hurt); camp hitting 96% → 44% at enemy distance 4; no pursuit beyond sight or hunting.
- **Micro:** basics to min EHP (93.6%), no focus-fire term; first capable actor kills (84–89%);
  ranged walkers pick tiles 3+ from melee (90%); bushes a path habit; no camp-aggro play.
- **Forced vs free:** re-scoring on rows where the alternative was legal downgrades the "cast iff
  still" rules (free rows = always cast; stand-and-cast vs walk is 69% from turn start), Cassi's
  stun "unless", the ward gap, melee tile and Marcella re-hit, TEAM's camp-range stay and Willow
  rules, walk-home ≤ 5 and kill securing. Positioning, chase, kill override, shield, heals, reset,
  targets and destinations hold. COMBAT rules on seventh: positioning 73.6% (57.2%), chase 73.4%
  (61.2%).

worth an A/B; nothing frozen, no CHANGES entry.** Plan, profile and tools: `research/ideas-2026-11-05/fuel7.md`,
`fuel7-tools/`. Suites: dev 537000-537039 (`maps/suites/merged/fuel7-dev`), confirm 537100-537139 (`fuel7-conf`).

| Candidate | Change | Exact (def / wide / pool) | Mean fuel a turn (pool) |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | pre_value and claim_most at the loop's top for groups with no approach slot | 16/16, **51/52, 126/128** | -0.3% |
| R1 | the first turn's rated bound after prunes(trip) on later turns | 16/16, 52/52, 128/128 | +0.0% |
| B1 | the crewable bound at k in [1, crew_most] before its ally pass | 16/16, 52/52, 128/128 | -0.0% |
| noop | an untaken branch (farm_turn's flatten codegen) | 16/16, 52/52, 128/128 | +0.02% |

- Profile (pool, 100M, ordinary loop: 16.5k a loop, 15.9 groups): pre-facts SIMD bounds prune 14% of loop fuel at
  237 a group; the post-live_steps pre_value / claim_most exits 11% at 1.4k; the claimed branch's share group (the
  loop's answer: crew_work + plan_crew) 15%; valued groups 23% (40% in the banking loop). The farm loop is ~9% of
  mean turn fuel at 100M. Prey is 1.7k a call (its sims ~70%), the step guard 1.0k (sims ~60%).
- E1 moved 148k of the 255k post-live_steps exits to the loop's top but its test on every surviving group took the
  saving back, and 3 of 196 games diverge (some read between facts and live_steps keeps state; not found). R1 and B1
  are exact but their tests cost what they skip: the remaining bounds are tight or cheap already (fuel rounds 4-6).
  `variants/oc-fuel7-dev` holds B1 (exact, level).
- **oc-astport (the astraeus-port loop reserve)** on the unused confirm suite against oc-retest-clean, own drafts,
  20,480 games: **49.8% (49.1-50.5)**; OOF turns 152.0k / 155.7k (-2.4%), farm-partial-evaluation -29%,
  farm-no-route -37%, prey-cut-short and step-guard-entry level. Level on a fourth unused set (its own three pooled
  ~50.3%). With no fuel7 change, fuel7 + loop_reserve is oc-astport itself, so the 0.8 / 1.0 scale re-check was not
  run.

  turn (~480 fuel an ally). Marking it noinline changed nothing, so the cost is the work, not codegen.

  its being in sight. Every purchase moves a stat. For ourselves, the key is our gold rate, since our stats lag a
  purchase made this turn: without that, 1 wide game differed.

**Dev SPRTs** (0.50/0.51, own drafts, real fuel, fast runner, against oc-retest-clean on `maps/suites/merged/ap-dev`,
fresh-536000..536039). An H0 stop after under ~3k games means the knob acts on few maps: most map pairs are identical
games, so it cannot move the total by a point.

**loop_reserve.** Real-budget wide bench (52 games against oc-retest-clean): OOF turns 662 -> 576, farm partial
evaluations 9,552 -> 7,131, prey-cut-short 1,058 -> 803, turn-order 1,251 -> 1,087, mean fuel 50,562 -> 50,003.
A scale on its fitted part (`loop_reserve_scale`, all but end_reserve), dev SPRTs:

| scale | win % | games | OOF cand / ref | bench OOF / farm cuts | SPRT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.8 | 51.0 | 11,834 | 94.9k / 87.1k | 664 / 5,304 | H1 |
| 0.9 | 50.8 | 19,323 | 147.4k / 144.1k | 656 / 6,424 | H1 |
| 1.0 (astraeus's fit) | 51.1 | 11,247 | 82.8k / 84.4k | 576 / 7,131 | H1 |
