| 1.3 | 49.9 | 12,185 | 81.1k / 91.4k | | H0 |

More of the loop evaluated is worth more than fewer out-of-fuel turns: 0.8-1.0 are level with each other, and a
larger reserve loses despite 7-11% fewer OOF turns. 1.0 is kept (fewest OOF of the flat range).

**loop_reserve at 1.0, frozen as `bots/variants/oc-astport`** (oc-astport-dev with `loop_reserve` on; bench.py at
100M identical to oc-retest-clean 16/16, 52/52, 128/128 at +0.01% fuel, and to oc-ap-loop-reserve at the real budget
52/52). Full runs against oc-retest-clean, 20,480 games each:

| suite | seeds | win % | 95% CI | OOF cand / ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ap-dev (full) | 536000-536039 | 51.0 | 50.3-51.7 | 151.3k / 154.3k |
| ap-conf (unused) | 536100-536139 | **50.7** | 50.0-51.4 | 151.9k / 155.6k |
| ap-combo (unused) | 536200-536239 | 50.1 | 49.4-50.7 | 155.8k / 159.8k |
| ap-conf2 (unused) | 536400-536439 | 50.0 | 49.3-50.7 | 156.9k / 160.6k |
| ap-varied (`--mix varied`) | 536300-536309 | 50.0 (5,120) | 48.6-51.3 | 44.1k / 45.0k |

On unused seeds it pools to ~50.3% of 61,440 (CI about 49.9-50.7), out-of-fuel turns -2.4%: the dev read was high.
The combination step had only this one winner, so ap-combo is a second confirm of the same bot, and ap-conf2
(536400-536439) a third.

**Panel** (panel-check-514510, 5,120 games a member; oc-retest-clean's rates from `replays/ab/pchk-orc-vs-*`, the
fuel-budget agent's runs, with astraeus-now-1106 as the panel's astraeus):

| member | oc-astport | oc-retest-clean | diff |
|---|---|---|---|
| astraeus-now-1106 | 53.9 | 53.1 | +0.8 |
| panel-proteus | 63.6 | 63.3 | +0.3 |
| panel-demeter | 66.2 | 66.0 | +0.2 |
| panel-ocean-td | 81.5 | 82.1 | -0.6 |
| baselines/v67 | 78.2 | 77.2 | +1.0 |

Mean +0.34, no member below its line (ocean-td's band is about 1.5 points).

**Verdict.** None of 410's parts, 412, the prices tolerance, the turn-1 spawn field or the beaten_near fix helps
ocean: all level or slightly losing, and most act on too few maps to matter. The state-sized reserve is the one gain:
+0.7 on one unused set, level on two more (~+0.3 pooled), no varied loss, the panel up on average, and 2.4% fewer
out-of-fuel turns with 25% fewer farm-loop cuts. It meets the letter of the keep bar on ap-conf only; on astraeus it
also read level-to-ahead (rsv2 51.1/51.3, the refit 50.2 over 30,720) and shipped as a cut-reducing change.

## Cooked comebacks (ocean, 2026-11-06)

The user's idea: gambits for a game that is cooked (far behind; normal play comes back 8-16% of the time). Design,
evidence, every variant and the tools are in `research/ideas-2026-11-05/comeback.md` (tools in `comeback-tools/`).
Base `bots/ocean` (= `variants/oc-retest-clean`); dev copy `variants/oc-comeback-dev` (knobs in
`params::comeback`, off = bench byte-identical, 16/16), each variant `variants/oc-cb-<name>`. All A/Bs at 2x fuel
(200k a turn), own drafts, fast runner; screens on `cb-e` (544000-544039) with SPRT 0.50/0.51, confirms on `cb-c`
(544100-544139), all 20,480 games. Comeback rates are CAND-cooked against REF-cooked in the same A/B. Triggers: g600
= enemy 600+ and 200+ ahead (altar_guard's), g4 = 400+ and 150+ ahead.
- Measurement (self-play, 2,560 games): g600 is reached by one side in 95% of games, comeback 8.7%, median 61 rounds
  left; g4 15.5%. Comebacks are kills on the leader carrying its bags (6.1 kills on the leader, 198 gems taken against
  far fewer in lost games), 4.3x as often on its own half, 2.85x within 3 of an altar. Flips against self-play are
  2-5% of games for any gambit: the ceiling is small.
- **Losers** (every gambit that takes bodies off the farm): (b) pack hunting 3 or 5 hunters, bars 0-2, bold, bank
  first, carrier-only lost fights, at g600 / g4 / need ratio / race margin: 47.6-50.0%, comeback 3-10 points under
  REF's at g4 (s-hunt3b-g4 12.3 / 16.3, t-race 16.1 / 26.1); hunt forensics: +0.5 kills on the leader for +1.6 deaths
  and +27 gems lost. (b) with the ground at their altar 47.8-49.0%. (f) ambush bush 48.8% (13.1 / 16.1). (g) crystal
  hop (wait out of sight within 3, own ward, teleport on engage; census: a wall site with 3 wait tiles on 55% of maps,
  on a group worth 30%+ of their camps 21%) 47.0-48.0% in four forms (11.1-13.2 / 17.1-17.4); teleports are rare.
- **Level**: (a) mirror pull 49.8-50.2%; (c) deny (their-side camps' exposure x1.5 or x2) 50.3% of 3,960-5,683;
  (e) items (fight value x1.5 / 2 / 3, damage only) 49.9-50.1%; snipe (lost fights against carriers of 40+ gems)
  50.2-50.3%; snipe + items 50.2% of 4,957; g5 trigger 50.2% of 5,013.
- **Early SPRT H1s on cb-e**, all with deny and a g4 or earlier trigger: deny + snipe + items (w-free-g4) 51.3% of
  1,688 (18.2 / 15.2); deny + pull + snipe 51.2% of 2,066; deny + snipe 50.9% of 2,952; deny + items 51.6% of 1,800;
  deny + snipe + items at 300 / 100 ahead 51.6% of 2,535.
- **w-free-g4 held-out on cb-c: 50.4% of 20,480 (95% CI 49.7-51.1), comeback 17.3 / 16.6, out-of-fuel turns 1,251 /
  1,295.** The early stop read high.
- Random gambit logger (9 arms by a hash of map and episode, g4, `cb-L` 544300-544339, 20,480 games, 10,017
  CAND-cooked): items 17.0 ± 2.2, snipe 16.0, normal 15.9, pull 15.8, deny 15.7, hunt 11.0, ambush 10.3, hunt + items
  10.1, hop 9.9. A learned selector (logistic, cook state + 14 map metrics, held out by map, off-policy value) reads
  16.5-16.8 ± 2.2: no margin over the best single arm, not baked in.

## Draft model features: one-altar and misspecification (ocean, 2026-11-06)

Offline, no games: draft5's 1,088,482 games, 5-fold CV over maps scored on wins (changes x1e-4, fold SE; the deployed
model is 0.59876, its map terms worth 233). Details, tables and scripts: `research/ideas-2026-11-05/draftfeat.md`.
- **one_altar** alone -0.42 ±0.16 (4/5 folds; -6.6 ±3.3 on one-altar maps); odd_altar -0.72 ±0.26; bins and squares
  of the altar count about the same; zero_altar is constant (no pool map has 0 altars). Special, but small: a few
  points per champion (Vendetta -3.5 to -3.9, Prism +2.7 to +2.9 on 3-4 picks; Tavi +2.8, Varg -3.0 on 5).
- **GBM** (HistGradientBoosting, same folds) 0.59131: **-74.5**. The logistic is misspecified, but not by
  calibration or side. Missing: mapgen's monoliths, golems, camps_side, walls, shared_groups (-16.0 ±0.3),
  squares and products of the economy features. **F92** (those five, one_altar, 25 squares, 36 products; w penalty
  320) **-53.4 ±0.35**, 5/5 folds, -52 ±3 reweighted to ladder-mix altar counts. A residual GBM still finds -16 of
  higher-order champion x map structure. Counters (never searched since draft3) -2.9 ±0.2.
- F92 (`replays/draftlab/draft5-feat`) changes the deployed team on 83 of 126 ladder maps and 1,271 of 2,047 fresh
  ladder-mix maps. Under F92 its teams beat draft5's by +2.1 to +3.4 points against the ladder prior on the ladder (+1.6
  to +1.8 fresh, +2.2 to +4.3 on one-altar maps). Under draft5 the switch costs 1.4 to 2.8.
- Candidate `bots/variants/oc-draftfeat` (oc-base4 plus F92's header and the 67 features in map_features.cc): native
  parity on 384 maps gave 0 team mismatches, and the derived values are within 2 ulp (log's last bit). The first draft
  turn costs ~55k more fuel, max 6.88M of 10M, and none ran out. Lab data is `variants/ocean-base` self-play.
- **A/B: no gain.** `oc-draftfeat2` (oc-retest-clean plus F92), own drafts, 2x fuel. **df-e 49.9% of 20,480
  (49.2-50.6)**, with SPRT 0.50/0.51 accepting H0 at 4,927 games (49.4%). One-altar maps 49.7% (48.5-51.0), df-v
  (`--mix varied`) 50.6% of 5,120, ladder head-to-head 49.6% of 256. Not run: the real budget, the confirm and the panel.
- Where the teams differ (12,576 games: 49.9%), F92 predicted 53.7% and draft5 46.5%, both worse than a coin there.
  Each model's argmax looks ~3.5 points better to itself than it is (optimizer's curse, plus another bot's lab games).
  Better CV on random teams does not draft better. Keep draft5. A draft6 lab is not worth it for the features alone;
  if one runs, include them and judge candidate teams head-to-head.

Full record: `research/ideas-2026-11-05/draft6.md`; tools in `research/ideas-2026-11-05/draft6-tools/`; lab

and `variants/panel-proteus`, each drafting from its own vehicles. The model gains a per-opponent offset and per-opponent
champion deviations (`model.mjs`: groups `opp`, `dev`). Pool: the ladder maps plus fresh ladder-mix seeds
548000-548099. Sampling as in draft5 (Thompson, explore, probe, current; half against ladder compositions).

  - 25 features: CV 0.5698 (lam b 4, w 5120, syn 320, dev 1024).
  - Counters: -3.7 (1e-4) in CV, left off.
  - F92 (draftfeat's 92 features): 0.5658 (-39).
  - Leaving one opponent bot out costs 5-16 (1e-4).
  - The per-bot deviations help in-sample but not on the held-out bot.

  - Split-half selection (`model.mjs selcheck`): self-assessed gains run ~0.35 points above honest ones.
  - An LCB team rule (kappa, posterior draws) changes nothing measurable.
  - x4 shrinkage looks +0.3 better offline but is level in play (C2 against C1, 49.9%).
  - Deployed: the posterior mean at the CV's penalties.
- **Gates:** for every candidate, JS/C++ parity on 384 maps (ladder + fresh-548200..548239) gives 0 team mismatches. The first draft turn stays within 10M: max 9.23M against the base's 9.17M, 0 of 1,348 drafts out of fuel.

(548200-548239), d6-c (548300-548339), d6-v (548400-548409, `--mix varied`), d6-p2 (548500-548509). df-c is
545100-545139.

## Teacher regression: missing crew index (2026-11-06; CHANGES 443)

The initial teacher’s 47.38% came from a merge bug: the copied wip crew reader
never populated current astraeus’s `claiming[]` / `n_claiming` index. Farm’s
optimized crew-work forecast and claimed-group bound therefore saw no claimers,
while the crew planner saw them. It overvalued joining camps allies would finish
before arrival and repeatedly switched targets. Restoring the index retains
exact walks and all wip assumptions; no fuel limits or warm-up are restored.
A separate live-visibility check fixes shield reads of allies hidden by our move.

Each completed diagnostic A/B used 10,000 games on the same 5,000 maps, both
sides, own drafts, unchanged normal-fuel astraeus opponent. Unmodified astraeus
with per-bot 10M fuel: 52.73% (zero OOF). Teacher with old search budgets: 47.30%;
visibility fix: 47.35%; original combat planner: 47.31%; original crew model:
53.25%; original shop: 47.17%; eager warm-up: 47.28%; original crew recruitment
policy only: 47.72%; original crew model with exact walks: 53.43%.

**Current teacher (crew index fixed): 52.48% (5,248–4,752; 95% Wilson
51.50–53.46)**. Initial-to-fixed paired delta +5.10 points. Crew-join log entries
fall from 4,820,383 to 811,771. **Confirmation: 52.62% (5,262–4,738;
51.64–53.60)** on 5,000 newly seeded maps (862001–862020, sampling seed 862000),
10,000 games. Content hashes reveal three repeated layouts; excluding their
six games leaves 52.61% on 9,994 unseen-layout games. No failed matches or teacher
OOF in either final run. Opponent OOF: 42,851 (original suite), 42,591 (confirmation).

Final teacher frozen at `replays/frozen/a299d95209c9/astraeus_teacher`, opponent
at `replays/frozen/60d2c6a7c8ab/astraeus`. Full per-run summaries, provenance,
source hashes, paired intervals, log counts and caveats are in
[research/astraeus-teacher-2026-11-06/README.md](astraeus-teacher-2026-11-06/README.md).
`tools/teacher_ab.py` also supports finite per-bot fuel controls; native default
stock parity and asymmetric finite/unlimited behavior passed the runner probe.
`astraeus_wip` is deleted at the user’s request after this port and diagnosis.

## Teacher audit: fresh search after a blocked opening walk (2026-11-06; CHANGES 449)

A hidden blocker on the first planned walk now triggers a complete new search
and pricing pass after restoring guards and releasing the previous search's
references to shared storage. Each bumped tile remains excluded, so retries
make progress without a fuel/retry cap. Other failure cases retain their current
fallback. Source `ef72ff1e6bf6`.

Unlimited teacher versus identical normal-fuel astraeus executable, 20,000 games:
**53.280% versus 53.300%** (10,656 vs 10,660); 12 gained, 16 lost; paired 95% delta
interval −0.072 to +0.032 points. No match errors or teacher fuel exhaustion.
Kept as a search-completeness improvement under the user's exception; no WR gain
established. This concludes the pass at the user's request. Results and deferred
work: [teacher audit](astraeus-teacher-2026-11-06/AUDIT.md).

## Draft first turn bounded by map structure (oc-draftfix, 2026-11-07; CHANGES 456)

`variants/oc-draftfix` is oc-base14 with three changes. (1) The clearance sum is computed exactly with bitboard host
erosions instead of a BFS (about 1.5M down to about 0.1M fuel). (2) The level-1/2 dash search only tries dashes from
tiles next to a hole or altar, also exact. (3) A structural work bound fitted as an LP envelope over map geometry and
deterministic feature work counts (`work_budget` in draft.cc, limit 8.7M) cuts attack groups from the end, then ward
sites, on maps it predicts would overrun. The fuel cap stays as a last resort; the local guards are unchanged.

- Base profile over 41,216 drafts: max 12.59M; 394 drafts over 9M, 109 over 10M. Heavy sections were clearance (up
  to 1.8M), dash (2.6M), sight (2.5M), crystal travel (3.7M), attacks (2.4M) and wards (2.8M). The PLAN-CHECK on
  gen-maze-65502003001 came from features using 9.4M, which left analyse too little for the map build.
- `firstturn.py --need` on ladder plus `draftfix-held` (23,168 maps, `--mix varied` included): p50 3.31M, p99 7.42M,
  max 8,695,372. Across all 107,776 drafts profiled (ladder, held, d7port, vtrain), the max is 8.75M.
- Real budget on 53,888 maps (107,776 drafts): 0 lost, 0 unfinished, 0 capped. The maze map is fixed.
- Feature parity (debug, ladder plus d7port): 41,216/41,216 identical. `bench.py` wide at 100M: 52/52 identical.
- Plan identity: 0 of 256 ladder drafts change. About 1% of ladder-mix generated drafts change (d7port 392/40,960,
  held 308/30,720, varied 632/15,360), all on maps the bound flags; about 40% of those are under 9.2M in the base.
- A/B against oc-base14 on `draftfix-943` (943000-943079), fast runner, real budget, own drafts: **50.0 (49.5-50.5)**
  of 40,960. 0 handoff failures; capped drafts CAND 0, REF 290; OOF level (302.7k vs 302.6k).

Sources: `replays/ab/draftfix-943/`; profiles and scripts in `/home/ubuntu/tmp-offload/draftfix/` (v7/ is the final run).

Merged afterwards as CHANGES 456 onto ocean with 455 (`variants/oc-base15`, pre-merge `variants/oc-base14-455`).
`bench.py` at 100M: 136/136 identical. `firstturn.py`, ladder + draftfix-held (46,336 drafts): need max 8,695,372; at
the real budget 0 lost, unfinished, capped or PLAN-CHECK.

## Willow arms (ocean, 2026-11-07)

Analysis first: research/ideas-2026-11-07/willow.md, from 16,467 ladder replays with a Willow, split by version era.
Fish's Willow takes 2.8% of its team's camp gems and ours 12.7%. Fish's stays within 2 of some teammate (ours 3-4;
1.5 allies in heal range in quiet rounds, ours 0.9), not near the carry. It heals 6.6 times per 100 rounds against
our 5.2.

`variants/oc-willow-dev` is `bots/ocean` as of 2026-11-07 morning (frozen as `variants/oc-willow-base`) plus
`params::willow` knobs:
- `shy`: Willow is hold-shy like Cassi and Issac.
- `follow`: 1 follows the carry, 2 the group (the ally with the most allies within `crowd_radius`). On a farm turn
  more than `follow_dist` from it, Willow steps back instead of farming.
- `join_claim`: within the leash, hit the followed ally's claimed group if it is awake.
- `gate`: enemy near, ahead or not ahead.
- Ablations: the heal step, the bank heal step and the formation.
- Heal thresholds: `heal_least_scale`, `step_min_share`.

With every knob off, `bench.py` at 100M gives 16/16 and wide 52/52 replays identical, with identical fuel. Arms are
`variants/ow-<name>`, made by `/home/ubuntu/tmp-offload/willow/scripts/mkarm.py`.

**Willow maps.** Ocean's own draft picks Willow on both sides or on neither (5,187 of the 10,240 maps of
fresh-771000..771039; 32% of ladder+gen games). Willow-only changes leave every other game identical, so the
screens ran on `merged/willow-771`, the 5,187 maps where it is drafted (10,374 games). Screens were at 2x fuel, fast
runner, `--no-test-draft`, against oc-willow-base.

**SPRT screens (0.50/0.52, seeds 101-119; SPRT-stopped rates are biased up):**

- H0: shy alone 49.7; fg3a (only while ahead) 48.5; no heal step 50.6; no bank heal step 49.6; no formation 49.8;
  heal_least 0.5 48.3, 0.25 45.8; step_min_share 0.3 49.5; fc3e 50.6.

## Behaviour-gap arms (ocean, 2026-11-07)

Analysis first: research/ideas-2026-11-07/behaviour-gaps.md, a census of every champion type in 18,599 ladder
replays (all of Fish's and Mite's 11-05 games, 500 of each other top team's, and every capture game since v82 went
live, which v82 played). The four biggest gaps that a knob can move: we dash ~40% more (Vendetta, Vesper, Issac, Ren:
9.3-11.6 per 100 alive rounds against Fish's 6.2-7.6); we spread out early (Heart of Ruin, Vendetta, Cassi, Issac: 1.0-1.5
allies within 4 at ≤250 against Fish's 1.9-2.2); we bank small bags (18-28 gems a tribute against Fish's 25-50); our
Cassi stuns camps a third as often (1.1-1.6 per 100 alive rounds against 3.2-4.7).

`variants/gaps-dev` is oc-base16 plus `params::gaps` knobs, all off by default; with them off, `bench.py` at 100M gives
16/16 and wide test-draft 52/52 replays identical. Arms are `variants/gp-<name>` (`/home/ubuntu/tmp-offload/gaps/bin/mkarm.py`):
- `camp_stun_scale`: Cassi's stun on a camp member that reaches us or a seen ally passes the cast floor (40; a wolf's
  20 never did), worth Strength x scale.
- `travel_dash` (0: never travel-dash, per type mask), `travel_clearance` (the no-enemy radius for one, 10).
- `min_bank`: a bag under this many gems is not banked (bankable_bag returns 0), but for a winning bag or a closing game.
- `follow_until`, `follow_types`, `follow_dist`: until that round, those types follow the group as Willow does
  (willow_follow).

**Screens** (2x fuel, fast runner, own drafts, against oc-base16, SPRT 0.50/0.52, seeds 201-210 and 301-306;
`merged/gaps-pool-820` = fresh-820000..820039, or its 9,878 Cassi maps `gaps-ci-820`; SPRT-stopped rates are biased):
- H0: td0 (no travel dash) 30.0 of 287; td0x (no travel dash but Heart of Ruin) 41.2 of 493; fu250 (follow group
  to round 250, leash 3) 39.2; fu250d2 (leash 2) 36.0; fu120 43.2; cs4 (stun first) 45.9 of 567; cs1 (stun passes the
  floor) 49.9 of 2,318; tc16 (clearance 16) 49.4 of 1,679.
- H1: every min_bank from 15 to 80 (mb15 56.0, mb25 53.8, mb30 53.0, mb40 55.0, mb50 54.6, mb60 54.4, mb80 52.5;
  mb40nc, not for Cassi and Issac, 55.9).

**Bank family at full length** (2x fuel, gaps-pool-820, 20,480 games each, CI ±0.7): mb15 53.1, mb20 53.2, **mb25
54.4**, mb30 53.8, mb35 53.9, mb40 54.3, mb40nc 54.7, mb60 52.8. Flat from 25 to 40.

**Mechanism** (512 games each on fresh-820000, real fuel, base -> arm):
- mb25: gems a tribute 19-27 -> 35-45 for every non-Prism type (Fish 25-50); tributes -30 to -50%; recalls level;
  camp gems -3 to +20%; deaths level; gems lost at death up 0.3-1.8 per 100 rounds for Cassi and Issac.
- cs1: Cassi's camp stuns 1.34 -> 2.91 per 100 alive rounds (Fish 4.7); camp damage taken and deaths level.
- td0: dashes 9-11.5 -> 1.5-3 (below Fish's 7): travel dashes are most of ours, and they pay.
- tc16: dashes unchanged (travel dashes rarely start 10-16 tiles from an enemy).
- fu250: allies within 4 at ≤250 up to Fish's level (Heart of Ruin 1.18 -> 1.89, Vendetta 0.97 -> 1.75, Cassi
  1.46 -> 2.13), but early camp gems fall by a third to a half (Cassi 12.3 -> 6.1, Heart of Ruin 14.4 -> 10.0).

**Decisions at the real budget** (fast runner, own drafts, `merged/gaps-dec-821` = fresh-821000..821079, 20,480 maps,

classes from `turn_budget.py --by-bot`, OOF turns by the bag carried at the end of the round before):

## State-dependent behaviour model (ocean, 2026-11-07; level)

The user's idea: shift behaviour by game state (ahead / behind on gems, gold or items) instead of one fixed policy,
from a fitted model, aiming at +5 points. Design and data: research/ideas-2026-11-07/state-modes.md. Two passes of a
randomized factorial, against `variants/oc-base19` (oc-base17 without cbdp and the one-altar altar control; see
"CHANGES 459/460 removals measured"), own drafts, fast runner, real budget.
- **State** (model/modes.cc, read every 4th round): lead = tributed lead + carried lead (ours from comms, theirs as
  seen in the last 40 rounds) + item lead / 5, the items in gold from last-seen stats (30 a shard). Ahead or behind
  beyond 100.
- **Design:** each game draws a level in {-1, 0, +1} for every state x knob cell from a hash of the map and side (no
  comms; recomputed offline). Fit: win ~ mirror side control + per-cell level dummies, intent-to-treat (by the levels
  drawn, never by whether a state was reached), errors clustered by map.
- **Pass 1** (`oc-mode-rand`, modes-470, 40,960 games, 48.0% against oc-base19 as a logger): 5 states (even, ahead
  solid / fragile on the item lead's sign, behind soft / deep at -300 items) x 4 knobs: retreat (pack-zone ratio x 1.5
  / 0.67, brake_bag 30 / 12, bag_big 160 / 60), recall line ±0.08, bank (min_bank 40 / 12, chain 36 / 18), gold price
  x 0.7 / 1.4. SE 0.6 a level; 4 of 20 cells past 1.96 SE, about chance for ~60 comparisons. The argmax policy
  `oc-mode-p1` (even: bolder retreat and bags to 40; fragile: bags to 40; behind soft: bank from 12) read **49.5%
  (48.9-50.2) of 20,480** held out (modes-471).
- **Pass 2** (`oc-mode-rand2`, modes-fit2, 163,840 games, 48.4% as a logger): 3 states (even, ahead, behind) x 5 knobs:
  fight risk (plan.cc hit_given_reach x 0.5 / 2), kill value (life_value x 2 / 0.5), bank (min_bank 50 / 12, chain
  40 / 18), shop (shop_gain_scale x 0.5 / 2), camp risk (support.cc / farm.cc camp_risk x 0.65 / 1.5). SE 0.3 a level:

  | Cell | -1 vs 0 | +1 vs 0 |
  |---|---|---|
  | ahead.bank | -1.03 | -1.13 |
  | even.bank | -0.04 | -0.77 |
  | behind.bank | +0.49 | -0.29 |
  | ahead.shop | +0.54 | -0.15 |
  | even.shop | +0.37 | +0.28 |
  | behind.shop | +0.21 | -0.46 |
  | behind.camp | -0.46 | -0.08 |
  | every fight risk, kill value and other camp cell | within ±0.3 | within ±0.3 |

  min_bank 25 is the optimum while ahead or even; halving or doubling how bold fights are (hit_given_reach,
  life_value) or how much camp damage is accepted moves nothing in any state.
- **`oc-mode-p2`** (every state: shop x 0.5; behind: bags to 50, chain to 40): **50.4% (49.9-50.9) of 40,960** on
  modes-473 and **49.7% (49.0-50.4) of 20,480** on modes-471: **50.2% pooled over 61,440 held out**. Against
  astraeus on modes-474 (20,480 each): p2 61.7% (61.0-62.3), oc-base19 61.0% (60.3-61.6).
- **Mechanism** (2,400 sampled modes-473 games, p2 minus oc-base19 in the same games): unspent gold -4 ± 33 and shop
  trips -0.7 ± 0.8 (the shop knob moves nothing measurable); gems a tribute +1.9 ± 1.4 and tributes -0.6 ± 0.5;
  50+ bag deaths +0.09 ± 0.05; deaths and gems collected level.
- **Bench**: with `state_modes` 0 both code versions (`oc-mode-off`, `oc-mode-off2`) replay oc-base19 byte for byte
  at 100M (52/52). With it on at all-zero levels (`oc-mode-zero2`) 14 of 16 games diverge on fuel: the lead read costs
  +2.2% fuel.
- **Verdict:** level. Within this knob space the largest per-cell effects are about half a point, and summed over the
  chosen cells (before winner's-curse shrinkage) they reach ~+1.6; +5 is not there. Most of the knobs (aggression,
  camp risk) have no effect at 2x / 0.5x in any state, in self-play. Not tried: knobs that change where the team
  goes (camp sides, contested camps, home defence), opponents other than ocean (the effects are against a mirror),
  states finer than three bands, and per-map-type cells. The `oc-mode-*` variants, their suites (fresh-470000..478079)
  and replays are deleted; fits and scripts are in research/ideas-2026-11-07/state-modes-tools/.

## Willow early aggression (ocean, 2026-11-07/08; merged as CHANGES 463)

The user's idea: Willow's base Strength (55) is the highest of the ranged types, so use it early. Analysis in
research/ideas-2026-11-07/willow.md, "Early aggression": on camps ours is already as aggressive as Fish's (same
damage, hits and last-hit share); the gap is in fights. Fish's Willow deals twice our champion damage, takes part
in 38% of fights against 23%, and lands four times the kills.

`variants/wa-dev` is oc-base17 (= bots/ocean, live as v83) with `params::willow_aggr` knobs, all acting only before
round `until`:
- `stand`: an enemy's reach no longer sends Willow home while it is healthy (above `hurt_health_fraction`) with an
  ally within `stand_ally` (2): `stand_lost_at` decides.
- `chase`: Willow uses prey, pressed and team_pressed like the other types; `escort_chase` only while escorted.
- `hit`: within the follow leash, hit any enemy in reach, else any awake camp in reach.
- `reset`: after a follow hit, the reset unless the heal lands.
- `no_heal_step`, `free_guard` (the normal step guard while standing), `stand_fuel` (stand only with fuel for the
  simulation and a search).
- `turret`: escorted, under an enemy's reach and with an enemy in its own, Willow shoots it (the reset if the heal
  does not land) without the strike search.

All off: `bench.py` at 100M against `variants/wa-base` (a copy of oc-base17) gives 16/16, wide 52/52 and wide
test-draft 52/52 identical replays. Ocean's draft takes Willow on both sides or neither: on 5,227 of the 10,240
maps of fresh-886000..886039 (`merged/waggr-w886`) and 15,467 of the 30,720 of 887000..887119
(`merged/waggr-w887`). Every run below is on those maps, own drafts, fast runner, against wa-base.

**Screens at 2x fuel** (`waggr-w886`, 10,454 games at full length, CI about ±1.0; SPRT 0.50/0.52 seeds 101-111):
- H0: hit+reset+no_heal_step at R 150/250/400 (50.5, 47.3, 50.3); hit+reset 48.7; reset alone 50.6; stand alone
  49.7 (R 250), 49.1 (R 400); no_heal_step alone 50.2.
- H1, SPRT-stopped: all knobs at R 250, 52.8 of 1,886; at R 400, 51.6 of 6,246.
- Full length: stand+chase 51.1 (R 250), 50.7 (150), 50.9 (400), 51.3 (1000), 51.3 (whole game). With reset 51.3, hit
  50.4, hit+reset 51.2. All knobs 51.2 (R 250), 51.1 (150), 51.2 (400), with stand_ally 1 51.3, 3 51.0, 4 50.3.
  Chase alone 50.1. free_guard 50.5-50.6.
- The gain needs stand and chase together, and is about +1.2 on Willow games. Hitting more camps never helps.

**Mechanism** (stand+chase+reset at R 250 against base, 300 Willow maps, real budget, rounds 1-250, per 100
Willow-alive rounds): champion damage 43 -> 70 (Fish 112), champion hits 0.79 -> 1.27, fight participation 18% ->
23% (Fish 38%), Willow kills 0.025 -> 0.072 a game. Deaths 0.11 -> 0.13 early, 0.29 -> 0.21 in rounds 251-500.
Out-of-fuel turns in rounds 1-250 rise 38% (2,941 -> 4,069), and 18% over the game.

**Real budget.**
- stand+chase+reset (scr250), decided on `waggr-w887` (SPRT 0.50/0.51, from 20,000 games, seed 301): **50.6% (50.0-51.1)
  of 30,934**, undecided at full length. OOF 420.8k against 352.6k (+19%).
- On `waggr-w886` (10,454 each): scr250 49.9, sc250 50.0, all knobs 50.1, with `stand_fuel` 50.1, `escort_chase` 50.0,
  both 50.3 (R 1000 50.1). The fuel gates leave OOF at +18%: the extra fuel is the fights Willow now stays in.
- `turret` takes OOF back to level: t250 50.6, with escorted chase (tc250) 50.8, turret+reset 49.5, R 500 50.1, R 1000
  49.6.
- Decided on `waggr-w887` (seeds 311-312): **t250 50.3% (49.7-50.9) of 27,912, H0; tc250 50.0% (49.3-50.7) of 20,094,
  H0**.

The +1.2 at 2x fuel does not survive the real budget, and the cheap turret mode that keeps the fuel level does not
win. The held-out (`waggr-held-888`), varied (`waggr-varied-889`) and panel (`waggr-panel-8891`) suites were later
used by the follow-up below. Arms `variants/wa-*`, scripts and logs in

## min_bank by map features (ocean, 2026-11-07; merged as CHANGES 461)

The user's idea: a constant min_bank (25, CHANGES 458) could hide a map dependence. Fitted from the min_bank sweep's
per-map results, built on oc-base17 (the base was reset from oc-base19, which measured worse), merged as
`variants/oc-base21`.

**Analysis** (`/home/ubuntu/tmp-offload/mbmap/bin/`; data in `data/`)
- **Data:** the sweep's 529,181 games of mb20/30/35/40/50 against mb25 (oc-base17) on `mb-pool-810` (119,808 maps),
  joined to each suite's index.json metrics (`build.py`). Each arm played a random subset of maps.
- **Interaction scan** (`scan.py`): win ~ arm intercepts + u·z(feature), with u = (t - 25) / 25, SEs clustered by map.
  - gold_side gives **z = +9.2**, +1.3 points per SD per unit of u. Next: cluster_share −7.6, n_wolf +6.8,
    camps_side +6.4, the rest correlated with gold.
  - Permutation null (features shuffled across maps, 40 permutations): max |z| at 95% 3.3, at 99% 3.7.
  - Given u·gold (`partial.py`): altar_ratio **+4.8** (a farther nearest altar favours bigger bags), picks **−4.7**,
    camp_altar +4.0, log area −3.5; gems_side adds nothing.
- **Shape** (`bins.py`, gold_side deciles):
  - At gold under ~600, every arm loses: mb50 46.5-48.6, mb20 49.0-49.5.
  - Above ~1000, the bigger arms win: mb40 50.7-51.1, mb50 51.0-51.7.
  - mb20 never wins, so 25 is a floor, not the middle of a range.
- **Policy value**, cross-validated over map folds (5 folds, 3 seeds; `index.py`, `rules.py`). Off-policy: a rule's
  value is the sum over arms of the mean of 1{rule picks the arm}(win − 0.5) over that arm's games.
  - Ramp rules t = clamp(25 + (G - g0)/k, 25, tmax), with the grid chosen on the training folds:
    - G = gold: +0.15 to +0.18 (±0.28);
    - G = gold + altar_ratio + picks: **+0.48, +0.49, +0.66 (±0.30)**.
  - The in-sample best was g0 500, k 20, tmax 50, with weights 1000 (altar_ratio − 0.42) and −300 (picks − 4.5).
    That is the shipped function.
- **Second signal** (ladder replays, gaps/rows.pkl, `fish.py`): Fish's gems a tribute rise with the map's gold.
  - Spearman +0.30 (p 0.001) over 128 maps; 45 / 49 / 78 by gold tercile.
  - Map gems explain it equally well for Fish.
  - v82's (before mb25) is flat: 41 / 42 / 45.

**Build:** `PlanFacts` gains `gold` and `altar_pct`, measured in the draft (exact against mapgen on 32 maps). Picks are
read in play. Details in CHANGES 461. Checks:
- bench at 100M with the threshold held at 25 (`mbm17-c25`): identical, 16/16, 52/52 and 52/52.
- `firstturn.py --need`: 1,792 drafts, max 8.15M, 0 unfinished or capped.

## Counter-picking from ladder data (ocean, 2026-11-07/08; no arm)

Analysis in research/ideas-2026-11-07/counterpick.md.
- **Data:** big-arm's archive, 11-04 to 11-07: 762,746 games of 808 teams; the top subset (both ratings ≥ 2000) has
  142,985 games.
- **Model:** logistic. Antisymmetric champion, champion x map and synergy terms, team-day effects, rating, and 66
  counter pairs; L2, with the counter penalty chosen by map- and team-grouped CV.
- **Held out, counters improve log loss only a little** (1e-4):
  - top subset, map folds: -24.5, but -8.8 once a team-pair (bot-against-bot) term is added;
  - team folds: -3.3;
  - all games, team folds: -0.8;
  - lab draft7-f92 `--counters`: -4.4 (ctr penalty 1280).
- **Pairs:** with the matchup term, none is significant (0 of 66 at BH q < 0.05; 3 at |z| > 2, chance 3.3). At the
  CV penalty, |ctr| ≤ 0.036.
- **Our games** (fit without them): ocean v78-v84 +16.8 ± 8.1 (1e-4) better with counters. They transfer, but
  they are small.
- **Draft simulation** (oc-base21's `model_team` natively, 128 ladder maps x 16 test compositions):
  - shrunk counters change 0.3 / 6.8 / 12.8% of 3 / 4 / 5-pick teams, for a predicted ≤ +0.08 win-% points;
  - lightly penalised ones claim +6 but are worth -3.2 under the shrunk ones.
- **No arm:** the predicted gain is far under a 40k-game A/B's ±0.5. No games played.
- Scripts and data in `/home/ubuntu/tmp-offload/counter/`; link lab `replays/draftlab/draft7-f92-ctr`.

## Team-specific counters (ocean, 2026-11-08; no arm)

Analysis in research/ideas-2026-11-07/counterpick.md, "Team-specific counters".
- **Question:** are counters specific to the team that holds the champion (u[T, c, d]), and averaged away when pooled?
- **Model:** the ladder model with three random-effect blocks added: team x champion (tc), u[T, c, d], and team x
  champion x map (tcm, style by map).
- **Held out:** u does not transfer.
  - Map CV over tc: r2000 +11 to -1 (1e-4), all games +8 to -1. Over tc + tcm: +4 to +5, worse in 3-4 of 5 folds.
  - On a new day: -2 to -46.
  - tcm alone is worth -300 to -380 on a new day.
- **Variance:**
  - In-sample, u given tc is real: prior sd 0.09-0.18, LR 325-1,230, and every one of 18 team-label permutations
    is below (p < 0.05).
  - Given tcm, the variance's best estimate is 0. The "team-specific counters" are team style by map.
- **Ocean-specific:**
  - Largest posterior deviations ±0.094 (SE ~0.075); none has |z| > 1.3.
- **Opponent-specific:**
  - In our games, our champion x opponent is worth -29 (1e-4) on opponent-map folds; the largest is our HoR
    against Fish, -0.5 ± 0.2.
  - From their picks, Mite is identified 94% of the time after one pick and Fish 63-73%.
- **Draft value:** a Python port of oc-base25's draft (identical to the C++ sim), on our 4,774 games, cross-fitted by
  map halves over 6 splits:
  - ocean-specific: -0.07 ± 0.38 / +0.08 ± 0.08 win-% points (prior sd 0.088 / 0.044);
  - opponent-aware: -0.9 to +0.01;
  - against Mite: +0.34 ± 0.12; against Fish: -0.24 ± 0.10;
  - the in-sample estimates claim +0.75 to +4.7 (optimiser's curse).
- **No arm:** the predicted gain is under +0.3. Scripts in `/home/ubuntu/tmp-offload/counter2/`.

## 2026-11-08: Fish turn-order priority in ocean (merged as CHANGES 464)

The four modes of Intercontinental Fish's priority (research/fish-2026-11-05/TEAM.md; EXPERIMENTS "Fish priority
encoding") were ported as `params::fishprio` knobs in ocean's `plain_priority` (model/turn_order.cc). Bid bands
(kill, heal, channel) stay above them. With every knob off, bench.py at 100M was identical to oc-base21 and oc-base22:
16/16, wide 52/52 and wide test-draft 52/52, fuel included.
- **quiet:** a camp tie hit goes to the healthiest by health fraction in quarters, gemless first; ties go to the
  higher base max health, with Heart of Ruin just before Varg.
- **band:** Fish's idle formula replaces idle_priority: band = floor(4 (1 - min(1, ehp/max) x 0.65 if carrying)),
  with base health inside a band. This drops ocean's hits-in-hand camp order and the ostrich's enemy distance.
- **late:** at a contested camp, the idle value is shifted below every idle one (TEAM.md 1d, k = 1).
- **contact:** an enemy in reach seats us first next round if we start it, last if they do, with the most
  threatened outermost (j in sixteenths). This replaces the danger order and the ostrich.
- **Willow beside its ally** (TEAM.md 3d) is a movement rule, and support.cc has no priority input, so there was no
  priority arm for it.

Replay checks confirmed each mode writes its intended codes, e.g. late's idle values shifted by 24 and contact's at
24+j or below everything. The 2026-10-20 hecate port (read level) is superseded.

## min_bank learned from randomised thresholds (ocean, 2026-11-08; no merge)

Goal: a better per-map min_bank than CHANGES 461's hand-shaped ramp, learned from games with a random threshold.
After v84's live loss (multi-site maps) the reference became oc-base17 (flat 25), judged on the panel.

**Data** (`variants/mbl-data`: oc-base21 whose threshold is drawn per (map, side) by a hash of the draft facts and
the team, so games replay; the draft prints it and its picks. Checked: every champion's play value equals the
draft's print.) Real budget, fast runner, own drafts, `merged/mbl-data-c0..c7` (fresh-950000..950584, 149,760 maps):

| opponent | range | games |
|---|---|---|
| oc-base21 (mirror) | 15-70 | 115,200 |
| gp-panel-astraeus-td | 15-70, 0-70 | 76,800 |
| gp-panel-proteus-td | 0-70 | 69,120 |
| oc-base21-td | 0-70 | 38,400 |

Mean win at a random threshold against the mirror: 49.3%.

**Models** (`/home/ubuntu/tmp-offload/mblearn/bin/`; rows in `data/rows.jsonl`):
- Mirror (`bt.py`, `policy.py`): a Bradley-Terry model of a threshold's worth, s(x, t_ours) − s(x, t_theirs), pooled
  with the 461 sweep and decision games (835k games). Interactions with gold, altar ratio and picks beat a flat curve
  in held-out log loss; other map features add nothing.
  - By doubly robust value on held-out map folds (src-0 games, window ±8), nothing beats 461 in the mirror: argmax
    +0.19 ±0.41, refitted ramp +0.04, trees ±0.1, constants 25/40 −0.6/−0.7.
- Panel (`fitp.py`, per opponent and pooled; tent basis in t × map features, champions as main effects). Doubly
  robust values against flat 25, 184,320 games, window ±8:
  - 461 −0.14 ±0.38. Lower caps are worse: max 45 −0.48, max 40 −0.80. Floors 0/10 under 461's line are level.
    Constants 0 −2.5, 10 −0.8, 15 −0.3, 20 +0.17 ±0.27, 30 −0.23.
  - **20 on multi-site maps (altars > 1), 25 elsewhere: +0.29 ±0.24** (all three opponents +0.25 to +0.40; window ±4:
    +0.92 ±0.51). The model's argmax +0.67 ±0.38 (not compact; split very differently per opponent).
  - Agrees in direction with the live gate: smaller bags on multi-site maps.

**Decision** (`variants/mbl17-ms20` = oc-base17 + `min_bank_multi = 20`; with 25 it is bench-identical to oc-base17
at 100M: 16/16, 52/52, 52/52). The panel, cand and base on the same maps, paired by game:

| member | suite | base | ms20 | paired diff |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gp-panel-astraeus-td | `mbl-scr-955` | 79.53 | 79.76 | +0.22 ±0.52 |
| gp-panel-astraeus-td | `mbl-panel-959` | 79.60 | 79.41 | −0.19 ±0.53 |
| gp-panel-proteus-td | `mbl-scr-955` | 86.42 | 86.51 | +0.09 ±0.46 |
| oc-base17-td | `mbl-scr-955` | 73.74 | 72.92 | −0.82 ±0.59 |

20,480 games a row. On multi-site maps alone: astraeus +0.31 / −0.19, proteus +0.11, oc-base17-td −1.00 ±0.75.
- **Not merged.** No gain on astraeus or proteus, a loss against the ocean member. The off-policy +0.29 (chosen
  among ~25 policies on the same data) did not replicate. The decision was stopped there; the mirror held out and
  varied runs were not played.
- Conclusion: **no function found beats flat 25 on the panel.** Within the data, the threshold's worth is flat
  within about ±0.5 from 20 to 50 against every opponent. Below 15, it is clearly worse.
- Earlier screen against oc-base21 (`scr-*`, `mbl-scr-955`): 461 with floor 0 level (+0.02 astraeus, +0.14
  proteus). The steep-ramp and floor-10 arms were not played after the reference changed.
- In-play state (step 3) was not tried.
- Sources: `replays/ab/{mbl-d*,scr-*,d-*}`; batch replays deleted, results.json kept.

## Reply model: learned danger and pressure (ocean, 2026-11-08; not merged)

Danger at a strike end tile from how enemies actually answer, and next-turn pressure, learned from combat-lab rollouts
and wired into plan_strikes. Code: `bots/variants/oc-reply` (on oc-base21, frozen as `variants/rd-base`), scripts in
`research/reply-model/`, runner flag `--hitlog` (scenario.rs).
- **Data:** bank2 frames split by game (md5 % 10 == 0 held out): 120k train, 20k held-out frames, played ocean-ocean,
  ocean-astraeus and astraeus-ocean with lab copies that dump the features each turn (`labify_reply.py`). Labels from
  `--hitlog`: the damage e deals c until c's next turn (danger), and c's damage on e on its next turn (pressure).
  4.6M danger rows on oo alone. Counterfactual rows from `--alt 5` (`build_alt.py`): 274k danger, 144k pressure.
- **Features:** relational, from bot-visible beliefs (invisible enemies as safety's Reach sees them): e's source tiles
  for p by way and how many our side covers next turn, its turns before ours, its other targets, health near p on
  both sides, cooldowns, channel. 48 danger, 36 pressure.
- **Offline (held out):**

  | | Model | Ocean's 0.234 x blow | Refit |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Danger log loss | 0.42 | 0.64 | 0.62 |
  | Danger damage R2 | 0.44 | 0.21 | 0.25 |
  | Pressure log loss | 0.49 | | 0.66 |
  | Pressure damage R2 | 0.36 | | 0.19 |

  - The full model is GBDT P(hit) x E[dmg | hit], 4 x 60 trees of 16 leaves, compiled to if-else.
  - Ocean's flat danger is low on average: it predicts 41.5 against the true 56.
  - Ordering the alternatives of one decision (`--alt`):
    - danger: 0.845 (lean 0.839) against ocean's 0.775;
    - pressure: 0.758 (trained on alternatives 0.777, lean 0.759) against strike-at-d's 0.701.
- **Fuel:** the full model costs ~5.7k per danger query and 4k per pressure query.
  - The lean danger term is 1 regressor of 12 trees x 32 leaves on 28 cheap features. It reads ~51 splits, writes
    into the cached per-enemy vector and has R2 0.38. Below 40k fuel left, plan_strikes falls back to the flat term
    (`min_fuel`).
  - Lean pressure: 12 x 32, trained on the alternatives, top 3 tiles by bound only.
- **Lab, paired** (held-out val10k, H 30, real fuel, pooled over cand-vs-base, base-vs-cand and both against
  astraeus):
  - Reward: gem 0.0633, carried gems plus tributed during the rollout. The 0.01 readout agrees in sign everywhere.
  - Full danger: mark 10 -0.015 ± 0.011, mark 30 -0.061 ± 0.023. OOF 1.58% against base 0.57%.
  - The shadow arm computes the model and discards it: -0.032 at mark 10. So the loss was fuel. Full danger against
    shadow: +0.013 ± 0.008.
  - At 2x fuel: full danger +0.003 ± 0.008 / +0.010 ± 0.017. The first pressure arm (hit x hit_worth, all tiles,
    on-policy training) was -0.027 / -0.045, and -0.19 / -0.44 at real fuel.

  | Arm | Mark 10 | Mark 30 | OOF |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | lean, no gate | -0.002 ± 0.010 | -0.021 ± 0.019 | 0.92% |
  | lean, gate 40k (`rlg`) | +0.002 ± 0.006 | -0.005 ± 0.016 | 0.60% |
  | lean, gate 25k / 15k | +0.000 / -0.001 | -0.017 / -0.021 | 0.74 / 0.90% |
  | lean x 0.75, gate 40k | +0.002 ± 0.005 | -0.004 ± 0.015 | 0.60% |
  | + lean pressure 0.1 / 0.25 | +0.001 / -0.001 | +0.010 / +0.009 (± 0.02) | 0.75% |

- **A/B** against rd-base, own drafts, fast runner:
  - Dev, fresh-981000..981019, 10,240 games each:

    | Arm | Win % | OOF turns, CAND / REF |
    |---|---|---|
    | rlg | 50.2 (49.3-51.2) | 87.1k / 85.4k |
    | lean x 0.75 | 50.1 | |
    | lean, no gate | 49.1 (48.1-50.0) | 156k / 91k |
    | + pressure 0.1 | 48.9 (47.9-49.8) | 102k / 86k |
    | + pressure 0.25 | 50.0 | 101k / 86k |

  - Held out, fresh-982000..982039: **rlg 49.7% (49.1-50.4) of 20,480**, OOF 180.5k / 178.6k.
- **Not merged:** about 49.9% over 30,720 games.
  - The better prediction changes about 20% of lab fights but does not make them better on balance.
  - Ocean's other strike terms were tuned against the flat danger, and only the ~1.1 exactly priced tiles of a search
    use it.
  - Pressure is neutral to negative and costs +17% OOF.
- Sources: `replays/ab/reply-*`, `replays/combatlab/reply/` (npz data, models, base lab arms; batch replays deleted).

## Reply model phase 2: one danger (dg-*, ocean 7fc160d6d, 2026-11-08; nothing merged)

This ran `research/reply-model/PLAN2.md` from step 0. It stopped by the plan's own rules after step 2.
- **Setup:**
  - Base `bots/variants/dg-base` = `./copybot -r 7fc160d6d ocean`. Work is in `bots/variants/dg-dev`: `model/danger.{h,cc}` (namespace `hazard`), the generated `model/danger_model.h` and the `params::danger` knobs. Variants are `dg-*` and lab copies `lab-dg-*`.
  - Scripts: `research/reply-model/export_gam.py`, `calib.py`, `consistency.py`, `dg_lab.sh` and `dg_variant.sh`.
  - Suites:
    - dev `maps/suites/merged/dg-dev-984` (fresh-984000..019, 5,120 maps);
    - held out `dg-held-985` (985000..039);
    - varied `dg-varied-986` (986000..019, `--mix varied`).
  - Every A/B ran on the fast runner with own drafts (`--no-test-draft`), against dg-base.
  - Lab: val10k frames, H 30, paired against lab-dg-base. The base lab averages 68.2k fuel per fight turn and runs out of fuel on 0.65% of turns.
- **Step 0, export: passes.**
  - `danger_model.h` holds the full GAM (folded per enemy) and min5.
  - C++ against Python on 20k held-out rows: the logit differs by at most 6.9e-7 (full) and 3.0e-7 (min5), p by at most 4.7e-6.
  - Mean calibration k: full 0.939, min5 0.918, flat 0.326. Unseen enemies get 0.316 x blow.
  - Per-opponent p_kill calibration was not done.
- **Step 1, shadow (compute and discard): fails the OOF bar (≤ +3% relative), and so does the min5 fallback.**
  - With the shadow off, bench replays at 100M are identical (16/16 and 52/52).
  - The shadow costs +1.0-1.3% mean fuel in the bench. In the lab it is +0.2-0.3k a fight turn, well inside §4's 3-6k.
  - Even so, out-of-fuel turns rise:

    | Arm | Sites | Lab OOF | Lab mark-10 reward | Dev A/B (10,240) | Game OOF turns |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | base | | 0.65% | | | |
    | burn (no model, ~1k fuel loop per pricing search) | | 0.67% | +0.001 ± 0.002 | | |
    | shm5c (min5 only) | plan model sites | 0.875% | −0.006 ± 0.006 | 48.8% (47.9-49.8) | +42% |
    | shmc (full by fuel, else min5/flat) | plan model sites | 0.925% | −0.007 ± 0.006 | 49.3% (48.4-50.3) | +43% |
    | shc | all 15 sites | 1.27% | −0.025 ± 0.014 | | |

  - The census bench at real fuel (25 heavy maps) rose from 265 to 629 OOF turns.
  - The burn arm shows that ocean's gates absorb a flat per-search cost of the same mean size. What runs them out is the hazard's cost growing with query count, which concentrates it in the turns that are already heaviest.
  - The shadow alone loses about a point in games (shm5c's CI excludes 50).
  - Full arms: sh1, sh2, shm, shm5, shmb, shm5b and sht are in the scratch logs `replays/combatlab/dg-lab-*.log`.
- **Step 2, consistency fixes with flat danger kept (`dg-s2`): counters fall, A/B level, dropped.**
  - What it changes:
    - the step guard keeps a stands-only pass after a won union;
    - a fuel-gated per-tile stand check;
    - unknown tiles are walled by a Strike bound, where before the guard was dropped;
    - plan_strikes skips grid_r tiles that `stand_leaves`.
  - Counters, 512 games on fresh-984000:

    | Counter (among turns that moved) | dg-base | dg-s2 |
    |---|---|---|
    | Chosen tile that want_home would leave | 16.8% | 15.1% |
    | Strike then leave | 23.8% | 22.9% |
    | A-B-A flips | 10.2% | 9.9% |

    In dg-base, 75.8% of rejected tiles are left on the next turn.
  - Lab: mark 10 +0.005 ± 0.011, mark 30 −0.012 ± 0.019; OOF 0.78%.
  - A/Bs:

    | Suite | Win rate | Games | 95% CI | Game OOF turns |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | dev | 49.7% | 10,240 | 48.7-50.6 | +16% |
    | held out | 50.0% | 20,480 | 49.3-50.7 | +16% |
    | varied | 49.9% | 10,240 | 49.0-50.9 | +20% |

  - Level, with extra fuel and code, so §6's rule drops it.
- **Step 2's fallback alone** (`variants/oc-unk` on ocean 9c8a7ae5b, against `variants/oc-unk-ref-9c8a7ae5b`): where
  the step guard runs out of fuel or cannot simulate, wall the tiles the foes' open-ground bound plus full camp damage
  could kill us on, instead of no guard. **49.9% of 40,960** (49.5-50.4) on the fresh `unk-held-991` (991000-991079),
  own drafts. OOF turns +14% (489k vs 430k): the fallback's per-tile `camp_damage` runs exactly on turns already out
  of fuel. A cheap form (`variants/oc-unk2`: the bound alone, no camps, skipped when every reaching foe's best blow
  together cannot kill us) is **50.1% of 40,960** (49.6-50.6) on the fresh `unk2-held-992`, OOF +1.6%: the fuel hid
  no gain. Not merged.
- **Stop:**
  - §7's rule: min5 also over +3% OOF means keep flat danger and do only step 2. Step 2 is level, so steps 3-10 are skipped.
  - The oscillation counters move about 1-2 points without changing results. That fits §7's reading: the oscillation is not costing games.
- **Next, if this is picked up again:**
  - The model's cost is small but lands in the worst turns.
  - Any retry has to budget hazard queries inside ocean's fuel gates (`fight_cost_estimate`-style accounting, or an anytime cap per turn) before step 3 can be judged on behaviour. Alternatively, it should use a bar for OOF that a burn arm of equal cost tests.
- Sources:
  - `replays/ab/dg-*`, `replays/combatlab/dg/`, `replays/combatlab/dg-lab-*.log`;
  - `replays/fuel/dg/`.
  - Batch replays deleted.

## Position comms (ocean, 2026-11-07/08; merged as CHANGES 465)

Whether ocean should share positions through comms: allies' own and enemy sightings. Scripts in
`research/comms-positions-2026-11-07/` (`analyse.py`, `mech.py`, `panel.py`); arms `variants/cm-*`.

**Analysis** (600 mirror games of oc-base21 on 300 `g2-pool-840` maps, both teams, replay vision `sees`):
- Of 8,254 deaths to champions, the victim saw a damager in the 3 rounds before the first hit in 79%; a teammate saw it
  first, within 12 of the victim, in 9.9% (817 deaths, 8.6% of the gems lost to kills); nobody in 9.8%. That 10% is
  the ceiling for threat sharing, and the victim often dies anyway.
- 5.2% of champion turns have an enemy within 8 that a teammate saw this round or last and we do not.
- An enemy carrying 40+ gems that a teammate sees goes unseen by another ally within 10 in 35% of samples.
- Willow's follow target: visible 75.5%, seen within 2 rounds 4.2%, claim centre 20.3% (37,160 of 183,485 turns);
  the claim centre was within 5 of the ally in 42% and 15+ off in 30%.
- Free bits after claims, bag and camp record: mean 16; 13+ in 80% of bot instances, 18+ in 43% (the worst case is
  full, comms.cc). The priority payload is no channel for positions: it is read only while the sender is in sight.

**Arms** (free bits only, nothing traded; each record left out where it does not fit; c x c cells, c = 1/3/5):
- `cm-ally`: each non-healer posts its own position in turn while a healer lives; Willow's follow uses it before the
  claim centre. Fits 80% of instances; posted tile within 2 of the ally in 91%; claim-centre turns 17.4k -> 4.9k.
- `cm-sight1`: the most urgent visible enemy for a teammate (nearest one that may not see it, carriers -4) fixes the
  reader's belief (`World::note_told`, a cell-shaped `possible`). Fits 66%; within 2 tiles in 97%; 36% already seen.
- `cm-sight2`: carriers (30+ gems) only, and prey() chases a told carrier within 10. `cm-sight3`: as sight1, applied
  only by a reader carrying 20+ gems.
- Knobs off: bench 100M identical to oc-base21 (16/16, wide 52/52, wide test-draft 52/52) and to oc-base17 (16/16,
  52/52), +0.04% fuel.

**Screens** at 2x fuel against oc-base21, `merged/cm-pool-925` (925000-925039), 20,480 games each: ally 50.3
(49.7-51.0); sight1 **48.4** (47.8-49.1, out-of-fuel turns +29%); sight2 49.7 (49.0-50.4); sight3 49.2 (48.5-49.9).
Sightings lose again, as in macro-4 and river: allies give way to enemies they cannot see, and bag-only or
carrier-only use does not change that.

**cm-ally at the real budget**, own drafts:

## Gold price: enemy term, split, exchange rate (ocean = oc-base23, 2026-11-08; mid125 merged as CHANGES 466)

The user's three ideas on `per_gold` / `gems_share` (analysis and design: research/ideas-2026-11-08/gold-price.md).
Dev copy `bots/variants/oc-gp-dev` (`params::gp::`, off: bench 100M identical to oc-base23, 16/16, wide 52/52);
arms `variants/oc-gp-<arm>`. Against `variants/oc-base23`, own drafts, fast runner, real fuel, SPRT 0.50/0.5025 (one
seed per screen; none decided, all ran the suite).

**Data.** Top-ladder close games (archive 2026-11-05..07, both ratings > 2150) put gold at 0.35 / 0.57 / 0.30 / 0.17
/ 0.07 / 0.02 gems a gold by max tributed (0-100 / -250 / -400 / -600 / -800 / -1000), confounded by carried gems;
our own 4,239 traced games with carried gems: 0.32 (250-400), 0.19 (400-600), 0.07 (600-800). ocean's per_gold
(oc-gp-trace): median 0.27 / 0.20 / 0.13 / 0.085 / 0.052 / 0.011, mean ~1.4x. So a ~1.5x mid-game lean at most. The
enemy term binds 14-40% of turns (half when the enemy leads by 100+); dropping it mostly raises the share past 800
(6x). Bodies' actual gem shares are uneven (Vesper 1.7x, Prism 1.6x, Cassi 0.44x, Willow 0.62x of an even split).

Wave 1, `merged/gp-dev` (fresh-673000..673039), 20,480 games each:

| arm | change | win % | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|
| em1 | no enemy term | 49.7 | 49.0-50.4 |
| em2 | enemy term at the pace ratio (ours / theirs) | 49.7 | 49.0-50.4 |
| em2s | same, ratio clamped 0.67-1.5 | 50.2 | 49.5-50.9 |
| sp1 | split by camp output | **48.9** | 48.2-49.6 |
| sp3 | split by the measured type shares | **48.9** | 48.2-49.6 |
| sph5 | Willow counts as half a body | 50.3 | 49.6-51.0 |
| mid15 | per_gold x1.5 hump over 100-700 tributed | 50.2 | 49.5-50.9 |
| mid20 | same, x2 | 49.9 | 49.2-50.6 |

## Codegen pragmas (ocean, 2026-11-08; nothing merged)

**Ladder flags, inferred.** The CLI ships the submission service's compiler as a hidden `cambc compile-job --input
bundle.zip --language cpp --output out.zip`; it needs cmake and ninja on PATH, from `~/.cache/cambc/`. It calls
`cambc __compile-bot`, which configures the embedded `cmake/CMakeLists.txt` with `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`
and `CAMBC_DEBUG=OFF`. The compile line is `-O3 -DNDEBUG -std=c++20 -msimd128 -mbulk-memory -mbulk-memory-opt
-fwasm-exceptions -mllvm -wasm-use-legacy-eh=false`. The link is `-O3 -fwasm-exceptions --no-wasm-opt -lunwind`, with no
LTO, then a check-injection pass. This is the same as a local `cambc build --release`. The asset SDK equals `sdk/cpp`, minus
`cambc_local.h`. This assumes the platform runs this CLI's `compile-job`; nothing was submitted to check it. Local
A/Bs and `bench.py` never pass `--release`, so they play the `CAMBC_DEBUG` build. On ocean, the release build is −0.42%
fuel against debug (wide set, 52/52 identical).

**What clang (wasi-sdk-33, wasm32) honours**, by probe (`~/tmp-offload/codegen/probe/`, objdump instruction counts):
- **Ignored:** `#pragma GCC optimize` (silently), `__attribute__((optimize))` (warns). `hot` has no effect, and
  `target("simd128")` is a no-op because -msimd128 is already global.
- **Honoured:**
  - `#pragma clang optimize off` (optnone, so it can only cost);
  - `#pragma clang loop unroll(disable|full)`, `unroll_count`, `vectorize(disable)`, `vectorize_width`, `interleave`;
  - `always_inline` and `noinline`, also as statement attributes (`[[clang::always_inline]] r = f(x);`);
  - `flatten`, including callees too big to inline;
  - `cold`, `minsize` and `#pragma clang attribute push(..., apply_to=function)`, which act as size optimisation for
    that function;
  - `target("no-simd128")`, `__restrict` and `__builtin_assume`;
  - `#pragma clang fp reassociate(on)`: vectorises float reductions but changes results.
- **No change in the probe:** `[[likely]]` / `__builtin_expect`. `fp contract` does nothing, as wasm has no FMA.

**Headroom, with global CXXFLAGS as a ceiling** (oc-base25 copies, wide set, 100M, against oc-base25, mean / total fuel):

| Flags | Mean | Total | p99 |
|---|---|---|---|
| no loop vectoriser | −0.2% | +0.05% | +0.2% |
| no SLP / no vectorising | +0.2% / +0.3% | | |
| no unrolling | +5.5% | | +5.1% |
| `-mllvm -unroll-threshold=600` / `1500` | −0.4% / +0.7% | | |
| runtime unrolling | +0.1% | | |
| `-mllvm -inline-threshold=1000` / `3000` | −0.8% / −1.1% | | −1.2% (3000) |
| inline-threshold 3000, release | −1.2% | | −1.1% |

Flag builds change 1-5 of 52 replays even at 100M: ocean has fixed spent-fuel budgets (e.g. `reveal_grow_fuel`
in bot.cc, `used` in plan.cc), so codegen can move decisions.

**Source levers on the hottest functions.** All-turn self profile, `replays/fuel/fc7/prof`, 26 maps, 275k turns,
mean 45.5k: farm_turn 13.8% (already flatten), update_champion 5.3%, static_window 3.5%, sight 3.1%, update_camps
2.9% (flatten), attack_viewers 2.6%, set_turn_order 2.4%. Ocean already carries 222 such annotations (26 flattens,
6 loop pragmas). Effect of `[[gnu::flatten]]` on each, total fuel:

| Function | Total fuel | Replays identical |
|---|---|---|
| all 10 together | +2.66% | 50/52 |
| static_window | +2.46% | |
| Reach::build | +1.00% | |
| find_members | +0.20% | |
| update_champion | +0.11% | |
| set_turn_order | +0.07% | |
| sight, rank_turns, read_priorities | 0 | |
| comms::send | −0.02% | |
| attack_viewers | −0.24% | 52/52, debug and release |

The attack_viewers flatten (`bots/variants/oc-cg`) does not clear the out-of-fuel bar. At the real budget, on the same
52 games (which diverge), out-of-fuel turns were 705 → 770 on the debug build. Turns at 99.9k or more were 1,040 → 1,102
on debug and 1,022 → 1,098 on release. Not merged, no A/B. Verdict: pragmas work but leave no 2% here. The inliner
ceiling is ~1% and can only be set by flags, which the ladder fixes. Hand flattening mostly costs.

## Camp-group draft features (ocean = oc-base25, 2026-11-08; no arm)

Write-up: research/ideas-2026-11-08/campfeat.md. These are the teammate's features: gem and gold cluster group
counts, "exactly one" flags, and a light (no Golem or Monolith), compact (seen whole from one tile), high-value
group (`hv_compact`, `hv_rate`).
- **Draft:** on draft7's lab (1M games, map-grouped CV, 1e-4 log loss), an offset screen over F92:
  - `hv_compact` -0.67 ± 0.22, `hv_rate` -0.70 ± 0.24;
  - the counts and flags +0.62 ± 0.30;
  - over F25 the same features find -6.8 ± 0.8, so F92 already holds that information.
- **Value:** cross-fitted by map halves through pysim, `hv_compact` + `hv_rate` changes ocean's team on 15% of maps
  for +0.026 ± 0.002 win-% points (in-sample +0.085). Under a tenth of the +0.25 bar: no candidate, no games.
- **Knobs:** beyond the ctxknob agent's cells, no feature has a consistent slope for mid_gold or invade deny
  (3 of 40 tests |z| >= 2).
- **mapgen:** ladder-mix suites give 51% of maps a gem-cluster-only group of 3+, against 28% on the ladder
  (`LADDER_GROUPS` gem-only make-ups and the `classic` gems templates). That gap drives `hv_rate`: median 15.4 against
  12.0. The counts match. A `GEM_BALL` 0.5 factor closes about half the gap. It is proposed, not applied.
- The archive's 128 maps are `maps/`'s 128 byte for byte; the names differ only by `_` against `-`.

of games, net +47 flips (z +0.74); cap 3 changes 30%, net -12 (dropped). cap 2 SPRT on the Monolith maps of

**Lock deny** (`params::lock_deny_from`: before this round, bank.cc `place_lock` places no lock only to deny an altar;
locks that cancel an enemy tribute and the one-altar guard's lock stay). Sweep against oc-base25, every threshold on

| threshold | 250 | 400 | 500 | 600 | 700 | 750 | 800 | 900 | 1200 | never |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| points | +0.35 | +0.39 | +0.60 | +0.55 | +0.48 | +0.43 | +0.43 | +0.46 | +0.56 | +0.55 |

All ±0.5. A plateau from 500 on; 0 against 600 changes 86% of games, 600..never are mostly identical (1200 against
never 94.5% the same). Post-hoc SPRT along completion order: only 600 crossed H1 (35,048 games, 50.69%).

**The fitted function loses to the fixed round.** A regularised logistic P(win | threshold, map features: altar
count, size, picks, spawn distance, Monolith, sites), C by map-grouped CV, chosen on one map half and valued on the
other: CV picks the strongest regularisation; fitted policy 50.13 / 50.34 on the two halves, a site-class policy
(one-tile / one-site / multi-site) 50.09 / 50.43, the best fixed threshold per half 50.28 / 50.26, and the fixed argmax
flips between halves (1200/never on one, 250/400 on the other). By site class and by game length the gain is flat
(one-tile 22% of maps, one-site 10%, multi 68%: all +0.4..+0.6 from 600 on). No map or state structure to gate on, so
the deny rule is one round: don't spend a lock to deny an altar before round 600.

## Ocean follow-up cleanup (2026-11-08): shared readers, slots and unreachable combat code

Initially implemented and validated in the separate `work/ocean-cleanup` worktree, based on `859dd01e3` (CHANGES
470). Integration onto CHANGES 471 and shipment as CHANGES 472 are recorded below. Reference
`variants/ocean-cleanup-base` is the original base commit's ocean, and the opponent is a frozen copy of its
hyperion (`variants/ocean-cleanup-opponent`).

Removed `Search::walk_only` and its unreachable read/grow branches, redundant `ready_known` plumbing, unused
`Pathing::travel_turns` and `unseen_probe`, and unused arguments to `idle_priority` and `recall_outruns`. Shared the
slot mapping, champion/buff readers, bush-ward setup and `farms_gold` predicate. Reader buffers remain owned by their
original callers; checked and unchecked reads and the two stun-duration interpretations remain distinct. Ward
callers retain their own exclusions and host-call ordering.

The initial candidate inverted the alternating-prefix/contiguous-tail formula instead of scanning ranks. Exhaustive
comparison against the previous loop passed 228,690 cases: each team size 0..32, both starting sides, slots -4..100.
Inlining the ward helpers and their score lambda, and checking the buff error before reading its count, avoid
helper-extraction overhead found in the initial benches.

**Combat branch review.** The obsolete branch came from CHANGES 352's reduced search for `strike_free == 4`.
CHANGES 422 deliberately added an earlier return for precisely that condition; when `debug_strike_free` is true,
the old assignment also sets `walk_only` false. It therefore has no reachable use in either mode. Restoring it
would undo an intentional decision change: the ranged walk spent the attack and disrupted farming. K1 won 51.3%
of 20,480 confirmation games and passed the panel. Full searches still offer a walk-only leaf when a strike is
reachable; removing that separate candidate (K5) lost. No behavioral restoration is warranted by this review.
Evidence: [fuel6.md, results and interpretation](ideas-2026-11-05/fuel6.md#results-k1-wins-frozen-as-variantsoc-fuel6-everything-else-lost-or-was-level),
CHANGES 352/422, and the `ffa016c74` plan.cc diff.

**Validation.** Release and benchmark builds passed. Native fastrunner, 100M fuel, `bench.py --set wide`, 26 maps
on both sides, matching draft modes and the same frozen opponent:

| Drafts | Byte-identical replays | Total play fuel, before -> after | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Own | 52/52 | 12,503,156,837 -> 12,493,831,070 | -0.0746% |
| Test | 52/52 | 12,367,354,577 -> 12,358,154,648 | -0.0744% |

All 104 pairs passed both SHA-256 and direct comparison of uncompressed `replay.repl26a` bytes. No game errors,
out-of-fuel play turns, broken draft handoffs or capped drafts. Draft fuel was identical (184,783,673 own;
79,306,259 test). After round 1, mean/p50/p90/p99/max fuel all fell in both modes; maxima 294,856 -> 294,605 own and
304,093 -> 303,816 test. Round-1 means fell, but its maximum rose by 1 fuel in each mode.

This is an aggregate fuel reduction, not a guarantee that every game or turn is cheaper. Seven own-draft and five
test-draft games used slightly more total play fuel (largest +11,429); 159,809 of 242,179 own-draft turns and 158,296
of 245,184 test-draft turns were dearer. Full per-turn/game deltas are in `verification.json`. Real-budget
equivalence was not tested.

Evidence in this worktree: `replays/fuel/ocean-cleanup/{base-wide,base-wide-td,verified-wide,verified-wide-td}.json`,
`verification.json`, `verify.py`, `cleanup.patch` and build/run logs; bundles under
`replays/fuel/games/{base-wide,base-wide-td,verified-wide,verified-wide-td}/`. For the original cleanup commit
(`5335dffc1`), the own-draft candidate `variants/ocean-cleanup-final` and release-build copy
`variants/ocean-cleanup-release` matched all 57 tracked ocean files; `variants/bench-td-ocean` matched except for
`test_draft=true`. The original source hashes are in `source-sha256.json`.

**Integration onto CHANGES 471: replay divergence investigated.** Repeated the wide benches against ocean at
`eda909f76`, retaining that commit's tuning constants and the same frozen opponent. The initial merged candidate
(`72bea1487`) matched 51/52 own-draft replays and 52/52 test-draft replays. The difference was `00monolith`, side A.
The first 27,352 replay events agree; at round 798, Willow (champion 4) starts at (26,36). The reference farms via
(27,36) and starts recall; the candidate takes a support step to (27,37) towards Prism at (30,33), carrying 278 gems.
Both win: reference round 885, 1206-531 gems; candidate round 868, 1147-531. This single game is not win-rate evidence.

Restoring combat/plan.cc, ward setup, or the champion/buff readers separately preserved the candidate replay.
Restoring the slot code restored the reference replay; narrowing that restoration to `ranks_before`'s original
loop was sufficient, while restoring only World::slot was not. The inverse formula gives the same ranks: this is
a fuel-dependent cache effect, not a turn-order error or a consequence of deleting the unreachable combat branch.

Traces at the decision show the same support inputs except for the cached farm route. Willow's heal is not ready;
`local_support` permits the step only if `approach_ready` already holds and the step advances that route. At the end
of round 797, the candidate has 207 more fuel at `prepare_approach`'s check. The trace reports remaining fuel
99,914,648 (reference) versus 99,914,855 (candidate), with floor 99,909,983 and estimated route cost 4,675. The
reference skips preparing the route and the candidate prepares it. These are diagnostic fuel readings, not an
uninstrumented measurement of the exact margin. Both traced versions retain their respective original replay
bytes on both sides of the map.

`TurnEndQueue::run` deliberately raises its floor by the excess over 100k (200k on the first turn), so this queue
still has a real-budget-sized allowance during the 100M benchmark. The benchmark's general claim that no fuel
gate trips at 100M does not hold for this queue. A cheaper calculation can therefore change subsequent support
decisions through cache availability even when its result is mathematically identical. Restoring the rank loop
passes all 104 replay comparisons on CHANGES 471, but alone leaves a small aggregate fuel increase (own +0.00570%,
test +0.00501%); further helper code-generation work is required before this version meets the cleanup's fuel gate.

Evidence: `replays/fuel/ocean-cleanup/{main-base-wide,main-base-wide-td,main-verified-wide,main-verified-wide-td}.json`,
`probe-{plan,wards,readers,slots,slot-loop,slot-world}.json`, `main-loop-wide{,-td}.json`,
`trace-{base,current}.json`, `trace-queue-{base,current}.json`, and `monolith-analysis/`. Corresponding replay bundles
are under `replays/fuel/games/`. Trace variants and isolation variants are ignored local copies, not shipped code.

**Final integrated cleanup (CHANGES 472).** Retained the original rank-count loop and the shared slot mapping.
Kept buff counts and error checks in their callers through one raw reader; the alive reader also preserves each
caller's original scratch buffer and inlining. Search receives its known readiness with the original assignment
after construction, without the redundant `ready_known` flag. Explicitly inlined `count_within`: the extracted
ward scoring had made the compiler leave that small helper out of line. No support policy or queue budget changed.

Release and benchmark builds passed. Native fastrunner, 100M, the same 26 wide maps on both sides and frozen
opponent, against `eda909f76`:

| Drafts | Byte-identical replays | Total play fuel, before -> after | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Own | 52/52 | 12,005,635,027 -> 12,005,550,007 | -0.000708% |
| Test | 52/52 | 12,208,856,050 -> 12,208,738,657 | -0.000962% |

All 104 pairs passed SHA-256 and direct comparison of uncompressed replay bytes, including `00monolith` side A.
No game errors, out-of-fuel play turns, failed handoffs or capped drafts. Draft fuel is unchanged: 184,783,673 own,
79,306,259 test. This is an aggregate saving: five own-draft games are dearer (at most 41 fuel), and 13 test-draft
games are dearer (at most 475 fuel). 38,846/234,686 own-draft turns and 49,276/241,965 test-draft turns are dearer;
the largest single-turn increases are 3,660 and 5,441 respectively, including shifted precomputation. Real-budget
equivalence was not tested.

Final evidence: `replays/fuel/ocean-cleanup/main-loop-inline-wide{,-td}.json`, `integrated-verification.json`,
`integrated-verify.py`, `integrated-source-sha256.json` and `integrated-cleanup.patch`. The tested
`variants/ocean-cleanup-loop-inline` and release copy `variants/ocean-cleanup-integrated-release` match all 57
tracked ocean files; `variants/bench-td-ocean-cleanup-loop-inline` differs only by `test_draft=true`.

## Exact ward sight (ocean = 97412ec7a, 2026-11-08; merged as CHANGES 473)

Three places that estimated a ward's sight now read it exactly (`variants/oc-wardexact` against
`variants/ocean-97412ec`, the ocean it was made from; only `fixc.cc`, `draft.cc` and `turn_order.cc` differ):

- `fixc_bush_rank`: an enemy ward sees bush tile p by its engine mask (`enemy_wards`), not "p's cluster within 8".
- The draft's `best_ward`: `own` is what every stand tile sees (camp tiles, or an altar's open tribute tiles),
  not the sight from the group's centre or the altar. A champion on an edge camp tile misses more than the centre.
- `real_distance`: our ward's mask from `ward_sight`'s cache instead of a fresh `sdk_wards` + `sdk_ward_vision` per
  call (fuel only).

One A/B, own drafts, real budget, fast runner, `wardexact-40k` (1200000-1200078, `--mix ladder-v2`, fresh):

| Variant | Games | CAND % | 95% CI | OOF CAND / REF | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all three | 40,448 | 50.3 | 49.8-50.8 | 399,918 / 401,514 (-0.4%) | level |

No failed games, broken draft handoffs or capped drafts. Not split per change, and `bench.py` identity for the
fuel-only part was not run. Left out, as riskier for fuel: exact tile ranking for the turn-end bush ward and the
reveal ward. Keeping the old bush ward by its exact mask alone would bias `ward_bushes` towards replacing it, since
the candidates keep the cluster estimate (exact <= estimate on the same tiles).

## Bad ladder maps: camp_bound and bank_floor (ocean = oc-base29, 2026-11-08; queued live, not merged)

Ocean's live losses to Fish/Mite concentrate on maps both top bots exploit (research/ideas-2026-11-08/big-levers.md). Two fixes from live replays, frozen as `bots/variants/bm-cb29` (+ `-td`) = oc-base29 + the diff in combat/fight.cc, model/safety.{h,cc}, economy/bank.cc:
- **camp_bound (A):** visible enemies in reach of a live, awake member of a group damaged within 2 rounds, a group that reaches neither us nor an ally we see, are "held by their own clear": `stand_lost_at` drops them from pursuit/join, and `recall_line` ignores them unless their blow hits us (with only those near, the line is halfway between recall and safe). Evidence: puppet reruns of v89's 00fragment games (debug traces) show our tank leaving the mirrored centre clear at 44% on `stand_lost_at` (the pursuer, Fish's Issac, was busy on its own group), then `drawn_home` at 38%; Fish cleared its group at r29 and stole ours at r37.
- **bank_floor (B):** `min_bank` becomes clamp(total map gems/4, 1, 25) (half a side's gems). This affects only gem-scarce maps (on the ladder: 03ultrastarvation 9, 00fragment 17, 01elk-arena 18, 01hooks 22; ~5% of local maps have <50 gems a side). Evidence: on ultrastarvation live, captures were equal (432/461) but tributes were 269/589, and we died carrying 171 gems against Fish's 31 (Fish tributes 52 times a game at an average bag of 11, we 11 times at 25).

The changes were judged by the non-negative bar locally (`--sprt 0.4975,0.50`), since the target is live. Blocks were continued by `~/tmp-offload/badmaps/bin/combine.py` (ab.py's per-map LLR, with block 1 first). Seeds were 1210000-1211119 (ladder-v2; varied 1210300-339, 1210700-779).

Results against oc-base29:
| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Held out (3 blocks, ladder-v2) | 49.9% (49.7-50.2) of 327,680 games (-0.09 pts); H1 at 156,739 map pairs |
| Comparison bots (direct + astraeus-td + proteus-td) | +0.14 pts pooled of 61,440 units; H1 at 35,187 |
| Harder varied mix | 50.0% of 61,440 games; undecided (LLR +1.16), not H0 |

The direct member read exactly 50.0% (10240-10240) on block 1. That is a coincidence (p ~1.5%), not a build error: the sources differ, and 2,914 of 10,240 maps changed outcome (1,457 each way). Block 2 read 49.7%. The candidate's out-of-fuel turns were up ~5% (1.73M vs 1.65M on block 3), from `camp_bound` in `stand_lost_at`. Verdict: no local regression and no local gain; queued live (priority 60, on oc-base29 = v91) to read 00fragment for A, the gem-scarce maps for B, and the overall paired score.

## Map paradigms: v87 against v86 by layout (`--mix paradigms`, 2026-11-08)

`--mix paradigms` (tools/mapgen/paradigms.mjs, commit ce7883e24) adds 12 layout styles. Their economy follows calibration 3's ladder rates. Over 2,048 maps the economy, size and count features all match the 128 ladder maps (p > 0.05). The layouts differ by design: fewer detours, fewer open maps and wider chokes. Over 1,200 maps, ocean's draft first turn peaked at 8.48M fuel (never over 10M). Suites came from seeds 1320000-1320047, one directory per paradigm (`~/tmp-offload/mapgen3/by-paradigm`). The pair was `variants/oc-base25` (v87) against `variants/oc-base23` (v86), `--no-test-draft`, release, fast runner. All games ran with 0 engine errors, so the paradigm maps are legal.

Results against oc-base23 (oc-base25's win %, 95% CI):
| Paradigm | Win % (CI) of n |
|---|---|
| braided-lanes | 51.3 (49.1-53.4) of 2,112 |
| ring-road | 51.2 (49.1-53.4) of 2,112 |
| colosseum | 51.1 (48.9-53.3) of 2,016 |
| corridors | 50.9 (48.8-53.1) of 2,016 |
| choke-web | 50.8 (48.7-53.0) of 2,016 |
| home-keeps | 50.5 (48.4-52.7) of 2,112 |
| contours | 50.4 (48.2-52.5) of 2,112 |
| mesa-field | 50.0 (47.8-52.2) of 2,016 |
| isles | 49.7 (47.5-51.9) of 2,016 |
| meander-river | 49.3 (47.1-51.5) of 2,016 |
| compartments | 48.8 (46.6-50.9) of 2,016 |
| stones | 48.6 (46.4-50.8) of 2,016 |
| **pooled** | **50.2 (49.6-50.9) of 24,576** |

- **The spread is noise.** A heterogeneity test across the 12 paradigms gives binomial chi2 8.0 (df 11, p 0.71). Using per-map scores with variance clustered by map gives chi2 9.3 (p 0.60). The DerSimonian-Laird estimate of between-paradigm spread (tau) is 0. Clustering by map barely changes the standard errors (1.0 vs 1.1 points): the two sides of a map are close to independent here.
- **Comparison.** Live (r2 gate), v87 scored -9 net flips against v86 (69 / 78 of 512, z -0.74; 64.1 vs 65.8%), so slightly worse but level. Locally, the ladder-v2 held-out SPRT `ch-held-25` (same pair, still running) read 49.9% of the first 22,258 games. The mid125 patch (CHANGES 466) on oc-base23 alone read 50.45% over 102,400 held-out games. All three readings are level and consistent within noise. No paradigm reproduces the live minus sign beyond noise: the worst, stones, is z -1.6 against the pool.
- **Verdict.** No layout effect for this pair. A per-paradigm reading needs roughly 10k games per paradigm to resolve a 1-point effect. At about 2k games per paradigm, the suites are only useful pooled, as a layout-robustness check.

## Fuel caps and budget table (v87 = oc-base25, 2026-11-09): no arm merged

[fuelcap-2026-11-09](fuelcap-2026-11-09/README.md) holds the details. All games are against oc-base25 at the real budget, with own drafts, on ladder-v2 suites with seeds 1370000-1370033.

- **Live drift is not fuel.** Live OOF per 1k rounds is flat across v86-v93 (10.6-11.7) while wins fell 65.8 → 60.5%. Local OOF matches it, and won games have as much OOF as lost ones.
- **Budget table.** It covers about 2.27M turns (`CHIST`, `tools/fuel/census/budget.py`). The mean turn is 53.6k and p99 93k. 71% of first-OOF turns passed no fuel check before running out. The ungated parts and their measured maxima: world update 36k, continue_recall's want_home 92k, wh.stand_lost 73k, strike search 82k.
- **Decomposition (8,192 games).** The 2x budget scores 53.6% (52.6-54.7). The 2x budget with gates seeing 1x scores 51.4% (50.3-52.5). So never running out is worth about +1.4 and the gated work about +2.2.
- **Per-gate arms (4,096 games each).** Raw fuel for one consumer, on top of the 1x view at 51.0: farm 54.1, guard 52.0, order 52.1, prey 51.8, queue 50.9. The farm's cut evaluation is what converts fuel into wins.
- **P1a: the strike search stops growing and pricing below `act_reserve`.** Bench-identical at 100M. Result: 49.5% (48.0-51.0) of 4,096, OOF -1.5%. Level, but it bounds the search.
- **Farm reserve.** The work after a cut uses a median of 0.47 of the reserve. Scaling the reserve by 0.75 gives 50.7% with OOF +11%; by 0.5, 50.0% with OOF +24%.
- **Step guard failing closed on lethal tiles.** 49.6% with OOF +28%.
- **Rejected.** None of the reserve or guard changes pays.
- **Raw SDK imports (v87-sdkraw): exact, -0.39% fuel.** The changes: `in_bounds` in two unsigned compares, and raw ward_cooldown, is_alive and recall. Bench replays were identical in 67/68. The remaining SDK-wrapper instructions are 1.84% of all fuel.
- **The 68th bench game changed play through the turn-end queue.** The queue reached `prepare_approach` on a cheaper turn. Without it in the queue, base and patch are identical.

## Farm loop: what finishing it is worth, and why a speedup can't finish it (v87 = oc-base25, 2026-11-09): no arm

The details are in [fuelcap-2026-11-09](fuelcap-2026-11-09/README.md#the-farm-loop-second-round-2026-11-09).

- **Raw fuel in the farm loop alone is worth about +1.5.** The 2x view arm with raw fuel only in the loop scores 52.5% (50.9-54.0) of 4,096 on dec8. The view arm scores 51.0, and raw fuel in all of `farm_turn` 54.1.
- **A cut loop has done 8 of 24 groups at about 2k a pass.** Crew pricing (`plan_crew`, 3.6k a call) is about 30% of its fuel, `live_steps` 8%, and the header and pre-bounds 11%.
- **An exact speedup finishes few cut loops.** Reaching the stop needs a median 20k more. A 20% speedup finishes 16% of cut loops, and a 50% speedup 40%.
- **A full evaluation changes the best in 29% of cut loops.** In another 29% the loop was cut before it found any best (14% before the first pass).
- **Carrying the cut loop to the next turn (v87-fresume) fails.** It is bench-identical at 100M, but dgate gives H0 at +0.04 points (6,528 units, 26,624 games).
